subject: Function-identifier
notes: PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. The FUNCTION-keyword form is fully enforced: the lexer already gives the '(' after a function name to the argument list, and a ref-mod written there instead is rejected with COBOLNET1543 citing SR6 (the standard's own RANDOM trap). The KEYWORD-OMITTED form rejects the same shape through the ordinary unresolved-name path rather than the SR6 message, and RANDOM in particular cannot be written keyword-omitted at all because it lexes as a reserved word - fix-queue PB9 owns that.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: The POSITIVE half (a function-identifier IS admissible as identifier-1) and the NEGATIVE half (it shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function) are both enforced. Before fix-queue PB8 the shape was a COBOL0001 parse error at every edition, so neither half could be reached. A non-conforming class is rejected with COBOLNET1629; national and alphanumeric results are covered by the golden, and the user-defined-function result reference-modifies through RefModPlace using the RETURNING item's own category.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: Found unenforced by the PB8 sibling sweep, not by PB8's own repro: MOVE A (3:4)(2:2) COMPILED CLEAN and silently returned A(2:2), because dataReferenceSuffix* admits unlimited ref-mods and the resolver kept only the first of each carrier while the DEFAULT-mode form outranked the SUBSCRIPT-mode one. Now counted in ONE place per reference kind and rejected with COBOLNET1630. A subscript followed by a ref-mod (the legal 8.4.3.1.4 GR1 a-to-g order) is unaffected.

subject: ACOS function
notes: PB1 EXTENDED. ACOS is now in the Verified table, so 15.8.3 r1 (a bare class-numeric constraint) is enforced end to end. The batch-2 finding was precisely a table MISS, not a missing mechanism.

subject: ACOS function
notes: HALF ENFORCED — BOTH ARMS RE-RUN IN THIS PASS. §15.8.3 r2 (validated: cite.py --check 15.8.3 "greater than or equal to" -> OK §15.8.3 2)) is a VALUE constraint; §15.3 item 14 governs the consequence (validated: "the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist" and "the implementor defines the result of the function reference" both resolve to §15.3 14)), and that condition is FATAL per §14.6.13.1.6 (validated: "| EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION | Fatal |"). ⚠ CITATION CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD AND RE-VERIFIED: the source comment at CobolIntrinsics.cs said "§14.6.13.1.1 Table 13"; cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.1 "EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION" FAILS (that clause is titled "General"). The correct clause is §14.6.13.1.6, "Exception-names and exception conditions". THE DEFECT: there is no domain test at the function body — CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs line 22 is `public static double Acos(double x) => Math.Acos(x);` — the violation is inferred downstream from NaN inside FromDouble, and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat ends `return num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true) : new NumX(RuntimeApi.Intrinsic("FromDouble", $"{call}, {ws}"), ws);`, so a FLOATING-POINT receiver bypasses the sole raise point entirely. MEASURED HERE: fixed receiver + checking ON aborts correctly ("abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): floating-point intrinsic argument out of domain (NaN result)"); an IF-condition context + checking ON also aborts correctly; fixed receiver + checking OFF gives 000000000{ = 0, which §15.3 14 permits as the implementor-defined result. The REAL-receiver arm does not raise at all. FAILING INPUT (prints `REAL  NaN`, run-unit terminates NORMALLY, with checking explicitly ENABLED): >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON / IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. ADVACOSEC2. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 D USAGE FLOAT-LONG. PROCEDURE DIVISION. MAIN-PARA. COMPUTE D = FUNCTION ACOS(2). DISPLAY "REAL  " D. STOP RUN.  §15.3 14 is receiver-independent — nothing in it conditions the exception on the receiver's USAGE. ⚠ SECOND-GAP CLAIM WITHDRAWN BY THIS PASS: the prior record charged a second defect, that a LITERAL out-of-range argument is statically decidable and so §4.2.2 "obliges" a compile-time diagnostic. Reading §4.2.2 to its end refutes that — para 3 closes "For elements not specified in general formats or in explicit syntax rules, it is left to the implementor's discretion to determine what is syntactically distinguishable." A compile-time reject of FUNCTION ACOS(2) is therefore a QUALITY improvement, not a conformance obligation, and must not be written into the fix as a spec requirement. The conformance defect is the real-receiver bypass alone. FIX (root cause, not the call site): move the domain test to the BODY, as LOG/LOG10 already do — `Log(double x) => x <= 0 ? Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...) : Math.Log(x)` — so the raise is independent of how the result is later quantized. SIBLING SWEEP RE-RUN HERE, same program with a FLOAT-LONG receiver and checking ON: FUNCTION ASIN(2) prints `ASIN NaN` and FUNCTION SQRT(0 - 4) prints `SQRT NaN`, both terminating normally — the identical bypass, so the fix is one edit repeated across the trig/SQRT rows, not an ACOS special case. ⚠ TEST-REF REMAINS STRUCK, RE-CONFIRMED ON DISK: conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec exists (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs) and uses AssertSpec with no legacy oracle, but (a) its expected +000000 is precisely the value §15.3 14 leaves implementor-defined — the test's own comment says "the legacy-compatible default the goldens encode" — so it is not computed from the spec, and (b) it never enables checking, so it never exercises this rule's normative consequence. test-needed: a checking-ON arm and a real-receiver arm. Editions basis as for AR-15.8.3-1 (§8.11 list; no Annex E/F item; 85 = the amended 85) — NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: ACOS function
notes: DIVERGES SUSTAINED ON RE-MEASUREMENT (this pass re-ran every number below; the pre-adversarial record had this as PARTIAL, which understated a demonstrated wrong result). §15.8.4 r1 (validated: cite.py --check 15.8.4 "approximation of the arccosine" -> OK §15.8.4 1)) asserts THREE things: the value approximates arccos, it is >= 0, and it is <= π. THE LATITUDE DOES NOT COVER IT — this is the load-bearing derivation and it is stronger than the prior record's: §15.4.1 2) (validated) says "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION." §15.8 (read whole, §15.8.1 through §15.8.4) specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so ACOS falls in that sentence — and §15.8.4 r1 IS the "otherwise specified", so the two bounds survive the native-arithmetic latitude intact. The residual §15.4.1 latitude (validated: "the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor") is over CHARACTERISTICS and REPRESENTATION — the implementor may pick 9 fraction digits, but having picked them must still return a value satisfying r1, and 3.141592653 is representable and satisfies it. The implementation instead returns the next value UP. VIOLATION 1 — THE <= π CONJUNCT, MEASURED. ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9) in IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat sets a scale-9 floor, and FromDouble closes with `return (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);` — round-to-NEAREST, so π*1e9 = 3141592653.59 quantizes UP. Run here on one program: 01 R PIC S9(1)V9(17) -> `17dp 31415926535897932H` = 3.14159265358979328; 01 R9 PIC S9(1)V9(9) -> `9dp  314159265D` = 3.141592654, over π = 3.14159265358979323846 by ~4.1e-10; and `IF FUNCTION ACOS(-1) > 3.14159265358979324` takes the TRUE branch, printing "ACOS(-1) EXCEEDS PI" (a receiver-less condition renders at Receiver.Scale 0, so the floor still gives ws = 9). ⚠ FACTUAL CORRECTIONS RE-MEASURED HERE, both against the ORIGINAL adjudication: the overshoot is NOT present at every fixed-point scale and is NOT caused by MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero (that flag only breaks ties) — at 01 R6 PIC S9(1)V9(6) the stored value is `314159B` = 3.141592, WITHIN π, because the scale-9 temporary truncates on store. The normative returned value is the §15.4 temporary, which is 3.141592654 in every one of these cases, so the violation is IN THE TEMPORARY and merely masked at receiver scales below 9. VIOLATION 2 — INDEPENDENT OF ROUNDING: with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking ENABLED and a FLOAT-LONG receiver, FUNCTION ACOS(2) returns NaN and the run unit terminates normally (the AR-15.8.3-2 program, re-run here, prints `REAL  NaN`). §15.3 14's implementor-defined-result latitude is explicitly conditioned on "checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled", so it does not reach this case, and NaN satisfies neither conjunct. Same RenderFloat bypass, charged here as a second violation of r1 because the returned VALUE is wrong, not merely the exception. THE OTHER CONJUNCTS HOLD, MEASURED AT 01 R PIC S9(4)V9(9): ACOS(0)=1.570796327 (π/2), ACOS(1)=0.000000000, ACOS(0.5)=1.047197551 (π/3), ACOS((0.5+0.5)/2)=1.047197551; Math.Acos cannot return a negative, so >= 0 is never at risk on the fixed path. FIX: clamp the quantized result of a closed-bound float row to its normative interval at the working scale (or quantize toward the bound), inside the one FromDouble call site rather than per function. SIBLING SWEEP: every §15.4.1 float row with a CLOSED normative bound that quantizes through the one FromDouble is exposed identically — ASIN's ±π/2 (§15.10.4) and FUNCTION PI itself; ATAN's open bound (±π/2 exclusive) is not. test-needed: no spec-derived test pins any ACOS returned value. DELIBERATELY NOT CITED: FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy (which does carry FUNCTION ACOS(1)) is a legacy-oracle differential and its name ends in MatchesLegacy; tests/nist/programs/IF101A.cob and IF401M.cob are NIST regression goldens; no tests/conformance/**/*.cob case references ACOS. Editions basis as for AR-15.8.3-1 (§8.11 list; no Annex E/F item; 85 = the amended 85) — NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: ANNUITY function
notes: SURVIVED ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — NO DOMAIN CHECK. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.9.3 "greater than or equal to zero"` -> OK §15.9.3 2). §15.3's closing argument paragraph read verbatim: 'The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist. If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference' — with checking ENABLED it shall be raised. Body re-read at review time and unchanged: `public static double Annuity(double rate, double periods) => rate == 0 ? 1d / periods : rate / (1 - Math.Pow(1 + rate, -periods));` — no `rate < 0` guard, no ExceptionState.ArgumentError call, unlike Log/Log10 fourteen lines above in the same file which do call it for their §15.55.3/§15.56.3 domains. The runtime machinery exists and fires; ANNUITY never reaches it. FAILING INPUT re-run independently (PROGRAM-ID ADVD02): PROCEDURE begins `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, then `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( -0.5 3 ). DISPLAY "NEG-RATE=" R.` with `01 R PIC S9(5)V9(4).`, and a trailing `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION LOG ( 0 ).` -> prints `NEG-RATE=00000071D` (+0.0714) and only afterwards aborts on the LOG line with `abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): LOG argument must be > 0 (ISO 15.55.3 r2)`, proving checking was in force when ANNUITY silently accepted the negative rate. The literal -0.5 also makes this statically decidable, so §4.2.2 para 3 independently requires a compile-time indication. EDITIONS: all four — not derivable from the spec or Annex E (see AR-15.9.3-1). test-needed.

subject: ANNUITY function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM DIVERGES — THE PRIOR RECORD'S FAILING INPUTS NO LONGER REPRODUCE. Its DIVERGES rested entirely on CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble saturating at long.MaxValue (`if (scaled >= 9.2e18) return long.MaxValue;`) with the caller quantizing at `ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)`, so the clamp bit at |value| ~ 9.2e9. That defect is FIXED in the working tree (fix-queue PB5): FromDouble now returns Int128 and clamps at 1.7e38, which at ws >= 9 is past any declarable PICTURE. All of the prior record's inputs were re-run on the current build and every one is now right: `01 RB PIC 9(12)V99.` / `COMPUTE RB = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( 10000000000 1 ).` -> `01000000000099` = 10000000000.99 against the exact EAE 10000000001.00 (a cent at the 17th significant digit — squarely the §15.4.1 native approximation), NOT the 9223372036.85 previously reported; `01 RA PIC 9(2)V9(18).` / `ANNUITY ( 9 1 )` -> `10000000000000000000` = exactly 10; `01 R1 PIC 9(9)V9(15).` / `ANNUITY ( 9999 1 )` -> exactly 10000, as does `01 R2 PIC 9(9)V9(9).`. WHAT HOLDS: both EAE branches are written literally and correctly — `rate == 0 ? 1d / periods : rate / (1 - Math.Pow(1 + rate, -periods))` is §15.9.4 r1a and r1b; ANNUITY(0.05, 10) -> 0.1295045 (EAE 0.129504574965..., truncated by the un-ROUNDED COMPUTE) and the r1a branch gives 1/4 = 0.2500000. §15.4.1 validated: 'When native arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified, the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression' -> OK §15.4.1. WHY STILL PARTIAL — THE SECOND HALF: §15.4.1 r1 (validated: `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression"` -> OK §15.4.1 1)) makes the returned value under standard-decimal/standard-binary arithmetic *shall equal* the EAE, and that half is NOT implemented — IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore loud-rejects ANNUITY there. Reproduced on the current build (PROGRAM-ID ADVD06): with `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD.` and with `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( 0.05 10 ).` -> `error COBOLNET0899: FUNCTION ANNUITY under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD[-DECIMAL] is recognized but not yet implemented ...`, i.e. legal COBOL turned away. FIX: evaluate the §15.9.4 EAE in the §8.8.1.5 standard-decimal intermediate (CobolDec) so the staging can be lifted. EDITIONS: all four — not derivable from the spec or Annex E (see AR-15.9.3-1). test-needed: no spec-derived test covers §15.9.4. tests/conformance/negative/arith-standard-intrinsic-staged.cob names ANNUITY only in its comment — its program is FUNCTION VARIANCE — and the in-flight tests/conformance/2023/pb5_float_quantize_range.cob does call `FUNCTION ANNUITY(10000000000 1)` but never DISPLAYs the receiver for that statement (its golden pins only `NO-SIZE-ERROR`), so it does not assert the returned value and cannot close this row.

subject: ASIN function
notes: PB1 EXTENDED. NOTE THIS ROW DID NOT EXIST until the extractor fix: 15.10.3 is headed 'Argument*s* rules' and the literal-spelling KINDS map never recognised it, so ASIN's two rules were absent from the denominator entirely. Bare class-numeric constraint, now enforced.

subject: ASIN function
notes:
test-needed. VERDICT DIVERGES — upheld on adversarial re-adjudication and independently reproduced by this reviewer from a freshly written program.

CITATION RE-VALIDATED MECHANICALLY: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.10.4 "approximation of the arcsine of argument-1" -> OK §15.10.4 1). The rule is one sentence with TWO halves and only the first holds.

TEXT NOTE: §15.10.4 r1 as transcribed sets "-p/2 ... +p/2" with a lowercase Latin p. The sibling §15.11.4 r1 carries a real U+03C0 ("greater than -π/2 and less than +π/2"), as does §15.8.4 r1 ("less than or equal to π") — both cite.py-validated — so the p is a defect of the printed standard faithfully carried into specs/ISO_COBOL.md, not a transcription error. The only sensible reading is pi/2, and the ATAN/ACOS siblings confirm it.

HALF 1 — "the approximation of the arcsine of argument-1" — HOLDS. src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Asin is "public static double Asin(double x) => Math.Asin(x)", and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat routes the catalog's Float row to it. Measured by me: ASIN(0.5)=0.523598776, ASIN(-0.5)=-0.523598776, ASIN(0)=0.000000000, ASIN(FUNCTION SIN(0.5))=0.500000000. All correct to scale 9.

HALF 2 — "greater than or equal to -pi/2 and less than or equal to +pi/2" — IS VIOLATED, at both endpoints §15.10.3 r2 explicitly admits ("The value of argument-1 shall be greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1", cite.py-validated). These are not out-of-domain arguments; they are the legal edge of the domain.

§15.4.1 DOES NOT LICENSE IT. ASIN has no equivalent arithmetic expression, so the governing sentence is §15.4.1's last: "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION." §15.10.4 r1 does otherwise specify. The neighbouring "When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor" licenses the REPRESENTATION (here: 9 fraction digits) — having chosen that representation, the implementor must still pick a value inside the stated bound, and 1.570796326 is available and is an equally good approximation.

THE BREACH IS INTRODUCED BY THE QUANTIZATION, NOT BY Math.Asin. Binary64 Math.Asin(1) is 1.5707963267948965580, which IS <= pi/2 = 1.5707963267948966192. src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble then computes "double scaled = d * Pow10.AsDouble(scale)" and returns "(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)" with NO clamp to any per-function range; IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat calls it at "int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)". Rounding away from zero at the domain endpoint pushes the result OVER the bound.

CONCRETE FAILING INPUT — written and run by me with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file> --run:

       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ADVRV01.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> 1.57079632679489662 is pi/2 rounded UP at 17 fraction digits,
      *> so it is >= the true pi/2.
       01 HALFPI  PIC S9V9(17) VALUE 1.57079632679489662.
       01 NHALFPI PIC S9V9(17) VALUE -1.57079632679489662.
       01 R       PIC S9V9(9).
       01 R17     PIC S9V9(17).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           DISPLAY "ASIN1  = " R
           IF R > HALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION: ASIN(1) > PI/2" END-IF
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ASIN(-1)
           DISPLAY "ASINM1 = " R
           IF R < NHALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION: ASIN(-1) < -PI/2" END-IF
           COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           DISPLAY "ASIN1-17 = " R17
           IF R17 > HALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION17: ASIN(1) > PI/2" END-IF
           DISPLAY "DIRECT: " FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           STOP RUN.

ACTUAL OUTPUT (verbatim; the trailing letter is the signed-DISPLAY overpunch — G = +7, P = -7, D = +4):
    ASIN1  = 157079632G           -> +1.570796327, over pi/2 by ~2.05e-10
    VIOLATION: ASIN(1) > PI/2
    ASINM1 = 157079632P           -> -1.570796327
    VIOLATION: ASIN(-1) < -PI/2
    ASIN1-17 = 15707963267948966D -> +1.57079632679489664, still over pi/2
    VIOLATION17: ASIN(1) > PI/2
    DIRECT: 1.570796327

The scale-17 line matters: the breach is NOT a 9-digit artifact. At ws=17 the "d * 1e17" product rounds up to 157079632679489664, so widening the working scale does not fix it. The repair has to be at the quantization, not at the precision.

BOUNDARY OF THE DEFECT (checked, so the fix is aimed correctly): RenderFloat's other branch, "num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true)", bypasses FromDouble entirely, so a COMP-2 receiver keeps the conforming binary64 1.5707963267948966 and does NOT breach. The defect is exactly the fixed-point-receiver path.

PATTERN SWEEP (CLAUDE.md rule 4 — context for the fix, deliberately NOT extra records): the defect lives in the shared quantization, so every §15.4.1 float-family function whose returned-value rule states a RANGE is exposed. Confirmed by me in the same session by running it: FUNCTION ACOS(-1) yields 3.141592654, which exceeds pi = 3.14159265358979, against §15.8.4 r1 "greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to π". §15.11.4 r1 (ATAN — a STRICT "less than +π/2", so even more exposed) and §15.75.4 r1 (RANDOM, 0 <= r < 1) sit on the same round-up. The structural repair is a per-catalog-row returned-value range carried into the ONE FromDouble quantization site (clamp, or round toward zero at a stated endpoint), not a hand-written clamp per runtime body — a hand-maintained list where a structure belongs is what CLAUDE.md rule 5 forbids.

EDITIONS, ESTABLISHED FROM THE SPEC AND NOT FROM IntrinsicCatalog's ROW: ASIN occurs in specs/ISO_COBOL.md only in the table of contents, the index, §8.11 Intrinsic function names, the §15.6 summary table and §15.10 itself; it appears in NO Annex E added/changed list, so the returned-value rule is unchanged across the editions this compiler models. Caveat recorded: intrinsic functions reached the 85 line via the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment rather than base ISO 1989:1985; on this compiler's modelling of --std 85 the rule applies to all four, and I confirmed all four editions produce identical values.

COVERAGE: no spec-derived test. A grep of tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance and tests/conformance restricted to *.cs/*.cob/*.json finds no ASIN case at all; the frozen legacy tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Runtime/IntrinsicFunctionTests.cs#Asin_ViaDispatch and the NIST goldens IF103A/IF401M cannot close the row. The test this row needs is an ENDPOINT test (ASIN(1) and ASIN(-1)) with the bound computed from §15.10.4 — note that a test written only at ASIN(0.5) would pass today and pin the defect open.

subject: ATAN function
notes: PB1 EXTENDED. ATAN 15.11.3 r1, bare class-numeric constraint, enforced.

subject: ATAN function
notes:
SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS: verdict SURVIVES. Independently reproduced, and the ONE escape reading that could have rescued a CONFORMS is now closed by a receiver-free repro rather than by argument. Two factual errors in the prior record's CAUSE paragraph are corrected below — both would have misdirected the fix.

CITATION re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.11.4 "greater than"` => OK  §15.11.4 1). Confirmed against the PRINTED page (render-spec-page.py 850, folio 820): "The returned value is the approximation of the arctangent of argument-1 and is greater than −π/2 and less than +π/2." One rule, two halves — BOTH checked below.

THE BOUND IS NORMATIVE, chain re-derived from the spec text and each link validated. §15.4 (`cite.py --check 15.4 "temporary elementary data item"` => OK): "The evaluation of a function produces a returned value in a temporary elementary data item" — the returned value IS what that temporary holds. §15.4.1 (`cite.py --check 15.4.1 "unless otherwise specified in the function definition"` => OK): "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED in the function definition." ATAN has no equivalent arithmetic expression and §15.11.4 IS that otherwise-specification. That the interval is deliberate is confirmed by the neighbour: `cite.py --check 15.10.4 "greater than or equal to"` => OK — ASIN gets a CLOSED interval where ATAN gets an OPEN one.

HALF ONE (the approximation) IS CORRECT — verified, so this is a genuine one-sided defect and not an unexamined edge. Re-run: ATAN(1)=00078539816C (+0.785398163 = π/4, radians per §15.11.1), ATAN(-1)=00078539816L (−0.785398163), ATAN(0)=00000000000{, ATAN(0.5)=00046364760I (+0.463647609) both as a literal and as a PIC S9V9(9) item.

HALF TWO (the bound) FAILS, BOTH SIGNS — re-run by this reviewer, default --std 2023, exit 0, R PIC S9(3)V9(9):
  COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000).  => R=00157079632G  (overpunch G = 7+, i.e. +1.570796327 > +π/2 = 1.5707963267948966...)
  COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(-4000000000). => R=00157079632P  (overpunch P = 7−, i.e. −1.570796327 < −π/2)
Threshold measured, not estimated: ATAN(3392000000) => ...G (out of bound), ATAN(3000000000) and ATAN(2000000000) => ...F (+1.570796326, the largest scale-9 value INSIDE the interval, which is what a conforming implementation should return). An ordinary 10-digit argument suffices; this is not an exotic input.

ESCAPE READING CLOSED BY A RECEIVER-FREE REPRO (new this pass, and the reason a CONFORMS is not available). The only serious defence is: "§15.4.1 lets the implementor define the characteristics of the temporary under native arithmetic; our temporary is the binary64 double (in bounds) and the scale-9 value is a STORE artifact." It does not hold — with NO receiver at all, the function-identifier's own temporary is out of bounds. §15.4.1 NOTE 2 makes a relation on a function-identifier the standard's own probe of the returned value. All four of these DISPLAYs fired:

       01 P9 PIC S9V9(9) VALUE 1.570796326.
       ...
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) > P9        *> GT-LARGEST-INBOUND-SCALE9
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) = 1.570796327          *> EQ, out of bound
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(-4000000000) = -1.570796327        *> EQ, out of bound
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) > 1.570796326795       *> fired

The fourth is decisive: atan(4e9) = 1.5707963265448966 is LESS than 1.570796326795, so a binary64 temporary would make it FALSE. It fired, proving the materialized temporary in a relation is the scale-9 quantized 1.570796327 — quantization happens while PRODUCING the value, not while storing it.

CAUSE, read in the code — TWO CORRECTIONS to the prior record. `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat` computes `int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)` and, when the receiver is not real, wraps the call in FromDouble at ws; in a relation condition Receiver.Scale contributes nothing, so ws = 9 (the fourth probe above proves it — the prior record's "ws = 10 from the comparand" reasoning was wrong). `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble` ends `return (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);` — the cast is **Int128**, not `long` as the prior record wrote. ⛔ AND THE MIDPOINT MODE IS NOT THE CULPRIT: atan(4e9) x 1e9 = 1570796326.5448966, whose fraction is .5449, not a midpoint — EVERY round-to-nearest mode rounds it up. Changing MidpointRounding would NOT fix this; the defect is round-to-NEAREST at the quantization step having no knowledge of the function's declared open bound. `CobolIntrinsics.Float.Atan` is `Math.Atan(x)` and is itself fine (Math.Atan never returns a double outside the interval). All three symbols verified literally present.

CONFORMING PATH, re-run and confirmed: `01 D USAGE COMP-2. COMPUTE D = FUNCTION ATAN(1000000000000).` prints 1.5707963267938967, because RenderFloat returns `new NumX(call, 0, Real: true)` and skips FromDouble when num.Receiver.Real. So the defect is exactly the fixed-point quantization path.

FIX SHAPE: clamp the ATAN quantization to the largest value strictly inside (−π/2, +π/2) at the working scale — equivalently, round toward zero when the magnitude would land on or beyond the scale-ws representation of π/2. NOT a global switch to truncation: FromDouble's hazard-H2 comment records why round-to-nearest is right for the rest of the family (truncation turns LOG10(1000) = 2.9999999999999996 into 2.999999999). The bounded-range siblings ACOS (§15.8.4) and ASIN (§15.10.4) need the same audit; their CLOSED intervals make them a different and possibly non-defective case, so each needs its own rule read rather than a copied fix.

HARDENED AGAINST THE OTHER READING. If "π" meant the implementor's own approximation rather than exact π, the finding still stands: π/2 rounded to scale 9 is itself 1.570796327, so the returned value would then EQUAL the implementor's +π/2 and "less than" still fails. There is no reading of §15.11.4 r1 under which 1.570796327 at scale 9 is admissible.

EDITIONS: as for the other two rows — Annex E.2 item 13's list of names new in 2023 does not include ATAN, establishing 2014 and 2023; §15.11.4 carries no edition qualification and Annex E records no ATAN change; the 85/2002 boundary is not establishable from this document, so all four per the brief's fallback, NOT from IntrinsicCatalog's MinEdition column.

test-needed. No spec-derived test computes an ATAN value or its bounds; `grep -rln ATAN tests/conformance/` returns nothing. The only ATAN assertion on disk is IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy pinning ATAN(0) against the legacy oracle — struck as a MatchesLegacy differential, and it would in any case happily pin this defect, since it exercises only the one argument at which the bound cannot be reached. The covering test must assert the BOUND at a large argument (e.g. FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) < the scale-9 representation of π/2), expected value computed from §15.11.4 r1.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: UPHELD on adversarial re-review; every repro re-run against src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe. Citation re-validated (cite.py --check 15.12.3 'shall be a usage display or national data item or literal' -> OK, rule 1); the edition is established INDEPENDENTLY of IntrinsicCatalog from Annex E.3.3 item 22 -- 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT. This function has been added to enable conversion between different number bases in the range 2-16' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43956) -- so 2023 only. NEITHER half of r1 is enforced at bind time: BASECONVERT is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (the whole dictionary is 11 entries and none is BASECONVERT), and CheckArgumentClasses opens with `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;`, so the PB1 §15.3 screen is a no-op for this function; the only check anywhere is the runtime 2..16 range test. SIX violations, EVERY ONE compiled with ZERO diagnostics (cobol.exe with no --run: exit 0, no output) and run with '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' at the default --std 2023. (a) LEGAL SOURCE ABORTS AT RUN TIME: `01 R PIC X(24).` / `MOVE FUNCTION BASECONVERT(255, 10, 16) TO R.` throws `CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: intrinsic string argument 'BoundNumericLiteral'`. r1 explicitly admits that shape -- for a base below 11 argument-1 'shall ALSO be an unsigned integer data item or literal', and an unsigned integer literal is a numeric literal. The asymmetry proves defect, not policy: the data-item twin `01 ND PIC 9(4) VALUE 255.` / BASECONVERT(ND, 10, 16) prints FF correctly. Root cause is IntrinsicRenderer's StrArgVisitor: `public string Visit(BoundNumericLiteral n) => Loud(n);`. (b) EQUAL BASES accepted: BASECONVERT("FF", 16, 16) prints FF; r1 requires 'unequal values', a VALUE constraint, so §15.3 ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') requires the EC even with checking ON. (c) WRONG USAGE accepted: `01 NB PIC 9(4) COMP VALUE 255.` / BASECONVERT(NB, 10, 16) prints FF; usage binary is not 'a usage display or national data item'. (d) NUMERIC-EDITED accepted: `01 ED PIC ZZ9 VALUE 255.` / BASECONVERT(ED, 10, 16) prints FF; PIC ZZ9 is class alphanumeric (§8.5.2.1 Table 2) and is not an unsigned INTEGER data item, which r1 requires at base 10. (e) NON-INTEGER BASE accepted: BASECONVERT("FF", 16.5, 10) is silently truncated to 16 by IntrinsicRenderer.ArgInt and prints 255; r1 requires 'numeric integer literals'. (f) A STATICALLY DECIDABLE RANGE VIOLATION is run-time-only: BASECONVERT("FF", 20, 10) compiles clean and only aborts at run time, where §4.2.2 para 3 requires the warning mechanism to indicate violations of rules 'not identified as general formats or syntax rules, but nevertheless specify elements that are syntactically distinguishable'. Legal shapes that DO work, so the fix must not over-reject: alphanumeric literal, PIC X item, group item, PIC N national item, nested BASECONVERT, unsigned PIC 9 DISPLAY item, and argument-2/argument-3 supplied as PIC 99 DATA ITEMS. test-needed: no spec-derived test exercises any argument-rejection leg -- the only coverage that exists (IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.BaseConvert_ReExpressesInTargetBase_2023 and tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.cob) is valid conversions only.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD, NOTES CORRECTED. Citation re-validated (cite.py --check 15.12.3 'the basic-letters A to F are used in sequence' -> OK, rule 2). The digit-range core IS right: BaseConvert maps '0'-'9' and 'A'-'F' and calls ExceptionState.ArgumentError for an invalid digit or a digit >= fromBase -- re-verified, BASECONVERT("15", 2, 10) aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): BASECONVERT: 5 is not a base-2 digit', and an EMBEDDED space is rejected the same way (`01 EM PIC X(6) VALUE "F F".` / BASECONVERT(EM, 16, 10) -> "EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): ' ' is not a base-16 digit"). TWO defects, both re-run. (1) THE ZERO-DIGIT INPUT. The body does value.Trim() before the loop, so an argument-1 that is ALL SPACES -- not one character of which is a digit -- falls out of the loop with acc = 0 and returns "0" with no exception. Repro (compiles clean, checking ON): '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' / `01 BL PIC X(6) VALUE SPACES.` `01 R PIC X(24).` / `MOVE FUNCTION BASECONVERT(BL, 10, 16) TO R.` prints 'BLANK=[0                       ]'. r2 plus §15.3 require EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist, not a fabricated zero; §15.12.4 has no 'digits in argument-1' to represent. (2) THE TRIM POLICY IS UNDECIDED, NOT MERELY LENIENT, AND MUST BE SETTLED BY THE FIX. Trim() strips LEADING as well as trailing spaces, so BASECONVERT("  FF  ", 16, 10) prints 255. Stripping TRAILING blanks is defensible implementor latitude (a fixed-width item could otherwise never be an argument unless exactly filled); LEADING blanks in a left-justified alphanumeric item are CONTENT, not padding, and r2 says the characters used in argument-1 shall be digits. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION, which must not be inherited as settled: it asserted that accepting lowercase 'a'-'f' 'is admissible' on the strength of §3.16 alone. §3.16 does read 'uppercase letter A through Z or lowercase letter a through z' (cite.py --check 3.16 -> OK), but §8.1.3.2 GR3 a) (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 'treated in a case-sensitive manner' -> OK) says 'COBOL basic letters, when specified in the non-hexadecimal formats of alphanumeric and national literals, are treated in a case-sensitive manner, unless specific rules require otherwise', and §15.12.4 pins the RESULT to 'the upper-case letters A-F'. Argument-1's characters are literal/data content, not a COBOL word, so the case-sensitive limb governs unless r2's 'basic-letters A to F' is read as the specific rule requiring otherwise. Verified behaviour: BASECONVERT("ff", 16, 10) prints 255. The r2 fix must decide this deliberately (survey the other compilers, per the implementor-latitude doctrine) rather than bake the current acceptance in. test-needed.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: UPHELD. Citations validated: cite.py --check 15.12.3 'The maximum length of the input argument' -> OK rule 3, and the enforcing twin cite.py --check 15.4 'maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value' -> OK ('If the length of the returned value exceeds the maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value, an EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'). The rule is bounded by an implementor-defined maximum data-item length and THIS PROJECT DEFINES NONE: no maximum data-item or returned-value length appears anywhere in docs/CONFORMANCE.md, and BASECONVERT has no entry at all in docs/COBOLNET_INTRINSICS_DESIGN.md. VERIFIED HALF -- nothing legal is refused: a System.Numerics.BigInteger accumulator and an unbounded StringBuilder result, so `01 BIG PIC X(40) VALUE ALL "F".` / BASECONVERT(BIG, 16, 10) returns the exact 49-digit 1461501637330902918203684832716283019655932542975 untruncated, and `01 BIG PIC X(2000) VALUE ALL "F".` / BASECONVERT(BIG, 16, 2) yields a result of length exactly 8000 (FUNCTION LENGTH over the nested call reports 000008000), with no diagnostic and no cap. UNVERIFIED HALF -- the boundary itself: with no maximum defined or documented, nothing can set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION for an input or a returned value that exceeds it (§15.4), the failure mode at the de-facto .NET string limit is an OutOfMemory abort rather than the standard's exception condition, and there is no way to state whether the implementation honours r3. Defining AND documenting the maximum data-item / returned-value length is a project-wide implementor-defined element (the Annex A conformance statement), not a BASECONVERT-local fix; r3 cannot close until it exists. test-needed.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. Citation re-validated (cite.py --check 15.12.4 'used in ascending sequence to represent the digits 10 to 15' -> OK, rule 1). VERIFIED HALF -- for every argument shape that actually reaches the runtime the rule holds, and I recomputed every value by hand from r1 rather than from any oracle: the body accumulates acc = acc*fromBase + d and re-expresses acc with the literal table "0123456789ABCDEF" (upper-case, ascending). Re-run: "222" base 3 -> 26; "444" base 5 -> 124; "888" base 9 -> 728; "AAA" base 11 -> 1330; "BBB" base 12 -> 1727; "DDD" base 14 -> 2743; "CA" base 15 -> 190; "255" base 7 -> 138; 100 base 10 -> "91" base 11 and "72" base 14; 140 base 10 -> "AA" base 13; "1010" base 2 -> "A" base 16; "00FF" base 16 -> "11111111" base 2 (leading zeros absorbed); "0" -> "0"; a 40-digit hex input -> the exact 49-digit decimal (BigInteger, no precision loss); a 2000-character hex input -> an 8000-character base-2 result. subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2. The DIVERGES verdict is UPHELD - I reproduced both previously-reported divergences myself on the built CLI - but the RECORD IS CORRECTED: the prior adjudication wrongly pushed a THIRD site of the same defect out of scope, and that site is an UNHANDLED RUNTIME CRASH on legal COBOL. Every citation below re-validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check (§15.13.4 r1, §15.13.1, §15.2 item 2, §15.4, §8.8.1.1, §8.8.4.2.8, §8.3.3.3.2 all resolve to the quoted text).

DIVERGENCE 1 - SILENT WRONG BIT CONFIGURATION FOR ANY argument-1 >= 2^63. §15.13.4 r1: the returned value 'has the same bit configuration as the binary representation of the value of argument-1'. §8.3.3.3.2 ('The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals ... 31 digits', verified) and this compiler's own Int128 numeric channel make a 19-25 digit positive integer argument legal COBOL it otherwise handles correctly. MY OWN RUN (--std 2023, PIC 9(25) source items, argument-2 = 70 so the §15.13.4 left-truncation clause cannot apply): 2^62 -> correct; 2^63-1 -> correct (63 one-bits); 2^63 (9223372036854775808) -> SEVENTY ZEROS, required is 6 zeros then '1' then 63 zeros; 2^64+5 (18446744073709551621) -> '...000101' with the 2^64 bit SILENTLY DROPPED. No exception, no diagnostic - the cliff is exactly at 2^63. §15.4's implementor-maximum escape does not cover it: §15.4 scopes that maximum to 'the length of the returned value', and the returned length here is 70, far under this compiler's own documented 8191 cap; §15.13.3 r1 is satisfied (the argument IS a positive integer), so EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION does not cover it either. ROOT CAUSE, read in the generated C# (m1.g.cs): IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt renders EVERY integer-kind intrinsic argument as an unchecked truncating '(long)(...)' cast - the emitted line is literally 'CobolIntrinsics.BooleanOfInteger((long)(V63), (long)(70L))' where V63 is an Int128 - and the runtime body CobolIntrinsics.BooleanOfInteger(long value, long length) additionally caps its bit loop at 'i < 63'. BOTH sites must widen; widening one leaves the other as the cliff. AsInt is the SHARED integer-argument bridge, so every sibling integer-argument intrinsic needs the same sweep.

DIVERGENCE 2 - THE RESULT IS NOT OF CLASS/CATEGORY BOOLEAN. §15.13.4 r1 first sentence: 'The returned value is a boolean item of usage bit'; §15.13.1 'The function type is boolean'; §15.2 item 2 'Boolean functions. These are of the class and category boolean. Boolean functions have an implicit usage bit', plus §15.2's 'the function so described may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified'; §8.8.4.2.8 'An operand of class boolean may be compared with another operand of class boolean'. REPRODUCED BY ME at --std 2023 (the prior report states the same at 2002/2014): (i) 'IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(544, 6) = B"100000"' -> error COBOLNET0844 'a boolean operand may be compared only with another boolean operand or the figurative constant ZERO'; (ii) 'COMPUTE B8 = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) B-AND B"00001111"' -> error COBOLNET1511 'is not a valid boolean operand'. AND THE MIRROR, also reproduced: 'IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) = "00000101"' is ACCEPTED and evaluates TRUE, an alphanumeric relation over a class-boolean operand that COBOLNET0844's own message text cites §8.8.4.2.1 F1 SR2/SR3 as excluding. The divergence is bidirectional - legal boolean uses rejected, illegal alphanumeric uses accepted - because the result silently carries the alphanumeric '0'/'1' substrate. Also reproduced: 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) + 1' binds clean and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException('string-class FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER in a numeric context') at RUN time, where §8.8.1.1 ('An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal, the figurative constant ZERO ...', verified) makes it a compile-time error.

DIVERGENCE 3 - NEW IN THIS PASS; THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION WRONGLY FILED IT AS 'a §15.50 row, not §15.13.4'. THAT DISMISSAL IS WRONG, and I disproved it with a control run. §15.13.4 r1's SECOND sentence is 'in order to return a boolean item whose length is specified by argument-2 in terms of boolean positions'; §15.50.4 r1 makes FUNCTION LENGTH over an elementary boolean data item return that length in boolean positions, and §15.50.3 r1 admits 'a data item of any class or category'. MY RUN, one program, --std 2023: 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abcdef"))' prints LEN-UC=0006 (a nested ALPHANUMERIC intrinsic works), while the very next statement 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8))' - required value 8 - dies with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException('FUNCTION LENGTH argument (a numeric/figurative literal is not a valid argument, ISO 15.50.3)'). It is therefore NOT a generic §15.50 gap; it is specific to the BOOLEAN result and is the same root cause as divergence 2. NAMED SITE: in IntrinsicBinder.cs, BOTH BindLengthFold and IsStringOperand carry the nested-intrinsic pattern 'BoundComputedOperand { Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall { ResultCategory: PicCategory.Alphanumeric or PicCategory.National } }' - Boolean is absent from the list in both, so a boolean function result falls into the '_' error arm. Note IsStringOperand's BoundFieldOperand arm DOES include PicCategory.Boolean: the same rule is written twice and the second copy forgot boolean.

COMMON ROOT CAUSE (one rule, four places). IntrinsicCatalog.ResultCategory correctly maps IntrinsicType.Boolean -> PicCategory.Boolean, and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is the ONLY IntrinsicType.Boolean row in the catalog. That single fact is then never read at the class-boolean checkpoints: StatementValidation.CheckRelationalOperands (whose local IsBoolOperand and BoolCompatible are themselves the same predicate written twice), ConditionBinder.BindBoolOperandValue, IntrinsicBinder.BindLengthFold and IntrinsicBinder.IsStringOperand. None has an arm for a BoundComputedOperand wrapping a BoundIntrinsicCall whose ResultCategory is Boolean - which is exactly what a function-identifier binds to. The fix is the extraction (one predicate answering 'is this operand class boolean', consulted at all four sites), not four patches.

WHAT IS CORRECT: the rightmost-is-low-order ordering, the left zero-fill, the left truncation (2^70 over 70 positions -> all zeros IS correct, since 2^70 mod 2^70 = 0 - I checked this before calling anything a defect), and the returned length being argument-2 including a RUNTIME argument-2 ('DISPLAY FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, LN)' with LN=12 prints 12 positions).

TEST-REF: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob (+ .out) exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, is spec-derived (values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example; not characterization/nist/legacy), and I re-ran it - it reproduces its golden. It covers the ordering, zero-fill and truncation halves FOR SMALL VALUES ONLY, and it would stay GREEN through all three divergences. test-needed for all three: nothing covers argument-1 >= 2^63; nothing covers the class-boolean half (every existing case MOVEs the result into a PIC 1(n) BIT item first, which is exactly why the defects survived); nothing covers FUNCTION LENGTH over the result.

EDITIONS derived as for FMT-15.13.2 - Annex E (2014 -> 2023 substantive changes) does not mention the function, and the 85 exclusion is external knowledge (boolean data is a COBOL-2002 addition) rather than a spec quotation - NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE, no record added (no AR rule for this function was in my input, and I verified these are not §15.13.4 issues): BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, so §15.13.3 r1/r2 remain UNSCREENED by the PB1 §15.3 class screen; and the FUNCTION-omitted form without a REPOSITORY entry is undiagnosed at bind, which I confirmed is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap (an undefined user name and UPPER-CASE behave identically), not this function's.

notes: test-needed. §15.14.3 r1 (cite.py --check OK) admits FOUR argument forms. Re-verified by running src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe: an alphanumeric literal ("ABCDE"=5), a national literal (N"ABCD"=8), a BASED entry (`01 BE BASED. 05 BA PIC X(6).` = 6) and a data item of any class/category all answer. (1) TYPE-NAME. `01 TN TYPEDEF. 05 TA PIC X(7).` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(TN).` -> compiles clean, then throws "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH argument (a numeric/figurative literal is not a valid argument, ISO 15.14.3)" (the `_ =>` fall-through, whose message also MISDIAGNOSES a legal argument as an illegal literal). Expected 7. A type-name IS legal: §15.14.3 r1 names it, §15.3 item 14 defines it ("A type-name shall be specified", cite.py OK), Table 21's BYTE-LENGTH row lists Type1, and §15.14.4 r2 a) presupposes it. (2) REFERENCE-MODIFIED DATA ITEM — MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS. `01 X PIC X(10) VALUE "ABCDEFGHIJ".` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(X(1:3)).` -> compiles clean, then throws "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a reference-modified argument (runtime length, 15.14.4)" (the `BoundFieldOperand { Place: RefModPlace }` arm). Expected 3. §8.4.3.3.4 GR5 (cite.py OK) "Reference modification creates a unique data item that is a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1" and GR6 (cite.py OK) "The unique data item ... has the same class, category, and usage as that defined for identifier-1" — so a reference-modified operand IS 'a data item of any class or category' and r1 admits it; with a LITERAL length it is even foldable. SIBLING: BindLengthFold has the identical RefModPlace arm — `FUNCTION LENGTH(X(1:3))` throws the same way (verified). SECOND HALF, also wrong: the NEGATIVE side of r1 is enforced only as a RUN-TIME loud stage — `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(12345)` compiles with ZERO diagnostics and then throws; §4.2.2 (cite.py OK: "There are rules in standard COBOL that are not identified as general formats or syntax rules, but nevertheless specify elements that are syntactically distinguishable. This warning mechanism shall indicate violations of ...") requires the compile-time mechanism to flag exactly this. BYTE-LENGTH is deliberately ABSENT from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and its doc-comment says so at line 125 ("BYTE-LENGTH is declared \"s\" while §15.14.3 admits an argument ...") — correct, because §15.14.3 admits any CLASS, so the PB1 class screen is the wrong mechanism; the literal/type-name/ref-mod restriction is a SHAPE rule. TEST-REF STRUCK ON REVIEW: the prior pass cited conformance:2002/intrinsics_byte_length; that case exists on disk and I read it, but its only §15.14.3 line is `BYTE-LENGTH("ABCDE")` and its stated purpose is the r1 byte-width table — it exercises NONE of the rule's substance (type-name, based entry, national literal, ref-mod, or any rejected argument), so it does not cover this rule. Editions: derived from the SPEC, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row (which I did not read for this purpose) — Annex E of the 2023 standard lists the substantive changes since 2014 and contains no BYTE-LENGTH entry (grep-verified: BYTE-LENGTH occurs nowhere in §E), so the rule provably applies to 2014 and 2023; §8.11 lists BYTE-LENGTH among the intrinsic function names; the 2023 document carries NO evidence on the 85-vs-2002 boundary, so all four are listed per the batch convention.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: OVERTURNED ON REVIEW: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. The prior pass verified only NON-EMPTY literals and so missed a SILENT wrong value on the ZERO-LENGTH LITERAL, which the fold's own `Math.Max(1, ...)` guarantees. Failing input, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVZL01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 W PIC X(3). PROCEDURE DIVISION. DISPLAY "ZLA=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(""). DISPLAY "ZLN=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(N""). DISPLAY "LENZLA=" FUNCTION LENGTH(""). STOP RUN.` -> prints `ZLA=1`, `ZLN=2`, `LENZLA=1`. The spec answer is 0, 0 and 0: §8.3.3.1 (cite.py OK) "If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero, and it is known as a zero-length literal"; §8.5.4 (cite.py OK) "A zero-length item is a data item or a literal whose minimum length is zero and whose length at runtime is zero", item 8 "A zero-length literal"; §15.14.4 r1 (cite.py OK) "The returned value is an integer that is the length of argument-1 in number of bytes" = 0. No diagnostic is issued. ROOT CAUSE is one expression in each literal arm of BindByteLengthFold: `Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length)` and `2 * Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length)` clamp a legal zero to one; the data-item arm carries the same clamp, `Math.Max(1, f.Place.Item.ByteWidth)`. SIBLING TO SWEEP: BindLengthFold in the same file has the identical clamp (LENGTH("") = 1, §15.50.4 r1 says 0). VERIFIED-CORRECT HALF (all run through the CLI): for a fixed-length data item or a non-empty literal the fold returns the right byte count against COBOL.NET's pinned implementor widths (§13.18.60.4 GR4/GR5/GR10 leave them implementor-defined; docs/CONFORMANCE.md rows 205/211 document them) — PIC X(5)=5, PIC N(4)=8, PIC 9(4)=4, PIC 9(4) COMP=2, PIC S9(5) COMP-3=3, BINARY-CHAR=1, INDEX=8, POINTER=8, group X(3)+N(2)=7, "ABCDE"=5, N"ABCD"=8. STILL-OPEN HALVES: a USAGE BIT item answers n instead of ceil(n/8) (RV-15.14.4-4) and a variable-length group answers a silently short constant (RV-15.14.4-6); a reference-modified argument and an ANY LENGTH item are staged loud (AR-15.14.3-1). The cited conformance-test was READ ON DISK at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 928 and its AssertSpec helper (line 26) compiles under COBOL.NET at the named dialect and asserts a LITERAL expected string with NO oracle call — genuinely spec-derived, and it exercises r1 head-on (6 from §15.14.4 r1 vs 3 from §15.50.4 r2). It covers only the fixed-width half; the zero-length, BIT and variable-length legs are test-needed. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW; BOTH legs re-verified by running, and BOTH are loud (never a wrong value), which is why this is NOT-IMPLEMENTED and not DIVERGES. Leg b) — `01 N PIC 9(2) VALUE 3. 01 ODOG. 05 T OCCURS 1 TO 5 TIMES DEPENDING ON N PIC X(3).` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(ODOG)` -> compiles clean, then NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a variable-length (OCCURS DEPENDING) group (runtime length, 15.14.4 r6)". Per r2 b) the OCCURS rules for a SENDING data item apply, so the answer is 3 x 3 = 9. Leg a) — `01 BE BASED. 05 N2 PIC 9(2). 05 T OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING ON N2 PIC X(3).` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(BE)` -> the IDENTICAL exception text, so a based entry not associated with actual data is NOT distinguished from the sending case and the RECEIVING-item (maximum-occurrences) reading of r2 a) has no arm at all; the answer there is 2 + 5 x 3 = 17. The guard reached is `f.Place.Item.IsGroup && OdoModel.TableUnder(f.Place.Item) is { OccursSpec.Depending: not null }`; TableUnder recurses into nested groups (line 77), so a deeply-subordinate ODO table is also caught — the r2 precondition ('any data description entry SUBORDINATE to') is matched, only the answer is missing. SECONDARY DEFECT: the diagnostic text cites '15.14.4 r6', but r6 governs a VARIABLE-LENGTH GROUP as defined by §8.5.1.12.1 (cite.py OK: 'a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item') — an OCCURS DEPENDING table is NEITHER, so the governing rule is r2. The identical mis-citation sits in BindLengthFold naming §15.50.4 r7. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW. SATISFIED VACUOUSLY, and the vacuity is only half-safe — deliberately NOT rounded up to CONFORMS. COBOL.NET generates NO implicit FILLER: no SYNCHRONIZED padding (re-verified by running `01 SY. 05 S1 PIC X. 05 S2 PIC 9(4) COMP SYNCHRONIZED.` -> BYTE-LENGTH(SY) = 3, i.e. 1+2 with no alignment gap), no ALIGNED clause arm, and no GROUP-USAGE BIT (GROUP_USAGE has zero hits under src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/). Zero SYNC padding is a CONFORMING implementor choice: §13.18.55.4 GR9 (cite.py OK, and I read the lead-in) opens 'The effect of this clause is defined by the implementor' and its sub-rule b) is 'Any necessary generation of implicit FILLER, if the elementary item immediately preceding an item containing the SYNCHRONIZED clause does not terminate at an appropriate natural boundary'; docs/CONFORMANCE.md row 205 documents the choice. DataItem.ByteWidth's plain non-redefining child sum therefore includes every filler position that exists, which is none. THE UNREACHABLE HALF: §8.5.1.6.3 (cite.py OK) mandates implicit filler BITS — not implementor-defined — 'Following a bit data item within an alphanumeric group item, within a strongly-typed group item, or within a bit group item, as needed to advance alignment to a required natural boundary' and again at the end of such a record. COBOL.NET cannot generate them because it stores a boolean position as a whole byte (RV-15.14.4-4), so no bit item is ever sub-byte. Fixing the USAGE BIT representation RE-OPENS this rule; closing it CONFORMS now would freeze that hole. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified by running. A USAGE BIT item never occupies a non-integral number of bytes in COBOL.NET, because ElementaryByteWidth's `_ => ElementaryImageWidth` arm gives it ONE BYTE PER BOOLEAN POSITION — r4's rounding is unreachable and the answer is n, not ceil(n/8). Failing input, SILENTLY wrong, no diagnostic: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVBIT01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 BB PIC 1(5) USAGE BIT. 01 BGRP. 05 C1 PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT. 05 C2 PIC 1(2) USAGE BIT. 01 BD PIC 1(5). PROCEDURE DIVISION. DISPLAY "BB=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(BB). DISPLAY "BGRP=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(BGRP). DISPLAY "BD=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(BD). STOP RUN.` -> prints BB=5, BGRP=5, BD=5; the spec answer is 1, 1 and 5. DERIVATION, every citation run through cite.py --check: §13.18.60.4 GR5 'The USAGE BIT clause specifies that bits shall be used to represent a boolean data item'; §8.5.1.6.3 aligns an elementary bit item 'at the next bit position in storage' when it follows a sibling bit item; §14.6.8.6 NOTE 'the item need not occupy an integral number of bytes'; §3.28-region term 'byte' = 'sequence of bits representing the smallest addressable character unit'. Five boolean positions are five bits; r4 rounds to the next larger integer = 1. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, CHECKED AND REJECTED: PicInfo's Usage.Bit doc-comment (lines 89-93) defends the byte-per-position storage with 'the §13.18.40.4 GR14 R14 representation license'. That citation resolves (cite.py --check 13.18.40.4 'represented in storage as a bit' -> GR14, the symbol-'1' description: 'Each boolean character can be represented in storage as a bit, an alphanumeric character, or a national character') and IS a genuine licence for a boolean position GENERALLY — which is why `01 BD PIC 1(5).` (usage DISPLAY) correctly answers 5. But it is the GENERAL rule; §13.18.60.4 GR5 is the SPECIFIC one and controls when USAGE BIT is written explicitly. docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries NO row for USAGE BIT (grep-verified), so this is not a documented implementor choice. The divergence is confined to explicitly-USAGE-BIT items and (once implemented) bit group items. Root cause is the data model, not the intrinsic; fixing it re-opens RV-15.14.4-3. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified by running. A dynamic-length elementary item is STAGED LOUD by name — never a wrong value, hence NOT-IMPLEMENTED. Input: `01 DL PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.` + `MOVE "HELLO" TO DL` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(DL)` -> compiles clean, then NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a DYNAMIC LENGTH item (current length in bytes at runtime, ISO 15.14.4 rule 5)" (the `BoundFieldOperand { Place.Item.IsDynamicLength: true }` arm). Per r5 the answer is the CURRENT length in bytes = 5, and that value is ALREADY reachable at run time: `FUNCTION LENGTH(DL)` prints 5 in the same program, so the alphanumeric case is one arm away from a BoundIntrinsicCall. The NATIONAL case additionally needs the 2-bytes-per-position doubling (D-N1) that BindLengthFold also stages loud. The r5 NOTE (prefixed fields / delimiter characters excluded from the current length) is likewise unimplemented — DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE PREFIXED/DELIMITED is a separate §13.18.20 surface. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified by running — the worst finding in this batch, a SILENT wrong value with no diagnostic and no loud stage. A variable-length group (§8.5.1.12.1, cite.py OK: 'a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item') folds to a compile-time constant that omits exactly the variable part. §15.3 permits it as an argument ('A variable-length group shall be referenced as an argument to a function only when explicitly permitted in the function definition' — §15.14.4 r6/r7 explicitly permit it). Failing input, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVVLG01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 VLG. 05 F1 PIC X(4). 05 DL PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH. 01 DCG. 05 F2 PIC X(2). 05 DT OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP PIC X(3). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE "HELLO" TO DL DISPLAY "LEN-DL=" FUNCTION LENGTH(DL). DISPLAY "BL-VLG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(VLG). DISPLAY "CAP=" CAP. DISPLAY "BL-DCG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(DCG). STOP RUN.` -> prints LEN-DL=5, BL-VLG=4, CAP=0000000000, BL-DCG=5. Spec: BYTE-LENGTH(VLG) = r6 a) 4 + r6 b) 5 = 9, COBOL.NET says 4 (DL contributes 0 because ElementaryImageWidth returns 0 for IsDynamicLength). BYTE-LENGTH(DCG) at capacity 0 = r6 a) 2 + r6 c) 0 = 2, COBOL.NET says 5 (ByteWidth multiplies the dynamic table by `c.Occurs ?? 1`, one phantom element). A SECOND run confirms the constant never tracks capacity: after `MOVE "AAA" TO DT(4)` the program prints CAP=0000000004 and BL-DCG=5, where r6 c) requires 2 + 4 x 3 = 14. ROOT CAUSE, one place: BindByteLengthFold's ONLY variable-length guard is `OdoModel.TableUnder(item) is { OccursSpec.Depending: not null }`, and OdoModel.TableUnder walks for OCCURS DEPENDING children ONLY (`c.OccursSpec is { DependingName: not null }`) — it sees neither a DYNAMIC LENGTH item nor an OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY table, so the variable-length-group case falls through to the plain `BoundFieldOperand f => BoundNumLiteral(f.Place.Item.ByteWidth)` arm. The predicate the code needs is the §8.5.1.12.1 one (ANY subordinate dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table) and it does not exist in the model; that structural predicate is the fix, not a fourth pattern arm. SIBLING TO SWEEP: BindLengthFold carries the identical guard and the identical hole for §15.50.4 r7. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: CHAR function
notes: test-needed. UPHELD by adversarial re-review; code-location EXTENDED to name DataBinder.Switches.cs#AlphabetBind, which is where the defect's root (the 256-entry domain) is built and where the fix belongs. §15.3's closing paragraph (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29556) makes this a runtime rule: an incorrect argument value sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, and 'if checking ... is not enabled, the implementor defines the result'. IDENTITY-PCS HALF IS CORRECT and was re-measured, not inherited: CobolIntrinsics.Char(long) computes c = n-1 and rejects 'c is < 0 or > 0xFFFF' via Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError (symbol present — instance body plus static forwarder), admitting exactly 1..65536, which is the number of positions in the UTF-16 alphanumeric repertoire. Measured: CHAR(0), CHAR(-3) and CHAR(65537) all yield the §15.3 one-space default, CHAR(65536) round-trips through ORD to 65536, and with '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' CHAR(0) aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)'. NON-IDENTITY-PCS HALF IS WRONG AT BOTH ENDS. Char(long, ushort[]) receives the 256-entry table AlphabetBind builds ('var pos = new ushort[256]') and treats positions 0..weights.Length-1 as always occupied; an ALSO phrase COLLAPSES positions, so the top of the Latin-1 block goes empty and the >Latin-1 tail shifts down. Re-ran at --std 2023 and --std 85, identical: OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B". 01 N PIC 9(6). MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(255)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD255=" N. MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(65536)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD65536=" N. -> ORD255=000034 and ORD65536=065534. SPEC DERIVATION (independently recomputed in this review): §12.3.7.4 GR7 1.6 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "first character in the sequence of multiple characters" -> OK) puts A/B/C at position 0, and GR7 1.3 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "shall assume a position in the collating sequence that is greater than" -> OK) puts the remaining 65533 code units at distinct ascending positions 1..65533, so the sequence has 65534 positions. Therefore ordinal 255 IS in range (position 254 = code 256 = U+0100) yet CHAR(255) raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and returns the one-space default (ORD of a space under this alphabet is 34: space = code 32, unspecified codes 0..64 take positions 1..65, so space is at position 33, ordinal 34 — matches the measured 000034); and ordinal 65536 is OUT of range (max is 65534) yet is accepted, returning U+FFFF, whose true ordinal is 65534 — the out-of-range value is not merely accepted, it ALIASES a legal one and is indistinguishable from it. ALSO ACTIONABLE: both ArgumentError messages in Char cite '§15.15.3 rule 1' when the rule actually violated is r2 (the range rule); r1 is the integer rule. TEST-REF STRUCK AND RE-VERIFIED STRUCK: tests/conformance/2002/ca26_char_unicode_pcs.cob (read in full) shows only two IN-RANGE ordinals (256, 257) under a bijective 26-letter permutation alphabet; it never uses an ALSO phrase and never probes 0, a negative or an above-maximum ordinal, so it cannot cover this rule.

subject: CHAR function
notes: UPHELD by adversarial re-review and independently reproduced. The identity-PCS path conforms (position n = code unit n-1; CHAR(66)='A' re-measured at all four editions). The NON-IDENTITY path carries the exact defect fix-queue PB3 removed from the INVERSE function and never swept into CHAR (CLAUDE.md rule 4 — every bug is a pattern). Both bodies read side by side: Char(long, ushort[]) still has 'if (wanted >= weights.Length && wanted <= 0xFFFF) return ((char)wanted).ToString();' — a position past the 256-entry table falls back to its NATIVE code unit. Ord(string, ushort[]) no longer does: it computes 'highest + 1L + (c - weights.Length) + 1L' with a remark documenting the removed fallback ('a character one past the table was numbered by a different rule than its neighbour and left a HOLE'). The two are inverses only while the table is a bijection over 0..255; any ALSO phrase collapses positions and they disagree. Re-ran at --std 2023 and --std 85, identical output both: OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B". 01 N PIC 9(6). MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(255)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD255=" N. MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(257)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD257=" N. -> ORD255=000034 and ORD257=000255 (a third probe, ORD(CHAR(65534)) -> 065532, shows the same two-position shift at the top). DERIVATION RECOMPUTED FROM THE STANDARD IN THIS REVIEW, not from the code: §12.3.7.4 GR7 1.6 puts A, B and C at ordinal position 0 and GR7 1.3 puts the 65533 unspecified code units at distinct ascending positions 1..65533 in native order (both cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 -> OK), so position p>=66 holds code p+2; position 254 = code 256 = U+0100 = ordinal 255, and position 256 = code 258 = U+0102 = ordinal 257. CHAR(255) shall be U+0100 but returns the one-space EC default; CHAR(257) shall be U+0102 but returns U+0100. ORD is the half that is RIGHT here — ORD(U+0100) = 253+1+0+1 = 255 agrees with the spec derivation — so the fix belongs in Char, mirroring Ord's arithmetic, not the reverse. TEST-REF KEPT, RE-VERIFIED ON DISK AND RE-DERIVED: tests/conformance/2002/ca26_char_unicode_pcs.cob exists with its .out, and its expected values are COMPUTED from the standard rather than captured — I recomputed them independently: under ALPHABET AL IS "ZYXWVUTSRQPONMLKJIHGFEDCBA", Z..A occupy positions 0..25, the 230 unspecified Latin-1 code units occupy 26..255 (so CHAR(256) = X"FF"), and code 256 = U+0100 sits at position 256 = ordinal 257, which is exactly the golden's 'ORD=00257' and 'P-GT-R'. It genuinely exercises this rule under a non-identity PCS, but only over a BIJECTIVE alphabet with NO ALSO phrase — precisely the case the defect cannot reach — so it does not close the row and an ALSO variant is still needed. (Note for whoever lands the fix: that fixture's header comment cites '§12.3.7 k)3', the one-level-short form; the clause that actually carries the rule is §12.3.7.4 GR7 1.3.)

subject: CHAR function
notes: test-needed. UPHELD by adversarial re-review and independently reproduced. THE SECOND SENTENCE'S IMPLEMENTOR LATITUDE DOES NOT APPLY to an ALPHABET literal phrase, because the order IS defined: §12.3.7.4 GR7 1.6, revalidated mechanically here (python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "first character in the sequence of multiple characters" -> OK; read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 12725) — 'If the ALSO phrase is specified, the characters ... are assigned to the same ordinal position ... Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence of multiple characters defined at that ordinal position.' So §15.15.4 r2's FIRST sentence governs and CHAR shall return literal-1. It returns the LOWEST-CODED member instead: Char(long, ushort[]) scans 'for (int i = 0; i < weights.Length; i++) if (weights[i] == wanted) return ((char)i).ToString();'. The source order is BUILT at bind time and then DISCARDED — AlphabetBind maintains 'var specOrder = new List<char>();  // every specified char in source order (tie rules)', uses it for the GR8/GR9 HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE ties, and then constructs 'new CollatingTable(pos, high, low)', whose record declaration (CollatingModel.cs line 21: 'public sealed record CollatingTable(ushort[] Positions, char HighValue, char LowValue);') carries no representative array at all. The NATIONAL twin in the same file got it right: NationalCollatingTable carries 'RepByPos', documented as 'the FIRST character SPECIFIED at that position'. One rule, two implementations, only the alphanumeric one incomplete — the same shape as PB3. Re-ran at --std 2023 and --std 85, identical: OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B". 01 R PIC X. MOVE FUNCTION CHAR(1) TO R. DISPLAY "POS1=[" R "]". -> POS1=[A]; literal-1 is "C", so §15.15.4 r2 requires POS1=[C]. CORROBORATION that this is a dropped hand-off, not a design disagreement: AlphabetBind's own ALSO arm comment reads 'operand-1 is the position's first character (the CHAR() pick and the LOW-VALUE tie winner)', and the very next lines compute LOW-VALUE from specOrder, so under this alphabet LOW-VALUE = 'C' while CHAR(1) = 'A' — the compiler already contradicts itself about which character occupies position 0. The rule's DETERMINISM half DOES hold (the scan is deterministic, so implementor item 21 — specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34241, 'CHAR function (which one of the multiple characters is returned) ... (15.15, CHAR function, Returned value, rule 2)' — remains satisfiable), but the first half fails, and one failing half is DIVERGES.
