subject: CHAR-NATIONAL function
notes:
OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. The bound check is real but it sits DOWNSTREAM OF A LOSSY NARROWING, so it can be walked straight past. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits '(long)({a.Expr})' over an Int128-typed argument expression; the C# Int128->long conversion is UNCHECKED and wraps modulo 2^64. An argument value of magnitude >= 2^63 therefore ALIASES into the valid 1..65536 window before CobolIntrinsics.CharNational's 'if (c is < 0 or > 0xFFFF)' ever sees it, and §15.16.3 rule 2 is violated with no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION at all.
PREMISE VALIDATED (not just the rule): §8.3.3.3.2 — 'The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length' and 'An integer literal is a fixed-point numeric literal that contains no decimal point'. A 20-digit unsigned integer literal, and a PIC 9(20) item holding it, are both legal and both satisfy §15.16.3 rule 1 — so this is a pure rule-2 violation, not a rule-1 one. §15.3 (validated with cite.py) then requires: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' It is not set.
RAN, with checking explicitly ENABLED so the §15.3 implementor-defined-result latitude cannot excuse it — exit 0, no diagnostic, no exception, execution continues past the call:
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ADVCN15.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  N-CHAR   PIC N(1) USAGE NATIONAL.
       01  A-DISP   PIC X(1).
       01  BIGN     PIC 9(20) VALUE 18446744073709551682.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (BIGN) TO N-CHAR
           MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF (N-CHAR) TO A-DISP
           DISPLAY "ITEM-2POW64PLUS66=[" A-DISP "]"
           DISPLAY "NOT-RAISED"
           STOP RUN.
prints 'ITEM-2POW64PLUS66=[A]' then 'NOT-RAISED'. 18446744073709551682 = 2^64 + 66, so the wrap delivers 66 and the function answers with ordinal 66's character. Identical result for the LITERAL form 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (18446744073709551682)', and identical at --std 2002 and --std 2023.
CONTROL that isolates the wrap as the cause: 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (9223372036854775807)' (long.MaxValue — one below the wrap threshold, no aliasing) DOES abort correctly with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): CHAR-NATIONAL argument 9223372036854775807 outside the national collating sequence', exit 1. Same rule, same statement shape, opposite outcome, and the only difference is whether the value survives the (long) cast.
WHAT DOES WORK (read and run, so the fix is narrow): identity path rejects n<1 and n>65536 (ran n=0 -> space with checking off, fatal EC with checking on; n=65536 accepted, n=70000 rejected). Non-native path routes through NationalCollation.CharAt, bounded by PositionCount = NextFree + (0x10000 - |specified codes|), which correctly SHRINKS under ALSO — ran 'ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C"' with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL: ordinal 65535 accepted, 65536 rejected. So the DEFECT IS THE ARGUMENT CHANNEL, not the bound.
FIX (root cause, CLAUDE.md rule 4): ArgInt/IntArg must not silently narrow. Either render a checked/saturating conversion, or carry the argument as Int128 to the runtime and let the runtime's own range test see the true value. This is a WHOLE-CHANNEL defect, not a CHAR-NATIONAL one — every 'i' argument rendered through AsInt has it (CHAR §15.15.3, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER §15.13.3, BASE-CONVERT §15.12.3, FORMATTED-DATE/-TIME/-DATETIME offsets, the DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD / DAY-TO-YYYYDDD / YEAR-TO-YYYY windowing trio); sweep them together.
test-needed. The previously cited unit:NationalCollationTests.CharAt_IsTheExactInverseOfWeight is STRUCK as a cover: it never invokes CHAR-NATIONAL, never exercises the n->position-1 mapping, and never asserts that EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is set — it pins NationalCollation.CharAt(-1)/CharAt(0x10000) == -1 one layer below the rule, and would have stayed green through the defect above. Needed: a conformance case with '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' asserting the abort for n=0, n=65537 and n=2^64+66 on the identity path, plus the ALSO-shrunk bound on the non-native path.
EDITIONS: as for AR-15.16.3-1 — Annex E establishes 2014/2023 unchanged; the national type excludes 85; the 2002 lower bound is national data's introduction in ISO/IEC 1989:2002 and is not derivable from the 2023 text. Not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: CHAR-NATIONAL function
notes: UPHELD — both collating paths re-derived from the spec and re-run, plus three shapes the original review did not exercise. Citation validated: §15.16.4 r1 OK via cite.py; the unspecified-character placement is §12.3.7.4 7) 1. 3. ('Any characters of the native collating sequence that are not specified in the literal phrase shall assume a position in the collating sequence that is greater than that of the highest character specified in this literal phrase') — validated, and note the real numbering is 7) 1. 3., not the 'GR7 k3' shorthand the design docs use. IDENTITY path (no PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL, or NATIVE/UCS-4, which bind Table = null): ordinal n is code unit n-1 — golden gives C1=A for 66 and WIDE=YES for 19991 (U+4E16), LEN=01 through FUNCTION LENGTH proving one character position, result category National from the catalog row. NON-NATIVE path: re-ran three distinct alphabet shapes the earlier pass did not — (a) 'ALPHABET NAT-B FOR NATIONAL IS N"Z" THRU N"X"' (a DESCENDING THROUGH run) gives ordinals 1,2,3 = Z,Y,X and ORD(CHAR-NATIONAL(i)) = i for i in 1..5; (b) 'ALPHABET NAT-C FOR NATIONAL IS 66, 65' (the SR14c1 numeric-literal form, 1-based native ordinals) gives ordinal 1 = A and ordinal 2 = @; (c) 'ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C"' gives 1=B, 2=C. ISOLATION CHECK: a program declaring only an ALPHANUMERIC PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ('ALPHABET REV IS "CBA"') leaves CHAR-NATIONAL(66) = A — the 256-entry alphanumeric weights are correctly NOT applied, because IntrinsicBinder's 'collate' flag is keyed to CHAR/ORD/MAX-MIN only and CHAR-NATIONAL takes the separate CollateNat/__COLLATE_NAT channel. The (long) wrap defect recorded under AR-15.16.3-2 cannot reach this rule: it needs |value| >= 2^63, which is always outside the sequence, so no in-range ordinal is affected. BOTH cited goldens exist on disk and were re-run green: char_national.cob covers the identity leg, alphabet_national.cob covers the non-native leg (CN1=C under 'ALPHABET REV-NAT FOR NATIONAL IS N"CBA"'). EDITIONS: Annex E establishes 2014/2023; the national type excludes 85; the 2002 lower bound is national data's introduction, not derivable from the 2023 text and not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: CHAR-NATIONAL function
notes:
PARTIAL upheld, but the COVERAGE CLAIM IS OVERTURNED — test-ref struck, see below.
HALF 1 — 'the character returned is the first character defined for that character position', plus 'every invocation ... shall return the same character'. CONFORMS, verified by reading BOTH halves of the mechanism and running it. Only an ALSO phrase can put two characters at one national position; AlphabetBindNationalLiteralPhrase records the representative with 'if (repByPos.Count == next) repByPos.Add(c);' inside Assign, and the ALSO arm calls Assign(op[0], advance: false) over the operands IN SOURCE ORDER, so operand-1 (literal-1) claims the position and later members are recorded in 'pos'/'positions' but never in repByPos. I also checked the invariant that makes the lookup safe: Assign returns EARLY on a duplicate WITHOUT advancing 'next', and the ALSO arm advances only 'if (repByPos.Count > before)', so repByPos.Count == nextFree always holds and _repByPos[position] can never be a stale or missing slot. NationalCollation.CharAt returns _repByPos[position] for the specified block; the table is built at compile time and emitted once as __COLLATE_NAT, so the value is invocation-invariant. RAN: 'ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C"' under 'PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL IS NAT-A' gives CHAR-NATIONAL(1) = B (the ALSO group's literal-1, NOT the lower code unit A) and CHAR-NATIONAL(2) = C. On the identity path no two characters share a position, so the clause is vacuous there.
HALF 2 — 'If the order of multiple characters having the same position is undefined, the implementor shall define which of those multiple characters is returned.' UNMET. Annex A.1 item 22 (read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md, verbatim: 'CHAR-NATIONAL function (which one of the multiple characters is returned). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.16, CHAR-NATIONAL function, Returned value, rule 2)') makes this a REQUIRED documented determination. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 is the §4.2.16 implementor's user documentation; I read its A.1 register and it carries only items 2, 59, 158, 205, 206, 207, 208, 211, 215 plus two unnumbered §15.4.1 rows — item 22 is absent, and §7's own banner registers the register as an open v1.0 conformance gap. Under D13 ('100% conforming' = the mandatory core plus every required implementor documentation item) this half is open. The determination itself is settled and needs only to be written down: COBOL.NET admits shared national positions ONLY through ALSO, whose order §12.3.7.3 SR14c/§12.3.7.4 GR7 k6 defines, so the 'order is undefined' arm is never reached and the returned character is always the ALSO group's literal-1, from a compile-time table. ACTION: one row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 — no code change.
TEST-REF STRUCK (this is the overturn). The previously cited unit:NationalCollationTests.AlsoGroup_SharesOnePosition_CharAtReturnsTheFirstDefined exists on disk and passes, but it does NOT exercise this rule's decision point: it HAND-BUILDS the collation with 'repByPos: [(ushort)'X', (ushort)'Z']' and then asserts CharAt(0) == 'X' — i.e. it asserts the runtime returns the array element the test itself supplied. Which character is 'the first character defined for that character position' is decided in AlphabetBindNationalLiteralPhrase, which the test never runs, and CHAR-NATIONAL is never invoked. The assertion would stay green if the binder picked the WRONG representative, so it cannot close this row.
test-needed: a tests/conformance/2002 case declaring 'ALPHABET x FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C"' with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL, asserting CHAR-NATIONAL(1) = N"B" end to end (the existing alphabet_national.cob uses N"CBA" with no ALSO, so no golden anywhere exercises a shared position). EDITIONS: Annex E establishes 2014/2023; the national type excludes 85; the 2002 lower bound is national data's introduction, not derivable from the 2023 text and not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: COMBINED-DATETIME function
notes: VERDICT RETAINED, NOTES OVERTURNED - the prior record's root cause and BOTH of its failing inputs are FALSE against the current tree, and a fixer sent to them would find nothing. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.17.4 "equivalent arithmetic expression"` -> OK. REFUTED CLAIM 1: 'CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble returns a long and saturates at 9.2e18'. It does not. Read it: `public static Int128 FromDouble(double d, int scale)` with `if (scaled >= 1.7e38) return Int128.MaxValue;`. REFUTED CLAIM 2: `COMPUTE <PIC 9(9)V9(14)> = FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(143951, <COMP-2 18867.8125>)` was said to print 92233.72036854775807. RE-RAN it: it prints `F14=00014395118867812501504` (= 143951.18867812501504). REFUTED CLAIM 3 (its collateral repro): `COMPUTE <PIC 9(9)V9(17)> = FUNCTION SQRT(20000000)` was said to print long.MaxValue. RE-RAN: `SQ=00000447213595499957977088` (= 4472.13595499957977088, correct). There is no saturation anywhere in this family at reachable magnitudes. EXACT LEG - CONFORMS, re-verified: `CombinedDatetime(long integerDate, Int128 secUnscaled, int secScale) => (Int128)integerDate * Pow10.AsWide(secScale + 5) + secUnscaled`, read by RenderNum at scale secScale+5, which is algebraically a1 + a2/100000 with no rounding. Battery re-run at --std 2023, every value exact: scale-12 argument-2 18867.812479168304 into PIC Z(6)9.9(17) -> `143951.18867812479168304`, bit-for-bit the standard's own worked value in D.31.5.11; literal arguments -> 143951.45296; argument-2 = 1 -> 143951.00001; COMP-3 45296.125 -> 143951.45296125; the expression form (WS-ID + 1, WS-SEC / 2) -> 143952.22648; argument-2 = 0.5 -> 143951.000005. Under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` it is exact and the §15.4.1 NOTE 2 relation holds (`IF FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-S12) = WS-ID + (WS-S12 / 100000)` prints EAE-EQUAL). FLOATING-POINT LEG - THE REAL DEFECT, correctly attributed this time. A COMP-2 argument-2 is legal (§15.6 types it Num2) and routes through `RenderNum`'s `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(...)` to `CombinedDatetimeReal`, whose expression is right. But `RenderFloat` quantizes at `int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)`, and on the MOVE path `num.Receiver.Scale` is not the MOVE's receiver, so the float leg quantizes at 9 regardless of what the receiver holds. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` at --std 2023: `01 WS-ID PIC 9(7) VALUE 143951. 01 WS-SEC USAGE COMP-2. 01 WS-13 PIC 9(9)V9(13). 01 WS-13B PIC 9(9)V9(13). MOVE 18867.812479168304 TO WS-SEC. MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-13. COMPUTE WS-13B = FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC). COMPUTE WS-13B = WS-ID + (WS-SEC / 100000).` prints `MOVE13=0001439511886781250000`, `COMP13=0001439511886781248000`, `EAE13 =0001439511886781247916` - i.e. the SAME function reference with the SAME arguments returns TWO DIFFERENT values in one execution, and neither equals the equivalent arithmetic expression. That violates §15.4.1's standard-arithmetic paragraph (cite.py --check 15.4.1 "same for all instances of a given function" -> OK): 'the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element so long as the value and order of the arguments, the collating sequence, and the locale are unchanged' - COMBINED-DATETIME is not one of the four excepted functions (DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, RANDOM, YEAR-TO-YYYY) - and the same paragraph's rule 1, 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'. Under NATIVE arithmetic the same divergence is defensible, because §15.4.1 there permits 'an implementor-defined approximation'; under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is not. ROOT CAUSE IS SHARED, not this function's body: it is the same `FromDouble(call, ws)` fixed-point RECEIVER path already recorded PARTIAL for RANDOM in docs/rearchitecture/CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE.md. PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS because a legal program gets two different answers for one function reference; PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because the exact leg - which is what §15.17.4 r1 and the standard's own worked example exercise - is bit-exact. TEST: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob with golden `CDT= 153569.45296` = 153569 + 45296/100000 computed from §15.17.4 r1 (file and .out read on disk) covers the EXACT leg only; test-needed for the floating-point leg and for the standard-arithmetic 'same for all instances' invariant. EDITIONS: Annex E.2 item 13 establishes >= 2014; the 2002/85 boundary is not derivable from the 2023 document and is asserted. Not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: test-needed. Edition window from ISO Annex E.3.3 item 23 ('The CONCAT function has been added', cite.py --check OK) and the front-matter new-in-2023 intrinsic list — NOT from the catalog row. CONCAT is ABSENT from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (the dictionary holds ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI — no CONCAT), so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its first line ('if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;') and no COBOLNET1627 is ever raised. §15.18.3 r1 is violated in BOTH directions. (a) OVER-ACCEPT of a class r1 excludes — pointer is not among alphabetic/alphanumeric/boolean/numeric/national: '01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 P USAGE POINTER. 01 R PIC X(20). MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A P) TO R DISPLAY "P[" R "]"' compiles clean and prints 'P[AB CobolNet.Runtime.]' — a .NET type name emitted into a COBOL result (re-run on src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe for this review). (b) UNDER-ACCEPT of THREE literal kinds r1 ADMITS, all of which reach the Loud() arms of IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor and abort the run with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: 'CONCAT(A 12)' (a numeric literal — r1 names class numeric explicitly, and §15.18.1's own type table has a 'Numeric usage Display ⇒ Alphanumeric' row) fails 'intrinsic string argument BoundNumericLiteral'; 'CONCAT(A SPACE)' (a figurative constant — §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 'A figurative constant may be used whenever literal appears in a format or when a rule allows it', cite.py --check OK, and r1 is a rule allowing a literal; neither SR1a nor SR1b bars it since r1 is not restricted to a numeric literal; length one character per §8.3.3.6.4 GR3b) fails 'BoundFigurative'; 'CONCAT(A ALL "X")' fails 'BoundAllLiteral' (§8.3.3.6.4 GR3c — length is the length of literal-1). All three re-reproduced for this review. The screen must ALSO admit these, not merely reject pointer/object/index. Contrast: a boolean literal (CONCAT(A B"1010") ⇒ 'AB 1010') and a national literal (CONCAT(NA N"ZZ") ⇒ 'PQ ZZ') DO bind and run, so the defect is specific to the three visitor arms above.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: test-needed. Edition window from Annex E.3.3 item 23, not from the catalog. NO code implements the cross-argument usage-homogeneity screen of §15.18.3 r2 ('If any argument is usage national, all arguments shall be usage national, otherwise all arguments shall be usage display', cite.py --check OK). BindIntrinsicCore computes 'bool nationalArg = args.Any(a => OperandCategory(a) is PicCategory.National)', but that flag is consumed ONLY by the CHAR/CHAR-NATIONAL/ORD/MAX-MIN collating-sequence decision (collate / collateNat) and by the CHAR-takes-an-integer arm — there is no CONCAT arm anywhere in the binder. IntrinsicArgumentRules is a PER-ARGUMENT class table (Violation(kind, op) sees one operand at a time) and structurally cannot express a cross-argument constraint, so this needs a NEW mechanism, not a new table row. Both halves re-verified on the built CLI for this review, silently accepted: mixed display+national '01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 NB PIC N(2) VALUE N"RS". 01 R PIC X(20). MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A NB) TO R' prints 'XN[AB RS               ]'; and the 'otherwise all arguments shall be usage display' half — '01 C PIC 9(4) COMP VALUE 12. MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A C) TO R' (usage binary) prints 'C[AB 0012             ]'. Both shall be rejected. NOTE the screen is also CLASS-only by construction: usage is not a CobolClass, so even adding a CONCAT row to Verified could not carry r2.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: test-needed. Edition window from Annex E.3.3 item 23, not from the catalog. Nothing enforces §15.18.3 r3 ('If argument-1 or argument-2 is numeric, it shall be usage display or national and shall be an unsigned integer', cite.py --check OK). No CONCAT arm exists in BindIntrinsicCore; CONCAT is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified; and IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible maps a kind char to a CobolClass[] — signedness, integer-ness and USAGE are not class properties and the mechanism cannot express any of the three (its own comment on 'i' says so: 'integer-ness of a VALUE is not a class property and is not decided here'). All three illegal shapes re-verified silently accepted on the built CLI for this review, with '01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 R PIC X(20).': '01 S PIC S9(4) VALUE -12.' → 'MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A S) TO R' prints 'S[AB 001K             ]' (SIGNED, overpunch image — r3 requires UNSIGNED); '01 F PIC 9(3)V99 VALUE 1.25.' → prints 'F[AB 00125            ]' (NON-integer); '01 C PIC 9(4) COMP VALUE 12.' → prints 'C[AB 0012             ]' (usage binary, neither display nor national). ⚠ SECOND HALF, found in this review: r3's 'or NATIONAL' permission is not merely unenforced, it is UNREACHABLE — '01 NN PIC 9(4) USAGE NATIONAL VALUE 12.' is rejected before CONCAT is ever consulted by 'COBOLNET0899: national-form numeric data ... is recognized but not yet implemented (Phase 4a residue) ... (ISO 13.18.60.3 SR12)', so the legal 'numeric usage national' argument shape (also a row of §15.18.1's own type table, 'Numeric usage National ⇒ National') cannot be written at all. That is a separate data-description gap, not a CONCAT defect, but it blocks any future r3 test of the national half and must be sequenced first. COBOLNET1627 is the sibling §15.3 diagnostic but its driver cannot carry this rule.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: The concatenation is correct for the argument shapes that reach the runtime — 'Concat(params string[] parts) => string.Concat(parts)' over 'StrArgList', each argument as its full fixed-width image so 'all of the characters' includes trailing padding (all re-verified on the built CLI for this review: PIC X(3) "AB" + PIC X(2) "CD" → 'AB CD'; group → 'AB CD-CD'; ref-mod A(1:2) → 'ABCD'; numeric-edited PIC ZZ9.99 → 'AB  12.50'; boolean PIC 1(4) DISPLAY → 'AB 1010'; boolean literal B"1010" → 'AB 1010'; numeric display PIC 9(4) → 'AB 0012'; national N(3)+N(2) → 'PQ RS'; national literal → 'PQ ZZ'; nested UPPER-CASE → 'AB CD'; and through the DISPLAY, IF-relation and STRING channels as well as MOVE). But this is a DIVERGES, not an unverified edge: THREE distinct literal kinds that §15.18.3 r1 explicitly admits return NO VALUE AT ALL — the emitter routes them to StrArgVisitor's Loud() arms and the program compiles clean then aborts with CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. All three re-reproduced here with '01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 R PIC X(20).': 'MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A 12) TO R' → 'intrinsic string argument BoundNumericLiteral' (§15.18.4 r1 requires 'AB 12'); 'MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A SPACE) TO R' → 'BoundFigurative' (admissible per §8.3.3.6.3 SR1, one character per §8.3.3.6.4 GR3b — expected 'AB  '); 'MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A ALL "X") TO R' → 'BoundAllLiteral' (§8.3.3.6.4 GR3c — expected 'AB X'). The cited test is spec-derived (AssertSpec compares against a literal expected value computed from r1/r4 in its own comment, no oracle; the method name carries no MatchesLegacy/GnuCobol/Oracle suffix despite the file's 'Differential' name) and pins the conforming half only; tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.cob + .out (manifest-enabled) cover the same half. Nothing covers a literal argument of any of the three failing kinds.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: test-needed. Edition window from Annex E.3.3 item 23, not from the catalog. The CONCAT catalog row hardcodes 'IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric', whose 'IntrinsicCatalog.ResultCategory' is 'PicCategory.Alphanumeric', and BindIntrinsicCore's category-resolution block promotes to National ONLY for 'sig.RuntimeMethod is "UpperCase" or "LowerCase" or "Reverse"' (the CA25 arm) and for the MAX/MIN all-national string form (V54) — there is no CONCAT arm, so a national argument-1 yields an ALPHANUMERIC-labelled result. §15.18.4 r2 ('If argument-1 is of class or usage national, the function will return a national value', cite.py --check OK) requires national; ISO Table 16 (§14.9.25.3 SR10 — read directly in the spec for this review: National sender row × 'Alphanumeric-edited, Alphanumeric' receiver column = 'No') therefore forbids the MOVE. Concrete failing input, re-run on the built CLI: '01 NA PIC N(3) VALUE N"PQ". 01 NB PIC N(2) VALUE N"RS". 01 R PIC X(20). MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(NA NB) TO R DISPLAY "C[" R "]"' compiles CLEAN and prints 'C[PQ RS               ]' (NA is N(3), so its image is 'PQ ' — the padding is part of the result per r1). The identical shape through a correctly-categorised sibling, 'MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(NA) TO R', IS rejected: 'COBOLNET0819: MOVE of a national sending operand to an alphabetic, alphanumeric, or alphanumeric-edited receiver is invalid (ISO 14.9.25.3 SR10, Table 16)'. So the guard exists and works — CONCAT's result label is what bypasses it. MoveBinder.MoveCategoryLegality reads the sender category for a function call from ic.ResultCategory, the mislabelled value. ⚠ SECOND HALF, unreachable today: r2 says 'of class OR USAGE national', so a class-numeric/class-boolean item with USAGE NATIONAL also mandates a national result (§15.18.1's type table, rows 'Boolean usage National' and 'Numeric usage National'). '01 NN PIC 9(4) USAGE NATIONAL' is rejected up front by COBOLNET0899 (§13.18.60.3 SR12, Phase-4a residue), so that half cannot be exercised or tested until national-form numeric data lands — fixing the category label alone will not close it.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: test-needed. §15.18.4 r3's ALPHABETIC half is unimplemented and observably wrong; the 'otherwise alphanumeric' half conforms. Verified on src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe for this review: '01 A PIC A(3) VALUE "AB". 01 BOOLR PIC 1(8) USAGE DISPLAY. MOVE A TO BOOLR' is REJECTED with 'COBOLNET0819: MOVE of an alphabetic, alphanumeric-edited, numeric, or numeric-edited operand to a boolean data item is invalid (ISO 14.9.25.3 SR10, Table 16)'; but '01 A PIC A(3) VALUE "AB". 01 B PIC A(2) VALUE "CD". 01 BOOLR PIC 1(8) USAGE DISPLAY. MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(A B) TO BOOLR DISPLAY "B[" BOOLR "]"' compiles CLEAN and prints 'B[AB CD000]'. Per r3 ('if argument-1 is usage display, then if argument-1 and all argument-2 are of class alphabetic, the function will return an alphabetic value, otherwise ... alphanumeric', cite.py --check OK) argument-1 is usage display and every argument is class alphabetic, so the function returns an ALPHABETIC value, and Table 16 read directly in the spec (Alphabetic sender row × Boolean receiver column = 'No', versus Alphanumeric × Boolean = 'Yes') forbids that MOVE. The alphabetic result category is REPRESENTABLE at the sender end — 'PicInfo.IsAlphabetic' exists and MoveBinder.MoveCategoryLegality already consumes it ('bool senderIsAlphabetic = source is BoundFieldOperand fa && fa.Place.Item.Pic is { IsAlphabetic: true };') — what is missing is a channel to carry alphabetic-ness on an intrinsic RESULT: BoundIntrinsicCall.ResultCategory is a PicCategory, which has no Alphabetic member (IntrinsicArgumentRules' own remark records that PicCategory deliberately folds PIC A into Alphanumeric), and senderIsAlphabetic is computed only for a BoundFieldOperand. This is a result-category channel change, not a PicCategory rewrite.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: 'StrArgList(ic) => string.Join(", ", ic.Args.Select(Str))' renders every argument in SOURCE ORDER into one 'Concat(params string[] parts) => string.Concat(parts)' call, a left-to-right fold — the iterated form §15.18.4 r4 prescribes (each concatenation's result becomes argument-1 of the next iteration). Concatenation is associative and no iteration truncates (the intermediate is not a fixed-size receiver anywhere in the model), so the flat n-ary call and the iterated model produce the identical value at every argument count. The TYPE consequence of the iteration was worked through explicitly and adds nothing beyond r2/r3: for every legal mix, the iterated result category (r3 applied per iteration with the intermediate as argument-1) equals the flat reading — e.g. CONCAT(alphabetic, alphabetic, alphanumeric) is alphanumeric both ways — so no r4-specific defect exists; the r2/r3 mislabelling is carried on those rows and is open there. Re-verified on the built CLI for this review: 'FUNCTION CONCAT("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")' → 'ABCDE'; 8 arguments → '1234567AB'; 'FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b" "c")' → 'abc' and the explicitly nested 'FUNCTION CONCAT(FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b") "c")' → the same 'abc'; and the §15.3 variable-repetition ALL subscript 'FUNCTION CONCAT(A TE(ALL))' over '05 TE PIC X(2) OCCURS 3' → 'AB P1P2P3', i.e. one implicit argument-2 per occurrence, left to right, which is r4's trigger reached through a single written argument. The cited test resolves on disk (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs, method at the 'Concat_ConcatenatesArgumentImages_2023' [Fact]) and is spec-derived: AssertSpec compares against a literal expected value the test's own comment derives from r1/r4, with no oracle, and the method name carries none of the MatchesLegacy/MatchesGnuCobol/MatchesOracle suffixes. It pins 'FUNCTION CONCAT("X", "Y", "Z")' = 'XYZ' — 'more than one argument-2', precisely r4's trigger, and an ordering or dropped-argument defect would fail it. tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.cob + .out (manifest-enabled, golden 'VAR=XYZ') pins the same case a second way. Editions from Annex E.3.3 item 23, not from the catalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed. SUSTAINED ON RE-CHECK. TWO HALVES, ONE IMPLEMENTED. BindConvert catches only a zero-length LITERAL (`operands[0] is BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 }` -> COBOLNET1514). I re-ran both halves myself: FUNCTION CONVERT("" ANUM NAT) -> "error COBOLNET1514: FUNCTION CONVERT: argument-1 is of zero length (ISO 15.19.3 SR1)", but
       01 WS-D  PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-D ANUM ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> DL=[        ] and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS all spaces: no diagnostic and no EC even with checking EXPLICITLY ON. 15.3 rule 14 (validated: cite.py --check 15.3 "The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments") requires the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION condition to be SET TO EXIST when an argument's value is incorrect; only the RESULT is implementor-defined when checking is off, so the silence is a divergence in the half that is missing.
CITATION: the zero-length-item taxonomy is 8.5.4 "Zero-length items" (validated: --check 8.5.4 "A zero-length item is a data item or a literal whose minimum length is zero"); 8.5.1.4 does NOT resolve. 8.5.4 lists six shapes (ODO group with zero occurrences, group whose only subordinate is zero-length, ANY LENGTH, DYNAMIC LENGTH, zero-length variable-length record, zero-length intrinsic result) - none is screened at bind time or at runtime.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24 ("FUNCTION CONVERT. This function has been added to enable conversion between data representations") - a spec source, verified at specs/ISO_COBOL.md; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes: Verdict unchanged; supplies the missing spec-derived test. The rule states an EQUIVALENCE, so the test asserts it directly - the long and short spellings must give identical results - rather than pinning one answer, and it does so in BOTH positions the words appear in per 15.19.2 (source-format AND destination-format), plus the NATIONAL/NAT half. Each line prints the shared value so the equality cannot pass vacuously.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED - exhaustiveness re-derived, then confirmed BY EXECUTION rather than by reading. Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "The source-format shall be different from the destination-format" -> OK, rule 3). The source-format space is {ANY, ANUM, HEX, NAT} and the destination space is {ANUM, ANUM HEX, NAT, NAT HEX, BYTE}, so the only pairs that can be the SAME format are ANUM->ANUM and NAT->NAT with no HEX - which is exactly `(src==1 && dst==1 && !hex) || (src==3 && dst==3 && !hex)`. ANUM -> ANUM HEX must NOT be diagnosed and is not (15.19.4 NOTE 3 a depends on it, and the corpus golden AH=41 pins it). ANY and BYTE cannot appear on both sides; a bare HEX destination is not in the format and is rejected earlier by the pair check (verified: CONVERT(WS-A ANUM HEX) and CONVERT(WS-A HEX HEX) both -> COBOLNET1514 'not a valid source-format destination-format pair'). Ran a negative battery in one program: CONVERT(A ANUM ANUM) and CONVERT(N NAT NAT) each emit the SR3 message and nothing else. EditionContext.Error is unconditional, so the check is not dialect-gated away.
Test-ref audited and KEPT: Convert_SyntaxRuleViolations_1514 is a plain xUnit theory (not a legacy/GnuCobol comparison - it calls CobolNetCompiler(2023).CompileAndRun and asserts Assert.False(ok) with the spec reason "violates a 15.19.3 syntax rule"); its CONVERT(A ANUM ANUM) row can trip no other rule, which I confirmed from the emitted message text.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed. SUSTAINED, with the failing inputs re-run. TWO HALVES, ONE IMPLEMENTED, AND THE IMPLEMENTED HALF HAS A HOLE.
(a) 'valid string of hexadecimal digits ... representing complete bytes' is enforced at RUNTIME in HexDigitsToBytes: an odd digit count and a non-hex digit each call ExceptionState.ArgumentError (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION). HOLE: the method opens with `string t = s.Trim()`, so spaces are DISCARDED rather than diagnosed. Re-ran: `01 WS-LEAD PIC X(4) VALUE "  41".` / CONVERT(WS-LEAD HEX BYTE) -> "A" with no exception, and `01 WS-BLANK PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES.` / CONVERT(WS-BLANK HEX BYTE) -> empty, again with no exception. The trim is needed for the fixed-width image, so the fix is a trailing-image trim plus a digits-only screen, not deleting the trim.
(b) 'of display or national usage' is NOWHERE enforced - nothing inspects argument-1's USAGE. Re-ran:
       01 WS-N9 PIC 9(4) BINARY VALUE 4142.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-N9 HEX ANUM) TO WS-R.
-> R4=[AB]. A BINARY item is neither display nor national usage, so 15.19.3 rule 4 makes it an illegal HEX source and 15.3 rule 14 (validated) requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION; the compiler silently converts its display image instead.
ALSO RE-RUN: 15.19.4 NOTE 3 b as literally written, FUNCTION CONVERT (X"41" HEX ANUM), returns U+00A0 here (re-hexed: A0), not "A". That is DEFENSIBLE - X"41" is the one character 'A', i.e. a single hex digit, which rule 4 forbids as not 'complete bytes', so the compiler takes the odd-count path and pads; the NOTE's literal form is self-inconsistent and must NOT become a golden. Its evident intent, CONVERT("41" HEX ANUM) -> "A", IS met (corpus golden HA=A).
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed. SUSTAINED - I re-read IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified line by line and CONVERT is genuinely absent from it (the dictionary holds ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI and nothing else), so the PB1 15.3 class screen never runs for CONVERT; and BindConvert performs no class, category or repertoire check on argument-1 - only zero-length-literal, the format-pair shape, SR3, SR8 and SR9. Two failing inputs, both re-run:
(1) a class-numeric BINARY item accepted as an ANUM source:
       01 WS-N9 PIC 9(4) BINARY VALUE 4142.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-N9 ANUM ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> R5=[34313432] - the hex of the CHARACTERS "4142". A BINARY item is not 'a valid string of characters from the program's alphanumeric coded character set'; 15.3 rule 14 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION.
(2) a character outside the set CONVERT's own byte model assumes, silently corrupted instead of diagnosed:
       01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE "A<U+0160>B".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-X ANUM ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> XHEX=[413F4220]: the U+0160 position came back as 3F ('?'). I confirmed the item really does hold U+0160 - FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) returns 353 (= 352 + 1). So under CONVERT's own Latin-1 byte reading argument-1 violates rule 5 and should raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, and under the compiler's UTF-16 alphanumeric repertoire it is valid and must round-trip as 0160. It does neither.
The rule's own NOTE ('This is distinct from simply requiring the string to be of class alphanumeric') means a class screen is the MINIMUM this rule demands, not the whole of it - so adding the CONVERT row to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified closes case (1) but not case (2).
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed. SUSTAINED, re-run. Same root as AR-15.19.3-5: no class or repertoire screen for CONVERT anywhere. A class-alphanumeric item is accepted as a NAT source:
       01 WS-X2 PIC XX VALUE "AB".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-X2 NAT ANUM) TO WS-R.
-> R6=[AB]. A PIC XX item is not 'a valid string of national characters' (15.19.3 rule 6); 15.3 rule 14 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION.
ONE RULE, TWO PLACES: I read CheckRepertoireArgs and it enforces the IDENTICAL constraint for the sibling function - DISPLAY-OF's 15.26.3 rule 1 ('argument-1 shall be of class national') via OperandCategory, emitting COBOLNET1546 - and CONVERT's 15.19.4 r1/r3 route through the very same Repertoire translator in the runtime. The screen exists; CONVERT is simply not wired to it. The fix is to extract/reuse that screen (or add the CONVERT row to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified), never a second hand-written copy.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed. SUSTAINED and re-run; this is the most serious single finding on the function. BOTH halves fail.
(a) The EXCLUSION LIST is unenforced - nothing rejects an index, message-tag, object-reference, pointer, function-pointer or program-pointer argument-1 under ANY.
(b) 'It is not necessary for the contents to be valid according to the usage' means ANY reads the item's RAW STORAGE (15.19.1: 'the representation of most types of data item in hexadecimal'). The implementation passes the operand's DISPLAY IMAGE instead: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderString emits `CobolIntrinsics.Convert(Str(ic.Args[0]), {ic.ConvertSource}, {ic.ConvertDest}, ...)` - Str() is the display-image channel - and BindConvert's only concession is re-tagging ANY as NAT when the operand is national (`int runtimeSrc = src == 0 && IsNationalOperand(operands[0]) ? 3 : src;`).
Re-run verbatim:
       01 WS-PTR USAGE POINTER.  01 WS-IDX USAGE INDEX.  01 WS-B PIC S9(4) BINARY VALUE 1.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-PTR ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> PTR=[436F626F6C4E65742E52756E74696D65]
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-IDX ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> IDX=[] (empty)
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-B   ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> BIN=[30303031]
436F626F6C4E65742E52756E74696D65 decodes to the ASCII text "CobolNet.Runtime" - a leaked .NET type name reaching COBOL storage through a legal COBOL construct. 30303031 is the hex of the CHARACTERS "0001"; the raw storage of a 2-byte COMP S9(4) holding 1 is two bytes, so a conforming answer is FOUR hex digits, not eight. Expected: the pointer and index calls rejected per rule 7, and the BINARY call hexing the item's storage bytes.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED - and this time confirmed by EXHAUSTIVE EXECUTION over the whole destination space, not by reading the guard. Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "the destination-format shall be ANUM HEX or NAT HEX" -> OK, rule 8). `if (src == 0 && !(hex && dst is 1 or 3))` covers dst in {1, 3, 4}: I ran ALL FIVE destination shapes with an ANY source in one program - ANY ANUM, ANY NAT, ANY BYTE, ANY ALPHANUMERIC, ANY NATIONAL - and every one emits the SR8 message; ANY ANUM HEX and ANY NAT HEX are correctly accepted (Convert_AnyOverNational_ResolvesToNatStorage_2023 pins the latter at 0041). ANY in the DESTINATION position is rejected one step earlier by the pair check. The guard reads `src`, captured BEFORE the ANY->NAT storage remap that later produces `runtimeSrc`, so the remap cannot mask it. Single clause, no second half.
Test-ref audited and KEPT: the theory's CONVERT(A ANY ANUM) row can trip no other rule (confirmed from the emitted message), the assertion is Assert.False(ok) on the spec's 'shall', and the method is not a legacy/GnuCobol comparison.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED - confirmed by exhaustive execution over the source space. Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "the source-format shall be HEX" -> OK, rule 9). `if (dst == 4 && src != 2)`: I ran all three non-HEX sources with a BYTE destination - ANUM BYTE, NAT BYTE, ANY BYTE - and each emits the SR9 message (ANY BYTE correctly emits SR8 as well, both rules being violated), while CONVERT(WS-HX HEX BYTE) is accepted and returns "A" (corpus golden HB=A). 'BYTE HEX' and any bare-HEX destination are rejected earlier by the pair check, so dst == 4 is reachable only from a literal BYTE word. Single clause, no second half; the guard is unreachable-by-construction from any other path.
Test-ref audited and KEPT: the CONVERT(A ANUM BYTE) row trips SR9 and nothing else (confirmed from the emitted message).
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED at PARTIAL. The VALUE half conforms on both reachable sources (rule 8 bars ANY and rule 3 bars ANUM, so a bare-ANUM destination comes only from NAT or HEX): NAT->ANUM routes to the ONE shared Repertoire translator, HEX->ANUM emits one alphanumeric position per byte (verified CONVERT("41" HEX ANUM) = "A"). The SUBSTITUTION half does not close, for two reasons.
(a) ABSENT ON THE HEX->ANUM PATH. That path is `chars[i] = (char)bytes[i]` with no validity test of any kind, making it byte-for-byte identical to the BYTE destination (rule 5) - yet rule 1 and rule 5 differ PRECISELY in that rule 1 carries a coded-character-set screen and rule 5 does not.
(b) THE HALF THAT IS PRESENT RESTS ON A CHARACTER SET THE COMPILER CONTRADICTS ELSEWHERE. Repertoire substitutes when `c > 0xFF` (`sb.Append(toNational || c <= 0xFF ? c : sub ?? Sub())`), i.e. rule 1's 'valid set of characters from the alphanumeric coded character set' is read as Latin-1. But a PIC X item in this compiler demonstrably holds U+0160: `01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE "A<U+0160>B".` / FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) returns 353 - I re-ran this myself - and the project's stated alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16. If the alphanumeric coded set is UTF-16, rule 1 must return U+0160 unchanged and must NOT set EC-DATA-CONVERSION, and the cited test is pinning the wrong answer; if it is Latin-1, then (a) is a real gap AND a PIC X item may not hold U+0160 at all. Exactly one of the two is wrong under either reading, and choosing between them is an implementor-defined-set decision the project has not written down in one place.
Mechanics that DO check out and that I re-verified rather than assuming: Sub() returns the implementor-defined '?' AND calls ExceptionState.DataConversionError, and BOTH effects are observable - CONVERT(N"A<U+0160>" NAT ANUM) yields "A?" and the cited test asserts EXCEPTION-STATUS = EC-DATA-CONVERSION. Test-ref audited and KEPT (a plain CompileAndRun with a hardcoded spec-derived expectation, not a legacy comparison), but it covers only the contested half.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL TO DIVERGES. The prior verdict treated the second half as merely 'unimplemented', but I RAN two inputs that each return a value WRONG under rule 2's own normative text, so this is demonstrated divergence, not an unverified edge. Citation validated (--check 15.19.4 "the trailing portion needed to make up a complete multiple is padded with zero bits" -> OK, rule 2).
(a) CONFORMS: 'a string of hexadecimal digits in display format' for all three legal character sources (ANUM "A" -> "41" = NOTE 3 a; ANUM "AB " -> "414220"; NAT N"A" -> "0041" over UTF-16BE), spec-tested by the cited theory.
(b) DIVERGES - the ZERO-BIT PADDING clause. CobolIntrinsics.Convert reduces argument-1 to a byte[] built from CHARACTERS (one byte per code unit for ANUM/ANY, two for NAT) and has NO sub-byte path, so an argument whose bit count is not a multiple of 8 is never padded. Re-run:
       01 ITEM-B PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(ITEM-B ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> BITANUM=[313031], the hex of the CHARACTERS "101". Rule 2's own arithmetic (an alphanumeric character being 8 bits in this implementation) gives 101 + five zero bits = 1010 0000 = "A0". 313031 is wrong under every reading of the clause. NOTE: do NOT carry "E0" from NOTE 3 c into an ANUM-HEX golden - 1010 0000 is 0xA0, and E0 is not derivable from B"101" under rule 2 at all.
(c) DIVERGES - THE IMPLEMENTED HALF IS LOSSY AND RULE 2 AUTHORIZES NO LOSS. Unlike rules 1 and 3, rule 2 has no substitution clause whatsoever, yet `bytes[i] = arg[i] <= 0xFF ? (byte)arg[i] : ByteSub()` replaces any code unit above 0xFF with 0x3F and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION. Re-run: `01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE "A<U+0160>B".` / CONVERT(WS-X ANUM ANUM HEX) -> XHEX=[413F4220], with FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) = 353 proving the item really holds U+0160. See RV-15.19.4-1 note (b) - the same unmade character-set decision.
Reachability note for (b): with an ANUM source (8 bits/char), a NAT source (16) or a HEX source (8/byte) the bit count is ALWAYS a multiple of 8, so rule 2's padding clause is reachable only through an ANY source over a sub-byte item - which makes its root cause shared with AR-15.19.3-7 (ANY delivers Str(arg), the display image, not the storage bits).
Test-ref kept for half (a) only; halves (b) and (c) still need spec-derived tests.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED at PARTIAL (deliberately NOT raised to DIVERGES: the only demonstrable failing value depends on a national-character-set definition the project has not fixed, so the missing half is absent rather than provably wrong). TWO HALVES, ONE VERIFIED. The value half conforms on both paths that can reach a bare NAT destination (rule 8 bars ANY, rule 3 bars NAT): ANUM->NAT through Repertoire (identity, the alphanumeric set being a subset of national - covered by the cited round-trip test, which is a plain spec-expectation assertion, not a legacy comparison) and HEX->NAT through the byte pathway (two bytes -> one UTF-16BE code unit, a trailing odd byte zero-filled).
The 'does not correspond to a valid set of national characters -> implementor-defined substitution character + EC-DATA-CONVERSION' half is ABSENT on the HEX->NAT path: Repertoire never substitutes when toNational is true (`sb.Append(toNational || c <= 0xFF ? c : sub ?? Sub())`) and the byte pathway performs no validity check at all. With checking explicitly on:
       01 WS-HX PIC X(4) VALUE "D800".   01 WS-NR PIC N(4).
       >>TURN EC-DATA-CONVERSION CHECKING ON
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-HX HEX NAT) TO WS-NR.
-> FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS all spaces and WS-NR holding the lone surrogate U+D800. Whether an unpaired surrogate is 'not a valid national character' is exactly the implementor-defined decision above; but under ANY definition narrower than 'all 65536 code units' something is invalid, and NOTHING is checked on this path, so the half cannot be closed.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed - no existing test uses a NAT HEX destination at all (Convert_Formats_2023's national row is NAT -> ANUM HEX). SUSTAINED, and STRENGTHENED with a repro the prior record did not have.
NEW, CLEANER REPRO - the padding defect is NOT confined to the ANY/BIT path, which is what the prior record implied. Rule 4 pads to 'a multiple of those needed for a single NATIONAL character' = 16 bits here (national is UTF-16, two bytes per position, D-N1). An ALPHANUMERIC source of ODD byte length therefore needs padding too. Run:
       01 WS-A  PIC X VALUE "A".   01 WS-NR PIC N(8).
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-A ANUM NAT HEX) TO WS-NR.
-> ANATHEX=[41]. Argument-1 is 8 bits, not a multiple of 16, so rule 4 requires 8 trailing zero bits -> 0x4100 -> "4100". The compiler emits "41". No BIT usage, no ANY source, no reliance on NOTE 3.
ORIGINAL REPRO, re-run: `01 ITEM-B PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101".` / MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(ITEM-B ANY NAT HEX) TO WS-NR -> BITNAT=[313031], the hex of the CHARACTERS "101" rather than of the item's three data bits. Two defects compound there: the ANY source delivers the display image instead of the storage bits (AR-15.19.3-7), and there is no bit-level padding step before ToHex.
WHAT THE EXPECTED VALUE IS NOT: "E0" from 15.19.4 NOTE 3 c must NOT become a golden. Under rule 4's own arithmetic B"101" pads to 1010 0000 0000 0000 = "A000"; "E0" is reachable only by padding to EIGHT bits (rule 2's multiple, not rule 4's) AND reading the value as B"111". The NOTE is wrong on both counts. This DIVERGENCE rests on rule 4's normative text alone.
The digit-CODE-POINT half of the rule ('in national format') IS correct and I re-verified it independently: BindConvert sets `category = dst == 3 ? PicCategory.National : PicCategory.Alphanumeric` per the 15.19.1 table, and CONVERT(WS-N NAT NAT HEX) re-hexed through ANUM HEX gives 0030 0030 0034 0031 - the digits "0041" as national positions.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS TO PARTIAL. Rule 5's own normative SENTENCE conforms - that part of the prior record survives re-checking, and I extended it: rule 9 forces a HEX source, so the rule reduces to hex-digit pairs -> bytes -> one alphanumeric position per byte, which is exactly the fall-through `for (int i = 0; i < bytes.Length; i++) chars[i] = (char)bytes[i];`, with the 15.19.1 Alphanumeric result type (dst == 4 is not 3, so PicCategory.Alphanumeric). Beyond the golden I ran four more edges myself: CONVERT("4142" HEX BYTE) = "AB" (multi-byte), CONVERT("FF" HEX BYTE) -> FUNCTION ORD = 256, i.e. U+00FF (high-byte edge), CONVERT("00" HEX BYTE) -> one U+0000 position (re-hexed: 00), and a NATIONAL-usage hex source `01 WS-NH PIC N(2) VALUE N"41".` -> "A" (which matters because rule 4 admits national hex digits). Citation validated (--check 15.19.4 "the returned value is a string of bytes that represents the value expressed in argument-1" -> OK, rule 5). The cited corpus case exists on disk (tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_convert.cob, `MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-HX HEX BYTE) TO WS-R.`), is listed in the "enabled" array of tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json, and its golden line is `HB=A` - a spec-derived value compared by CorpusRunnerTests, not a recorded oracle.
WHY THE ROW STILL CANNOT BE CLOSED. The rule text carried by this row includes 15.19.4 NOTE 3 and its three worked examples, and two of the three do not reproduce - I ran both:
  - NOTE 3 c, `CONVERT(item-b ANY NAT HEX)` over `PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101"`, returns 313031. (Root cause charged on RV-15.19.4-4; listed here because it is part of THIS row's text.)
  - NOTE 3 b as literally written in the BYTE family, `FUNCTION CONVERT (X"41" HEX BYTE)` and `... HEX ANUM`, both return U+00A0, not "A".
And the premise rule 5 depends on - that argument-1 IS 'a valid string of hexadecimal digits ... representing complete bytes' - is only half enforced (AR-15.19.3-4): HexDigitsToBytes silently `Trim()`s, so CONVERT("  41" HEX BYTE) returns "A" and an all-blank source returns an empty byte string, both with no exception. Rule 5 therefore returns a 'string of bytes' for arguments that are not byte strings.
NOTED, not charged here: this implementation makes a BYTE destination byte-for-byte identical to a bare ANUM destination, so the cited golden HB=A would pass even if BYTE were routed through the rule-1 path. Under the compiler's Latin-1 byte model every byte maps to a valid alphanumeric character, so the identity is not itself a defect - but it does mean the golden cannot discriminate rule 5 from rule 1, and a discriminating test needs the rule-1 screen that RV-15.19.4-1 (a) says is missing.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24 ("FUNCTION CONVERT. This function has been added to enable conversion between data representations"), read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: COS function
notes:
test-needed. RULE (validated: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.20.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric." -> OK §15.20.3 1)) requires argument-1 to be of CLASS numeric, which resolves through the §8.5.2.1 Table-2 CLASS column. UNENFORCED. The PB1 §15.3 class screen exists and is the project's settled disposition for exactly this rule text (COBOLNET1627 — reject under strict conformance, warn under --permissive), but IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses is driven ONLY by IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified: "if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;". COS appears in NEITHER Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened (both dictionaries read in full), so the screen returns early and every class-alphanumeric argument is silently coerced. Identical rule text is ALREADY enforced for ACOS §15.8.3 r1 / ASIN §15.10.3 r1 / ATAN §15.11.3 r1, so the correct behaviour is unambiguous; the fix is one row ["COS"] = ('n', "§15.20.3 r1"). REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY against src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe at strict --std 2023 — exit 0, ZERO diagnostics:
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RCOSA1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "abc".
       01 R PIC S9(6)V9(9).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION COS(A).
           DISPLAY "COS-ALNUM=" R.
           STOP RUN.
prints COS-ALNUM=00000100000000{ (= 1.000000000, i.e. "abc" coerced to 0). SHAPE SWEEP (added by the refutation — all inadmissible classes go through, not just a PIC X): 01 NE PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE 12.34 (numeric-EDITED, class ALPHANUMERIC per Table 2, the row most easily misread) gives NUMEDIT=097448739I = cos(12.34); an alphanumeric GROUP item (01 GRP / 05 GA PIC X(2) VALUE "12") gives GROUP=084385395I = cos(12). Both compile clean at --std 2023 with zero diagnostics. NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST: tests/conformance/negative/pb1-numeric-arg-trig-family.cob was read on disk and exercises ACOS/ASIN/ATAN only; the only other COS references in the tree are tests/nist/programs/IF106A.cob (a NIST CCVS regression net) and IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy line 51, both of which the gate rejects. Nor is COS's absence pinned by a green test — IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests only validates the rows that ARE present (EveryVerifiedRule_CitesItsClause / EveryVerifiedRule_NamesARealFunction_WithAHandledCode); it does not enumerate an expected function list. EDITIONS derived from the standard's change record, not from the catalog row: COS carries no entry in docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md, and COS compiles and runs at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (verified), so the argument rule and the divergence exist at every edition.

subject: COS function
notes:
test-needed. RULE (validated: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.20.4 "greater than or equal to" -> OK §15.20.4 1)) has TWO halves: the returned value IS the approximation of the cosine of argument-1, AND it lies in [-1, +1]. ⚠ THE ADJUDICATED RECORD'S CHARACTERISATION IS OVERTURNED. It asserted "HALF ONE HOLDS" and that "the escape is confined to the non-finite path" / "Every FINITE argument tested stays inside the bound". Half one does NOT hold, and its failure is reachable with an ORDINARY FINITE ARGUMENT; it was missed because every sample used a scale-9 receiver. That is the PB5 trap verbatim: vary the RECEIVER. (A) BOUND HALF — fails on a non-finite argument. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat bypasses the FromDouble quantizer for a floating receiver ("return num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true) : ..."), so Math.Cos(+INF) = NaN is returned raw — neither >= -1 nor <= +1. §15.3 (validated: cite.py --check 15.3 "incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value" -> OK) requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist when the RETURNED value is incorrect per the function definition; none is set even with checking explicitly enabled. Reproduced (exit 0, no diagnostic): 01 X COMP-2. / >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON / COMPUTE X = FUNCTION COS(FUNCTION EXP(1000)). prints COS-EXP1000=NaN and an EMPTY FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS; 01 G COMP-1 gives the same NaN. A FIXED receiver behaves differently again (01 F PIC S9(4)V9(9) prints 0.433260489, because the nested EXP saturates through FromDouble to Int128.MaxValue first, and still no EC) — so one source text yields NaN, 0.433260489, or the FromDouble NaN arm purely by receiver kind. The upstream enabler also reproduces: 01 BIG COMP-2 VALUE 1.0E300. / COMPUTE INF = BIG * BIG ON SIZE ERROR ... NOT ON SIZE ERROR ... stores Infinity and takes the NOT ON SIZE ERROR branch. (B) APPROXIMATION HALF — ALSO FAILS, on finite in-domain arguments. RenderFloat quantizes at ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), so the RETURNED VALUE is a function of the RECEIVER rather than of argument-1 alone, and RenderFloat carries NO arithmetic-mode branch at all (the only num.StandardDecimal test in IntrinsicRenderer.cs is MEAN's, line 128). Under standard arithmetic that violates §15.4.1 (validated: cite.py --check 15.4.1 "the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function" -> OK): "the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element so long as the value and order of the arguments ... are unchanged". Reproduced with OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. at --std 2023 (and with ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD at --std 2002):
       01 P09 PIC S9V9(9).
       01 P17 PIC S9V9(17).
           COMPUTE P09 = FUNCTION COS(1).   *> prints 0.540302306
           COMPUTE P17 = FUNCTION COS(1).   *> prints 0.54030230586813976
Two instances, same argument, DIFFERENT returned values — and it is the returned VALUE, not the store: COMPUTE Q09 = P17 (a plain unrounded store of the wider value into 9 fraction digits) gives 0.540302305, not 0.540302306. The generated C# is the direct proof: CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(CobolIntrinsics.Cos((double)(1L)), 9) in one statement and (..., 17) in the other, in the SAME program under STANDARD-DECIMAL. The OPTIONS paragraph is genuinely honoured (the MEAN emission switches to CobolDec.Div under the same clause), so this is COS ignoring the mode, not an ignored OPTIONS clause. (C) Most visible instance of (B): at receiver scale >= 23 the value is corrupted outright — 01 P30 PIC SV9(30). COMPUTE P30 = FUNCTION COS(0). prints 0.999999999999999879147136483328 instead of 1, because Pow10.BuildDouble builds 10^n with a cumulative x10 DOUBLE recurrence that is exact only through 10^22 (10^30 comes out ~1.2e14 low). Every cumulative error is negative, so this path cannot push the value ABOVE +1 — the bound survives here; it is half ONE that breaks. FIX SITE — ONE PLACE, NOT PER FUNCTION: the §15.4.1 float boundary (IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat + CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble + Pow10.BuildDouble), which owns the receiver-scale choice, the non-finite arm and the power-of-ten table. Sibling sweep confirms it is not a COS defect: SIN (§15.82.4 carries the identical [-1,+1] bound) and TAN also return NaN, SQRT returns Infinity, and every float-family function inherits the receiver-dependent quantization. EDITION SCOPE of the sub-findings (the rule itself applies at all four editions, where COS compiles and runs): (A) reproduces at 85/2002/2014/2023; (B) needs a selectable standard-arithmetic mode, so 2002/2014/2023 (--std 85 rejects the OPTIONS paragraph with COBOLNET0804); (C) needs a 23+-digit PICTURE, so 2002/2014/2023 (--std 85 rejects PIC SV9(30) with COBOLNET0802). NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST: the only COS coverage on disk is tests/nist/programs/IF106A.cob (NIST CCVS regression net) and IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy line 51 — the gate rejects both.

subject: CURRENT-DATE function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. The prior verdict rested on TWO edges it called unverified; I executed BOTH against the shipping binary, so its stated basis no longer holds - one edge is CORRECT and the other emits a value 15.21.3 forbids, with no conforming alternative available in the standard, which is an owner call, not a mechanical fix. Citation re-run: cite.py --check 15.21.3 'The character positions returned, numbered from left to right' OK (rule 1, Returned value rule); 7.3.17.4 GR2 'the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59 may be reported' OK. PATH READ: IntrinsicRenderer#RenderString maps "CurrentDate" to RuntimeApi.DateFn with an empty argument list; CobolDate#CurrentDate is Format21(DateTimeOffset.Now); CobolDate#Format21 is t.ToString("yyyyMMddHHmmssff", InvariantCulture) + (t.Offset >= TimeSpan.Zero ? "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00"). InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits (positions 1-4). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, COBOL side: 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD' (PIC X(21)) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 -> '2026073010404830-0700'; FUNCTION LENGTH of the function = 0021. Receiver varied per the PB5 lesson - PIC X(30) space-pads to '...-0700         ', PIC X(8) truncates to '20260730', PIC N(21) carries all 21, and STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE contributes exactly 21 characters - so no receiver scale hides a layout defect. VERIFIED BY DIRECT EXECUTION OF THE SHIPPING METHOD (loaded src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll and invoked CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Format21 over fixed DateTimeOffsets, since TimeZoneInfo.Local reads the Windows registry and ignores TZ): +05:45 -> '2026073010331564+0545', -09:30 -> '...-0930', +12:45 -> '...+1245', 00:00 -> '...+0000', -12:00 -> '...-1200', +13:00 -> '...+1300'. So positions 20-21 (the prior pass's unverified edge (b)) are CORRECT for non-zero minute offsets, position 17 is correct on BOTH branches including the 'same as UTC' => '+' boundary, and the '-' branch of 18-19 cannot exceed 12 because no TimeZoneInfo zone is below -12:00. THE ONE OPEN POINT, now demonstrated rather than suspected: +14:00 -> '2026073010331564+1400'. 15.21.3 positions 18-19 state 'If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13', and Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) is UNCLAMPED, so a run on a host whose TimeZoneInfo.Local is 'Line Islands Standard Time' / Pacific-Kiritimati (UTC+14, a zone Windows and IANA both ship) returns '14' there. The reason this is NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION and not DIVERGES: the standard's table offers NO in-range value for a +14 host, so no behavior conforms - emitting 14 (today) is an out-of-range implementor extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and returning '0'/'00'/'00' means 'the system has no facility to provide the local time differential factor', which is false. Nothing in CobolDate.cs, docs/CONFORMANCE.md or the design docs records a decision, and the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table). THE BARE OWNER QUESTION: on a host whose local UTC offset is +14:00, what shall CURRENT-DATE (and WHEN-COMPILED) return in character positions 17-19? CORRECTED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD: positions 13-14 do conform without qualification - 7.3.17.4 GR1 implies OFF when no LEAP-SECOND directive is written and GR3 then forbids >59, which .NET's 'ss' can never emit; GR2's ON case leaves >59 to the implementor, so ignoring the directive (it sits in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.KnownIgnoredDirectives) is conforming on both branches, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md's 'documented non-support' wording for >>LEAP-SECOND overstates the exposure for THIS rule. NOT a defect but worth recording: CurrentDate() reads DateTimeOffset.Now directly instead of the injectable RunUnit.Current.Clock (CobolDate.cs's SecondsPastMidnight doc comment says so - 'NOT the CurrentDate direct-DateTimeOffset.Now path, which predates the seam'), so under COBOLNET_CLOCK a program observes CURRENT-DATE disagreeing with SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT / YEAR-TO-YYYY, and 15.100.3 r5 DEFINES YEAR-TO-YYYY's argument-3 default as FUNCTION NUMVAL(FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:4)) - an identity the seam split breaks. test-needed: (i) a unit test over CobolDate.Format21 with fixed DateTimeOffsets (+14:00, +13:00, -12:00, +05:45, -09:30, a zero-hundredths instant, a single-digit month/day) asserting every position's 15.21.3 range, and (ii) a conformance case pinning CURRENT-DATE through the injectable clock once that seam covers it. The only existing spec-derived test touching CURRENT-DATE (IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec, verified on disk) asserts only the ordering CURRENT-DATE >= WHEN-COMPILED and inspects NO character position of the CURRENT-DATE value, so it does not cover this rule and test-ref stays empty.

subject: DATE-OF-INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL. The prior adjudication called the VALUE half CONFORMS after sampling only SMALL out-of-range arguments (0, -5, 3067672) — exactly the PB5 failure mode. THE RANGE GUARD IS UNREACHABLE FOR ANY ARGUMENT OF MAGNITUDE >= 2^63, so the value half DIVERGES too. Root cause, read out of the emitter rather than sampled: IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt renders every integer-kind argument as `(long)(<Int128 expr>)`, an UNCHECKED C# narrowing that WRAPS modulo 2^64 BEFORE CobolDate.DateOfInteger's `if (integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671)` ever sees the value. Generated C# from the repro below, verbatim: `CobolDate.DateOfInteger((long)(Int128.Parse("18446744073709695567")))`. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, ACTUALLY RUN (E:/Temp/.../scratchpad/doi-refute/q2.cob, q3.cob): `01 P PIC 9(18) VALUE 184467440737096955.` / `01 R PIC 9(18).` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(P * 100 + 67)` — the argument value is 18,446,744,073,709,695,567 = 2^64 + 143,951 — prints 000000000019950215 (i.e. 1995-02-15) under --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023, and prints the SAME thing with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` in effect. §15.5.2 (cite.py --check 15.5.2 OK): 'It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'; §15.3 (cite.py --check 15.3 OK): 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' The EC is never set, so neither the implementor-defined default (0) nor the fatal checked raise happens — the function silently returns a PLAUSIBLE WRONG DATE. That the guard works for a small argument is proved by the control run: DATE-OF-INTEGER(3067672) with checking ON aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): DATE-OF-INTEGER argument 3067672 outside 1..3,067,671', so the divergence is precisely the pre-guard truncation, not a missing EC mechanism. The literal form `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(18446744073709695567)` and a `PIC 9(20)` operand reproduce it identically at 2002+; the arithmetic-expression form above reaches it at COBOL-85 as well, because §8.8.1.2 r7 (cite.py --check 8.8.1.2 OK) is explicit that 'Arithmetic expressions allow the user to combine arithmetic operations without the restrictions on composite of operands and receiving data items', so the 18-digit COBOL-85 literal cap does not protect the 85 edition. Second wrap witness: DATE-OF-INTEGER(36893488147419246903) = 2*2^64 + 143,671 prints 19940511. THE SECOND HALF ALSO FAILS, as the prior report found and I confirm: 'a value in integer date form' carries §15.6 Table 21's argument type Int (cite.py --check 15.6 OK: '| DATE-OF-INTEGER | Int1 | Int | Standard date equivalent (YYYYMMDD) of integer date in argument-1 |') = §15.3 type 6 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified' (cite.py --check 15.3 OK). DATE-OF-INTEGER is absent from BOTH IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and DeliberatelyUnscreened, so IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses returns immediately and the PB1 §15.3 screen (COBOLNET1627) never runs. RAN: `01 A PIC X(6) VALUE "143951".` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(A)` prints 19950215 with zero diagnostics, and `01 N PIC 9(6)V99 VALUE 143951.75.` prints 19950215 (silent truncation), both with checking ON. FIX SHAPE — TWO FIXES, NOT ONE: (1) the pre-guard truncation is the ROOT and it is NOT specific to this function — IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt feeds DAY-OF-INTEGER, INTEGER-OF-DATE, INTEGER-OF-DAY, FACTORIAL, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, YEAR-TO-YYYY, COMBINED-DATETIME and FIND-STRING through the same `(long)` cast, so the range check must move to (or be duplicated in) the Int128 domain, or AsInt must raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION itself on an out-of-long value; (2) add ["DATE-OF-INTEGER"] = ('i', "§15.22.3 r1") to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and sweep the unscreened siblings DAY-OF-INTEGER §15.24.3 / INTEGER-OF-DATE §15.46.3 / INTEGER-OF-DAY §15.47.3 / FORMATTED-DATE §15.39.3 / FORMATTED-DATETIME §15.40.3 with it. EDITIONS derived independently of the catalog row: DATE-OF-INTEGER appears in NO Annex E addition list in specs/ISO_COBOL.md (its only occurrences are the TOC, the §8.9 reserved-word list, Table 21, §15.22 itself, the informative D.31.3.6 and the index) and in no row of docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md, so it is present in all four editions; both halves of the divergence reproduce under --std 85/2002/2014/2023. test-needed: nothing spec-derived pins the range boundaries, the >2^63 wrap, the class rejection or the fractional-operand case.

subject: DATE-OF-INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS. The §15.5.2 -> §15.5.3 correspondence itself is right — I re-derived thirteen values from the spec definition alone (integer date 1 = 1601-01-01 per §15.5.2, proleptic Gregorian per §15.5.1, cite.py --check 15.5.1/15.5.2 OK) and every one matched what the compiler printed: 1->16010101, 59->16010228, 60->16010301, 365->16011231, 366->16020101, 1155->16040229, 36218->17000228, 36219->17000301 (the 1700 non-leap century), 145791->20000229, 143951->19950215, 730000->35990903, 3067670->99991230, 3067671->99991231. BUT THERE IS A LEGAL ARGUMENT FOR WHICH NO VALUE IS RETURNED AT ALL — the compiler fails with a RAW BACKEND ERROR on conforming source, which is the PB2 defect class re-appearing on this function through a hole PB2's own drift test deliberately leaves open. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, ACTUALLY RUN (E:/Temp/.../scratchpad/doi-refute/q1.cob): `01 R PIC 9(8).` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(1.43951E5)` -> `error: backend compilation failed (generated C# at q1.g.cs): (44,90): error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DateOfIntegerReal'`. Reproduces at --std 85 AND 2023. The same failure with a data item: `01 F USAGE COMP-2 VALUE 143951.` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(F)`. THE ARGUMENT IS LEGAL, checked as a syntactic question and not only as a rule question: §8.3.3.3.3 r1 makes `1.43951E5` a floating-point NUMERIC literal (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.3 OK); §8.3.3.3.1 'Numeric literals are of the class and category numeric' (OK); §8.8.1.1 'An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal, ...' (OK), so it IS an arithmetic expression; its value is exactly 143,951, so it 'will always result in an integer value' (§15.3 type 6, OK) and it is a positive integer <= 3,067,671, i.e. a value in integer date form (§15.5.2, OK). §15.22.3 r1 is satisfied, therefore §15.22.4 r1 obliges the function to return 19950215. It returns nothing. ROOT CAUSE, read out of the code: IntrinsicRenderer routes `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` before the exact switch, RealMethod maps DateOfInteger -> DateOfIntegerReal by convention, and CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs has NO such body (it has AbsReal, FloorReal, ... CombinedDatetimeReal, but nothing for the four date conversions). The guard that should have caught this, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.cs#EveryExactArm_HasItsRealCounterpart, scopes itself to catalog rows whose ArgKinds contains 'n' and explicitly reasons in its own remarks that "an integer-argument function ('i' - DATE-OF-INTEGER, FACTORIAL) ... cannot receive a float without violating their own argument rule first, which is PB1's business" — that premise is false twice over: PB1 does not screen DATE-OF-INTEGER at all, and even the 'i' screen (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible('i') = {Numeric, NumericEditedDeEditing}) ADMITS class-numeric COMP-2, so adding the row would not close this. FIX SHAPE: add DateOfIntegerReal (and DayOfIntegerReal / IntegerOfDateReal / IntegerOfDayReal / the Y2K trio, all reachable the same way) to CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs, or make the date family reject a real argument with a diagnostic instead of emitting a call to a non-existent member; and widen IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests' scope to the 'i' rows. Test-ref re-verified on disk and genuinely spec-derived (AssertSpec, hand-derived expectation, no oracle) — but it covers only the DEGENERATE epoch case DATE-OF-INTEGER(1) -> 16010101; nothing checked in pins a non-degenerate value or the floating-point argument path.

subject: DATE-OF-INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS. The COMPOSITION is right where a value is produced: `d.Year * 10000L + d.Month * 100L + d.Day` is the §15.5.3 standard date form 'The standard date form is YYYYMMDD' (cite.py --check 15.5.3 OK), the function type is integer (§15.22.1 'The type of this function is integer', OK) and the catalog row declares IntrinsicType.Integer rendered at scale 0. RAN, exercising all three named subfields non-degenerately: 16011231 (DD=31), 16040229 / 20000229 (MM=02 DD=29 leap), 17000301 (the non-leap-century boundary), 19950215, 35990903; and the form survives every receiver shape I varied — PIC 9(8) -> 19950215, PIC S9(8) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -> +19950215, an alphanumeric PIC X(8) receiver via MOVE -> [19950215], and direct DISPLAY of the raw function value -> [16010101]. WHY NOT CONFORMS: there is a class of LEGAL argument-1 for which no value in YYYYMMDD form is returned at all, so this rule is verified on only one of the two argument-rendering paths. `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(1.43951E5)` — a §8.8.1.1 arithmetic expression whose value is always the integer 143,951 and therefore a §15.5.2 value in integer date form, i.e. conforming under §15.22.3 r1 — fails to compile with `error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DateOfIntegerReal'` at --std 85 and 2023 (full derivation and root cause in the RV-15.22.4-1 record; same defect, and it blocks this rule as well). Second unverified edge: because IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt truncates the argument with an unchecked `(long)` cast before CobolDate.DateOfInteger's range guard, an argument of magnitude >= 2^63 yields a value that LOOKS like a well-formed YYYYMMDD (19950215) but is the standard date of a wrapped integer, not of argument-1 — see AR-15.22.3-1. test-needed: the cited test is spec-derived and verified on disk, but its DATE-OF-INTEGER case is the degenerate 16010101 (MM=01, DD=01), so no checked-in spec-derived test pins non-degenerate MM/DD placement or the float-argument path; the leap/century values above should be added to it.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: OVERTURNED from PARTIAL. BOTH halves of 15.23.3 r1 fail; the RANGE half only LOOKS enforced. (a) VALUE HALF - CobolDate.DateToYyyymmdd screens `date is < 1 or > 999999`, but the compiler truncates the argument to 64 bits BEFORE the runtime ever sees it: IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits `(long)(<expr>)` over an Int128-carried operand, so any legal COBOL integer wider than 64 bits wraps modulo 2^64 and the screen tests the WRONG NUMBER. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, compiled and run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe: `01 D8 PIC S9(18). 01 A1 PIC S9(31) VALUE 18446744073710402619.` ... `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(A1, 10, 2002)` / `DISPLAY "A1WRAP=" D8` prints A1WRAP=19851003 and the run continues. `DISPLAY A1` confirms the item really holds 18446744073710402619 (= 2^64 + 851003), which is NOT 'a positive integer less than 1000000', so 15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist; none is. The narrow control `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(1000000, 10, 2002)` DOES abort fatally, which is exactly why sampling only small arguments hid this. (b) INTEGER/CLASS HALF - DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD is in neither IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified nor DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at `if (!Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and no COBOLNET1627 is ever emitted. `01 X6 PIC X(6) VALUE "851003".` -> `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(X6, 10, 2002)` prints 19851003 (class ALPHANUMERIC per 8.5.2.1 Table 2, and 15.3 type 6 requires 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item'); `01 F6 PIC 9(6)V9 VALUE 851003.7.` likewise prints 19851003, silently truncated by IntArg. A COMP-2 argument is worse still: it routes through AnyRealArgument -> RealMethod and emits `CobolIntrinsics.DateToYyyymmddReal`, which does not exist, so the user gets `error CS0117` from the generated C# - an internal backend failure instead of a diagnostic (IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests deliberately scopes itself to 'n' rows, leaving the 'i' rows to PB1). ROOT FIX: carry intrinsic integer arguments at their real width (Int128) and range-screen before narrowing, and add the DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD row to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified. The r1 NOTE (no calendar validation) IS honoured: (850000, 10, 2002) -> 19850000. test-needed.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED (independently reproduced). 15.23.3 r2 'Argument-2 shall be an integer' is enforced nowhere: no compile-time screen (DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its guard) and no runtime check (CobolDate.DateToYyyymmdd validates only argument-1; the delegated YearToYyyy checks only r4 on argument-3 and the r6 sum). 15.3 type 6 requires 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item'; 15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when an argument value is incorrect. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe: `01 D8 PIC 9(8). 01 E6 PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE 851.00.` ... `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, E6, 2002) DISPLAY "EDITED-A2=" D8` prints EDITED-A2=27851003. PIC ZZ9.99 is category numeric-edited, i.e. CLASS ALPHANUMERIC per 8.5.2.1 Table 2 ('Numeric-edited (if usage is display)'), and it de-edits to 851.00, which is not an integer under either reading of r2; IntArg silently truncates it to 851, giving maximum-year 2853 and a fabricated year 2785. No diagnostic, no EC. Unlike r1 there is no half that is enforced at all. test-needed.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED. The omission default is the C# optional parameter `long off = 50` on CobolDate.DateToYyyymmdd, and the renderer's `case "DateToYyyymmdd" or "DayToYyyyddd" or "YearToYyyy"` arm emits ONLY the arguments actually written (`string.Join(", ", Enumerable.Range(0, ic.Args.Count).Select(i => IntArg(ic, i)))`), so an omitted argument-2 reaches 50 rather than a zero.
