DEFECT 1 -- r2a is OVER-APPLIED, so r2b is under-applied. 15.28.4 r2a (validated: cite.py --check 15.28.4 "has never been opened, attempted to be opened, or otherwise attempted to be accessed" -> OK) gives two spaces ONLY while the connector has never been opened, attempted to be opened, OR OTHERWISE ATTEMPTED TO BE ACCESSED; the statements that access a connector are named in 9.1.13.1 (validated: "The value of the I-O status is set during the execution of a CLOSE, DELETE, OPEN, READ, REWRITE, START, UNLOCK or WRITE"). The implementation gates r2a on FileConnector.EverAccessed, and I confirmed by grep that that flag is written in exactly TWO places in the whole tree -- FileConnector.Open and FileRegistry.DeleteFile -- so a CLOSE/READ/WRITE/START/REWRITE/DELETE/UNLOCK attempted on a never-opened connector sets that connector's I-O status but leaves EverAccessed false, and FileRegistry.ExceptionFile returns "  " where r2b requires status + SELECT-spelled name.
FAILING INPUT (re-run by me, verbatim output below):
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFEF1.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT Closed ASSIGN TO "refef1b.dat" FILE STATUS IS FS1.
           SELECT Readf  ASSIGN TO "refef1c.dat" FILE STATUS IS FS2.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD Closed.
       01 R2 PIC X(10).
       FD Readf.
       01 R3 PIC X(10).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 FS1 PIC XX.
       01 FS2 PIC XX.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           CLOSE Closed.
           DISPLAY "FS1=[" FS1 "]".
           READ Readf AT END CONTINUE END-READ.
           DISPLAY "FS2=[" FS2 "]".
           DISPLAY "EFC=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(Closed) "]".
           DISPLAY "EFR=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(Readf)  "]".
           STOP RUN.
ACTUAL:   FS1=[42] FS2=[47] EFC=[  ] EFR=[  ]
EXPECTED: FS1=[42] FS2=[47] EFC=[42Closed] EFR=[47Readf]
The two FILE STATUS values prove both connectors were attempted to be accessed and DO hold an I-O status, so r2a's condition is false for both and r2b governs. Root cause is the flag's DEFINITION, not the two call sites: EverAccessed belongs on the one status-setting path every connector operation passes through, not on a hand-maintained per-verb list that makes the next verb wrong by default.
DEFECT 2 (new, same rule, different half) -- r2b's returned NAME is wrong for the same two connector kinds as 15.28.4 r1c, because FileRegistry.ExceptionFile recovers the display name by the identical `LastIndexOf("::")` surgery on the runtime key. Ran and confirmed: an OO per-object instance file `SELECT OFile` gives `ARG=[10OFile#1]` (the MintInstanceKey `#N` counter leaks) where r2b requires `10OFile`; an EXTERNAL file `SELECT ExtF` / `FD ExtF IS EXTERNAL` gives `ARG=[10EXTF]` (DataBinder.cs uppercases ExternalName) where r2b requires `10ExtF`. So r2b fails on BOTH connector kinds even when EverAccessed is correctly true.
OPEN READING on r2b, unresolved and needing an owner eye (NOT scored as a third defect): the implementation reports the connector's CURRENT I-O status, while 15.28.1 frames the argument form as the status "associated with the last exception status for that file-name" (validated: cite.py --check 15.28.1 "associated with the last exception status for that file-name" -> OK). Discriminating run -- OPEN INPUT, READ to AT END, CLOSE, then interrogate -- gives NOARG=[10MyFile] but ARG=[00MyFile]. The current-status reading is what makes r2a/r2b total (r2a is exactly 'the connector has no I-O status yet' per 9.1.13.1) and the standard defines no per-file-name last exception status (14.6.13.1.1 defines ONE per run unit), so it cannot be settled from the rules alone. Note it does NOT rescue either defect above: in the DEFECT 1 input both readings yield 42Closed / 47Readf.
Test coverage: tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob exists on disk with its golden (INF=[10INF], UNU=[  ]) and is spec-derived, pinning r2b for an ordinary opened file and the never-touched leg of r2a. test-needed for the attempted-access leg (DEFECT 1) and for the EXTERNAL / per-object-instance naming leg (DEFECT 2).

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: The rule has TWO requirements and only the first is enforced. BindExceptionFileArg resolves argument-1 with `ctx.Data.Files.FirstOrDefault(f => f.CobolName.Equals(name, OrdinalIgnoreCase))` and issues COBOLNET1574 when nothing matches, so 'shall be the name of a file connector' is screened; 'that is specified in an FD statement' (ISO §15.29.3 rule 1) is NOT screened at all — the lookup filters on neither FileModel.IsSortMerge nor FileModel.HasFd, both of which the model already carries. TWO concrete illegal programs compile with NO diagnostic (run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe, default --std 2023; source at E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/40a0808e-7312-48f6-807b-5112b1d817cf/scratchpad/refute/r2.cob): (1) `SELECT SRTF ASSIGN TO "rfn002s.tmp".` + `SD SRTF.` + `01 RSRT PIC X(5).` then `DISPLAY "SD=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(SRTF) "]".` prints `SD=[  ]` — an SD (sort-merge file description entry, ISO §13.4.6) is not an FD statement, so §15.29.3 rule 1 is violated and must be diagnosed; (2) `SELECT NOFD ASSIGN TO "rfn002n.txt".` with NO FD and NO SD anywhere then `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(NOFD)` prints `NOFD=[  ]` — likewise undiagnosed, and note that FileModel.HasFd's own doc comment asserts 'a SELECT with no FD is an error the front-end already diagnoses', which this run shows is FALSE (the independent ISO §12.4.5.2 SR3 requirement — 'For each file-name specified in a SELECT clause, there shall be a file description entry or a sort-merge file description entry' — is also unenforced; that is a separate row, but it is why HasFd cannot be assumed true here). The fix is a filter on the ONE resolver: `f.HasFd && !f.IsSortMerge`. SIBLING: the same arm serves FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE (§15.28.3 rule 1) — sweep both. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME ARM: the COBOLNET1574 message hard-codes 'ISO §15.28.3 rule 1' for BOTH functions, so an EXCEPTION-FILE-N violation is handed the wrong clause (observed on r6.cob: `error COBOLNET1574: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N argument 'WS-ITEM' is not the name of a file connector specified in an FD statement (ISO 15.28.3 rule 1)`); for EXCEPTION-FILE-N the clause is §15.29.3 rule 1. The 'argument-1 is optional' half IS honoured (0-arg, empty-parens and 1-arg forms all accepted; 2 args rejected COBOLNET1504). EXCEPTION-FILE-N appears in neither IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified nor DeliberatelyUnscreened — behaviourally right (argument-1 is a file-connector-name, not a class-bearing operand, and BindExceptionFileArg returns before CheckArgumentClasses) but it leaves the PB1 drift test blind to this row; it belongs in DeliberatelyUnscreened with the §15.29.3 reason. test-needed: a negative spec-derived case for an SD argument-1, a negative case for a SELECT-without-FD argument-1, and a case pinning COBOLNET1574 with the §15.29.3 clause.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: OVERTURNS the CONFORMS. r1a and r1b are correct, but r1c is NOT: §15.29.4 r1c requires 'The succeeding characters contain the file-name exactly as specified in the SELECT clause converted at runtime to the runtime national character set' (cite.py-checked), and EcFunctions.File() does not carry that name — it DERIVES it from the runtime connector KEY by stripping everything up to the last '::' (`int sep = file.LastIndexOf("::"); string display = sep >= 0 ? file[(sep + 2)..] : file;`). That key is an emit-side namespace, and for two legal file kinds it is NOT the SELECT spelling. (1) An OBJECT-paragraph (per-instance) file connector: BinderDriver.QualifyClassFiles rewrites CobolName to `Class::INST::NAME` and FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey appends `"#" + N`, so the key is `OFCLS8::INST::OFILE#1` and the strip yields `OFILE#1`. Actually run (scratchpad/refute/r8.cob, --std 2023, a CLASS-ID with an OBJECT FILE-CONTROL `SELECT OFILE ASSIGN TO "rfn008.dat".`, two READs to end-of-file under >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON): observed `NOARG=[10OFILE#1]` with `LEN=009`; §15.29.4 r1c requires `10OFILE` with FUNCTION LENGTH 7. The returned value contains two characters ('#','1') that are not part of the file-name at all — '#' is not even in the COBOL word repertoire — so this is not a case quibble, and the length is wrong too. (2) An EXTERNAL file connector: BinderDriver rewrites CobolName to `"::EXT::" + ExternalName` where ExternalName is set in DataBinder.BindFileSection as `name.ToUpperInvariant()`, so the strip yields the UPPERCASED FD-derived externalized name (ISO §13.18.22.4 GR5), not the SELECT spelling. Actually run (scratchpad/refute/r7.cob): `SELECT MixedExtFile ASSIGN TO "rfn007.dat" FILE STATUS IS WS-FS.` + `FD MixedExtFile IS EXTERNAL.` gives `NOARG=[10MIXEDEXTFILE]`, `LEN=014`; r1c requires `10MixedExtFile`. That the ordinary case is right (scratchpad/refute/r1.cob: `SELECT MixedCaseVeryLongFileNameXY` + `FD MIXEDCASEVERYLONGFILENAMEXY` -> `FN=[10MixedCaseVeryLongFileNameXY]`, LEN=029, SELECT spelling preserved exactly) proves the intended reading and makes the EXTERNAL/OBJECT paths an inconsistency, not a design choice. ROOT CAUSE (one rule written in two places): the SELECT-spelled DISPLAY name is being recovered from the DISPATCH key, so every future key band ('::EXT::', '::INST::', '::FACT::', '::SORT::', the '#N' mint) silently corrupts a §15.28/§15.29 returned value. The structural fix is to carry the SELECT-spelled name as its own registry/connector field (set once from FileModel at registration) and delete both LastIndexOf('::') strips — one field, and the NEXT band is automatic. SIBLING: identical defect in §15.28.4 r1c (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE) through the same EcFunctions.File(), and in §15.29.4 r2b / §15.28.4 r2b through FileRegistry.ExceptionFile's own copy of the strip — sweep all four. VERIFIED-GOOD halves: r1a — EcFunctions.File() returns "00" when ExceptionState.LastName is null or !ExceptionCatalog.IsIoName(name) (StartsWith "EC-I-O"), projected national by CobolIntrinsics.NationalOf; golden tests/conformance/2002/exception_file_n.out shows `PRE=00` / `LEN-PRE=02`. r1b — ExceptionEngine.Set() nulls LastFile and only SetIo() sets it, so all three listed origins return two national spaces; I ran the EXIT leg myself (scratchpad/refute/r5.cob, `EXIT PROGRAM RAISING EXCEPTION EC-I-O-AT-END` in a nested program after a real status-10 READ: sub-program shows `SUB-EFN=[10TF]`, activator shows `AFTER-CALL=[  ]`, `LEN=002`, `ST=EC-I-O-AT-END`), and `GOBACK RAISING LAST EXCEPTION` correctly does NOT take the r1b path (scratchpad/refute/r3.cob -> `AFTER-CALL=[10TF]`, LEN=004 — the RAISING phrase specifies no exception-name, so r1c applies). The result category is national and lengths are counted in character positions (golden `NAT=YES` against N"10TF", `LEN-FN=04`). The cited conformance-test is spec-derived and exercises r1a + the ordinary r1c; it does not reach either divergent file kind, and r1b has no spec-derived test. test-needed: a 2023 case pinning EXCEPTION-FILE-N over an EXTERNAL file connector and over an OBJECT-paragraph file connector, plus an r1b case.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: BOTH halves of rule 2 diverge — the prior adjudication called r2b 'verified-good', and that is wrong. (A) r2a is over-broad. §15.29.4 r2a returns two national spaces only when the connector 'has never been opened, attempted to be opened, or otherwise attempted to be accessed' (cite.py-checked). FileConnector.EverAccessed — the ONLY flag FileRegistry.ExceptionFile tests — is written in exactly two places: FileConnector.Open and FileRegistry.DeleteFile. A READ / CLOSE / WRITE / START / REWRITE / DELETE against a never-opened connector IS an attempted access: ISO §9.1.13 makes those the very statements that set the connector's I-O status, so r2b must apply. Concrete failing input, actually run (scratchpad/phaseb3/t7.cob, --std 2023): `SELECT INF ASSIGN TO "efnacces.txt" FILE STATUS IS WS-FS.` + `FD INF.` + `READ INF AT END CONTINUE END-READ.` on a never-opened file -> `FS-AFTER-READ=47` but `EFN=[  ]`; then `CLOSE INF.` -> `FS-AFTER-CLOSE=42` but `EFN2=[  ]`. Expected per r2b: `EFN=[47INF]`, `EFN2=[42INF]` — the FILE STATUS item proves the I-O status was set, i.e. the connector was attempted to be accessed. Fix: set EverAccessed on every connector-touching verb, or better, derive it from 'the I-O status has ever been assigned' so the next verb is automatic. (B) r2b returns the WRONG file-name for two legal file kinds — the same root cause as §15.29.4 r1c. FileRegistry.ExceptionFile builds the name by `name.LastIndexOf("::")` over the runtime connector KEY, but that key is an emit-side namespace. Actually run: for an OBJECT-paragraph (per-instance) file (scratchpad/refute/r8.cob, `SELECT OFILE ...` inside an OBJECT paragraph) `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(OFILE)` returns `ARG=[10OFILE#1]` — the per-object mint suffix from FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey (`baseKey + "#" + N`) leaks into the returned value; r2b requires `10OFILE`. For an EXTERNAL file (scratchpad/refute/r7.cob, `SELECT MixedExtFile ...` + `FD MixedExtFile IS EXTERNAL.`) it returns `ARG=[10MIXEDEXTFILE]`, the uppercased ISO §13.18.22.4 GR5 externalized name, where r2b requires the SELECT spelling `10MixedExtFile`. The non-EXTERNAL, non-OO path IS correct (SELECT spelling preserved exactly, category national, length in character positions — tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob's alphanumeric twin shows `INF=[10INF]`), and r2a is correct for a purely SELECTed-never-touched connector (`UNU=[  ]`). SIBLING: both defects are shared verbatim with §15.28.4 r2a/r2b (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE) through the same FileRegistry.ExceptionFile — sweep both, and fold the r2b half into the ONE display-name fix described on RV-15.29.4-1. test-needed: there is NO spec-derived test for the EXCEPTION-FILE-N argument form at all (tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob is the alphanumeric EXCEPTION-FILE); a 2023 case is needed covering r2a (never accessed), r2a-vs-r2b (attempted-but-never-opened), r2b over an ordinary FD, r2b over an EXTERNAL FD and r2b over an OBJECT-paragraph file.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION function
notes:
OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. The prior CONFORMS was reached from a single-directive happy path. VERIFIED CORRECT FIRST: with one >>TURN and no LOCATION the returned value is exactly one alphanumeric space (FUNCTION LENGTH = 1), and - the half nobody checked - the rule's 'or PERFORM statement' leg is honoured too: a Format-3 `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-USER-L ... END-PERFORM` with no WITH LOCATION returns one space, and `PERFORM WITH LOCATION` returns the full string (EcBinder.ExceptionPerform's `savedTurn.WithImplicitEnable(overlay, withLocation, p.Start.Line)` carries SS14.9.28.4 GR14's 'If LOCATION is specified, that implicit TURN directive contains LOCATION' correctly).

THE DEFECT - the WITH LOCATION decision is per-STATEMENT, not per-exception-condition, so an unrelated directive leaks. SS15.30.3 r1 keys the choice on 'the TURN directive or PERFORM statement that enabled checking for THE EXCEPTION CONDITION ASSOCIATED WITH THE LAST EXCEPTION STATUS'; r2 likewise says 'the ASSOCIATED TURN directive'. EcBinder.EcWrap collapses that to ONE boolean - `bool withLoc = enabled.Any(e => ctx.EcState.Turn.WithLocation(e.Ec, e.File?.CobolName, line));` - and EcEmitter.EcStmtLoc keys the emitted (statement, location) pair on it, so ANY enabled condition at that statement carrying WITH LOCATION makes the location be saved for EVERY condition the statement can raise. TurnState.WithLocation already answers the question per (name, file); the answer is simply thrown away at the wrap site.

Ran (E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/40a0808e-7312-48f6-807b-5112b1d817cf/scratchpad/phaseb3/ref/r2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       >>TURN EC-OVERFLOW-STRING CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFR2.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-T PIC X(4).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           STRING "ABCDEFGH" DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-T.
           DISPLAY "S=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           DISPLAY "T=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT "]".
           STOP RUN.
The last exception status is EC-OVERFLOW-STRING (S=[EC-OVERFLOW-STRING ...]), whose enabling directive has NO LOCATION option, and this implementation's documented SS7.3.25.4 GR7 choice is to save nothing (docs/COBOLNET_CONDITIONS_EXCEPTIONS_DESIGN.md: 'without the LOCATION phrase this implementation saves NO location information - EXCEPTION-LOCATION returns one space, EXCEPTION-STATEMENT 63 spaces'). EXPECTED 'L=[ ]' (r1); ACTUAL 'L=[REFR2; MAIN-PARA; 10]'. CONTROL (ref/r3.cob - byte-identical but with the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT directive removed) gives 'L=[ ]', which isolates the leak to the unrelated directive. The behaviour therefore contradicts the implementor's own specified GR7 answer, which Annex-D implementor-defined item 204 ('TURN directive - whether location information is available when the LOCATION phrase is not specified ... shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') requires to be stated and honoured; item 139 is the identical requirement for the PERFORM leg.

SIBLING DEFECT, SAME ROOT AND SAME LINE OF CODE: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT returns 'T=[STRING...]' on the same run where SS15.32.3 r1 requires 63 spaces - worth its own queue row.

FIX SHAPE (rule 5): EcStatementInfo should carry the WITH LOCATION decision PER enabled (name, file) pair - the data is already there in the `enabled` list - and EcEmitter should select the pair matching the name it is about to Set(), rather than one whole-statement flag. That also makes the EXCEPTION-STATEMENT sibling correct automatically.

test-needed: the cited test exists (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.cs line 214) and is spec-derived, but it pins only the single-directive path; there is no test for two directives of differing LOCATION at one statement, and none for the 'or PERFORM statement' leg of r1.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION function
notes:
VERDICT SURVIVES; one root-cause claim CORRECTED and a FIFTH defect added. Re-verified correct: r2a (no exception raised, or after SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF -> one space, FUNCTION LENGTH = 1); the string is genuinely variable-length (LENGTH = 20 for 'REFZ1; MAIN-PARA; 13') and behaves as an ordinary alphanumeric sending operand under both a wide (PIC X(50), space-filled) and a narrow (PIC X(5), truncated) receiver; r2b part 1 for a PROGRAM-ID; and - not checked before - r2b part 1's SECOND SENTENCE, the propagated case: a nested PROGRAM-ID REFP1SUB raising EC-USER-L and returning by plain GOBACK reports 'L=[REFP1SUB; SUB-PARA; 14]' in the activator, i.e. the element in which the condition actually occurred (ref/p1.cob). r2b part 2b (paragraph alone, and paragraph + ' OF ' + section) is correct.

FIVE DEFECTS, all reachable from EcBinder.EcLocation and its inputs:

(1) r2b part 2a - 'If there is no paragraph-name or section-name in the source element, a semicolon and a space character are appended.' EcLocation reads `ctx.Table.Paragraphs[ctx.BindCursor].Cobol` unconditionally and ProcedureTableBuilder.AddAnonymousParagraph names the SS14.4.3 paragraph-name-OMITTED paragraph '(sentences without a paragraph-name)', so that internal display label leaks into the returned value. Ran (ref/e2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE2.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "M=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
EXPECTED 'M=[REFE2; ; 5]'; ACTUAL 'M=[REFE2; (sentences without a paragraph-name); 5]'.

(2) r2b part 2c - 'If there is a section-name and no paragraph-name, the section-name is appended followed by a semicolon and a space character.' Ran (ref/e3.cob), a section header followed directly by unnamed sentences:
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE3.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       ONLY-SECT SECTION.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
EXPECTED 'L=[REFE3; ONLY-SECT; 6]'; ACTUAL 'L=[REFE3; (sentences without a paragraph-name) OF ONLY-SECT; 6]'.

(3) NEW - and it CORRECTS the earlier claim that the 2c branch 'is unreachable'. The 2c branch IS reachable; it is simply keyed on the wrong predicate. EcLocation selects it with the heuristic `sec is not null && para.Equals(sec, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`, which fires whenever a real paragraph happens to be NAMED the same as its containing section - legal COBOL (SS8.4.2.2 SR7 bars a duplicate paragraph-name only WITHIN a section; nothing bars a paragraph-name equal to a section-name, and the paragraph here is never explicitly referenced). Ran (ref/e1.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE1.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       ONLY-SECT SECTION.
       ONLY-SECT.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
There IS a paragraph-name, so r2b part 2b applies and the section-name must be appended prefixed by ' OF '. EXPECTED 'L=[REFE1; ONLY-SECT OF ONLY-SECT; 7]'; ACTUAL 'L=[REFE1; ONLY-SECT; 7]' - the required ' OF ' + section-name is silently dropped. So the ONE heuristic is wrong in BOTH directions: it never fires where 2c is required and it fires where 2b is required. The structural fix (rule 5) is to make the anonymous paragraph carry an explicit 'no paragraph-name' FLAG on the procedure table instead of a display label, and to select 2a/2b/2c from that flag plus the section, deleting the name-comparison heuristic entirely.

(4) r2b part 1 for a METHOD. 'The name of the runtime element as specified in the FUNCTION-ID, METHOD-ID, or PROGRAM-ID paragraph of the ... method ... containing the statement' (a method is a runtime element, SS10.5). Verified by reading: OoDriver.BindClassBody calls `binder.ConfigureEc(session.Turn, cls.Name)` for the whole method roster (and again for the factory roster), EcBinder.ConfigureEc stores it in `ctx.EcState.ProgramName`, and grep shows EcState.ProgramName is assigned in exactly ONE place - so no method can ever supply its own METHOD-ID name. A CLASS-ID MyCls containing METHOD-ID DoIt whose M-PARA raises reports 'L=[MyCls; M-PARA; 9]' where r2b part 1 requires 'L=[DoIt; M-PARA; 9]'.

(5) The GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING path captures NO location at all under WITH LOCATION. Verified by reading and by running. `public sealed record BoundRaising(string? EcName, bool IsLast, bool Fatal, bool Enabled, Place? ObjectSource = null)` has no WithLocation/Location member - unlike BoundRaise and BoundEcChecked - and ExceptionState.SetPropagating(name, fatal) calls `Set(name, fatal)`, the two-argument overload that leaves LastLocation null. Ran (ref/p2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFP2.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           CALL "REFP2SUB".
           DISPLAY "S=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           DISPLAY "T=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT "]".
           STOP RUN.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFP2SUB.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION RAISING EC-USER-L.
       SUB-PARA.
           GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
       END PROGRAM REFP2SUB.
       END PROGRAM REFP2.
ACTUAL 'S=[EC-USER-L ...]' (so the last exception status DOES indicate a raised condition and r2a does not apply) but 'L=[ ]'; EXPECTED 'L=[REFP2SUB; SUB-PARA; 15]'. SS7.3.25.4 GR6 puts the file-level >>TURN in scope for the nested program's statements and GR7 then requires the information to be made available. Sibling on the same path: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT is 63 spaces (SS15.32.3 r2).

A SIXTH way to get a wrong r2 result comes from RV-15.30.3-1's per-statement WITH LOCATION collapse: an r2b-shaped string is produced for a condition whose own enabling directive specified no LOCATION, where neither r2 nor r1's save branch licenses one.

test-needed. The cited test exists on disk (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.cs line 194) and is spec-derived, but it asserts only `Assert.Contains("LOC: ECT010; MAIN-PARA;")` - the r2b 1 + 2b happy path. Untested: r2b 2a, 2b with a paragraph inside a section named like it, 2c, the METHOD-ID and FUNCTION-ID element names, the propagated-name sentence, and the GOBACK/EXIT ... RAISING path.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION function
notes:
OVERTURNED from PARTIAL, and the PARTIAL's principal ground WITHDRAWN as unsound. test-needed.

VERIFIED CORRECT: the identifier IS appended as the third part on every path that builds a location string, and it names the line containing the BEGINNING of the statement, not the enclosing construct - a RAISE, an ambient-EC path, a Format-3 PERFORM WITH LOCATION (ref/q1.cob reports the RAISE's own line 6, not the PERFORM's line 5), and a statement whose verb begins on a later line than its enclosing IF. Directive lines are counted, so in a COPY-free unit the number equals the source line.

WITHDRAWN GROUND (the prior report's edge (a)). The post-COPY ordinal is NOT a divergence and must not hold this row open on its own. I reproduced it (ref/c1.cob: a 9-line unit whose 3-line copybook precedes a RAISE on source line 7 reports 'L=[REFC1; MAIN-PARA; 12]'), but (i) the identifier is expressly implementor-DEFINED, (ii) SS7.2's COPY makes the copied library text part of the resulting source text, so an ordinal into that text does identify a line of it, and (iii) I searched the implementor-defined-items annex mechanically: it carries item 139 (PERFORM) and item 204 (TURN directive), both only for 'whether location information is available when the LOCATION phrase is not specified' - there is NO required item, and no 'shall be documented' obligation anywhere, for the FORM of this line identifier. The earlier 'the latitude is unclaimed' argument therefore does not stand.

THE ACTUAL DIVERGENCE: on the GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING path the implementor-defined identifier is not appended at all, because no location string is built. Ran ref/p2.cob (reproduced verbatim in the RV-15.30.3-2 notes): under a file-level `>>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION`, a nested REFP2SUB executing `GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-USER-L` leaves 'S=[EC-USER-L ...]' - the last exception status indicates a raised condition, so SS15.30.3 r2b governs and r2b part 3 requires the identifier - yet 'L=[ ]'. EXPECTED 'L=[REFP2SUB; SUB-PARA; 15]'. The rule is unsatisfied on a real, runnable, legal input, which is DIVERGES, not PARTIAL; the shared root with RV-15.30.3-2 defect 5 is that BoundRaising carries no location member and ExceptionState.SetPropagating stores none. Fixing r2 defect 5 discharges this row too - keep both rows so neither closes on the other's fix.

test-needed: no spec-derived test asserts part 3 at all. ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.WithLocation_CapturesStatementAndLocation (verified on disk, line 194) asserts `Assert.Contains("LOC: ECT010; MAIN-PARA;")`, stopping at the semicolon BEFORE the line identifier, so the whole of rule 3 is unpinned; a covering test must assert the concatenated third part and must include the GOBACK ... RAISING path.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:
OVERTURNS the prior CONFORMS -- reached from the happy path only. Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.31.3 "the returned value is one national space character" -> OK 15.31.3 1); 7.3.25.4 "If the LOCATION phrase is not specified, the implementor shall specify" -> OK GR7.

Rule 1's antecedent is a property OF THE CONDITION: "the LOCATION option of the TURN directive or PERFORM statement that ENABLED CHECKING FOR THE EXCEPTION CONDITION ASSOCIATED WITH THE LAST EXCEPTION STATUS is not specified". The implementation makes it a property of the STATEMENT: EcBinder.EcWrap computes `bool withLoc = enabled.Any(e => ctx.EcState.Turn.WithLocation(e.Ec, e.File?.CobolName, line));` -- ANY over every EC enabled at that statement -- and EcEmitter.EcStmtLoc then bakes the location literals into the raise site for WHICHEVER condition actually fires. So a condition whose own enabling TURN had NO LOCATION gets a full location string as soon as some UNRELATED condition at the same statement was turned on WITH LOCATION.

RAN, two programs differing by ONE directive line (cobol.exe --run):
BASELINE m3.cob
       >>TURN EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELNM3.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 R PIC 9(2).
       01 L PIC 9(3).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           COMPUTE R = 99 + 99
               ON SIZE ERROR CONTINUE
           END-COMPUTE.
           DISPLAY "S=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           MOVE FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N) TO L.
           DISPLAY "LEN=" L.
           STOP RUN.
Got   S=[EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION ...]  LEN=001   <- CORRECT (r1: one national space)

MIXED m4.cob = the same program with ONE extra directive after the first:
       >>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
Got   S=[EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION ...]  LEN=021  and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION = "RELNM4; MAIN-PARA; 12"
Spec  LEN=001 -- the raised condition is still EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, whose enabling TURN carries no LOCATION option, and this implementation's DOCUMENTED 15.30.3/15.31.3 r1 choice is to save no location information without it. EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT was never raised and is irrelevant to the last exception status.

Why this is a rule-1 defect and not merely untidy: 7.3.25.4 GR7 second sentence requires the implementor to SPECIFY (one answer, and Annex conformance item 204 makes documenting it REQUIRED) whether the information is made available when LOCATION is absent. This implementation answers BOTH ways depending on an unrelated co-enabled exception-name at the same statement, so no documented implementor choice can describe it; and under the choice it does document ("saves none" -- the wording in EcFunctions.Location's XML doc, in ExceptionEngine.LastLocation's, and in the tests/conformance/2002/exception_file_n.cob header) the m4 answer is simply wrong.

FIX SHAPE (rule 5, not the smallest diff): the (statement -> one WithLocation bool + one Location literal) pair has to become per-CONDITION, because EcStatementInfo already carries the per-(name,file) Enabled list -- the raise sites that select an EC by name at run time (EmitArgOrPlain's `__af.EcName`, EmitSizeHandling's `ecnVar`, __IoCheckEc's `__ec`) must select the location operands by that same name rather than from one statement-wide literal pair.

SIBLING SWEEP: identical defect in FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION (15.30.3 r1 -- the m4 run above IS that twin, "A=[RELNM4; MAIN-PARA; 12]" where one space is required) and in FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT (15.32.3 r1 requires 63 spaces; the same EcStmtLoc pair supplies the statement name).

What DOES conform and was re-verified: EcFunctions.LocationN() = NationalOf(Location()) returns NationalOf(" ") -- one national space -- whenever LastLocation is null, which is every no-LOCATION-anywhere case; the two cited spec-derived tests both exist on disk and both pin that simple case (exception_file_n.cob LEN-LN=01 under `>>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON`, and the xunit twin asserting L2 = 1), so they hold r1's happy path. NEITHER covers the mixed case -- test-needed for it.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:
UPHELD as DIVERGES; I reproduced all three of the prior report's failures myself and found a FOURTH, independent root cause. test-needed. Citations validated: cite.py --check 15.31.3 "If the LOCATION option of the associated TURN directive or PERFORM statement was specified" -> OK 2); "If there is a section-name and no paragraph-name" -> OK 2) b) 2. c.; "In the case of a propagated exception condition" -> OK 2) b) 1.

r2 a) IS correct (LocationN returns NationalOf(" ") when LastName is null). r2 b) fails four ways.

(1) r2 b) 2. a) "If there is no paragraph-name or section-name in the source element, a semicolon and a space character are appended" -- the procedure field must be EMPTY. RAN:
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELNP1.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "N=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N "]".
           STOP RUN.
Got   N=[RELNP1; (sentences without a paragraph-name); 5]
Spec  N=[RELNP1; ; 5]

(2) r2 b) 2. c) "If there is a section-name and no paragraph-name, the section-name is appended followed by a semicolon and a space character." Same program with `MAIN SECTION.` before the RAISE (RELNP2):
Got   N=[RELNP2; (sentences without a paragraph-name) OF MAIN; 6]
Spec  N=[RELNP2; MAIN; 6]

(3) r2 b) 1. second sentence "In the case of a propagated exception condition, the name is that of the function, method, or program in which the exception condition that was propagated actually occurred." RAN RELNP3 calling contained RELNP3S whose `PROCEDURE DIVISION RAISING EC-USER-P.` / `SUB-PARA. GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-USER-P.` propagates:
Got   N=[ ]  while  S=[EC-USER-P ...]  -- an exception condition WAS raised and the enabling TURN DID carry LOCATION, so neither r1 nor r2 a) can apply.
Spec  N=[RELNP3S; SUB-PARA; 14]
CAUSE: ExceptionEngine.SetPropagating(name, fatal) calls Set(name, fatal) with the `statement` and `location` parameters DEFAULTED TO NULL.

(4) NEW -- the NONFATAL ambient EC gates never carry location at all. EcEmitter.EmitChecked wraps them in a bare set/reset with NO catch (correct -- nonfatal never throws), so the only writer is the runtime helper, and ExceptionEngine.BoundOverflowError / DataConversionError call `Set(name, fatal)` with statement/location defaulted null. RAN:
       >>TURN EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELNQ1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 WS-TABLE.
          05 WS-E PIC 9(3) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN WS-CAP FROM 2 TO 4.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           MOVE 7 TO WS-E (9).
           DISPLAY "S=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           DISPLAY "N=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N "]".
           STOP RUN.
Got   S=[EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW ...]   N=[ ]
Spec  N=[RELNQ1; MAIN-PARA; 10] -- LOCATION was specified and the condition was raised, so r2 b) governs. Same hole for EC-DATA-CONVERSION (15.19.4 r1/r3), the other entry in EcEmitter.NonfatalAmbientGates.

(5) READ FROM CODE, NOT RUN: r2 b) 1. requires "the name of the runtime element as specified in the FUNCTION-ID, METHOD-ID, or PROGRAM-ID paragraph". OoDriver.BindClassBody calls `binder.ConfigureEc(session.Turn, cls.Name)` for both method rosters, so EcBinder.EcLocation's `ctx.EcState.ProgramName` is the CLASS-ID for a statement inside a METHOD, never its METHOD-ID.

ROOT CAUSES, and they are four separate ones: (1)+(2) are one defect -- ProcedureTableBuilder.AddAnonymousParagraph stores the DISPLAY placeholder "(sentences without a paragraph-name)" as a paragraph NAME, and EcBinder.EcLocation has no branch for the three r2 b) 2. cases (its only special case is `para.Equals(sec)`, which the placeholder never satisfies); the fix is for the anonymous pc to carry a null/empty name and for EcLocation to render a. / b. / c. explicitly. (3) and (4) are the same SHAPE -- a raise path that calls Set() without the location operands -- but different sites. (5) is a name-source defect.

SIBLING SWEEP: every one of these is shared verbatim with the alphanumeric twin FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION (15.30.3 r2 -- confirmed in the same runs, e.g. RELNQ1 printed A=[ ] too), and (3)/(4) equally break FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT (15.32.3 r2 -- the statement name is lost on the same paths).

NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST covers this rule: nothing exercises EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N under WITH LOCATION at all. The only WITH LOCATION test on disk, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.cs#WithLocation_CapturesStatementAndLocation, uses the ALPHANUMERIC twin and covers only case b) (paragraph in no section).

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:
DOWNGRADED from CONFORMS to PARTIAL -- one half verified, the other is an unrecorded implementor choice that a run shows is NOT the source line. test-needed. Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.31.3 "An implementor-defined identifier of the source line that contains the beginning of the statement" -> OK 15.31.3 2) b) 2. (a transcription indentation artifact prints the printed part 3 as a sub-item of 2.).

VERIFIED HALF -- "the BEGINNING of the statement", and "is THEN APPENDED" (last, after the procedure part). EcBinder.EcWrap takes `int line = s.Start.Line` and BindRaise takes the RAISE context's Start.Line, so it is the statement's FIRST token, and EcLocation appends it last: `$"{ctx.EcState.ProgramName}; {proc}; {line}"`. Re-verified by run on a three-line COMPUTE beginning on source line 12 -> "RELNM4; MAIN-PARA; 12" (not the ON SIZE ERROR line, not END-COMPUTE).

UNVERIFIED/DIVERGENT HALF -- "an identifier of THE SOURCE LINE". The number appended is the POST-EXPANSION preprocessed-text ordinal, not the source line. RAN:
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELNC1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY "CPYA.cpy".
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "N=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N "]".
           STOP RUN.
with CPYA.cpy = three 01-level lines. The RAISE is on SOURCE line 9; got N=[RELNC1; MAIN-PARA; 14] -- and the source file has only 11 lines, so 14 names no line of it. The identifier IS expressly implementor-defined and the clause's NOTE disclaims cross-compilation stability, so the choice is arguably inside the granted latitude (post-COPY resultant text is what is compiled); it is NOT a decided divergence. But it is an owner-visible implementor choice that (a) no design doc or user documentation records, and (b) no test pins, so this row must not be closed as CONFORMS.

DEPENDENCY, not a defect of this rule: part 3 is only reachable when the r2 b) string is produced at all, and it is produced WRONGLY or not at all in five cases -- RV-15.31.3-2 (1)(2)(3)(4)(5) -- and produced where it must NOT be at all in the RV-15.31.3-1 mixed-TURN case, where the line identifier is appended to a string that rule 1 says shall be a single national space.

No spec-derived test asserts the line identifier: ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.WithLocation_CapturesStatementAndLocation asserts only the prefix "LOC: ECT010; MAIN-PARA;" and stops BEFORE it, and it exercises the alphanumeric twin, not -N.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. Citation re-validated (--check 15.32.3 'the returned value is 63 spaces' -> OK 15.32.3 rule 1). The adjudicator sampled the SINGLE-TURN path (which is right) and never read the quantifier. r1's antecedent is per-CONDITION: 'the LOCATION option of the TURN directive ... that enabled checking for THE exception condition associated with the last exception status'. TurnState.WithLocation(level3, file, line) is correctly per-condition (its own doc comment says 'Did the event that ENABLED level3 at this statement carry WITH LOCATION'), but EcBinder.EcWrap COLLAPSES it: `bool withLoc = enabled.Any(e => ctx.EcState.Turn.WithLocation(e.Ec, e.File?.CobolName, line));` -- ONE bool for the whole statement, stored in EcStatementInfo.WithLocation and consumed by EcEmitter.EcStmtLoc for EVERY condition the statement guards. So when a statement has two conditions enabled and only ONE carries WITH LOCATION, a raise of the OTHER one is recorded WITH the statement name and location. The documented implementor choice under 7.3.25.4 GR7 (--check 7.3.25.4 'all information necessary to identify a source statement for the EXCEPTION-LOCATION' -> OK; docs/COBOLNET_CONDITIONS_EXCEPTIONS_DESIGN.md 'WITH LOCATION (15.30.3 r1 choice)': 'without the LOCATION phrase this implementation saves NO location information') makes r1's second conjunct hold, so 63 spaces is REQUIRED and the name is returned instead. Reachability confirmed at TurnState.Fold: two independent >>TURN directives for two different level-3 names keep independent WithLocation flags; the ambient tail gates in EcWrap (EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT / EC-BOUND-ODO / EC-BOUND-REF-MOD / EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE / ...) are added to `enabled` on EVERY statement in a checking region, so one stray `WITH LOCATION` directive anywhere in the program contaminates every other condition's r1 answer. REPRO in defects. The RAISE path is NOT affected (BoundRaise carries its own per-condition WithLocation from EcBinder), which is exactly why the cited spec-derived test WithoutLocation_StatementAndLocationAreSpaces is green: it is a single-EC-USER RAISE and pins the uniform case only. Corroboration, not closure -- test-ref left empty. EcFunctions.Statement itself is correct (`new string(' ', 63)`); the wrong ANSWER is manufactured upstream. Unconstrained-not-charged: an exception-OBJECT status (ExceptionState.SetObject nulls LastStatement) also yields 63 spaces -- 15.32.3 states no rule for that state.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES, and the site inventory is INCOMPLETE -- I found one more, and it is structural rather than a forgotten argument. Citation re-validated (--check 15.32.3 '63-character alphanumeric character-string that is the name of the statement' -> OK rule 2). I independently verified each claimed site by reading it: ControlFlowEmitter#EmitSearchScan emits the bare `ExceptionState.Set("EC-RANGE-SEARCH-...", false)`; CobolTiming.cs, CobolDynString.cs (two calls) and CobolString.cs (three ThruMember calls) all use the 2-arg Set; ExceptionEngine.DataConversionError and BoundOverflowError both call `Set(name, fatal:false)` with no pair, and EcEmitter.EmitChecked wraps those two NONFATAL gates in a bare try/finally with no catch that could re-set the status; CallEmitter's activator-side EC-OO-EXCEPTION is likewise 2-arg. The 7 threading sites (EcEmitter.EmitArgOrPlain / EmitRaise / EmitSizeHandling / EmitOverflow, the __IoCheckEc bridge, CallEmitter.EmitProgramEcCatch, PtrEmitter -- actually TWO PtrEmitter calls, EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND and EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC) are confirmed. NEW SITE THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED: GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING exception-name-1. CallEmitter emits `ExceptionState.SetPropagating(name, fatal)`, and ExceptionEngine.SetPropagating calls `Set(name, fatal)` -- statement and location null. This is not an omitted argument: the bound record `BoundRaising(string? EcName, bool IsLast, bool Fatal, bool Enabled, Place? ObjectSource)` has NO WithLocation and NO Location fields at all, unlike its sibling BoundRaise which has both. So under `>>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION`, `GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-USER-X` yields 63 spaces where r2+r3 require 'GOBACK' (Table 12 lists GOBACK) and EXCEPTION-LOCATION yields one space -- and no amount of argument-passing fixes it without changing the record. That makes the rule-5 ambient-channel restructuring the adjudicator proposed the only workable shape, not merely the preferred one. The FORMATTING half of r2 is correct (`LastStatement.ToUpperInvariant().PadRight(63)[..63]`) but has NO spec-derived test: WithLocation_CapturesStatementAndLocation asserts with Contains and never pins the 63-character space-fill. Also falsifies the design SSOT's claim that 'with it ... the uppercase statement name [is] recorded at the raise site'.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES on independent evidence. Citation re-validated (--check 15.32.3 'The names of the statements are given in Table 12' -> OK rule 3). I read Table 12 in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 14.5.1 rather than trusting the adjudicator's summary: 50 rows, and `GO TO` is indeed the ONLY multi-word 'Statement name' (verified against the canonical PDF text layer as well). EcBinder.EcWrap takes `Core.StatementContext s` and sets StatementName from `s.Start.Text.ToUpperInvariant()`; CobolControlFlow.g4 has `goToStatement : GO TO? procedureName? (procedureName)* (DEPENDING ON? dataReference)?`, so the first token is GO and the function reports 'GO'. I also walked EVERY alternative of the `statement` rule head-token by head-token to test the adjudicator's 'wrong for exactly one' claim: it holds for the raise-capable set. searchAllStatement -> SEARCH, deleteFileStatement -> DELETE, exitStatement -> EXIT, stopStatement -> STOP, and the four Wave-H facility arms (RECEIVE/SEND/VALIDATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) all coincide with their Table-12 rows. The non-Table-12 heads are alterStatement/entryStatement/enterStatement/useStatement/nextSentenceStatement (which report ALTER/ENTRY/ENTER/USE/NEXT, none of them Table-12 names) and the 2023 `inlineMethodInvocationStatement : dataReference LPAREN argumentList? RPAREN`, which would report the RECEIVER identifier -- currently unreachable because BindStatementCore has no arm for it, so latent, not charged. NEXT SENTENCE is additionally reachable-and-wrappable today: EcWrap's ambient tail gates attach to ANY statement in a checking region, so a >>TURN ... WITH LOCATION region containing NEXT SENTENCE can stamp the non-Table-12 name 'NEXT'. The rule-5 fix shape stands: a Table-12-derived statement-name map keyed by bound-node kind (or parse-rule index) plus a drift test asserting every mapped name is a Table-12 row. Patching GO TO alone leaves the first-token heuristic in place.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATUS function
notes:
OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator verified the RENDERING of the returned value exhaustively and correctly. What was never exercised is the other half of the same sentence — the VALUE DOMAIN. 15.33.3 r1 says the string IS "the exception-name"; the compiler cannot represent an entire family of exception-names the standard defines, and it silently truncates another.

WHAT WAS MISSED #1 — THE UNDERSCORE FAMILY IS UNREACHABLE (rejects legal COBOL). §14.6.13.1.1 (validated: cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.1 "The level-3 exception-names for user-defined exceptions shall start with the characters 'EC-USER-' and end with a suffix containing only characters selected from the set of basic letters, basic digits, and the hyphen and underscore basic special characters." -> OK) EXPLICITLY names the underscore, and §8.3.2.1 (validated: cite.py --check 8.3.2.1 "Each character of a COBOL word that is not a special character word shall be selected from the set of basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore." -> OK) permits it in ANY COBOL word from 2002. MEASURED (--std 2023, prebuilt cobol.exe): `RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-A_B.` -> error COBOL0001 "no viable alternative at input '_'". So a legal level-3 exception-name can never be raised, never reach the last exception status, and can never be the value this rule returns. Every one of the adjudicator's five raise origins used a HYPHENATED name, which is exactly why the hole was invisible. ROOT CAUSE READ FROM THE GRAMMAR, not inferred: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 `fragment NAME_BODY` is `[a-z] [a-z0-9-]* [a-z0-9]` (and the two digit-start arms) — the underscore is in NO alternative. It is general (`01 WS_A PIC X(5)` fails the same way), so this is a lexer-wide 2002+ conformance hole that this rule INHERITS.

WHAT WAS MISSED #2 — THE >31 TRUNCATION IS SILENT *AND UNDOCUMENTED*. The implementation is one expression: EcFunctions.Status() = (ExceptionState.LastName ?? "").PadRight(31)[..31]. The adjudicator found the truncation and dismissed it as "the standard's conflict, not the implementation's — the width wins". The ANSWER may well be right, but I grepped docs/ for any record of the choice and there is NONE (no "31-character"/"PadRight(31)" note in any design doc, deep-dive or user documentation). A 44-character EC-USER name at --std 2023 returns `EC-USER-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVW` with no diagnostic, and two distinct names sharing a 31-character prefix become INDISTINGUISHABLE through this function. An undocumented silent truncation is not a closed row; it is at minimum an owner-visible implementor choice that must be written down before the row closes.

WHAT I RE-RAN AND CONFIRMS THE ADJUDICATOR (corroboration, not closure): width 31 before any raise and after a raise (FUNCTION LENGTH -> 0031); left-justification and space fill (`[EC-USER-DEMO` + 19 spaces `]`, MOVE to PIC X(40) -> name + 28 spaces); uppercase from lower/mixed-case source (`raise exception ec-user-Mixed-Case` -> EC-USER-MIXED-CASE); all three no-exception states -> 31 spaces; padding-aware comparison (`IF FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS = "EC-USER-DEMO"` is TRUE); ref-mod (1:12) equal, and the out-of-range edges (30:5)/(40:2)/(31:1) return the documented lenient space-pad rather than crashing. Re-ran the WHOLE probe at --std 2002, 2014 and 2023 with byte-identical output, and confirmed --std 85 rejects. Additional origins I checked that the adjudicator did not: a LEVEL-2 USE selector reporting the LEVEL-3 name (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-BOUND over a subscript violation -> `[EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT ...]` both inside the declarative and after); EC-I-O-AT-END BOTH with the AT END phrase present (declarative correctly not run, register still set) and absent (declarative runs, `DECL=[EC-I-O-AT-END ...]`); a Format-3 PERFORM WHEN (`WHEN=[EC-USER-PF ...]`); and run-unit scope in the CALLER->CALLEE direction (a raise in the caller is visible inside the contained program and after it) — the adjudicator only tested callee->caller.

A LEADING HYPOTHESIS I CHASED AND CLEARED — recorded so nobody re-files it. I audited every write to the register: ExceptionEngine.Set / SetIo / SetObject / Clear are the ONLY assignments to LastName anywhere in src/, so the ToUpperInvariant normalization cannot be bypassed by a raise site that forgot to fold. I then audited the inverse bug (a register write with NO checking gate, which would make EXCEPTION-STATUS report a condition §14.6.13.1.1 says was never raised): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Text/CobolString.cs#ThruMember sets EC-RANGE-INVALID in all three overloads with NO runtime checking test — but the emission site (ConditionRenderer's RenderMembershipTest / BoundRangeMembership) is COMPILE-TIME gated on checkRangeInvalid, so the unguarded Set is unreachable with checking off. CobolTiming (EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO) and CobolDynString (EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL) are gated at the call. No corrupt-register path found.

test-ref lists SPEC-DERIVED tests only. All three use AssertSpec with expected values derived from the cited rules (the EC model has no legacy oracle — COBOL-2002+) and all three BRACKET the operand, so CutRunner.Normalize's trailing-space trim cannot hide the padding: together they pin the 31-space no-exception arm exactly, in three distinct ways of meaning "no exception". They do NOT pin the NAME arm's padding, the uppercase normalization, or the EXCEPTION-OBJECT arm. Corroboration only, not counted: tests/conformance/2002/oo_ec_raise_object.out carries `BASE-HANDLER EXCEPTION-OBJECT` padded to 31, but that corpus documents trailing whitespace as ignored.

test-needed to reach CONFORMS: the underscore family must first be REPRESENTABLE (a spec-derived case raising EC-USER-A_B and asserting the returned name); the >31 choice must be documented (or the row raised to the owner); plus a bracketed NAME-arm padding case, an uppercase-normalization case, and an EXCEPTION-OBJECT-arm case.

subject: EXP function
notes: CONFIRMED as DIVERGES; three corrections to the reasoning, one of which changes the FIX. §15.34.3 r1 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric." is --check verified and is UNENFORCED for EXP: re-read of IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs shows EXP in neither `Verified` nor `DeliberatelyUnscreened`, and IntrinsicBinder#CheckArgumentClasses returns at `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;`. Independently confirmed that nothing else catches it: ExpressionBinder#OperandRef's DA6 §8.8.1.1 screen (COBOLNET0844) is guarded by `context is OperandContext.Arithmetic`, and an intrinsic argument binds through BindArgOperand → `host.Expr.BindFunctionArgumentExpr(...)` = OperandContext.FunctionArgument. CORRECTION 1 — WRONG CODE PATH NAMED, and it would have sent the fix to the wrong file. A numeric-edited argument does NOT reach NumericRenderer#FieldNumCore; that method's numeric-edited arm is a LOUD staged-out value. A float-family intrinsic renders each argument via IntrinsicRenderer#Dbl → NumericRenderer.Real(num.AsNum(...)), i.e. the INSTANCE NumericRenderer#FieldNum, whose numeric-edited arm is `CobolEdit.DeEdit`. Only the ALPHANUMERIC / NATIONAL / ref-modified shapes decode through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric. The reported OUTCOMES are right; the cited path was not. CORRECTION 2 — THE PROPOSED ONE-LINE FIX IS PARTIAL, NOT A CLOSURE, and the row must not be closed on it. IntrinsicArgumentRules#ClassOf maps `BoundComputedOperand => CobolClass.Numeric` for anything that is not a nested intrinsic call, so even after `["EXP"] = ('n', "§15.34.3 r1")` lands, `FUNCTION EXP((A))` and `FUNCTION EXP(A + 0)` over `A PIC X(4)` stay silently unscreened — only the BARE data-reference shape (which OperandOf maps `BoundNumRef → BoundFieldOperand`) is screened. That is the documented fail-open, but it means the rule remains half-enforced after the fix and the queue entry should say so. CORRECTION 3 — the class/category argument is sound and I re-verified §8.5.2.1's closing sentence with --check, so numeric-edited (Table 2 class ALPHANUMERIC under usage display) is genuinely inadmissible under a CLASS-NUMERIC rule; note this is the 'n' vs 'i' distinction the table already encodes, and EXP is squarely 'n' because §15.34.3 r1 names the CLASS, not §15.3's integer type. The POSITIVE half does conform: a class-numeric argument of any magnitude is accepted (no upper bound is imposed) and is passed as a double. test-ref EMPTY — no spec-derived test exercises the class screen for EXP, and the CA24 golden only shows a legal argument is not wrongly rejected.

subject: EXP function
notes: DIVERGES confirmed, but the adjudicator's "NATIVE half CONFORMS" is OVERTURNED — the native half diverges too, and it is the PB5 defect one decade of magnitude out. §15.4.1's native licence (--check OK: "the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression") does NOT cover a result that is wrong by a factor of 15 with no size error. CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble clamps `if (scaled >= 1.7e38) return Int128.MaxValue;` after `scaled = d * Pow10.AsDouble(scale)`, and RenderFloat quantizes at `ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)`, so the clamp bites at |value| ≈ 1.7 × 10²⁹. FromDouble's own remark asserts that is "past the 10¹⁸ any PICTURE can describe" — FALSE at exactly the editions EXP exists in: EditionInfo.MaxDigits is 31 for 2002+ (`Year < 2002 ? 18 : 31`), EditionContext#CheckDigitCapacity accepts 19–31 digits at --std 2002+, and PicInfo backs a >18-digit fixed-point item with Int128 (`Digits > 18 ? "Int128" : "long"`). REPRO: `01 R PIC 9(31). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION EXP(70) ON SIZE ERROR … NOT ON SIZE ERROR ….` e⁷⁰ ≈ 2.5154 × 10³⁰ is IN RANGE for a 31-digit receiver, so §14.7.4 correctly raises nothing; the emitted `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(CobolIntrinsics.Exp((double)70), 9)` returns Int128.MaxValue, which unscales to 170141183460469231731687303715 — NOT ON SIZE ERROR taken, no diagnostic, value off by ~14.8×. Worse, FromDouble's doc names `EXP10(30)` as its example of a "genuine huge result under §14.7.4 receiver handling": 10³⁰ likewise fits a 31-digit receiver, so the comment's own justifying example is a live wrong-value case. The cited golden CANNOT see this — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_exp_overflow.cob uses `01 R PIC 9(5)`, a SMALL receiver where the clamp is indistinguishable from a real size error; that is precisely the sampling blind spot PB5 was caught by, and PB5 MOVED the clamp rather than removing it. A receiver-less `DISPLAY FUNCTION EXP(70)` renders at ws=9 and is wrong the same way. STANDARD half — the adjudicator's finding CONFIRMED and re-verified independently: §15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression" (--check OK); §15.34.4 r1's EAE `(FUNCTION E ** (argument-1))` (--check OK); §8.8.1.5.4 r2b makes `operand-1 ** 2` exactly `(operand-1 * operand-1)` (--check OK) and §15.27.3 r3 fixes FUNCTION E under standard-decimal at the exact 2.7182818284590452353602874713 52662 (--check OK), so §15.4.1 rule 2)b) grants no escape for an integer argument. IntrinsicRenderer#RenderNum dispatches `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(...)` BEFORE any arithmetic-mode test (EXP's catalog row carries Float=true), and RenderFloat has no mode arm, while NumericRenderer#Power's `if (StandardDecimal) return … DecPow(…)` sends the written-out `FUNCTION E ** 2` to CobolDec.Pow — the two disagree. `NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal` is `Arithmetic is StandardDecimal or Standard`, so ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD reaches the same engine. The single staging site (IntrinsicBinder, DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic) lists only ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION on the premise that the approximation functions have no EAE — true for SQRT and the trig/log rows, false for EXP §15.34.4 and EXP10 §15.35.4 (--check OK). FUNCTION E itself is Float=true → FromDouble(Math.E, ws), so it also ignores §15.27.3 r3. test-ref left EMPTY deliberately: intrinsic_exp_overflow.cob is spec-derived and manifest-registered but covers ONLY the PIC 9(5) over-range leg, and naming it on a DIVERGES row would read as partial closure of a rule whose native half is now known to be broken.

subject: EXP10 function
notes:
CONFIRMED DIVERGES, BUT THE CONSEQUENCE IS WIDER THAN REPORTED — the first pass characterized ONE inadmissible shape and missed three more, two of which fail differently.

RULE re-validated independently: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.35.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric." -> OK §15.35.3 1); --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified." -> OK §15.3 10); --check 8.5.2.1 "refers to the category unless class is specifically indicated" -> OK §8.5.2.1. So "class numeric" resolves through §8.5.2.1 Table 2 and admits ONLY class numeric.

MECHANISM RE-VERIFIED BY READING, not by inheriting: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified holds 22 entries (§15.7, §15.70–15.79, §15.8–15.19); EXP10 is in neither Verified nor DeliberatelyUnscreened. IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` — so the screen returns before looking at the operand and COBOLNET1627 can never fire for EXP10. The catalog's ArgKinds "n" is read by nothing (only the `== "p"` MAX/MIN test consumes ArgKinds), so the declared class is a dead lookup. Accept-half (every class-numeric argument binds) HOLDS — re-checked through functionArgument -> arithmeticExpression -> the ONE NumericRenderer.

⚠ FOUR INADMISSIBLE SHAPES, THREE FAILURE MODES — traced through NumericRenderer, not sampled:
1) class ALPHANUMERIC data item (`01 A PIC X(4)`): NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore's `{ Category: PicCategory.Alphanumeric or PicCategory.National }` arm emits `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(...)` — SILENT reinterpretation. This is the shape the first pass reported.
2) class NATIONAL data item (`01 N PIC N(4)`) — the SAME arm, same silent FromAlphanumeric. §15.35.3 admits national no more than alphanumeric; the first pass named only alphanumeric and numeric-edited, so the national category was never checked.
3) an alphanumeric or HEX LITERAL argument (`FUNCTION EXP10("ABC")`, `FUNCTION EXP10(X"32")`): BindArgOperand -> NonNumericOperand -> BoundStringLiteral -> NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundStringLiteral) -> `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(...)` — SILENT, and it never touches a data item at all, so the AR fix must be justified on ClassOf(BoundStringLiteral)=Alphanumeric, not only on ClassOfPlace.
4) class BOOLEAN (`01 B PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT`, or a B"1010" literal): FieldNumCore/Visit emit `EmitText.LoudValue` -> `NotImplemented.Value<long>(...)` -> the program COMPILES CLEAN and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN TIME. No compile diagnostic anywhere. That is the PB7 shape and it is invisible to any output-sampling adjudication.
Numeric-edited (usage display) additionally de-edits silently through FieldNum's CobolEdit.DeEdit arm.

NOTHING ELSE CATCHES ANY OF THEM: the §8.8.1.1 arithmetic-operand screen is deliberately suppressed in a function-argument position (BindArgOperand routes through BindFunctionArgumentExpr with the comment stating exactly that), and CheckArgumentClasses is the only §15.3 screen.

The ONE-ROW fix does close all four (IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf already classifies each), so the remedy is unchanged: ["EXP10"] = ('n', "§15.35.3 r1") plus the identical sibling ["EXP"] = ('n', "§15.34.3 r1") — --check 15.34.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric." -> OK §15.34.3 1). But the row's SEVERITY is not "silent garbage for PIC X": it is silent garbage for three categories plus an uncaught run-time throw for a fourth.

EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023, derived independently of IntrinsicCatalog: EXP10 is in the §8.11 intrinsic-function-name list of the 2023 text and has its own §15.35; Annex E (2014->2023 substantive changes) contains no EXP10 entry, so it is unchanged from 2014; Annex F lists it as neither obsolete nor archaic. The 85 exclusion rests on the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment's 42-function list, which contains neither EXP nor EXP10 — a PRIOR-EDITION fact the 2023 text alone cannot settle, and it is recorded as such rather than as a derivation from the catalog row.

NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST. IntrinsicSpecTests#ExpAndExp10 is a captured-output characterization by its own class header; IntrinsicFunctionTests drives the LEGACY CobolSharp.Runtime.IntrinsicFunctions.Call. Neither exercises an argument-class rejection. test-ref left empty.

subject: EXP10 function
notes:
CONFIRMED DIVERGES — but sub-finding (A)'s SCOPE is wrong in the first pass, in the direction that matters: it under-states reach by two whole dimensions, and a fix-queue entry scoped to its "narrow band" would land an incomplete fix.

RULES re-validated: --check 15.35.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is:" -> OK §15.35.4 1) (`(10 ** (argument-1))`); --check 15.4.1 "the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function" -> OK; --check 15.4 "If the length of the returned value exceeds the maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value, an EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist." -> OK; --check 8.8.1.5.4 "Otherwise, the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor." -> OK §8.8.1.5.4 2). I read §8.8.1.5.4 in full: items 1, 2a–d pin exponent 0..4 exactly and item 3 pins negatives as `1 / (operand-1 ** ABS(operand-2))`. §8.8.1.2 rule 6a/6c cannot fire (base 10 is positive and non-zero), and §15.35.3 imposes no domain limit, so no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is owed for a domain reason — `Math.Pow(10, x)` unguarded is right.

(A) SILENT WRONG VALUE — REACH CORRECTED. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes at `ws = max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)` through FromDouble, whose over-range arm is `if (scaled >= 1.7e38) return Int128.MaxValue;`. At ws = 9 that pins the returned value at ~1.70141183460469231731687303e29. PB5's replacement premise — "past the 10^18 any PICTURE can describe, so the saturation is now unreachable from a declarable receiver" — is false, and the first pass was right that it is false but wrong about WHY and HOW WIDELY:
  ⛔ THE CLAMP FIRES AT THE FUNCTION'S OWN QUANTIZATION POINT, BEFORE ANY RECEIVER STORE. The receiver's CAPACITY therefore does not decide whether the clamp fires — only whether the wrongness is visible in one COMPUTE. The first pass's "exactly characterizable band: PIC 9(31), PIC 9(30), PIC 9(30)V9" is a property of one statement shape, not of the defect.
  · RECEIVER-FREE REPRO, no wide PICTURE anywhere (--std 2002/2014/2023): `IF FUNCTION EXP10(30) = FUNCTION EXP10(31)`. ConditionRenderer renders BOTH relation operands under ReceiverContext.None (`num.AsNum(r.Left, ReceiverContext.None)`), whose Scale is 0, so ws = 9; 1e30*1e9 and 1e31*1e9 are both >= 1.7e38, both become Int128.MaxValue, and the condition is TRUE. Two arguments a factor of ten apart compare EQUAL, with no receiver involved at all.
  · ORDINARY-RECEIVER REPRO: `01 R PIC 9(18). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION EXP10(30) / FUNCTION EXP10(15).` Spec: 1e15, fits 18 digits. Actual: 1.70141183460469231731687303e29 / 1e15 -> R = 000170141183460469, no size error.
  ⛔ AND IT IS NOT A 2002+ DEFECT. The first pass tied reachability to EditionContext.MaxDigits = 31 (EditionInfo.MaxDigits => Year < 2002 ? 18 : 31 — verified), i.e. to a 30/31-digit PICTURE. But the same clamp is reachable at --std 85 through the 1989-amendment float family with plain PIC 9(18) data: `IF FUNCTION VARIANCE(0 A) = FUNCTION VARIANCE(0 B)` with distinct A, B near 1e18 gives variances ~2.5e35 and ~1.97e35, both >= 1.7e38 after the *1e9, both Int128.MaxValue, condition TRUE. So the PB5 remark must be corrected as edition-blind AND receiver-blind, and the fix cannot be scoped to "three PICTUREs at 2002+".
  · Minor extra on the same line: the threshold is a hand-written 1.7e38 rather than the true Int128 ceiling ~1.70141183460469231731687303715884105727e38, so the band [1.7e38, 1.70141...e38) is clamped although Int128 could hold it.
  §15.4.1's native licence covers an "approximation"; 1.7e29 for 1e30 is not one. And if 1.7e29 is instead taken to BE our implementor maximum returned-value length, §15.4 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be SET. The code does neither.

(B) RECEIVER-DEPENDENT RETURNED VALUE — CONFIRMED by reading RenderFloat: `ws = max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)` and no arithmetic-mode branch anywhere in the method. `01 P09 PIC 9V9(9). 01 P17 PIC 9V9(17).` with `COMPUTE P09 = FUNCTION EXP10(0.5)` and `COMPUTE P17 = FUNCTION EXP10(0.5)` emit FromDouble(..., 9) and FromDouble(..., 17) in one run unit -> 3.162277660 vs 3.16227766016837950, violating §15.4.1's unconditional invariance sentence under STANDARD / STANDARD-DECIMAL. The float-receiver escape is also confirmed: `return num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true) : ...` bypasses FromDouble entirely, so `01 D COMP-2. COMPUTE D = FUNCTION EXP10(400).` stores +Infinity raw. And Pow10.BuildDouble was read: `for (int i = 0; i < t.Length; i++) { t[i] = r; if (i < t.Length - 1) r *= 10; }` — a cumulative x10 recurrence, so D[23]..D[38] are not the correctly-rounded 10^n; ws can reach 31 (MaxDigits), so a high-scale receiver quantizes against a drifted power of ten. Shared root with the recorded §15.20.4 (COS) finding; recorded here, not re-queued.

(C) THE STAGING PREMISE IS FALSE FOR THIS FUNCTION — CONFIRMED. IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore stages only ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION loud (COBOLNET0899) on the stated ground that "the prose-'approximation' functions (SQRT, the trig/log family) have NO equivalent arithmetic expression"; CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs's family header repeats it. EXP10 §15.35.4 and EXP §15.34.4 DO have equivalent arithmetic expressions, so both comments are wrong about them.
  ⚠ I OVERTURN THE FIRST PASS'S REMEDY GUIDANCE HERE. It asserts §8.8.1.5.4 2)e "already makes the non-integer-exponent value implementor-defined", so staging EXP/EXP10 loud "would REJECT source we already serve correctly". Read 2)e to its END (validated above): "Operands used in the development of that value shall be in SDIDI form. All additions, subtractions, multiplications and divisions performed in the development of the result shall be performed in accordance with the corresponding rules in ISO/IEC 60559:2020." That is a CONSTRAINT on the implementor's freedom, not a blanket licence — a binary64 Math.Pow is not SDIDI-form arithmetic. So under STANDARD-DECIMAL a non-integer-exponent EXP10 is NOT "served correctly today", and whether the disposition is loud staging or an SDIDI evaluation is an owner call that the queue note must not foreclose.

WHAT DOES HOLD: the ordinary mid-range value is right (10**2 = 100 exactly; 10**-3 = 0.001 exactly at scale 9); CA24's NaN/+-Inf split is intact and correct for EXP10; no legal argument is rejected.

EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023 as in the AR row (§8.11 + Annex E silence + Annex F silence + the 1989 amendment's 42-function list). Contrary to the first pass, sub-finding (A) does NOT additionally require a 30–31-digit PICTURE.

NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST. IntrinsicSpecTests#ExpAndExp10 asserts the right value for EXP10(2) but its class header declares the assertions were captured from compiled+executed CLI output — corroboration only. tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_exp_overflow.cob is spec-derived but exercises EXP(710), not EXP10. IntrinsicFunctionTests drives the legacy runtime. test-ref left empty.

subject: FACTORIAL function
notes:
OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the test-ref is WITHDRAWN. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.36.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer greater than or equal to zero."` => OK §15.36.3 1). The completing rule is §15.3 (`--check 15.3` OK at item 14: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... and checking ... is not enabled, the implementor defines the result'), and §14.6.13.1.6 classifies EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION as **Fatal**, so with checking enabled the run unit must terminate.
WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED — THE RULE IS ENFORCED AGAINST A VALUE THAT IS NOT THE ARGUMENT. It read `CobolIntrinsics.Factorial(long n)`'s `n is < 0 or > 33` guard and called half A 'IMPLEMENTED'. That guard runs on the result of `IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt`, which is `(long)({a.Expr})` when Scale==0 and `(long)(CobolNum.Rescale(...))` otherwise. Both operands are Int128: `PicInfo.ElementType` is `Digits > 18 ? "Int128" : "long"`, `EmitText.IntLiteral` emits `Int128.Parse("...")` past 18 digits, `CobolNum.Rescale` returns Int128, and `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric` returns Int128. `RoslynBackend.Compile` passes `new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.ConsoleApplication, optimizationLevel: Release, nullableContextOptions: Disable)` and NEVER sets checkOverflow, so the generated C# is UNCHECKED and `(long)` on an Int128 SILENTLY WRAPS modulo 2^64. §8.3.3.3.2 (`--check` OK) requires fixed-point literals of 1..31 digits, and `EditionContext` accepts 19..31-digit pictures/literals at 2002+ — so an argument of 2^64 + k is CONFORMING source under §15.36.3 r1 (it is an integer >= 0) and arrives at the guard as k. The guard therefore approves it, and §15.4's returned-value-length EC is never reached either. This is the PB5 shape exactly: an extreme magnitude the adjudicator never sampled. See defect 1.
HALF B (integer-ness) CONFIRMED ABSENT, and its consequence is a §15.3 divergence rather than a mere gap: `CheckArgumentClasses` opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and I confirmed by reading the whole table that FACTORIAL is in NEITHER `Verified` (which holds ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI, ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, ANNUITY, CHAR, CHAR-NATIONAL, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER, COMBINED-DATETIME) NOR `DeliberatelyUnscreened`. So (i) a class-ALPHANUMERIC operand is coerced by `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric`, whose body is literally `foreach (char c in image) if (c is >= '0' and <= '9') mag = mag * 10 + (c - '0');` (defect 3), and (ii) a class-numeric NON-INTEGER operand is truncated by `AsInt`'s Rescale-with-Truncation arm and NO EC is set even with checking ON (defect 4). §15.3 says the condition 'is set to exist'; it is not. A required fatal condition that never fires on non-conforming input is active divergence, not absence.
TEST-REF WITHDRAWN. `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests#OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec` IS an `AssertSpec` (not `*MatchesLegacy`, not nist/characterization) and does contain `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL(0 - 1). DISPLAY R.` expecting `+000000`. But the spec derives only 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is set and, checking off, the implementor defines the result' — the specific value is not spec-derived, and the test's own comment says so: 'the legacy-compatible default the goldens encode'. Under the brief's rule 3 that is corroboration for one leg (checking OFF, negative argument, native arithmetic), not a spec-derived test, so the field is left empty. Everything else is untested: checking ON (must terminate), a non-integer argument, an alphanumeric argument, a >18-digit argument, any argument under STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL, and the compile-time-known `FUNCTION FACTORIAL(-1)` literal form (the existing test writes `0 - 1`, an expression, so the literal path is unexercised).
EDITIONS: derived as for FMT-15.36.2 — 2014/2023 mechanical (Table 21 + absent from the 2023 added/enhanced list + absent from Annex E); 85/2002 are the project's 1989-amendment convention and are NOT checkable against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. Never read from the IntrinsicCatalog row. The truncation defect itself is scoped 2002,2014,2023 because 19+ digit pictures/literals require --std 2002 (EditionContext).

subject: FACTORIAL function
notes:
OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.36.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` => OK §15.36.4 1); §15.36.1 'The type of this function is integer.' => OK; §15.4 'If the length of the returned value exceeds the maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value' => OK; §15.4.1 1) 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression.' => OK.
CONFIRMED FROM THE ADJUDICATOR: the pure fixed-point kernel is right — `Int128 r = 1; for (long i = 2; i <= n; i++) r *= i;` gives leg (a) 0/1 => 1, leg (b) 2 => 2, leg (c) the exact n!, in exact base-10 Int128; the 33/34 boundary is arithmetically correct (33! = 8.68e36 < Int128.Max = 1.70e38; 34! = 3.05e38 overflows); and folding the n<0 (argument-rule, §15.3) and n>33 (returned-value-length, §15.4) legs into one `ExceptionState.ArgumentError` is right because §15.4 names EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION for both. `ArgumentError` re-read at ExceptionState.cs: `if (ArgumentFunctionChecking) { Set("EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION", fatal: true); throw ... } return 0;` — correct shape, and Fatal matches §14.6.13.1.6.
WHY DIVERGES RATHER THAN PARTIAL — TWO ACTIVE WRONG BEHAVIOURS, not two absences.
(1) THE RETURNED VALUE IS THE FACTORIAL OF A DIFFERENT NUMBER. `RenderNum`'s Factorial arm calls `IntArg(ic, 0)` -> `AsInt` -> `(long)(<Int128 expr>)` under an UNCHECKED Roslyn compilation (RoslynBackend sets no checkOverflow), so an argument of 2^64 + k reaches the runtime as k. `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL(18446744073709551621)` (a 20-digit fixed-point literal, legal per §8.3.3.3.2's 1..31 digits, emitted as `Int128.Parse("18446744073709551621")`) returns 120 — 5! — where §15.4 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set and, checking off, the implementor-defined result (this implementation's documented 0), and, checking on, TERMINATION. Neither the §15.36.4 value nor the §15.4 EC. That is a wrong value AND a missing fatal condition on conforming source. The adjudicator sampled only small arguments; the boundary is invisible to output sampling for exactly the reason PB5 was.
(2) THE §15.4.1 r1 STANDARD-ARITHMETIC LEG IS AN ACKNOWLEDGED, OBSERVABLE DEVIATION FROM A 'SHALL'. Under STANDARD-DECIMAL/STANDARD, §15.4.1 item 1 says the returned value SHALL EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression evaluated in the intermediate form (§8.8.1.5, 34 significant digits, rounded per operation). `RenderNum` returns `new NumX(call, 0)` with Dec:false, so the FACTORIAL result never enters SDIDI form and the multiplication chain is exact Int128 throughout. 31! is exactly 34 digits and agrees; 32! (36 digits) and 33! (37 digits) do NOT — the per-step-rounded SDIDI chain and the exact chain differ, and the difference is OBSERVABLE, because a receiver of PIC 9(31) keeps the LOW-order digits (§14.9.25.4 high-order truncation), which are precisely the digits that differ. The header of CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs and COBOLNET_NUMERIC_DESIGN §D3 both record this as 'a divergence in the direction of MORE precision'. A recorded divergence from a 'shall' is DIVERGES; the adjudicator carried it as an untested residue inside a PARTIAL.
(3) Two shapes §15.3 item 6 expressly permits do not compile at all (defects 4 and 5), so the returned value cannot even be evaluated there.
NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST EXISTS FOR THE VALUE — CONFIRMED. The only n>=2 greenfield coverage is `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests#ExactFamily_MatchesLegacy` with `[InlineData("01 R PIC S9(9).", "COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL(9).")]`, a `*MatchesLegacy` differential (explicitly non-qualifying); legs (a) 0/1, (b) 2, the n>33 EC leg, the checking-ON leg and every standard-arithmetic leg are unexercised. test-ref stays empty.
DOCUMENTATION OBLIGATION UNMET (carried forward from the adjudicator and independently verified, recorded here not as a defect because it neither rejects legal source nor produces a wrong value): `cite.py --check A.1 "Function returned values (returned value length exceeds implementor-defined limits)"` => OK §A.1 93) — 'This item is required. The value returned SHALL BE documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.4, Returned values)'. The 33 boundary and the 0 result live only in docs/COBOLNET_INTRINSICS_DESIGN.md; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 (the A.1 register) has no item-93 row — it carries only the two §15.4.1 rows on returned-value text image and float-argument evaluation. Item 93 is distinct from item 90 (argument-rule violation), which explicitly does NOT require documenting the value.

subject: FIND-STRING function
