notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES — I re-derived the defect from the source line rather than accepting it, and it is real. Citation re-run: `cite.py --check 15.37.4 "argument-3 represents the number of matches to ignore"` → OK §15.37.4 rule 2. The line is `int idx = last ? positions.Count - 1 - (int)skip : (int)skip;` — an UNCHECKED C# narrowing of the `long skip` parameter. No CheckForOverflowUnderflow property exists in any .csproj/.props in the repo (grep returns nothing), so the project builds unchecked and the cast WRAPS modulo 2^32 rather than throwing. The value arrives as a long: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum case "FindString" renders argument-3 through IntArg→AsInt, which emits `(long)(…)`. So argument-3 = 4294967296 truncates to 0 and the function returns positions[0]=1 (LAST: positions[Count−1]=7) where r2 followed by r3 requires 0. I ALSO WORKED THE ADJACENT VALUES, which is what makes this a sampling trap: 2^31 and 2^32−1 both land outside the trailing `idx >= 0 && idx < positions.Count` guard and return 0 BY LUCK, while 2^32 and 2^32+1 return a match — so probing 'some huge number' has a good chance of looking correct. Any argument-3 whose low 32 bits fall in 0..Count−1 reproduces. DISTINCT from the recorded IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt `(long)` narrowing GAP (inventory row AR-15.22.3-1 names FIND-STRING among its callers): that bites above 2^63, this at 2^32, and fixing AsInt leaves this live. FIX: compare in the long domain — `if (skip >= positions.Count) return 0;` before any narrowing, and keep idx a long. ⛔ TEST-REF STRIPPED (the adjudicator left one on a DIVERGES row): FindString_Positions_2023 cannot close this rule, and its `(H N LAST START AFTER 1) ⇒ 4` case additionally pins an UNSTATED interpretation — that with LAST the skip is counted FROM THE END. §15.37.4 r2 says only 'the number of matches to ignore before determining the character position'; it never fixes the direction. (b) LENGTH PRESERVATION — the adjudicator asserted ToLowerInvariant is 'one-to-one and length-preserving'; I MEASURED it (.NET, every non-surrogate BMP scalar plus supplementary samples U+10400/104B0/118A0/16E40/1E900): zero non-length-preserving cases, so the position arithmetic over the folded images stays aligned with the unfolded operands and the §15.57.4 r5 hazard does not bite. subject: FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE function
notes: CONFIRMED PARTIAL, with the second half's root cause corrected and widened. Citation re-validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.38.3 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal"` -> OK (rule 1). HALF A (literal-ness) IS enforced, and I verified it from the SOURCE rather than from sampled output: the arm in BindIntrinsicCore is `args.Count > 0 && args[0] is not BoundStringLiteral && sig.Name is "FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE" or ... -> COBOLNET1517`, sitting after the arity guard (which returns a BoundExprError, so the 0-arg case can never reach it). Every non-literal shape the binder can produce is a distinct node and therefore caught: BoundFieldOperand (identifier), BoundNumericLiteral, BoundFigurative (SPACE/ZERO), BoundAllLiteral (`ALL "..."`), BoundComputedOperand. Positively, no legal spelling is falsely rejected: the grammar's `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` and `nonNumericLiteral : concatenationExpression | STRINGLIT | NATLIT | BOOLLIT | HEXLIT | figurativeConstant` admit N"...", X"...", NX"..." and an 8.8.3 concatenation expression, and ExpressionBinder.ConstantOperand substitutes a 13.10 CONSTANT AS literal as a BoundStringLiteral (13.10.4 GR1), so all of those bind. HALF B (the CLASS 'national or alphanumeric') IS NOT enforced -- confirmed by reading IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs directly: FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE appears in NEITHER `Verified` (which currently holds only the batch-1 §15.7/§15.70-79 rows plus batch-2 §15.8-15.19) nor `DeliberatelyUnscreened` (BYTE-LENGTH/BASECONVERT/CONCAT/CONVERT), so `CheckArgumentClasses` returns at its first line and never looks at this function. CORRECTION/ADDITION the first pass under-stated: `IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf` maps `BoundStringLiteral => CobolClass.Alphanumeric` UNCONDITIONALLY while `BoundStringLiteral` carries its own `Category` init-property (Alphanumeric / National per 8.3.3.5 / Boolean per 8.3.3.4) -- so the screen cannot distinguish B"0101" (illegal here) from "..." from N"..." for ANY function, which means adding a row for this function would still not close the rule, AND it is the SAME root blindness that produces the wrong result category recorded on RV-15.38.4-1. NEW, and it is why the omission is not an oversight anyone could have caught: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests.cs asserts only Verified->Catalog (`EveryVerifiedRule_NamesARealFunction_WithAHandledCode`) and that the screen is wired; there is NO assertion in the Catalog->(Verified union DeliberatelyUnscreened) direction, so an unclassified catalog row is structurally invisible to the gate. The durable shape is that every catalog row must appear in exactly one of the two tables. NOTE on the empty literal: 8.3.3.2 makes `""` a legal ZERO-LENGTH LITERAL ("If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero"), so `""` satisfies THIS rule and is illegal only under rule 2 -- do not attribute it here. subject: FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE function
notes: OVERTURNED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the test-ref REMOVED. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.38.4 "The returned value is a representation of the current date and time provided by the system on which the function is evaluated"` -> OK (rule 1). BOTH sentences of the rule have a demonstrable silently-wrong path, which is DIVERGES rather than 'one half verified'. SENTENCE 1 ('the current date and time provided by the system') IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTED WITHIN ONE RUN UNIT -- and this is a divergence, not merely an untestable value. A grep of the whole runtime for direct clock reads returns exactly two sites, both in CobolDate: `CurrentDate() => Format21(DateTimeOffset.Now)` and `FormattedCurrentDate`'s `DateTimeOffset now = DateTimeOffset.Now`. Every OTHER temporal reading goes through the injectable seam -- `SecondsPastMidnight() => RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().TimeOfDay.Ticks`, `YearToYyyy`'s defaulted argument-3 `RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year` (15.100.3 r5), and ACCEPT ... FROM DATE (14.9.1.4 GR7). SystemClock honours COBOLNET_CLOCK, so under a pinned clock two functions that both report 'the current date and time provided by the system' return different instants in the same run unit. CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED FIX, which the first pass got wrong: 'route FormattedCurrentDate through RunUnit.Current.Clock' is NOT sufficient -- `IClock.Now()` returns a `DateTime` with NO UTC offset, and 15.38 needs one for the 15.3.3.6 offset subfield and the 15.3.3.5 UTC conversion. The seam has to widen to DateTimeOffset (which also fixes CurrentDate/Format21). SENTENCE 2 ('formatted according to the format in argument-1') produces WRONG CHARACTERS on input the compiler accepts. In EmitFormatted's Fld.Fraction arm, `(long)(frac * (decimal)(long)Pow10.AsWide(s.Width))`: Pow10.AsWide returns Int128 and 10^19 > long.MaxValue, so the `(long)` narrowing wraps. I verified this is silent rather than throwing -- Directory.Build.props sets no `CheckForOverflowUnderflow`, so the Int128->long conversion is the unchecked operator; and because |wrapped| <= 2^63 and frac < 1, the subsequent decimal->long cast never overflows either, so nothing is raised. The result is a NEGATIVE integer rendered by `.ToString(new string('0', s.Width))`, which also emits a leading '-' and so overruns the field width and shifts everything after it. 15.3.3.2 (`cite.py --check 15.3.3.2 "The implementor defines the maximum number of digit positions"` -> OK) lets the implementor cap the fraction width at any value >= 9, but COBOL.NET defines no maximum, documents none (see RV-15.38.4-2) and diagnoses none -- so the input is either legal-and-wrong or beyond an undefined cap, and both readings are defects. Additionally the offset+Z acceptance recorded on AR-15.38.3-2 emits a value that is simultaneously UTC-converted, offset-stamped and Z-marked. WHAT IS RIGHT, and it is a large correct core -- read from the source, not sampled: DateTimeOffset.Now is snapshotted ONCE so date/time/offset cannot straddle a boundary; `(now.Date - Epoch).Days + 1` is exact because both operands are midnight-aligned; the UTC arm `secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m` with the `while` day-roll runs BEFORE `Epoch.AddDays(day - 1)`, so the calendar conversion sees the adjusted day; `week = HasWeek(segs)` switches the Year field to `ISOWeek.GetYear` so a week format carries the ISO week-year; `isoD = ((int)dt.DayOfWeek + 6) % 7 + 1` maps Sunday->7 and Monday->1 per 15.3.1.7; `osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'` matches 15.3.3.6.1's sense; `oh/om` from `Math.Abs(offsetMinutes)` handle half- and quarter-hour zones; and Tokenize marks the basic-format decimal separator a PHANTOM, which reproduces the standard's own D.31.5.3 worked example 19950215T05142781-0500 exactly. THIRD DEFECT, result CATEGORY: 15.38.1's type table (Alphanumeric argument -> Alphanumeric function, National -> National; the 15.2 summary table prints it as 'Anum1 or Nat1 | Anum or Nat') is not implemented -- IntrinsicCatalog hardcodes IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric and IntrinsicBinder's category-follows-argument arm is a hand-written name list covering only UpperCase/LowerCase/Reverse and the MAX/MIN 'p' family, so a national argument yields an Alphanumeric result and the 14.9.25.3 Table-16 National->Alphanumeric MOVE guard is bypassed. Family-wide with 15.39/15.40/15.41. TEST-REF REMOVED, and this is the reason: `TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME(fmt, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE(fmt))` routes BOTH sides through the SAME CobolDate.Tokenize (EmitFormatted and Analyze share it), so it is a self-consistency round-trip, and the golden pins FCD=+000000000 -- the TEST result, never the timestamp. It would still print 0 with the month and day transposed (for days <= 12), with the wrong year, with the wrong clock, and with the fraction-width defect (that format has no fraction). It is corroboration that the call compiles and round-trips, and nothing more; it does not verify either sentence of this rule. EDITIONS: as for AR-15.38.3-1.

This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' The rule's entire content is 'the implementor shall DEFINE', and no definition exists in user documentation -- a behaviour that merely happens is not a definition, so NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than PARTIAL. CORRECTION 1 (the first pass's contrast is wrong and would mislead the fix): it held up SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT as 'the shape this row needs' because its code comment names implementor item 171 -- but a grep of docs/CONFORMANCE.md for '171' ALSO returns nothing. Item 171 is a code comment too, not user documentation. The register is systematically incomplete (it documents 2, 59, 158, 205, 206, 207, 208, 211, 215 and two unnumbered 15.4.1 entries), so item 87 is not an isolated omission and the fix is a register sweep, not a single row. CORRECTION 2 (the code comment is wrong in a third way the first pass did not catch): CobolDate.FormattedCurrentDate's comment says 'Time accuracy is to the tick the runtime clock provides' -- but this function does not read the runtime clock AT ALL (it reads DateTimeOffset.Now directly; see RV-15.38.4-1), AND the value is `(decimal)now.TimeOfDay.TotalSeconds` scaled by `(long)(sod * 1_000_000_000m)` to exactly NINE fraction digits. `TotalSeconds` is a double and the .NET double->decimal conversion rounds to 15 SIGNIFICANT digits, so for a late-day reading (five integer digits) at most ten fraction digits survive the conversion, from a source whose real resolution is the platform timer -- neither 'the tick' nor nine significant digits. A format asking for more than nine digits is padded with information-free zeros rather than truncated or diagnosed. WHAT A FIX MUST STATE, four facts: the clock source, the number of fraction digits actually significant, the behaviour when the format requests more, and the 15.3.3.2 maximum fraction width (which shall be >= 9, must be defined, and is not -- see RV-15.38.4-1). subject: FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL. The prior record found the rule half-enforced. It is broken in BOTH directions, and the direction it missed is the one CLAUDE.md rule 4 forbids outright: THE COMPILER REJECTS LEGAL COBOL.

CITATIONS, ALL RE-VALIDATED BY ME (not inherited): cite.py --check 15.39.3 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal." -> OK (§15.39.3 1)). cite.py --check 13.10.1 "A constant may be used in place of a literal." -> OK. cite.py --check 13.10.3 "constant-name-1 may be used anywhere that a format specifies a literal of the class and category of constant-name-1" -> OK (§13.10.3 SR2). cite.py --check 13.10.4 "the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1" -> OK (§13.10.4 GR1).

THE MISSED HALF — A CONSTANT-NAME IS A LITERAL, AND EVERY ONE IS REJECTED. §13.10.4 GR1 is unconditional: "the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1 ... were written where constant-name-1 is written". So `01 FMT-CONST CONSTANT AS "YYYYMMDD".` + `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE (FMT-CONST 143951) TO RA` IS, by rule, the program the prior record ran green. RAN IT (scratchpad/ref/rfd1.cob), --std 2023 AND --std 2014, identical both:
    error COBOLNET0844: constant-name 'FMT-CONST' substitutes a literal of category Alphanumeric and is not a numeric operand (ISO 8.8.1.1 / 13.10.3 SR2)
    error COBOLNET1517: FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE argument-1 shall be a literal date/time format
A NATIONAL constant — the other class §15.39.3 r1 names — fails the same way (rfd4.cob, `01 NAT-C CONSTANT AS N"YYYYMMDD".` -> the same 0844 with 'category National' + 1517). CONTROLS THAT ISOLATE THE CAUSE (rfd3.cob, both green): the written literal `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE ("YYYYMMDD" 143951)` prints 19950215, and a NUMERIC constant in argument-2, `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE ("YYYYMMDD" NUM-C)`, also prints 19950215 — so CONSTANT itself works and only the STRING-class constant in an argument position is refused.

ROOT CAUSE, READ IN THE CODE (this is a whole-channel defect, not this function's): ExpressionBinder#RefExpr resolves a constant-name BEFORE and INDEPENDENTLY of the OperandContext it was handed — `ctx.Data.ConstantOf(dref) is { } k ? k.Category is PicCategory.Numeric ? new BoundNumLiteral(...) : NonNumericConstantExpr(...)`. NonNumericConstantExpr raises COBOLNET0844 unconditionally. IntrinsicBinder#BindArgOperand routes every non-literal argument through host.Expr.BindFunctionArgumentExpr, i.e. OperandContext.FunctionArgument, and the sibling arm one line below (OperandRef) DOES consult that context — which is why a PIC X DATA ITEM argument is admitted and a constant-name substituting the identical characters is not. SWEPT (rule 4 — every bug is a pattern; rfd2.cob): the same 0844 fires for FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(TXT-C), FUNCTION TRIM(TXT-C) and FUNCTION LENGTH(TXT-C). ExpressionBinder#FieldOperand has the correct shape already (ConstantOperand -> BoundStringLiteral with the right Category) — RefExpr is the copy that never got it, so the fix is to give RefExpr the same substitution outside OperandContext.Arithmetic rather than to special-case FORMATTED-DATE.

THE UNDER-REJECT HALF (prior record's finding, RE-VERIFIED not inherited): `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE (B"1010" 143951) TO RA` compiles with ZERO diagnostics and prints spaces (rfd7.cob, at 2023 and 2014). The screen is `args[0] is not BoundStringLiteral` and a boolean literal binds as BoundStringLiteral{Category=Boolean}. A boolean literal is neither national nor alphanumeric.

SO: over-rejects a national/alphanumeric literal written as a constant-name, under-rejects a boolean literal. Neither direction of r1 holds — DIVERGES, not PARTIAL. The shared COBOLNET1517 arm names FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE / -DATETIME / -TIME / INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE / SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME / TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, so both directions are the family's.

RETAINED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD, RE-VERIFIED: the positive side draws no false reject for a WRITTEN literal — N"YYYYMMDD" -> 19950215 (rfd7.cob) and the §8.8.3 concatenation `"YYYY" & "MMDD"` -> 19950215 (rfd9.cob). And FORMATTED-DATE is absent from BOTH IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and .DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns on its first line — confirmed by reading it.

test-ref EMPTY: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob uses written alphanumeric literals only; it pins neither direction of r1.

EDITIONS: Annex E's 2014->2023 addition lists (E.2 item 13 / E.3.3) do not name FORMATTED-DATE, so it is present unchanged in 2014 and 2023. The 2002/85 boundary is NOT derivable from the 2023 text and is not asserted; not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row. Every reproduction above was run at BOTH 2014 and 2023.

subject: FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
CONFIRMED, with both halves independently re-run — this inventory already contains one refuted record whose 'saturation' claim was FALSE, so I re-executed rather than inherit. Code-location moved from CobolDate#FormattedDate to the site that must change: the guard in FormattedDate is correct; what defeats it is upstream.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.39.3 "Argument-2 shall be a value in integer date form." -> OK. cite.py --check 15.5.2 "It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231)" -> OK (the VALUE half). cite.py --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified" -> OK (§15.3 type 6, the CLASS half). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14 — EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION shall be set).

(A) THE §15.5.2 GUARD IS UNREACHABLE ABOVE 2^63 — RE-RUN AND REPRODUCED. Read the channel: IntrinsicRenderer's FormattedDate arm renders argument-2 through ArgInt -> AsInt, and AsInt is literally `(long)({expr})` over an Int128 expression — an UNCHECKED narrowing that wraps modulo 2^64 before CobolDate.FormattedDate's `if (integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671)` ever sees the value. RAN (scratchpad/ref/rfda.cob) WITH `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`: `01 P18 PIC 9(18) VALUE 184467440737096955.` + `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE ("YYYYMMDD" P18 * 100 + 67) TO R30` prints `WRP=[19950215]` then `NOT-RAISED`, exit 0. The argument value is 18,446,744,073,709,695,567 = 2^64 + 143,951. CONTROL in the SAME program, same statement shape: `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE ("YYYYMMDD" 3067672)` aborts with `EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-DATE argument 3067672 outside 1..3,067,671 (15.5.2)`. The only difference is whether the value survives the (long) cast.
⚠ SHARED ROOT CAUSE — do not double-count: this is the whole-channel IntrinsicRenderer#AsInt defect already recorded in the inventory against DATE-OF-INTEGER, whose note names FORMATTED-DATE among the siblings to sweep. One channel fix closes both.

(B) THE CLASS HALF IS COMPLETELY UNSCREENED — RE-VERIFIED IN CODE AND RE-RUN. Read CheckArgumentClasses: its first line is `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and FORMATTED-DATE is in neither Verified nor DeliberatelyUnscreened (I read both dictionaries), so COBOLNET1627 can never fire for it. RAN (rfd9.cob), both clean, no diagnostics, at 2023 and 2014: `01 A6 PIC X(6) VALUE "143951".` -> 19950215 (an alphanumeric item is not "an integer data item"); `01 NF PIC 9(6)V99 VALUE 143951.75.` -> 19950215 (silent truncation; not "an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value").

⚠ STRUCTURAL NOTE FOR THE FIX (CLAUDE.md rule 5), re-derived from the code rather than inherited: Verified's value is a SINGLE `char Kind` and CheckArgumentClasses applies it to EVERY position (`IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation(rule.Kind, args[i])` inside the loop). FORMATTED-DATE needs 's' for argument-1 and 'i' for argument-2, so the row cannot be added until the table is PER-POSITION. IntrinsicCatalog's row does carry a per-position hint ("si"), but IntrinsicArgumentRules' own class doc records why that column may not be read — it is unaudited and screening from it rejected 12 legal corpus programs — so the per-position structure has to be built in Verified, not harvested. The same blocks FORMATTED-DATETIME ('s','i','n','i'), FORMATTED-TIME, INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE and BASECONVERT. Restructure; do not special-case.

POSITIVE SIDE RE-VERIFIED (no false reject): an integer literal, a PIC 9(7) item, a signed literal +143951, a numeric CONSTANT-name (rfd3.cob) and a nested FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(19950215) all bind and return 19950215.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r1 'Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal.' The prior pass recorded the correct facts and then under-graded them. THE RULE EXPRESSLY ADMITS A NATIONAL LITERAL, AND A NATIONAL LITERAL IS SILENTLY MIS-TYPED — that is legal source getting a wrong result, which is DIVERGES, not an unverified edge. §15.40.1 (verified verbatim: 'The type of this function depends on the type of argument-1 as follows: Alphanumeric|Alphanumeric, National|National') and the §15.6 Table-21 row (`FORMATTED-DATETIME | Anum1 or Nat1, Int2, Num3, Int4 | Anum or Nat` — Table 21 lives in §15.6, NOT in §15.40.1 as the prior note asserted) make a national argument-1 give a NATIONAL function type. `IntrinsicCatalog` hardcodes `IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric` and `IntrinsicBinder`'s result-category resolution covers ONLY UpperCase/LowerCase/Reverse (a National-argument arm) and the MAX/MIN 'p' arm — the date/time family has no arm, so `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME(N"YYYYMMDDThhmmss", ...)` is labelled alphanumeric and the §14.9.25.4 Table-16 MOVE screen and national collation both see the wrong class. `ExpressionBinder.NationalLiteralOperand` does produce `BoundStringLiteral { Category = National }`, so the literal is ACCEPTED — the defect is purely the result type. LITERAL half — re-traced and confirmed sound: the COBOLNET1517 arm tests `args[0] is not BoundStringLiteral` for the seven FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE/SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME/TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME rows; an alphanumeric literal, a HEXLIT (§8.3.3.2 makes X".." a FORMAT of the alphanumeric literal — correct acceptance), a §8.8.3 concatenation (ConcatOperand folds to BoundStringLiteral, category preserved) and a §13.10 constant-name (ConstantOperand substitutes per §13.10.4 GR1) all pass; an identifier, a numeric literal, a figurative constant, `ALL "x"` and an arithmetic expression are rejected. CLASS half — NOT enforced: `BooleanLiteralOperand` also yields a `BoundStringLiteral` (Category = Boolean) and the arm tests only the bound SHAPE, so `B"0101"` compiles clean where r1 admits only national or alphanumeric. FORMATTED-DATETIME is absent from `IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified`, and `IntrinsicBinder#CheckArgumentClasses` returns immediately for an unlisted function — verified by reading the early-return, so per PB1's own doctrine this function is genuinely UNSCREENED. TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, on a defect the prior pass did not look for. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r3 'Argument-2 shall be a value in integer date form'; the FORM is §15.5.2 ('greater than zero and ... less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'). ⛔ NEW — LEGAL SOURCE PRODUCES UNCOMPILABLE C#, THE PB2 SHAPE IN THE CHANNEL PB2 DID NOT FIX. §15.3 type 6 (verbatim: 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified') and Table 21's `Int2` make an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION a legal argument-2. `RenderFormattedDatetime` renders it through `ArgInt` -> `AsInt`, whose scale-0 arm is `(long)({a.Expr})`. Under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (and STANDARD) `NumericRenderer.CombineCore` returns `new NumX("CobolDec.Add(...)", 0, Dec: true)` for every binary operator, and `CobolDec` is `readonly record struct CobolDec(Int128 Sig, int Exp)` with NO conversion operators — I grepped it: zero `operator` declarations. So `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss", WS-A + WS-B, 45296) TO R.` under standard-decimal emits `(long)(CobolDec.Add(...))`, a C# CS0030, i.e. an internal failure escaping as a backend error on conforming source. `AsInt` has no `.Dec` arm at all although `ConditionRenderer`, `DecOperand`, `Negate`, `Real` and `OperandText` all do — so this is one missing arm, and it is a PATTERN: the same `AsInt` serves every integer-kind intrinsic argument (DATE-OF-INTEGER, CHAR, BASE-CONVERT, FORMATTED-DATE, FORMATTED-TIME) in both channels. VALUE-RANGE half — sound: `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime` opens with `if (integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671)`, calls `ExceptionState.ArgumentError` with the §15.5.2 citation and returns "" (the §15.3 implementor-defined result; A.1 item 90 verified in the spec's own list: 'Function-identifier (result when argument rules are violated and checking for the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is not enabled). This item is required.'). I re-derived 3,067,671 independently (1601-01-01 + 3,067,670 days = 9999-12-31). INTEGRALITY half — NOT checked, and the prior pass did not name it: §15.5.2 requires a POSITIVE INTEGER, but `AsInt`'s scale-not-0 arm silently truncates a fractional argument-2 through `NumRescale(..., Truncation)` with no EC. CLASS half — NOT enforced (absent from `IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified`; an alphanumeric operand reaches `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric` and yields a garbage date). BOUNDARY half — the guard is never re-applied after the §15.40.4 r2 roll mutates `day` (full detail under RV-15.40.4-2). TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES; two additions and one citation correction. Citations re-validated: §15.40.3 r4 plus its NOTE; the FORM is §15.5.5 ('If the LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is in effect, the value shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400') — the only mode this compiler implements. INTERPRETATION half — correct: argument-3 is consumed as seconds past midnight and passed as an (unscaled, scale) pair, so a fixed-point fraction survives; `EmitFormatted` splits hh/mm/ss/fraction. RANGE half — NO CHECK EXISTS: I re-grepped, and the only occurrences of 86400 in non-generated src are the two roll loops in `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`. §15.3's argument paragraph makes SETTING EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION unconditional even though the RESULT is implementor-defined, and it is never set. PRECISION half — DIVERGES on legal source, unchanged: `NumX sec = ArgNum(ic.Args[2])` then `(long)({sec.Expr}), {sec.Scale}`; for a COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-LONG operand `NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore`'s `{ IsFloat: true }` arm returns `new NumX(..., 0, Real: true)`, so the cast truncates to whole seconds at scale 0. `RenderNum` guards this with `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(...)`; the STRING channel never consults `NumX.Real`. A COMP-2 item is class numeric and Table 21 types this argument `Num3`. ADDED (1): the standard-decimal `(long)(CobolDec…)` uncompilable path recorded under AR-15.40.3-3 hits argument-3 identically — §15.3 type 10 ('An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified') makes an expression legal here too. ADDED (2): the out-of-range consequence is worse than the prior pass's width argument — `int hh = (int)(tot / 3600), mi = (int)(tot % 3600 / 60), ss = (int)(tot % 60)` are `(int)` casts of a `long`, so a large argument-3 WRAPS rather than merely widening. subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED, independently re-verified. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r5 returns whole, including 'If argument-4 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' I re-ran the search rather than trusting the prior pass: `grep -rn 1439 src/ --include=*.cs | grep -v Generated/` returns NOTHING — not in the binder, not in the renderer, not in the runtime. Argument-4 flows `IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedDatetime` -> `ArgInt(ic.Args[3])` -> `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`, which only ever computes `offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); oh = (int)(offMag / 60); om = (int)(offMag % 60)`. Consequences, both silent: 2000 minutes renders offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 ('The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive'); 9999 minutes renders 166, so `oh.ToString("00")` emits three characters and the returned value grows past the width the format describes. §15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist for an out-of-range argument even though the VALUE is implementor-defined; it is never set. Because argument-4 may be an identifier or an expression this cannot be a compile-time check in general, but it is a one-line runtime guard beside the existing integer-date guard in `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime`. NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES because there is no implementation to diverge from. The identical rule text is §15.41.3 r4 for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented (same sweep). TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r6 'Argument-4 shall not be specified if the time portion of the format in argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format.' NO CODE IMPLEMENTS THIS RULE. Re-read `BindIntrinsicCore`: its only FORMATTED-DATETIME-specific arm is the COBOLNET1517 literal check, and nothing correlates the argument COUNT with the SHAPE of the format literal. `EmitFormatted` does compute both predicates the rule needs — `isUtc` (a 'Z' segment) and the OffSign/OffHour/OffMinute fields — but at RUN time and only to drive emission, never to reject. `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss", 153569, 45296, 120)` compiles with zero diagnostics, prints 20210616T123456 and discards argument-4 (`hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset` is false and there is no offset field to render into). FULLY COMPILE-TIME DECIDABLE: r1 already forces argument-1 to be a literal, so the binder holds the format string and the argument count at the same point, immediately after the COBOLNET1517 arm, and the tokenizer is already reachable from the compiler through `RuntimeApi.DateFormatFractionDigits`. Note the predicate the fix needs must be the §15.3.1/§15.3.2 FORMAT RECOGNIZER called for under AR-15.40.3-2, not the present `isUtc` proxy — 'Z' anywhere in the string is not 'the time portion is a UTC format' (§15.3.3.5 says a UTC format is a common time format FOLLOWED BY 'Z'). §15.41.3 r5 is the same rule for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented. TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r7 '... the function shall be evaluated as though 0 were specified for argument-4.' THE UTC LEG IS NOT 'EVALUATED AS THOUGH 0 WERE SPECIFIED' — IT TAKES A STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT PATH, AND THE PRIOR PASS DISMISSED THE DIFFERENCE ON AN ASSUMPTION THE COMPILER NEVER ENFORCES. `RenderFormattedDatetime` emits `{(hasOff ? ArgInt(ic.Args[3]) : "0")}, {(hasOff ? "true" : "false")}`, so an omitted argument-4 arrives as (offsetMinutes = 0, hasOffset = FALSE) and `EmitFormatted`'s `if (hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset)` block is SKIPPED entirely — including the two normalization loops `while (secs < 0) {...}` / `while (secs >= 86400m) {...}` that an explicit 0 WOULD execute. The prior pass called that 'observationally identical, since neither roll loop can then fire'; the loops cannot fire only while argument-3 is inside [0, 86400), and that is precisely the rule this compiler does not check (AR-15.40.3-4, verified: no 86400 comparison exists outside the loops themselves). Demonstrable asymmetry on the same source shape — format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ', argument-2 = 153569, argument-3 = 90000: with argument-4 OMITTED, tot = 90000 gives hh = 25 and the value is '20210616T250000Z'; with argument-4 written as 0 the roll fires, giving secs = 3600, day = 153570 and '20210617T010000Z'. r7's 'as though 0' is unconditional; two different answers from the two spellings is not conformance to it, whichever result §15.3 would license. SECOND, AND WHY THIS ROW CANNOT CLOSE: the rule's PREMISE ('the time portion ... is a UTC format or an offset format') is never computed as a predicate anywhere. The correct behaviour is an artifact of one literal `"0"` in the renderer's format string, with no drift test, no golden, and no spec-derived test — green by accident, and rule 7 was never implemented as a rule. WHAT IS GENUINELY RIGHT, verified by reading: the offset-format leg renders `osign` from `offsetMinutes >= 0` and oh/om from `Math.Abs(offsetMinutes)`, so an omitted argument-4 over an offset format yields '+0000' (and '+00:00' for the extended '+hh:mm' subformat, whose ':' Tokenize carries as an in-data separator) — which §15.3.3.6.1 independently requires: 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of data in a receiving field associated with an offset subformat are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign' (re-validated verbatim), with its NOTE 3 confirming '+0000'. TEST: none — the missing verification is a fixture asserting '+0000' for an omitted argument-4 over an offset format AND identical output for the omitted and explicit-0 spellings over a UTC format.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES; two errors in the prior pass's supporting reasoning corrected, because both were presented as verification. Citation re-validated: §15.40.4 r1. ⛔ CORRECTION 1 — THE STANDARD'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE IS REJECTED BY THIS IMPLEMENTATION AND THE PRIOR PASS ELIDED IT. D.31.5.7 reads verbatim: 'given as the first argument the format "YYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", as the second argument the value 143951, as the third argument the value 18867.812479168304, and as the fourth argument the value +300, the returned value would be "19950215T05142781+0500"'. That is TWO 'Y' characters. `Tokenize`'s `case 'Y': if (Run('Y') != 4) return null;` rejects it outright, so the literal as printed sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and returns "". Rejecting is CORRECT — §15.3.1.2 (re-validated: 'The basic calendar date format contains eight characters: four uppercase Y characters ...') and the example's own 4-digit returned year make the annex text internally inconsistent — but the prior pass silently substituted 'YYYY' and reported the trace as a match. The substitution must be stated, not assumed. With 'YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm' the trace does hold segment by segment: offset (non-Z) format leaves isUtc false so no adjustment; Epoch.AddDays(143950) = 1995-02-15; 'T' in data; tot = 18867 -> 05/14/27; frac .812479168304 at width 2 -> '81'; offsetMinutes 300 -> '+0500'. ⛔ CORRECTION 2 — the prior pass wrote 'truncation, not rounding, which is what the standard's own .81 shows'. That is not evidence: 0.812479168304 ROUNDS to 0.81 as well. D.31.5.7 does not discriminate truncation from rounding, so the fractional-seconds disposition remains UNVERIFIED and no clause in §15.3.3.2 or §15.40.4 settles it. THE DIVERGENCES, all silent and all confirmed: (1) a FLOATING-POINT argument-3 loses its entire fraction — the STRING channel never consults `NumX.Real`, so the D.31.5.7 value through a COMP-2 returns '...05142700+0500'; (2) the result CATEGORY is hardcoded Alphanumeric, so a national argument-1 does not produce the national returned value §15.40.1 and Table 21 require; (3) a fractional-seconds subfield of >= 19 's' characters overflows `(long)Pow10.AsWide(width)` — `Pow10.AsWide` returns Int128 and the `(long)` cast is unchecked — and §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction-digit count a REQUIRED implementor-defined item ('that maximum shall be greater than or equal to nine', re-validated) that is neither enforced nor documented; (4) NEW — a format with month/day/week fields but no 'YYYY' renders those subfields as ZERO, because `hasDate` keys solely on `Fld.Year`. ONE INTERPRETATION RECORDED, not a defect: the UTC adjustment rolls the DATE as well as the time; r1 and r2 are silent, and the roll rests on §15.40.1's 'convert and combine a date ... and a numeric time ... to produce a formatted date and time representation' — I agree with the reading, but it is ours, not the standard's words. TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES; arithmetic and reachability independently re-verified. Citation re-validated: §15.40.4 r2. DIRECTION — correct, and re-derived from the spec rather than from a golden: the code is `secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m`, and §15.3.3.6.1 item 1 (re-validated verbatim: 'A plus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC') makes a positive argument-4 subtract. Cross-checked against §15.3.3.6.1 NOTE 1 ('1014278124Z' per hhmmss.ssssZ equals '0514278124-0500' per hhmmss.ssss+hhmm): local 05:14 with offset -0500 gives 05:14 - (-5h) = 10:14, which the formula reproduces. `isUtc` is the presence of a 'Z' segment. THE DIVERGENCE IS AT THE ROLL BOUNDARY, AND IT IS A HARD FAILURE ON LEGAL SOURCE. The loops `while (secs < 0) { secs += 86400m; day--; }` / `while (secs >= 86400m) { secs -= 86400m; day++; }` move the LOCAL `day` outside the §15.5.2 range `FormattedDatetime` validated on entry, and `day` is then used unguarded at `DateTime dt = Epoch.AddDays(day - 1)`. Top end, every argument legal (argument-2 = 3067671 the §15.5.2 maximum, argument-3 = 86399 < 86400 per §15.5.5, argument-4 = -1439 with |v| <= 1439 per r5, argument-1 a basic combined UTC format): 86399 + 86340 = 172739 >= 86400, so day becomes 3067672 and `Epoch.AddDays(3067671)` yields 10000-01-01, past DateTime.MaxValue — an uncaught CLR ArgumentOutOfRangeException. I re-derived the boundary independently from the runtime's own INTEGER-OF-DATE algebra (1601-01-01 + 3,067,670 days = 9999-12-31 exactly, so +3,067,671 overflows) and confirmed there is no catch-all in `CobolDate`, in `ExceptionState` or in the generated program: `ExceptionState.ArgumentError` only throws `CobolFatalException` when `ArgumentFunctionChecking` is set, and nothing wraps `AddDays`. Bottom end: argument-2 = 1, argument-3 = 0, argument-4 = +1439 gives day = 0 -> 1600-12-31, and the year subfield emits 1600, violating §15.3.1.3 ('shall contain a value greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999') silently. §15.3's argument paragraph covers 'an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE', so the conforming behaviour is EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION plus the implementor-defined default (A.1 item 90), not an abort in the host runtime where no declarative can see it. SIBLING: `CobolDate.FormattedTime` reaches the same line whenever the format carries a date field. TEST: none for §15.40. `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedTime_UtcRollAcrossMidnight_2014` drives this shared path via §15.41 with a time-only format — corroboration only, and it cannot reach the boundary.

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. Citation re-validated: §15.40.4 r3. THE PRIOR PASS GRADED THE SAME DEFECT TWO WAYS: it marked AR-15.40.3-4 DIVERGES because a floating-point argument-3 is silently corrupted, then listed that identical corruption as edge (c) of this row and left the row PARTIAL. r3's whole content is that argument-3 is 'reflected DIRECTLY in the time portion' — a value whose fractional seconds are silently truncated away is not reflected directly, so this row carries the divergence at least as squarely as AR-15.40.3-4 does. WHAT IS RIGHT, re-traced: an offset format has no 'Z' segment, so `isUtc` is false and the `if (hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset)` block is skipped — argument-3 reaches hh/mm/ss/fraction untouched, which is exactly how r3 differs from r2. `Tokenize`'s '+' case sets `afterOffSign`, so the following 'hh'/'mm' runs become OffHour/OffMinute (§15.3.3.6.1's five-character basic subformat; with a colon the six-character extended one), and `EmitFormatted` renders `osign` from the SIGN of argument-4 and oh/om from `Math.Abs(offsetMinutes)` split at 60. Checked against D.31.5.7's corrected format: argument-4 = +300 -> '+0500' with the time portion '05142781' unadjusted; -30 -> '-0030'. WHY DIVERGES, not merely PARTIAL: (a) the float truncation above corrupts the value being 'reflected directly' on legal source (a COMP-2 item is class numeric; Table 21 types argument-3 `Num3`); (b) NEW — under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` an arithmetic-expression argument-3 or argument-4 renders as `(long)(CobolDec…)`, which does not compile (see AR-15.40.3-3); (c) argument-4's magnitude is never checked, so 'directly' includes reflecting 2000 minutes as offset-hours 33, illegal per §15.3.3.6.2, and 9999 minutes as a three-character subfield that lengthens the value beyond the format; (d) argument-3's range is never checked, and the `(int)` casts on hh/mi/ss wrap rather than merely widening; (e) `afterOffSign` is never reset once set, so any later 'hh'/'mm' run in a malformed format is silently re-classified as offset fields. NOT EXERCISED AT ALL: the extended offset subformat '+hh:mm' — the tokenizer has the ':' case and reading it says it works, but no test drives it. TEST: none.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (PARTIAL -> DIVERGES). Rule (cite-verified §15.41.3 1)): "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal." The adjudicator was right that the NATIONAL-OR-ALPHANUMERIC half is unenforced, but missed that the LITERAL half FALSELY REJECTS a legal literal form and that its own proposed fix cannot work. (a) FALSE REJECTION — the reason this is DIVERGES, not PARTIAL. ExpressionBinder#RefExpr resolves a bare constant-name BEFORE name resolution and routes any non-numeric one to NonNumericConstantExpr -> COBOLNET0844 ("…is not a numeric operand (ISO §8.8.1.1 / §13.10.3 SR2)") — and that arm IGNORES the OperandContext parameter that rides every other call, so OperandContext.FunctionArgument (the whole point of ExpressionBinder#BindFunctionArgumentExpr, whose doc comment says the §8.8.1.1 screen "does not apply" to arguments) does not suppress it. `01 TFMT CONSTANT AS "hh:mm:ss".` + `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(TFMT, 45296) TO R.` draws COBOLNET0844 AND then COBOLNET1517 (args[0] is a BoundOperandError, not a BoundStringLiteral) — two diagnostics on source §13.10.4 GR1 makes equivalent to writing the literal. The bug is not FORMATTED-TIME-shaped: the same arm rejects `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(C)` and `FUNCTION TRIM(C)` over an alphanumeric constant-name, where §15.97.3/§15.96.3 plainly admit the operand — so even on the narrowest reading of §13.10.3 SR2 ("anywhere that a FORMAT specifies a literal") the mechanism is wrong here, because for FORMATTED-TIME it cites §8.8.1.1 arithmetic-operand rules at a programmer who wrote a format literal. (b) The class half: unenforced, as adjudicated — B"0101" binds to BoundStringLiteral{Category=Boolean} and passes COBOLNET1517, failing only at run time inside CobolDate.Tokenize. (c) ⛔ THE ADJUDICATOR'S PROPOSED FIX DOES NOT FIX IT, and this is the part a merged record must not inherit: IntrinsicArgumentRules#ClassOf maps `BoundStringLiteral => CobolClass.Alphanumeric` UNCONDITIONALLY, never reading BoundStringLiteral.Category. Adding a FORMATTED-TIME ('s', …) row to Verified would therefore still admit B"0101" (boolean reported as alphanumeric) and would still be unable to distinguish national from alphanumeric — the §8.5.2.1 class of a national/boolean LITERAL is not recoverable from that screen as built. Fixing r1's class half requires ClassOf to honour Category first. (d) §15.41.1's function-type table (Alphanumeric->Alphanumeric, National->National) is still unimplemented as adjudicated — IntrinsicCatalog hardcodes IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric and only UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE/REVERSE and MAX/MIN follow their argument. See defects.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: Was DIVERGES. FORMATTED-TIME now requires a TIME format; a DATE format is rejected with COBOLNET1631 where it previously fabricated a value. The golden covers the common-time shapes of 15.3.3.1/15.3.3.2 plus the UTC (15.3.3.5) and offset (15.3.3.6) forms, including the extended offset subformat pairing 15.3.3.6.1 requires.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: CONFIRMED, with the evidence re-derived independently and one addition. Rule (cite-verified §15.41.3 3)): "Argument-2 shall be a value in standard numeric time form"; §15.5.5 (cite-verified) = a numeric value representing seconds past midnight, >= 0 and < 86,400 under LEAP-SECOND OFF (the only mode this compiler implements). NO enforcement on either axis, re-verified mechanically: `grep -rn '1439\|86400' src/Cobol.Net.Compiler src/Cobol.Net.Runtime --include=*.cs` (Generated/ excluded) returns 86400 ONLY at CobolDate.cs's two normalization `while` loops and an unrelated CobolTiming.MaxSeconds constant — never as a validation of argument-2. The asymmetry with the siblings in the same file is real: FormattedDate and FormattedDatetime both range-check 1..3,067,671 and call Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError; FormattedTime's body is a bare forward to EmitFormatted. CLASS is equally unscreened — FORMATTED-TIME is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (I read the table; the landed PB1 screen only runs for the 15 named rows), and NumericRenderer#Visit(BoundStringLiteral) renders an alphanumeric argument-2 as CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(...), so `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss", "ABC")` compiles clean. Per §15.3 an out-of-range argument-2 must SET EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (only the result is implementor-defined); it is not set. ADDITION the adjudicator did not reach: the value channel is defective even for an IN-RANGE argument-2 — see RV-15.41.4-1 — so "argument-2 is not validated" is the smaller half of this rule's exposure.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: CONFIRMED, evidence re-derived. Rule (cite-verified §15.41.3 4)): argument-3 is an INTEGER offset from UTC in minutes; if specified, |value| <= 1439. NEITHER half implemented. Magnitude: `grep -rn 1439 src/Cobol.Net.Compiler src/Cobol.Net.Runtime --include=*.cs` returns NOTHING outside Generated/ parser tables — the bound exists nowhere in compiler or runtime (I ran it; the adjudicator's claim holds). EmitFormatted computes oh = |off|/60, om = |off|%60 and renders each with ToString("00"), so 2000 minutes emits offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 (cite-verified: "The offset-hours subfield … shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive") and overrunning the subformat's five/six character width. INTEGER-ness: IntrinsicCatalog declares FORMATTED-TIME ArgKinds "snn" — argument-3 'n' (numeric) where §15.3 type 6 (cite-verified: "An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified") makes it an integer; dormant because the function is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, and IntrinsicRenderer#ArgInt truncates a fractional argument-3 silently. Secondary consequence, re-verified by reading: the normalization pair `while (secs < 0) { secs += 86400m; day--; }` / `while (secs >= 86400m)` is unbounded, so a large argument-3 iterates ~|a3|/1440 times (effective hang) and on the shared FORMATTED-DATETIME path drives `day` far enough for DateTime.AddDays to throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException out of the generated program. One fix site (EmitFormatted) serves FORMATTED-TIME, FORMATTED-DATETIME and FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: CONFIRMED (code-location supplied — the adjudicator left it EMPTY, which under the review's own rule 5 would read as "not located"; the rule's absence is locatable at the bind chokepoint where it belongs). Rule (cite-verified §15.41.3 5)): "Argument-3 shall not be specified if the time portion of the format in argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format." Nothing anywhere correlates the argument COUNT with the KIND of the format literal, re-verified by reading all three layers: IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore checks arity 2..3 (COBOLNET1504) and literal-ness (COBOLNET1517) and nothing else; IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedTime sets `hasOff = ic.Args.Count > 2` with no reference to the format text; CobolDate#EmitFormatted derives `isUtc` from a 'Z' segment and renders offset subfields only if the format carries them — so with a plain LOCAL format the third argument is computed, passed, and silently DISCARDED. Argument-1 is a literal by r1, so the format kind is known at compile time and this is statically distinguishable under §4.2.2 paragraph 3 (cite-verified). The classifier this needs is the same one AR-15.41.3-2 needs; they are one fix, not two. Over-acceptance of illegal source, not a false rejection.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL). Rule (cite-verified §15.41.3 6)): argument-3 omitted with a UTC or offset format ⇒ "the function shall be evaluated AS THOUGH 0 were specified for argument-3". The adjudicator's central claim — "the skip is behaviourally identical to specifying 0" — is NOT TRUE AS STATED, and the difference is visible in the very code it quoted. The block is `if (hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset) { secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m; while (secs < 0) {…} while (secs >= 86400m) {…} }`. Omitting argument-3 skips the WHOLE block including the two NORMALIZATION loops; specifying 0 executes it. The subtraction is a no-op at 0, but the loops are not: they normalize `secs` into [0, 86400). So the two forms agree only while argument-2 already lies in [0, 86400) — which is exactly what r3 requires and NOTHING ENFORCES (AR-15.41.3-3 = NOT-IMPLEMENTED). Demonstrable divergence between the two forms the rule declares equivalent: FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hh:mm:ssZ", 90000) ⇒ "25:00:00Z" (block skipped, hh = 90000/3600 = 25) versus FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hh:mm:ssZ", 90000, 0) ⇒ "01:00:00Z" (loop subtracts 86400). r6 states an EQUIVALENCE; the implementation achieves it by coincidence inside one range rather than structurally, so the row is PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. The offset-format half of r6 is correct on reading (offsetMinutes = 0 ⇒ oh = 0, om = 0, osign '+' because the test is `offsetMinutes >= 0`, satisfying §15.3.3.6.1's receiving-field rule that a zero magnitude take a plus sign, cite-verified) — but it has NO executable evidence at all: the only omitted-argument-3 case in tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob is T1, a LOCAL format "hh:mm:ss", which does not exercise this rule, and that file is a characterization snapshot (non-qualifying) regardless. test-ref left empty.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (PARTIAL -> DIVERGES) and the code-location MOVED — the adjudicator audited the runtime formatter and never audited the ARGUMENT CHANNEL that feeds it, which is where the returned value stops being a representation of argument-2. Rule (cite-verified §15.41.4 1)): "The returned value is a representation of the standard numeric time contained in argument-2 according to the format in argument-1." (1) ⛔ A FLOATING-POINT argument-2 SILENTLY LOSES ITS FRACTION. §15.3 type 10 (cite-verified) — "Numeric. An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified" — so a USAGE FLOAT-LONG item is a legal argument-2. RenderFormattedTime emits `(long)({sec.Expr}), {sec.Scale}` from `NumX sec = ArgNum(ic.Args[1])`, and NumericRenderer's Place switch returns a float leaf as `new NumX(CobolFloat.Sending((double)(read)), 0, Real: true)` — SCALE 0, value in the double. RenderFormattedTime never reads `.Real`, so the whole fractional part is truncated away. Repro: `01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 45296.5.` / `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss.ss", FL) TO R.` prints 12345600, not 12345650. NumericRenderer's own comment at that arm names this exact bug class — "NOT truncated to (long) at scale 0 (the pre-D16 stub that silently dropped the fraction)" — RenderFormattedTime, RenderFormattedDatetime and the CombinedDatetime arm are still that stub. (2) UNSCALED OVERFLOW. `(long)(sec.Expr)` takes the UNSCALED value: with argument-2 < 86,400 at scale s the unscaled magnitude reaches 8.64e4 x 10^s and passes long.MaxValue (9.22e18) at s = 15. `01 T PIC 9(5)V9(15) VALUE 45296.5.` is 20 digits — legal 2002+ and PicInfo.IsWide, i.e. Int128-backed — so the cast is an UNCHECKED truncation and the result is silently garbage (a decimal-backed operand throws System.OverflowException instead). (3) THE ADJUDICATOR'S OWN FINDING CONFIRMED: at a fractional-seconds width >= 19, `(long)(frac * (decimal)(long)Pow10.AsWide(s.Width))` wraps the Int128 10^19 negative and the decimal->long narrowing throws; and `(decimal)(long)Pow10.AsWide(secScale)` wraps the same way for an argument-2 SCALE >= 19, making the divisor negative. §15.3.3.2 (cite-verified) obliges the implementor to DEFINE the maximum fraction width (">= nine"); none is defined or diagnosed. (4) CORRECTION TO INHERITED REASONING — do not carry this forward: D.31.5.6 does NOT corroborate that the fraction is TRUNCATED rather than rounded. 18867.812479168304 under "hhmmss.ss" gives 81.2479…, which truncates AND rounds to 81; the example cannot distinguish them, so the truncate-vs-round choice is unverified against the standard and undocumented. What DOES verify by reading: hh/mi/ss decomposition, Tokenize's `extended` flag making the decimal separator a phantom in a basic format and a data character in an extended one per §15.3.3.2, and the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA case (Tokenize's default arm takes '.' or ',' and re-emits whichever the format carries). Corroboration only (non-qualifying): tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.out lines T1/T2/T3, which use only PIC 9(5) integer seconds and exercise none of (1)-(3). See defects.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL). Rule (cite-verified §15.41.4 2)): with a UTC format the time portion "reflects the adjustment of the value in argument-2 by the offset in argument-3". WHAT SURVIVES: the SIGN DIRECTION is right and is closed by a genuinely spec-derived test. I checked the test's oracle rather than its filename — AssertSpec compiles and runs COBOL.NET ONLY and asserts a hard-coded literal (no DifferentialGolden, no AssertSameAsLegacy, no snapshot), and "23:00:00Z" is derived from §15.3.3.6.1 item 1 (cite-verified: a plus sign means "the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC", i.e. UTC = local - offset), matching `secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m`. WHY IT IS NOT CONFORMS: (a) the rule says "the value in ARGUMENT-2" is what gets adjusted, and the channel delivering that value is defective for a whole legal argument class — a FLOAT-LONG argument-2 arrives already truncated to whole seconds, and an argument-2 at scale >= 15 arrives wrapped (RV-15.41.4-1 items 1-2). The adjustment is then applied to the wrong number, so the rule's own subject is only conditionally satisfied. (b) ONE POLARITY, ONE FORMAT. The single test uses +120 with "hh:mm:ssZ" and integer seconds. The NEGATIVE-offset upward adjustment of §15.3.3.6.1 item 2 — for which the standard supplies a checkable pair in §15.3.3.6.1 NOTE 1 ("1014278124Z" under 'hhmmss.ssssZ' and "0514278124-0500" under 'hhmmss.ssss+hhmm' represent the same instant) — has NO executable evidence, and neither does a UTC format with fractional seconds. Under the review's own rule 5 a rule verified in one direction is PARTIAL. (c) The adjustment loop is unbounded pending the missing |a3| <= 1439 bound (charged on AR-15.41.3-4, restated here because it is this rule's arithmetic).

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL). Rule (cite-verified §15.41.4 3)): with an offset format, argument-2 goes DIRECTLY into the time portion AND argument-3 DIRECTLY into the offset portion — an explicitly CONJUNCTIVE rule, and the review's rule 5 makes a rule with two halves where one is defective a PARTIAL. HALF ONE FAILS: "the value in argument-2 is reflected directly in the time portion" is not true for every legal argument-2. IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedTime hands the runtime `(long)(sec.Expr)` at `sec.Scale`, ignoring NumX.Real, so a USAGE FLOAT-LONG argument-2 (a numeric data item, legal under §15.3 type 10, cite-verified) is reflected only to whole seconds — `01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 45296.5.` with "hhmmss.ss+hhmm" emits 12345600+0000 rather than 12345650+0000 — and an argument-2 at scale >= 15 is reflected as a wrapped Int128. What is 'direct' about the time portion is only the ABSENCE of the UTC adjustment, which the adjudicator verified correctly (the block is guarded by `isUtc`, false with no 'Z' segment). HALF TWO HOLDS on reading: Tokenize flips `afterOffSign` at the '+' so the following hh/mm become Fld.OffHour/Fld.OffMinute (§15.3.3.6.1), EmitFormatted renders osign = (offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'), oh = |off|/60, om = |off|%60, and the extended "+hh:mm" subformat emits its colon from the format (§15.3.3.6.1 final paragraph, cite-verified). EVIDENCE IS THINNER THAN RECORDED: the only executable case anywhere is golden line T3 = 123456+0200 — basic subformat, POSITIVE offset, integer seconds — a characterization snapshot and therefore corroboration only. The negative offset (-300 ⇒ "-0500", the §15.3.3.6.1 item 2 direction) and the extended "+hh:mm" subformat have NO executable evidence of any kind. test-ref empty.

subject: FRACTION-PART function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES, and the OVER-ACCEPT IS WIDER THAN REPORTED. Citation re-validated: cite.py --check 15.42.3 "Argument-1 shall be of the class numeric." -> OK, rule 1; it resolves through 8.5.2.1 Table 2's CLASS column. (a) UNENFORCED, re-verified by reading: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified holds exactly 19 entries (ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI, ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, ANNUITY, CHAR, CHAR-NATIONAL, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER, COMBINED-DATETIME) -- FRACTION-PART is absent, and CheckArgumentClasses returns on its FIRST line (`if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;`), so COBOLNET1627 can never fire for this function. THE PRIOR PASS UNDERCOUNTED THE SILENTLY-ACCEPTED SHAPES: reading NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore end to end, FOUR distinct non-numeric argument classes reach the emitter with zero diagnostics, and every one of them lands on the `scale <= 0 ? 0` branch of the runtime body, i.e. FABRICATES 0 -- (1) ALPHANUMERIC (`PIC X(4)`) -> `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(...)` at SCALE 0; (2) NATIONAL, which the prior pass never mentioned -- it shares the SAME `{ Category: Alphanumeric or National }` arm, also scale 0, and 8.5.2.1 Table 2 makes it class NATIONAL, equally excluded by r1; (3) a REFERENCE-MODIFIED argument (`FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(A(1:2))`), class alphanumeric by 8.4.2.4 -- FieldNumCore's leading `p is RefModPlace` arm, again FromAlphanumeric at scale 0; (4) a GROUP item, which is class alphanumeric by 8.5.2.1 and is NOT caught by the 8.8.1.1 arithmetic screen because OperandContext.FunctionArgument deliberately suppresses it -- `null when p.Item.IsImageCapable` -> FromAlphanumeric(AsImage()) at scale 0 (a float/COMP-5/INDEX group falls to LoudValue instead). The sharpest shape stays the prior pass's REPRO B: a NUMERIC-EDITED argument (`PIC Z9.99`, class ALPHANUMERIC by Table 2) de-edits through the INSTANCE FieldNum arm (`CobolEdit.DeEdit` at MaskScale) and answers a PLAUSIBLE 0.75 -- an illegal program accepted and looking right. The internal inconsistency is the evidence: the identical violation on the identical operand is REJECTED for ABS (conformance:negative/pb1-numeric-arg-alphanumeric and .../pb1-numeric-arg-numeric-edited) purely because ABS is registered. Per-function registration follow-on to the landed PB1 MECHANISM, not a re-report of PB1. (b) UNDER-ACCEPT re-verified: 15.3 type 10 admits an arithmetic expression, and a compound argument under a standard arithmetic mode is a Roslyn CS1503 -- see the FMT-15.42.2 and RV-15.42.4-1 notes and defect 2. EDITIONS derived from the spec, not from the catalog row: FRACTION-PART is absent from the 42-function 1989 Amendment Intrinsic Function Module (corroborated in-repo by `grep -rn FRACTION tests/nist/` returning nothing across the exhaustive IF101A..IF142A suite), so 85 is excluded; Annex E lists no FRACTION-PART change, so it is unaltered 2014->2023. No spec-derived fixture exists for either direction -- test-ref intentionally empty.

subject: FRACTION-PART function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. A SECOND broken leg, missed by the prior pass, and it is a SILENT WRONG VALUE rather than a compile error. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.42.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is:" -> OK r1; ... "where the argument for the INTEGER-PART function is the same as for the FRACTION-PART function itself." -> OK r1; cite.py --check 15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression." -> OK r1; cite.py --check 15.49.4 -> OK (INTEGER-PART is SIGN*INTEGER(ABS), truncation toward zero, so FRACTION-PART keeps the ARGUMENT's sign -- the +1.5/-1.5 NOTE pair). NEW FINDING -- THE FLOAT ARGUMENT BYPASSES SDIDI ENTIRELY UNDER A STANDARD ARITHMETIC MODE. 15.4.1 r1 is normative and unconditional: under standard-decimal/standard-binary the returned value SHALL EQUAL the EAE, which 8.8.1.5.1 requires be evaluated in SDIDI form after converting a float operand in. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum instead runs `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(...); if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(...);` with NO arithmetic-mode guard whatsoever, and NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore's `{ IsFloat: true }` arm sets `Real: true` UNCONDITIONALLY -- so a COMP-2 argument routes to `FractionPartReal(v) => v - Math.Truncate(v)` in binary64 and quantizes through FromDouble at max(Receiver.Scale, 9), never touching CobolDec. THE COMPILER CONTRADICTS ITSELF, which is what makes this a defect rather than latitude: the SAME rule is written down correctly in three sibling seams and missing in this one -- NumericRenderer.CombineCore tests `if (StandardDecimal)` BEFORE its D16 float branch; NumericRenderer.Power does the same; ConditionRenderer guards `if ((l.Real || rr.Real) && !num.StandardDecimal)` and lifts via DecOperand otherwise, with a comment saying exactly why. So the hand-written EAE `D - FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(D)` and `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(D)` disagree -- precisely the equality 15.4.1 NOTE 2 states must hold. CONCRETE DIVERGENCE (small operands hide it, which is why the one golden value passes): D COMP-2 = 1234567890.123, receiver PIC 9V9(9), ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. SDIDI: the 8.8.1.5.1 float lift is the shortest-round-trip decimal 1234567890.123, EAE = 1234567890.123 - 1234567890 = 0.123000000 exactly. ACTUAL: binary64 holds 1234567890.1230000257..., the subtraction catastrophically cancels to 0.12300002574920654, FromDouble at scale 9 gives 0.123000026. Wrong, silent, and invisible to output-sampling on 3.5 -> 0.5. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's MeanScaled arm shows the gap was KNOWN for one function (`if (num.StandardDecimal && !anyReal)` with a comment that a float argument 'falls to the native rendering below') and never generalized. SECOND broken leg (as previously reported, re-verified): a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression argument under a standard mode is a Roslyn CS1503 -- Arg() returns CombineCore's `NumX(CobolDec..., 0, Dec: true)`, the FractionPart arm has no Dec arm, and CobolDec declares no conversion to Int128. Two legs of the one returned-value rule contradicted => DIVERGES, not PARTIAL. WHAT IS GENUINELY RIGHT (re-verified by reading, both carriers, both signs, and the edges the prior pass did not enumerate): `FractionPart(Int128 v, int scale) => scale <= 0 ? 0 : v % Pow10.AsWide(scale)` IS v - trunc(v) on the unscaled carrier -- C# % truncates toward zero and takes the dividend's sign, so -375 @ scale 2 gives -75; an INTEGER argument and a PICTURE-P TRAILING-scaled argument (negative scale) both correctly give 0 at that scale, and a PICTURE-P LEADING argument (`PIC PPP999`, scale 6 > digits) correctly returns the whole value; a negative literal (`-3.75` -> unscaled -375 @ 2) gives -0.75. The result is returned at the ARGUMENT's own scale, which is exact -- nothing is rounded away. NEGATIVE FINDING, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-CHASED: I suspected `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(7 / 2)` in a receiver-less context (ReceiverContext.None, scale 0) would collapse to 0 via a scale-0 intermediate quotient. It does not -- NumericRenderer.Divide's non-outermost branch uses ds = baseScale + min(DivGuardDigits=14, 20-...) guard digits and Arg() always renders with outermost:false, so the quotient arrives at scale 14 and the fraction survives. No defect there. UNTESTED LEGS: the ONLY FRACTION-PART fixture in the Cobol.Net corpus is conformance:2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family, one value -- COMP-2 3.5 into a COMP-2 receiver, golden `0.5` -- i.e. positive, float argument, FLOAT receiver (so RenderFloat's FromDouble quantizer is not even on that path). The NOTE's sign-discriminating -1.5 -> -0.5 case is NOT covered for FRACTION-PART even though C = -3.5 exists in that fixture for other functions, and the FIXED-POINT path -- the primary path -- has NO spec-derived test at all. test-ref therefore CLEARED: with the verdict DIVERGES the fixture is corroboration for one shape only, not closure. NON-QUALIFYING CORROBORATION: tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/IntrinsicSpecTests.cs#FractionPart_ReturnsFractionalDigits (0.75/-0.75 from 3.75/-3.75) and tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Runtime/IntrinsicFunctionTests.cs both exercise src/CobolSharp.Runtime/Intrinsics/IntrinsicFunctions.cs -- the LEGACY oracle's `decimal FractionPart(decimal)`, not Cobol.Net at all. To close: conformance goldens (2002 and 2023) over +/- fixed-point, +/- float, an integer argument, a PICTURE-P argument, and BOTH standard-mode argument shapes.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: CONFIRMED DIVERGES, and the record UNDERSTATED it in three ways. Re-verified independently: §15.83.3 has FOUR rules (r4 = 'If native arithmetic is in effect, the usage restrictions for argument-1 shall be implementor-defined' — `cite.py --check 15.83.3` OK) while §15.43.3 and §15.58.3 have exactly THREE; Annex A.1 item 180 names SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC only. §8.5.2.12 item 2 (checked) puts every float usage — binary-char … float-decimal-34 — in category NUMERIC, so a COMP-2 / FLOAT-LONG / FLOAT-BINARY-64 item satisfies r1 and the blanket `if (pic.IsFloat)` COBOLNET1516 rejects legal COBOL under NATIVE arithmetic (the default). THREE ADDITIONS. (a) ⛔ NEW — THE 'shall not be an integer function or numeric function' HALF IS NOT ENFORCED AT ALL FOR A USER-DEFINED FUNCTION. The adjudicator checked only nested INTRINSICS. IntrinsicBinder#OperandOf maps `BoundNumRef r => new BoundFieldOperand(r.Place)` — its own comment says 'a user-function result temp (M2-UDF-1)' — and UdfBinder#BindUserFunction returns exactly `new BoundNumRef(tempPlace)` over a temp cloned from the RETURNING item (§8.4.3.2.4 GR1). So `FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(FUNCTION MY-FN(A))` with MY-FN RETURNING `PIC S9(4)` reaches BindAlgebraicFold as a BoundFieldOperand with Category=Numeric, is ACCEPTED, and folds to +9999 off the temp's PICTURE — no diagnostic, and the UDF is still invoked (the pending BoundCallProgram is emitted) so its side effects run and its value is discarded. §15.2 item 4 (checked) makes a user-defined function returning a numeric item a numeric function, which r1 forbids by name. (b) ⛔ NEW — a second OVER-rejection: LINE-COUNTER / LINAGE-COUNTER / PAGE-COUNTER are data items of category numeric per §8.5.2.12 items 3/4/5 and bind as BoundComputedOperand, so COBOLNET1516 turns them away. (c) The NATIONAL sub-domain of r1 is unreachable: §15.43.1's own type table admits a National argument, and a category-numeric/numeric-edited item with USAGE NATIONAL is staged not-implemented at PictureAnalyzer#Analyze (national-form numeric data, DiagnosticCatalog.NationalData) before it can ever be an argument. ⛔ CORRECTION TO THE MERGED DEFECT TEXT: 'the fold's BoundNumLiteral carrier (Int128 unscaled + scale) cannot express 1.797E308, so this is a structural change to the result carrier' is FALSE. `BoundNumLiteral` is `record BoundNumLiteral(string Text)` — a STRING carrier — and EmitCore#UnscaledLit already has the floating path (`if (t.IndexOf('E') >= 0) return new NumX(t, 0, Real: true)`). Only IntrinsicBinder#Decimalize is fixed-point. The float arm is a new branch plus a Decimalize sibling, not a carrier redesign; the estimate should be corrected DOWN, not up. Still no spec-derived negative test in either direction.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, and the EDITION WINDOW WAS WRONG. (1) EDITIONS. Both concepts this rule names arrive at COBOL-2014, not 2002: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.5) and the §3.166 standard binary floating-point usages ('usages float-binary-32, float-binary-64, and float-binary-128' — checked mechanically), i.e. USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-32/64/128 (§13.18.60.4 GR14–GR16). Neither exists at COBOL-2002, so the rule as worded cannot be evaluated at 2002. The adjudicator wrote 2002,2014,2023 on all six rows without deriving any of them. (2) VERDICT. By the stated rule 'code not located ⇒ NOT-IMPLEMENTED': the adjudicator's own finding is that NOTHING in BindAlgebraicFold reads ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic (the only arithmetic-mode test in IntrinsicBinder is the ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION staging arm), so there is no code for this rule and citing BindAlgebraicFold as its code-location is citing the code of a DIFFERENT rule. Today's incidental coverage comes entirely from the blanket `pic.IsFloat` ban that AR-15.43.3-1 finds DIVERGENT — a rule enforced only by a bug is not implemented. (3) ⛔ NEW — THE ONE PLACE THE CODE CITES RULE 2, IT MIS-STATES IT. The COBOLNET1516 message asserts '…under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is barred by rule 2' while the guard fires for COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-EXTENDED — none of which is a standard binary floating-point usage under §3.166. That is a false statement of the rule shipped in a user-visible diagnostic, and it is precisely the inherited-citation failure mode. Confirmed live-and-writable: OptionsBinder#ArithmeticOf maps STANDARD-DECIMAL to ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal (only STANDARD-BINARY is rejected, at DataBinder COBOLNET0806), and FLOAT-BINARY-32/64 are LIVE usages (PicInfo#ClrType → float/double). FLOAT-BINARY-128 is out of reach (COBOLNET1564, Annex A.3 item 17). No spec-derived test.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, same two grounds as rule 2. (1) EDITIONS: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.4) and the §3.167 standard decimal floating-point usages (float-decimal-16, float-decimal-34 — USAGE per §13.18.60.4 GR17/GR18) are both COBOL-2014 additions; the rule as worded does not exist at COBOL-2002. (2) VERDICT: no code implements this rule anywhere — the prohibited combination is doubly unreachable through two INDEPENDENT non-supports that have nothing to do with §15.43, so nothing has ever evaluated the rule's condition. Both non-supports are conformance-legal and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them: DataBinder rejects STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806, and Annex A.3 item 2 reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (NOTE 1 adds that the mode is obsolete); FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are rejected at ParseUsage with COBOLNET1564 under A.3 item 19. Worth recording for whoever revisits this: A.3 item 3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent TOO, so COBOL.NET's support for it is a choice, not an obligation — which is why rule 2's combination is writable and rule 3's is not. Vacuous truth is not implementation: if either half is ever supported, nothing enforces this. No spec-derived test, and none constructible.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: VERDICT CONFIRMED, EDITION WINDOW CORRECTED, and one further reason added. The rule constrains exactly one construct — a floating-point numeric-edited item (an external floating-point PICTURE, symbol E) — and PictureAnalyzer#Analyze stages that NOT-IMPLEMENTED (Constructs.PicExternalFloat2002 → COBOLNET0899 at ≥2002 / COBOLNET0900 below) and returns PicInfo.Recovery, so the item never acquires PicCategory.NumericEdited and can never be presented to HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC. Nothing implements the rule; the construct's absence merely makes it unreachable — a green-looking zero fan-out. ⛔ ADDED: the rule's OTHER half is also absent. The well-formedness test it prescribes is an IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE class condition (§8.5's class-condition format, GR l: 'the condition is true if the numeric content … is neither farther from zero nor closer to zero than is permitted for the form of an intermediate data item appropriate to the mode of arithmetic in effect'), and IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE exists in COBOL.NET ONLY as a row in ReservedWords.Table — there is no grammar production, no binder arm and no ConstructRegistry row. So neither the domain nor the test exists. EDITIONS corrected to 2014,2023: the rule's domain (external float PICTURE) is a 2002 construct, but IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE is part of the COBOL-2014 IEEE-754 class-condition package (alongside FLOAT-INFINITY / FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER / FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO / NEAREST-TO-ZERO; the reserved-word table records 'added 2014'), so the rule AS WORDED cannot be stated at COBOL-2002. Re-adjudicate the day external floating-point PICTUREs land. No spec-derived test is constructible.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → DIVERGES. A rule that returns a value the program cannot use, and in one reachable case CRASHES AT RUN TIME, does not get to sit at PARTIAL. ⛔ NEW DEFECT the adjudicator missed — read from the code, PB7-shaped (compiles clean, throws at run time). For an UNSIGNED COMP-5 item of 19–31 digits the container branch computes `bits = 8 * pic.StorageWidth` where PicInfo#StorageWidth gives 16 for Usage.Comp5 with Digits > 18, so `unscaled = (BigInteger.One << 128) − 1` = 340282366920938463463374607431768211455. BigInteger does not mask the shift, so the value is genuine and 39 digits wide — it exceeds Int128.MaxValue, takes Decimalize's BigInteger fallback, and EmitCore#IntLiteral renders any magnitude over 18 digits as `Int128.Parse("…")`. `01 W PIC 9(19) COMP-5.` … `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(W)` therefore COMPILES CLEAN and throws OverflowException when the emitted Int128.Parse runs. PIC 9(19) is legal at 2002+ (EditionInfo#MaxDigits = 31) and nothing restricts COMP-5's digit count. IntrinsicBinder#Decimalize's own doc comment asserts this is impossible — 'Nothing here currently produces one — the widest value is all-nines over 38 digit positions … or a 128-bit COMP-5 container bound' — which is exactly the unverified claim that hid it: an unsigned 128-bit container bound is 2^128−1, twice Int128.MaxValue. (Signed S9(19) COMP-5 lands on exactly Int128.MaxValue and survives; only the unsigned leg crashes.) ⛔ NEW — the runtime does NOT agree with the fold, contrary to the merged defect #2's premise. CobolNum#WrapBinary computes `Int128 modulus = (Int128)1 << bits`; C# masks an Int128 shift count to 7 bits, so at bits = 128 the modulus is 1 and the runtime capacity of a 16-byte COMP-5 collapses to [0,1). The fold says 2^128−1, the runtime says 0. 'The fold agrees with the runtime's declared capacity' is true only for StorageWidth ≤ 8. CONFIRMED from the record: an unsigned COMP-5 of 10–18 digits folds to 2^64−1 while PicInfo#ClrType gives `long` for the same item — a value the item's own emitted field cannot hold. ⛔ TEST-REF OVERSTATED. The golden is spec-derived (header cites §15.43/§15.58 + Annex D.32, values hand-derived), but it covers only TWO of the seven §15.43.4 NOTE rows — 99V9(3)→+99.999 and $**,**9.99→+99999.99 (printed as +99999.990 by the PIC +99999.999 receiver). Its S99 and S9(4)-DISPLAY lines are NOT NOTE rows; the adjudicator counted them as such. S999, S9(4) BINARY, $**,**9.99BCR, BINARY-CHAR SIGNED and BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED — the exact rows the NOTE prints because they are the container/mask cases — are exercised by NO test. I traced them by hand and they compute correctly today (BINARY falls to DigitCount → 9999; CobolEdit#MaskCapacity gives (7,2) for $**,**9.99BCR because '$' occurs once so fixedCs suppresses it and FractionDigits breaks at the 'C' of CR; PicInfo#BinaryItem + the container branch give 127/255 with UNSIGNED correctly threaded from DataBinder's binaryUnsigned) — but hand-tracing is not a test. Also verified correct and untested: P-scaling in both branches, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, a non-default CURRENCY PICTURE SYMBOL, floating-string capacity (`hasFloating ? digits − 1 : digits`), and BLANK WHEN ZERO on PIC 9(9) (PictureAnalyzer makes it numeric-edited with EditMask = the expanded nines, so MaskCapacity returns (9,0) — no null-mask crash). Two halves of the rule's domain remain unreachable: floating-point (blocked by the AR-15.43.3-1 over-rejection) and floating-point numeric-edited (RV-15.43.4-1). ⚠ ARCHITECTURAL, carried forward and re-confirmed: the container branch's usage list (Comp5/BinaryChar/BinaryShort/BinaryLong/BinaryDouble) is a hand-maintained duplicate of PicInfo#Truncation's NumericTruncation.BinaryCapacity list; derive the branch from pic.Truncation or pin them with a drift test. ⚠ Citation hygiene in the same method: the Usage.Index guard cites '§13.18.60' where the rule is §13.18.60.4 GR10 — the one-level-short shape.

subject: INTEGER function
notes: CONFIRMED (verdict unchanged), re-derived from the code rather than from the prior record. SPEC (all --check OK): §15.44.3 1) 'Argument-1 shall be of class numeric.'; §15.3 10) 'Numeric. An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified.'; §8.5.2.1 Table 2 read in FULL: class Alphanumeric covers Alphanumeric, Alphanumeric-edited and 'Numeric-edited (if usage is display)'; class National covers National, National-edited and 'Numeric-edited (if usage is national)'; class Index covers category Index. All are excluded by r1. CODE (read, not sampled): Verified holds 20 rows and INTEGER is in NEITHER Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened; IntrinsicBinder#CheckArgumentClasses opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and so returns before inspecting anything. No other screen exists: BindArgOperand deliberately suppresses the §8.8.1.1 arithmetic screen for function arguments, and NumericRenderer#FieldNumCore silently decodes the operand — `{ Category: PicCategory.Alphanumeric or PicCategory.National } => CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(read)` at scale 0 — while FieldNum de-edits a numeric-edited sender through CobolEdit.DeEdit at the mask scale. So PIC X, PIC N and PIC ZZ9.99 arguments all compile clean under strict --std 2023 and all yield a value.
