EDGES THE PRIOR PASS DID NOT CHECK, each verified by reading the switch: (a) a class-BOOLEAN argument produces no §15.44.3 diagnostic either — it renders EmitText.LoudValue, i.e. it COMPILES and throws at RUN TIME, the PB7 failure shape; (b) a GROUP argument renders FromAlphanumeric over .AsImage() (class alphanumeric, still excluded); (c) a REFERENCE-MODIFIED argument is category alphanumeric (§8.4.3.3) and ClassOf does map RefModPlace to Alphanumeric, so it WOULD be caught once a row exists; (d) an INDEX data item and an index-NAME are NOT caught even after the proposed fix — recorded as DEFECT 5, because the CobolClass lattice has no Index member and ClassOfPlace fails open on a PIC-less leaf. EDITIONS: I searched Annex E of the 2023 text mechanically — its only INTEGER-bearing row is 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function 15.13', there is no row for §15.44, so no 2014→2023 delta; only the 2023 text is in-repo, so the 2002/2014 legs are inferred from Annex E's silence and the 85 leg from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment — neither was READ. NO spec-derived test exists for this rule.

subject: INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED: PARTIAL → DIVERGES. PARTIAL was the wrong shape — this is not 'one half verified', it is a rule whose prescribed VALUE is observably wrong on one path and whose legal source does not COMPILE on another. SPEC (all --check OK): §15.44.4 1) 'The returned value is the greatest integer less than or equal to the value of argument-1'; §15.2 5) — the sharper citation the prior pass missed — 'Integer functions. These are of the class and category numeric. An integer function has an operational sign and NO DIGITS TO THE RIGHT OF THE DECIMAL POINT'; §15.4.1 gives implementor latitude over 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value' ONLY when native arithmetic is in effect, and under standard-decimal/standard-binary it REQUIRES the value to sit 'in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect' — no latitude at all on that leg. PATH 1, EXACT FIXED-POINT: CobolIntrinsics.Floor `if (scale <= 0) return v * Pow10.AsWide(-scale); Int128 d = Pow10.AsWide(scale); Int128 q = v/d; return v < 0 && v % d != 0 ? q - 1 : q;` is a true floor — derived correct by reading for all three §15.44.4 NOTE cases, for a P-scaled negative scale (Pow10.AsWide tables 0..38 with a loop fallback, AsWide(0)=1), for FUNCTION INTEGER(ZERO) (Visit(BoundFigurative) → UnscaledLit("0") → 0), and for a nested division argument, where Arg() re-enters AsNum with outermost defaulted false so Divide takes the D2 guard-scale + TRUNCATION branch and INTEGER(-7 / 2) floors -3.50000000000000 to -4 rather than truncating first. NO spec-derived test covers this path. PATH 2, FLOAT ARGUMENT: FloorReal = Math.Floor is right, but IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFloat quantizes at `ws = max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)` with no integer-type arm, so the temporary carries nine fraction digits in direct contradiction of §15.2 5). CobolNum.FormatFunctionText emits `digits[..^scale] + "." + digits[^scale..]` for scale>0, so `DISPLAY FUNCTION INTEGER(comp2)` prints -4.000000000 while `DISPLAY FUNCTION INTEGER(-3.5)` prints -4 — one value, two spellings. The same ws makes CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble saturate at Int128.MaxValue once |v|x10^9 >= 1.7e38, from |v| ~ 1.7e29 — reachable from a DECLARABLE receiver, contrary to the claim in FromDouble's own XML doc, because PictureAnalyzer caps digit positions at 31 (CA33). PATH 3, STANDARD / STANDARD-DECIMAL: no path at all — CombineCore returns `NumX(..., 0, Dec: true)` for every + - * / under a standard mode, RenderNum routes only on `.Real`, and case "Floor" hands the CobolDec to `Floor(Int128,int)`. I read src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolDec.cs in full: `readonly record struct CobolDec(Int128 Sig, int Exp)` declares From/FromDouble/Pow/Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Compare/ToUnscaled/ToDouble/ToFunctionText and NOT ONE conversion operator, so the generated C# cannot compile. TEST-REF QUALIFIED: tests/conformance/2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family.cob IS spec-derived (its header derives INTEGER(-3.5) = -4 from §15.44 and pairs it against INTEGER-PART to discriminate floor from truncation), but its receiver is `01 R USAGE COMP-2`, so RenderFloat takes the `num.Receiver.Real` branch and the fixture NEVER exercises FromDouble for INTEGER and never touches the exact fixed-point body — it pins one slice of one of three paths and cannot catch DEFECT 3. EDITIONS: no Annex E row for §15.44, so §15.44.4 is constant across the window; the standard-decimal leg is reachable at 2014+ and plain STANDARD at 2002+ (Annex E.2 item 21 removes STANDARD at 2023).

subject: INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN function
notes:
REFUTER: verdict SUSTAINED at DIVERGES (already the strongest grade; nothing to downgrade). Every claim was re-verified against the source rather than accepted, two evidence details were corrected, and two code-locations were added.
CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED: `cite.py --check 15.45.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class boolean."` => OK §15.45.3 1). `--check 15.3 "Boolean. A bit group item, a boolean expression or literal, or an elementary boolean data item shall be specified."` => OK §15.3 3) — FOUR admissible shapes.
DEFECT 1 — THE RULE IS NOT SCREENED AT ALL, AND A WRONG-CLASS ARGUMENT PRODUCES A VALUE. `CheckArgumentClasses` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:973) opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;`. I read the WHOLE table line by line: INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN is in NEITHER `Verified` (ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI, ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, ANNUITY, CHAR, CHAR-NATIONAL, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER, COMBINED-DATETIME, EXP, EXP10, FRACTION-PART, INTEGER, FACTORIAL, EXCEPTION-STATEMENT, EXCEPTION-STATUS) NOR `DeliberatelyUnscreened` (BYTE-LENGTH, BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT). Per the brief's item 8 that absence is a genuine finding. ⚠ EMIT ROUTE CORRECTED (the prior write-up named the wrong first hop): `IntrinsicRenderer.Str` is `StrArgVisitor`, not `OperandText.AsString` directly; its `Visit(BoundFieldOperand n) => OperandText.AsString(n, owner.Num)` reaches `FieldAsString`. There, `01 A PIC X(8) VALUE "10101010"` takes the alphanumeric arm `PlaceRenderer.Read(p)` verbatim, and `01 N PIC 9(4) VALUE 1010` takes the `StoreAsImage` arm (zoned DISPLAY — `NonTextBytes` returns null for a zoned item) rather than the `CobolNum.FormatDisplay` arm the prior note named. The VALUES are unchanged: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(A)` returns 170 and the PIC 9(4) case returns 10 — a class-alphanumeric and a class-numeric argument, both forbidden by §15.45.3 r1, both silently ACCEPTED with a computed result and no diagnostic at any --std or strictness.
DEFECT 2 — THE SCREEN CANNOT EXPRESS THIS RULE, AND THE OBVIOUS ROW WOULD REJECT LEGAL SOURCE. `Admissible(char)` has NO code admitting `CobolClass.Boolean`: 'n' and 'i' => [Numeric], 's' => [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National], 'p' => the §15.71.3 negative list, default null. The catalog's unaudited hint column declares INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN as "s" (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:186) — the one kind that EXCLUDES boolean — so screening from the hint (the exact PB1 trap) would reject every conforming argument. A new 'b' kind is required. WORSE, and this must be recorded before anyone adds it: `ClassOfPlace` opens `if (p is RefModPlace) return CobolClass.Alphanumeric;` under the comment '§8.4.2.4 — the result of reference modification is of category alphanumeric'. ⛔ §8.4.2.4 DOES NOT EXIST — `cite.py --check 8.4.2.4 "reference modification"` => 'FAIL: there is no clause §8.4.2.4 in the transcription' (re-run by the refuter). §8.4.2 is Uniqueness of reference with subclauses .1/.2/.3 only; reference modification is §8.4.3.3. The REAL rule is §8.4.3.3.4 GR6: the unique data item 'has the same class, category, and usage as that defined for identifier-1' with only the edited/national exceptions — so a reference-modified BOOLEAN item stays class BOOLEAN. The standard's own worked example for THIS function is `COMPUTE integer-item-2 = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN (bit-item (1:6))` => 032 (Annex D, specs/ISO_COBOL.md:38919), so a naive 'b' row over today's `ClassOfPlace` would reject the standard's own example. The phantom clause is inherited across at least ten files (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:112, OperandText.cs:120, ExpressionBinder.cs, MoveBinder.cs x3, InitializeBinder.cs, OoBinder.cs x3, Place.cs, ReferenceResolver.cs, MoveClassifier.cs) — the CLAUDE.md rule-1 inherited-citation failure mode, and in the boolean/national cases the rule it states is substantively wrong as well.
DEFECT 3 — A FLOAT ARGUMENT PRODUCES A RAW ROSLYN ERROR, CONFIRMED BY READING BOTH SIDES. `RenderNum` line 71 runs `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` BEFORE its switch, and `RealMethod` is a naming CONVENTION (`Xxx` -> `XxxReal`), not a table — so `01 F USAGE COMP-2. COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(F)` emits `CobolIntrinsics.IntegerOfBooleanReal(<double>)`. Grep of the whole src tree for `IntegerOfBooleanReal` returns NOTHING, and the method list in CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs (AbsReal, SignOfReal, FloorReal, TruncateReal, FractionPartReal, ModReal, RemReal, MaxReal, MinReal, SumReal, RangeReal, MedianReal, MidrangeReal, MeanReal, OrdMaxReal, CombinedDatetimeReal, OrdMinReal) confirms it: the generated C# does not compile and the user sees a backend error, not a COBOLNET diagnostic. The guard that should have caught this exempts itself — IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.cs:81 scopes to `.Where(m => m.Groups["k"].Value.Contains('n') || m.Groups["k"].Value.Length == 0)`, and INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN's ArgKinds is "s". The test's stated premise is that an 's' row 'cannot receive a float without violating their own argument rule first, which is PB1's business' — FALSE here precisely because there is no `Verified` row. The exemption and the gap are one hole seen from two sides.
DEFECT 4 — TWO OF THE FOUR §15.3 ITEM-3 SHAPES ARE UNREACHABLE (see FMT-15.45.2 for the full trace): a BIT GROUP ITEM (GROUP-USAGE has no grammar production at all — grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/ is empty; DataBinder.cs:1491 says so outright) and a BOOLEAN EXPRESSION (`functionArgument` has no `booleanExpression` alternative; `BoundBoolOperand` is built only by ConditionBinder). That leaves an elementary boolean data item and a non-empty Format-1 boolean literal.
WHAT DOES EXIST IS A SUBSTRATE CHECK AT RUN TIME, NOT A CLASS CHECK. `CobolIntrinsics.IntegerOfBoolean` rejects any character that is not '0'/'1' via `ExceptionState.ArgumentError`, citing '§15.45.3 r1'. That is a DIFFERENT rule: it catches PIC X(4) VALUE "ABCD" but not PIC X(4) VALUE "1010"; it is a run-time not a compile-time determination (§4.2.2 — an operand's class is a static property of the source, the ground on which PB1's screen was justified for ABS/REVERSE); and with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking OFF, the default, `ArgumentError` simply returns 0, so even the substrate violation is silent.
NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST. Nothing anywhere pins a REJECTION for this argument rule; both AssertSpec tests and the corpus golden pass conforming boolean arguments only. test-ref deliberately EMPTY — no net was reached for.
EDITIONS: 2002,2014,2023, derived from the standard exactly as in FMT-15.45.2 and cross-checked against docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md (no pre-2023 row for these functions; only B-SHIFT-* is listed as the 2023 boolean addition). The IntrinsicCatalog row's own `2002` was NOT used as evidence.

subject: INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN function
notes:
REFUTER: verdict SUSTAINED at PARTIAL. I looked hard for a DIVERGES here and did not find one; the value arithmetic and the boundary were re-derived by hand from the source and are right. Two OVER-CLAIMS in the prior notes are corrected below, and the code-location list is completed (the prior list omitted the two symbols that actually carry the argument's width — `StrArgVisitor` and `PlaceRenderer.Read`).
CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED: `--check 15.45.4 "Argument-1 is assigned to a temporary boolean data item of usage bit described with the same number of boolean positions as argument-1."` => OK §15.45.4 1) a). `--check 15.4 "If the length of the returned value exceeds the maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value, an EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist."` => OK §15.4. `--check A.1 "Function returned values (returned value length exceeds implementor-defined limits)"` => OK §A.1 93) — 'This item is required. The value returned shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.4, Returned values)'. `--check 8.3.3.4.3 "8 191"` => OK SR1.
WHAT IS IMPLEMENTED AND CORRECT (read, not sampled). `IntegerOfBoolean(string boolean)` walks left to right accumulating `v = (v << 1) | (uint)(c - '0')` — the UNSIGNED value of the bit configuration, MOST-SIGNIFICANT FIRST, over exactly the positions argument-1 has (subrules 1b/1c). The argument reaches it as a '0'/'1' string: `RenderNum` case "IntegerOfBoolean" emits `new NumX(RuntimeApi.Intrinsic(sig.RuntimeMethod, Str(ic.Args[0])), 0)`; `Str` is `StrArgVisitor`, whose field arm reaches `OperandText.FieldAsString` and lands on `{ Category: ... or PicCategory.Boolean } => PlaceRenderer.Read(p)` (the D-B1 substrate is one character per boolean position), and whose nested-intrinsic arm re-enters `RenderString` for a boolean-category result. The Annex D worked example IS reachable and correct, and I traced it rather than trusting the prior claim: `FieldAsString` opens `if (p is RefModPlace) return PlaceRenderer.Read(p);`, and `PlaceRenderer.Read` line 31 is `RefModPlace r => RuntimeApi.StrRefMod(Read(r.Inner), RmStart(r), RmLen(r), r.AllowZeroLength)` — a substring of the '0'/'1' image — so `bit-item (1:6)` over B"10000000" arrives as the six-character "100000" and the temporary is six positions wide, giving 032 exactly as specs/ISO_COBOL.md:38919 states. The 63-bit boundary was re-derived by hand: `if (v > long.MaxValue >> 1)` fires at v >= 2^62, so the last admissible step yields 2^63-1 and a 64th significant bit takes the EC — the arithmetic is right, and leading zeros never trip it, so a wide item holding a small value is unaffected.
SPEC-DERIVED TESTS EXIST AND QUALIFY — RE-CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. Despite the file name, `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.AssertSpec` (line 26) is `var (cok, cout, cdetail) = new CobolNetCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun(source); Assert.True(cok); Assert.Equal(CutRunner.Normalize(expected), cout);` — COBOL.NET ONLY, compared to a hand-written expected string, with no legacy leg and no `*MatchesLegacy` shape. `BooleanOfInteger_MsbFirst_LeftTruncates_Spec` does exercise §15.45.4 despite its name (`COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(B-8)` => 128, where an LSB-first defect prints 1 — discriminating). The corpus golden's `.out` is git-tracked and hand-derived from §15.13.4/§15.45.4/Annex D.10, not a captured snapshot. ⚠ ONE LEG IS WEAKER THAN THE PRIOR NOTE ALLOWED: `IntegerOfBoolean_RoundTrip_Spec`'s first leg (200 -> BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER -> INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN -> 200) is SELF-INVERSE and would still pass if BOTH functions were LSB-first — it is structurally blind. Only its second leg (B"00000101" => 5, since LSB-first would give 160) discriminates.
WHY NOT CONFORMS — (i) THE IMPLEMENTOR MAXIMUM IS UNDOCUMENTED. The runtime caps at a signed 64-bit long with the message 'exceeds the 63-bit COBOL.NET integer maximum (§15.4)'. §15.4 genuinely authorises an implementor-defined maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, so the SHAPE of the choice is legal — but §A.1 item 93 makes documenting the value MANDATORY, and it is documented nowhere. I re-checked both candidate homes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md's A.1 register carries only the two §15.4.1 returned-value rows (lines 285-286: the numeric result's text image, and the float-argument evaluation) and no item-93 length row; and grep for INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN across docs/ returns ONLY PHASE4_RECONCILIATION.md (whose text is itself stale — it says these rows 'stay catalog-Deferred', which is no longer true) and the PHASE-11 scout notes. The subsystem SSOT docs/COBOLNET_INTRINSICS_DESIGN.md does not mention the function at all. The maximum exists only as a string literal inside a runtime error message.
(ii) THE CAP IS BELOW THE COMPILER'S OWN INTEGER CAPACITY AND IS NOT A SINGLE IMPLEMENTATION-WIDE MAXIMUM. 63 bits is ~19 decimal digits, while the fixed-point channel is Int128 at 31 digits (EditionInfo MaxDigits 31 at 2002+; PB5/PB13 moved NUMVAL/NUMVAL-C/NUMVAL-F to Int128 for exactly this reason) and §8.3.3.4.3 SR1 permits boolean values up to 8,191 positions. §15.4 speaks of 'THE maximum length specified by the implementor for a returned value' — singular — yet COBOL.NET now has two (19 digits here, 31 elsewhere), neither declared. `01 B70 PIC 1(70) USAGE BIT. ... COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(B70)` into a PIC 9(31) receiver has an exactly representable answer and instead takes EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION — and with checking OFF, the default, `ArgumentError` returns 0, so the program silently receives zero for a value its receiver could hold. This is the one function in the family still on `long`; the maximum looks inherited from the carrier rather than chosen.
(iii) NOTHING TESTS THE BOUNDARY: no test covers 63 vs 64 significant bits, the EC leg with checking ON, a bit-group argument, or the Annex D reference-modified form. All three tests use 8-position arguments.
⚠ CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR NOTES — SUBRULE 1a IS NOT FULLY VERIFIED, AND SAYING 'there is no width to get wrong' ROUNDED UP. The width is carried by construction only for the two argument shapes that are REACHABLE (an elementary boolean item, including the ref-modified form, and a non-empty Format-1 boolean literal). For the two shapes the compiler cannot accept at all — a bit group item and a boolean expression, see FMT-15.45.2 — r1a has never been exercised and cannot be. Half of the rule's domain is untestable, which is itself a reason this row is PARTIAL and not CONFORMS.
TWO FURTHER UNVERIFIED EDGES, recorded so they are not mistaken for coverage. (a) The runtime doc comment asserts 'A zero-length argument ... is value 0 — the natural reading of an empty configuration (no explicit rule)'. That branch is UNREACHABLE, because neither zero-length boolean-literal form lexes (`BOOL_BODY` requires [01]+; BX"…" is deferred, CobolLexer.g4 line 740) — an unreachable arm has never been contradicted. (b) SPEC-INTERNAL TENSION, flagged for whoever revisits the cap and NOT a compiler defect: Table 21 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29938) describes the result as 'The numeric value of a BINARY-DOUBLE item whose bit configuration is the same as argument-1, right-justified', which for a 64-position argument with a leading 1 would be NEGATIVE, whereas §15.45.4 r1b says 'the UNSIGNED binary value'. §15.45.4 is the definition and the summary is a summary; COBOL.NET follows r1b and refuses the 64-bit case, which is the defensible reading.
EDITIONS: 2002,2014,2023 — derived from the standard as in FMT-15.45.2, never from the catalog row.

subject: INTEGER-OF-DATE function
notes: REFUTED UP FROM PARTIAL. The prior pass verified the VALUE half and called the TYPE half merely 'unscreened'; reading the EMISSION path shows the type half is worse than unscreened - it emits a call to a runtime method THAT DOES NOT EXIST, so conforming source fails to compile. (1) THE VALUE HALF STILL HOLDS: CobolDate.IntegerOfDate decomposes yyyymmdd by /10000, /100%100, %100 and rejects year outside 1601..9999 (subrule a), month outside 1..12 (subrule b) and day <1 or >DateTime.DaysInMonth (subrule c); the || short-circuits so DaysInMonth only sees an in-range year/month, and .NET's proleptic Gregorian matches Sec 15.5.1 ('The date conversion functions shall use the Gregorian calendar as described in ISO 8601-1:2019, 4.2.1' - --check verified) over the whole window. Violations route to ExceptionState.ArgumentError -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when checking is enabled, else the Sec 15.3 item-14 implementor-defined 0 ('If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference' - --check verified against Sec 15.3, item 14). (2) NEW, AND THE REASON THIS IS DIVERGES - THE FLOATING-POINT ARGUMENT PATH EMITS A NONEXISTENT METHOD. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum line 71, 'if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod))', fires BEFORE the exact switch, so an argument whose NumX carries Real:true renders as CobolIntrinsics.IntegerOfDateReal(...). grep over the entire tree finds NO IntegerOfDateReal (nor DateOfIntegerReal / DayOfIntegerReal / IntegerOfDayReal / FactorialReal) - CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs stops at Abs/SignOf/Floor/Truncate/FractionPart/Mod/Rem/Max/Min/Sum/Range/Median/Midrange/Mean/OrdMax/OrdMin/CombinedDatetime. The generated C# therefore fails Roslyn with CS0117 after the compiler ACCEPTED the source, breaking this codebase's own stated bind-success-implies-compilable invariant (NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore states it in those words). A CONFORMING repro: 'IF FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(FUNCTION INTEGER(WS-COMP2)) = 1' - a relation operand renders under ReceiverContext.None (Receiverless), so RenderFloat returns NumX(call, 0, Real:true) for the inner INTEGER, the outer call sees AnyRealArgument true, and IntegerOfDateReal is emitted. That source is legal: Sec 15.44.1 makes INTEGER an integer function, Sec 15.2 says a function 'may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified' (--check verified), and Sec 15.3 item 6 admits 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item' (--check verified). The non-conforming direct form 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(WS-COMP2)' hits it too, at ANY receiver, because FieldNumCore returns Real:true for every float leaf. (3) WHY NO EXISTING GUARD CATCHES IT, and why the obvious one-row fix does NOT: IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.NumericArgumentMethods restricts its PB2 completeness guard to catalog rows whose ArgKinds contains 'n' or is empty, on the written assumption that an 'i' function 'cannot receive a float without violating their own argument rule first, which is PB1's business'. But INTEGER-OF-DATE has NO PB1 row at all - it is in NEITHER IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its TryGetValue guard - AND adding the obvious ('i', 'Sec 15.46.3 r1') row would NOT close it, because Admissible('i') is [CobolClass.Numeric] and PicInfo.FloatItem synthesises a float item as new(PicCategory.Numeric, ...), so a COMP-2 is class numeric and the screen ADMITS it. The two halves of PB2 and PB1 each assume the other covers the 'i' family; neither does. (4) THE ORDINARY PB1 HOLE IS ALSO REAL, and the prior pass's description of its second consequence was WRONG: an alphanumeric operand (FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(WS-X), WS-X PIC X(8), or a plain alphanumeric literal) is silently coerced through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric - that part is right - but a FLOAT operand is NOT 'silently truncated by IntArg/AsInt'; it never reaches IntArg, because line 71 diverts first. Only a FIXED-POINT fractional operand (PIC 9(6)V99) is silently truncated to scale 0 by NumRescale(..., Truncation). (5) Sec 8.4.3.2.3 SR11, 'A numeric function shall not be specified where an integer operand is required, even though a particular reference of the numeric function might yield an integer value' (--check verified - note the rule is at 8.4.3.2.3, not 8.4.3.2), is enforced NOWHERE in the tree: grep finds no reference, and ClassOf maps a nested BoundIntrinsicCall to its ResultCategory, so FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(FUNCTION SQRT(4)) binds clean. (6) A narrowing hazard in the same argument path: AsInt renders '(long)(expr)' with no range guard, the generated assembly is compiled unchecked (no CheckOverflow option is set anywhere), and a scale-0 operand wider than 18 digits is carried in Int128 - so an argument at or beyond 2^63 WRAPS into the 1601..9999 window instead of raising EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. The cited test is genuinely spec-derived (AssertSpec compiles with COBOL.NET only and asserts a literal expected string; no legacy oracle) and covers subrule c plus both subrule-a boundaries, but it covers NO argument-type case and no month>12 case, so it does not reach any of the above. SWEEP: the identical shape is open on INTEGER-OF-DAY (Sec 15.47.3 r1), DATE-OF-INTEGER (Sec 15.22.3), DAY-OF-INTEGER (Sec 15.24.3), FACTORIAL (Sec 15.36.3 - which DOES have an 'i' row and is still exposed, per point 3) and the Sec 15.23/15.25/15.100 windowing trio.

subject: INTEGER-OF-DATE function
notes: REFUTED DOWN FROM CONFORMS: the FIXED-POINT-argument path conforms and is pinned; the FLOATING-POINT-argument path produces no returned value at all. VERIFIED: integer date form is Sec 15.5.2 - 'A value in integer date form is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600 ... It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671' (--check verified). CobolDate.Epoch is new DateTime(1601,1,1) and IntegerOfDate returns (new DateTime(y,m,d) - Epoch).Days + 1, so 16010101 -> 1 and 99991231 -> 3067671; I recomputed both endpoints independently against the proleptic Gregorian ordinal and they match the standard's stated constant. The catalog row is IntrinsicType.Integer and the exact arm renders new NumX(CobolDate.IntegerOfDate(...), 0) - scale 0, a C# long, matching Sec 15.46.1 'The type of this function is integer' (--check verified). The 3,067,671 ceiling cannot overflow the long. The cited test is spec-derived (AssertSpec: COBOL.NET only, literal expected string) and pins BOTH Sec 15.5.2 endpoints. NOT VERIFIED / MISSING: (1) on the floating-point-argument path there is NO returned value to be in integer date form - IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum line 71 diverts to RenderFloat before the exact arm and emits CobolIntrinsics.IntegerOfDateReal(...), a method that exists nowhere in the runtime, so the generated C# fails Roslyn compilation. That path is reachable from conforming source (see AR-15.46.3-1 for the repro and the mechanism), which is why this row cannot be CONFORMS on the strength of the fixed-point path alone. (2) the 0 returned for an invalid argument is NOT in integer date form (Sec 15.5.2 requires it to be greater than zero); that is admissible only under Sec 15.3 item 14's implementor-defined latitude while EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking is disabled, and the choice IS recorded (docs/COBOLNET_INTRINSICS_DESIGN.md, 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with a defined default result') - but I did not verify the checking-ENABLED half end to end past ExceptionState.ArgumentError's Set + throw, and no spec-derived test exercises it, so it is asserted rather than demonstrated.

subject: INTEGER-OF-DAY function
notes: DIVERGES SUSTAINED, AND WIDENED — the first pass found two mechanisms; there is a THIRD, and it is the worst of them. Citations re-run, not inherited: `cite.py --check 15.47.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer of the form YYYYDDD"` OK (rule 1); `--check 15.3 "Integer. An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified."` OK (§15.3 item 6); `--check 15.47.1 "The type of this function is integer."` OK; Table 21's row re-read verbatim at §15.6 (`| INTEGER-OF-DAY | Int1 | Int | Integer date equivalent of Julian date (YYYYDDD) in argument-1 |`). (1) THE CLASS SCREEN IS ABSENT. INTEGER-OF-DAY appears in NEITHER IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened (both dictionaries read end to end), and IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses opens with `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` — so the PB1 §15.3 screen (COBOLNET1627) never runs for this function and a class-alphanumeric operand is reinterpreted as digits (the documented `FUNCTION ABS` over `PIC X(4)` failure mode). (2) A NON-INTEGER NUMERIC OPERAND IS SILENTLY TRUNCATED: IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt renders a scaled argument as `(long)(CobolNum.Rescale(<expr>, <scale>, 0, Truncation))` (RuntimeApi.NumRescale confirmed to emit exactly that text), so `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY` over a PIC 9(7)V99 holding 1995046.75 computes as 1995046 with no diagnostic and no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. (3) ⛔ THE THIRD MECHANISM, MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS AND FOUND BY READING THE RENDERER RATHER THAN SAMPLING VALUES: there is a class of LEGAL argument-1 for which the compiler emits a call to a runtime member THAT DOES NOT EXIST. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum routes `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` BEFORE the exact switch; RealMethod maps IntegerOfDay -> IntegerOfDayReal by convention; RuntimeApi.Intrinsic emits `CobolIntrinsics.{method}(...)`; and `grep -rn IntegerOfDayReal src/ tests/` returns NOTHING — CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs carries AbsReal/FloorReal/.../CombinedDatetimeReal and no body for any of the four date conversions. Failing input, legality checked as a SYNTACTIC question and not only a rule question: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY(1.995046E6)` — §8.3.3.3.3 r1/r2 make `1.995046E6` a floating-point NUMERIC literal (significand with a decimal point; --check OK), §8.8.1.1 "An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal, ..." (--check OK) makes it an arithmetic expression, its value is EXACTLY 1,995,046 so it "will always result in an integer value" (§15.3 item 6), and 1995046 satisfies §15.47.3 r1 a) YYYY=1995 in 1601..9999 and b) DDD=046 positive, <367 and valid for 1995. The identical failure with a data item: `01 F USAGE COMP-2 VALUE 1995046.` + `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY(F)`. NOT RUN HERE (read-only), but this is not speculation: the SIBLING function's row (inventory AR-15.22.3-1 / RV-15.22.4-1, DATE-OF-INTEGER) records the byte-identical repro EXECUTED — `error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DateOfIntegerReal'`, at --std 85 AND 2023 — and its own FIX SHAPE names `IntegerOfDayReal` as one of the still-missing bodies. The guard that should have caught it, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.cs#EveryExactArm_HasItsRealCounterpart, scopes itself to catalog rows whose ArgKinds contains 'n' and reasons in its own remarks that "an integer-argument function ('i' — DATE-OF-INTEGER, FACTORIAL) ... cannot receive a float without violating their own argument rule first, which is PB1's business" — a premise that is false twice for this function: PB1 does not screen INTEGER-OF-DAY at all, and IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible('i') = {Numeric} ADMITS a class-numeric COMP-2, so adding the row would not close it either. (4) THE VALUE HALVES ARE WRITTEN CORRECTLY BUT UNREACHABLE ABOVE 2^63. CobolDate.IntegerOfDay guards `year is < 1601 or > 9999 || day < 1 || day > (DateTime.IsLeapYear((int)year) ? 366 : 365)` into ExceptionState.ArgumentError (fatal EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when checking is on, else the §15.3 implementor-defined default 0 — §15.3's closing sentence and implementor item 90 both --checked), but AsInt narrows with an UNCHECKED `(long)` cast and no CheckForOverflowUnderflow/checkOverflow setting exists anywhere in the repo (grep over *.csproj/*.props/*.cs is empty), so an argument of magnitude >= 2^63 WRAPS modulo 2^64 before the guard sees it: `01 P PIC 9(18) VALUE 184467440737115466.` + `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY(P * 100 + 62)` presents 18,446,744,073,711,546,662 = 2^64 + 1,995,046, whose YYYY subfield is ~1.8e16, and the function returns 143951 with no exception even under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`. Same root cast as inventory row AR-15.22.3-1 (where the wrap was executed and confirmed); it feeds DAY-OF-INTEGER, INTEGER-OF-DATE, INTEGER-OF-DAY, FACTORIAL, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, YEAR-TO-YYYY, COMBINED-DATETIME and FIND-STRING through one line. FIX SHAPE: (a) add IntegerOfDayReal (and the DateOfIntegerReal / DayOfIntegerReal / IntegerOfDateReal / Y2K-trio siblings) or make the date family reject a real argument with a cited diagnostic instead of naming a non-existent member, and widen IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests to the 'i' rows; (b) move the range guard into the Int128 domain, or raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION in AsInt itself on an out-of-long value; (c) add ["INTEGER-OF-DAY"] = ('i', "§15.47.3 r1") to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified. CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a date format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid date in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 4)). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14), and I read that paragraph IN FULL because it is what forecloses every escape from the finding below: "... results in an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE according to the rules specified in the function definition ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

⛔ CORRECTION - THE WEEK-DATE CRASH WINDOW IS TWO DAYS WIDE, NOT ONE. The adjudicator cited only "9999W527". I recomputed .NET's ISOWeek.ToDateTime arithmetic by hand: 9999-01-04 is a MONDAY, so correction = 1 + 3 = 4 and ordinal = 52*7 + d - 4 = 360 + d, evaluated as `new DateTime(9999,1,1).AddDays(ordinal - 1)` against a 365-DAY year. d=5 gives 9999-12-31 (integer date 3,067,671, the §15.5.2 maximum - CORRECT and, usefully, the exact boundary the landed FORMATTED-DATE row pins as "9999W525"); d=6 gives 10000-01-01 and d=7 gives 10000-01-02, BOTH past DateTime.MaxValue, and BOTH throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. The extended forms "YYYY-Www-D"/"9999-W52-6" and "9999-W52-7" fault identically (same Analyze leg).

CORROBORATION, NOT INHERITANCE: the landed AR-15.79.3-5 RAN this input against the sibling and its own sweep records `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` as verified crashing identically. I re-derived it here from the code and the calendar arithmetic, and extended it to d=6, which no prior record had.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX - bound-check the week-date reconstruction in Analyze. Do not count this row, AR-15.48.3-5 and AR-15.79.3-5 as three queue items. THE LOW BOUNDARY IS CLEAN and I checked it rather than assuming it: 1601-01-01 is a Monday and lies in ISO 1601-W01, so ISO 1601-W01-1 = 1601-01-01 = integer date 1, and no week date can underflow the epoch.

DayOfWeek.Sunday : (DayOfWeek)wd) - Epoch).Days + 1;` computes ordinal = 52*7 + d - (jan4DayOfWeek(9999) + 3) = 360 + d against a 365-day year, i.e. 10000-01-01 and 10000-01-02, and throws System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. subject: INTEGER-PART function
notes: REFUTER: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. TEST SCOPE FIRST, so the row cannot be misread as closed: conformance:2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family is real (tests/conformance/2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family.cob) and genuinely spec-derived - its header derives the expected -3 from the §15.49 rule text, not from observation - and `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(C)` with C COMP-2 = -3.5 has golden line 4 = `-3` (verified in the .out). It covers the FLOAT carrier into a FLOAT receiver ONLY. The PRIMARY fixed-point path has NO spec-derived test; the only other fixture is IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests#ExactFamily_MatchesLegacy, a LEGACY-ENGINE differential, which never qualifies. Citations re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.49.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is:"` -> OK r1; `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression."` -> OK r1. WHAT IS CORRECT, verified by reading the bodies: (a) EXACT carrier `Truncate(Int128 v, int scale) => scale <= 0 ? v * Pow10.AsWide(-scale) : v / Pow10.AsWide(scale)` - C# Int128 division truncates toward zero, so every NOTE case holds (-1.5, +1.5, 0, -1.0, +1.0, and -0.5 -> 0 as SIGN(-0.5)*INTEGER(0.5) = 0), and the `scale <= 0` arm handles an integer and a PICTURE-P negative-scale argument; (b) FLOAT carrier `TruncateReal(double v) => Math.Truncate(v)`, also toward zero and distinct from FloorReal/§15.44 as the NOTE's closing sentence requires. WHY DIVERGES RATHER THAN PARTIAL - a confirmed HARD FAILURE on legal, reachable source, not a missing half. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL is a source-level OPTIONS clause (OptionsBinder.cs:47/63 `ArithmeticOf`; tests/conformance/2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal.cob proves it is honoured) and legal at 2014/2023, so `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(A + B).` is conforming COBOL. Trace, every link read: NumericRenderer.CombineCore's `if (StandardDecimal)` branch returns `new NumX("CobolDec.Add(...)", 0, Dec: true)`; IntrinsicRenderer.AnyRealArgument tests only `.Real`, never `.Dec`, so the Dec operand does NOT route to RenderFloat; `case "Truncate"` then emits `CobolIntrinsics.Truncate(<CobolDec expr>, 0)`; CobolIntrinsics declares exactly ONE Truncate, `Truncate(Int128, int)`, and CobolDec is `readonly record struct CobolDec(Int128 Sig, int Exp)` with NO conversion operator of any kind (grep for `operator` over CobolDec.cs returns NOTHING). The generated C# therefore fails Roslyn with CS1503 - legal COBOL yields no program and no returned value at all, which the §15.49.4 r1 / §15.4.1 r1 returned-value rule cannot be said to be partially meeting. THE DIVERGENCE IS ASSERTED CLOSED IN A COMMENT, which is why it is invisible: IntrinsicBinder's standard-arithmetic staging gate (:389-403) states "The exact-engine functions already satisfy that" and stages COBOLNET0899 for `sig.Name is "ANNUITY" or "PRESENT-VALUE" or "VARIANCE" or "STANDARD-DEVIATION"` only. That claim is true of the VALUE and false of the CODEGEN, so nothing stages INTEGER-PART and no diagnostic fires. FAMILY-WIDE (feedback_scan_all_similar): the same untested `.Dec` reaches Floor/AbsScaled/FractionPart/ModScaled/RemScaled, and NumericRenderer.Align - documented "TOTAL OVER THE CARRIER KINDS" - is `x.Real ? FloatToScaled(...) : toScale == x.Scale ? x.Expr : CobolNum.Rescale(...)`, so a Dec NumX either passes through raw at equal scale or lands in `CobolNum.Rescale(CobolDec ...)`, the same CS1503; every AlignedArgs statistics arm (Max/Min/Sum/Range/Median/Midrange/OrdMax/OrdMin) inherits it. NumericRenderer.Real DOES handle Dec via `.ToDouble()`, which is why the float family escaped. No existing fixture covers it - the ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD* conformance programs (2002/arith_standard, 2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal, 2014/options_paragraph, 2014/v56_reldec_float_sdidi, negative/arith-standard-intrinsic-staged) pass only literals or the four staged functions. NEGATIVE FINDING SUSTAINED: an argument division cannot be truncated prematurely or inherit ROUNDED - `Arg(ic,i) => num.AsNum(ic.Args[i], num.Receiver)` uses AsNum's default `outermost: false`, so Divide takes its NESTED branch (guard scale, TRUNCATION), and `COMPUTE R ROUNDED = FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(7 / 2)` returns 3, not 4. NEGATIVE FINDING NARROWED - do not record it as closed: the adjudicator argued the float-bypasses-SDIDI leg produces no wrong value for INTEGER-PART because truncation of a binary64 and of its §8.8.1.5.1 shortest-round-trip decimal lift always agree. That argument is sound only for |v| <= 2^53, where an integer between v and its lift would have to be exactly representable and hence equal v. ABOVE 2^53 the lift need not equal the binary64 (e.g. a value whose shortest round-trip form is 9.999999999999998E16), so the two evaluations can return DIFFERENT integral values; not shown reachable, but unproven, and it must not stand as a settled negative. EDITIONS derived from the standard: the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment (NIST IF114A corroborates), unchanged through 2023 per Annex E and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md; the broken path is arithmetic-mode-scoped (STANDARD at 2002/2014, STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2014/2023), not edition-scoped.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: REFUTER DOWNGRADE (was PARTIAL). The rule is not merely half-built: it REJECTS legal source and SILENTLY ACCEPTS illegal source, so the verdict is DIVERGES. WORKS: an alphanumeric/national/boolean literal (BoundStringLiteral arm, reached through ExpressionBinder.NonNumericLiteralOperand); a data item of any class or category (BoundFieldOperand arm - verified: ExpressionBinder.OperandRef applies the 8.8.1.1 screen only when `context is OperandContext.Arithmetic`, so under OperandContext.FunctionArgument a pointer/index/object item binds to BoundNumRef and IntrinsicBinder.OperandOf maps it to BoundFieldOperand); a BASED entry. (a) A TYPE-NAME ARGUMENT IS REJECTED - legal COBOL-2002+ per 15.50.3 and 15.3 argument type 14 ('Type declaration. A type-name shall be specified', --check OK). DataBinder.cs:582-586 routes a TYPEDEF to RegisterTypeDecl, which keeps it OFF Roots and off ByName; TypeDecls has exactly three readers (DataBinder.cs:656/1252/3017) and ReferenceResolver.cs mentions neither TypeDecls nor Roots, so FUNCTION LENGTH(my-type) fails name resolution and is reported as an unresolved data-name. (b) NEW, MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS - A REFERENCE-MODIFIED ARGUMENT IS STAGED LOUD. 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 'Unless otherwise specified, reference modification is allowed anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted' (--check OK) and 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 'The unique data item is considered to be an elementary data item without the JUSTIFIED clause' (--check OK) make FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-NAME(1:5)) legal and its answer the evaluated length. BindLengthFold's SECOND arm, `BoundFieldOperand { Place: RefModPlace }`, returns BoundExprError; NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundExprError) emits EmitCore.LoudValue -> `NotImplemented.Value<long>(...)`, so it COMPILES CLEAN and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. The mechanism is already present and unused: RefModPlace carries Start and the rendered Length expression (Place.cs#RefModPlace). No corpus program and no xUnit test reference-modifies a LENGTH argument. (c) The rule's NEGATIVE half is not a compile-time diagnostic either: the '_' arm returns BoundExprError the same way, so FUNCTION LENGTH(5), FUNCTION LENGTH(SPACE) (a figurative binds to BoundFigurative, verified at ExpressionBinder.cs:196-201, never BoundStringLiteral), FUNCTION LENGTH(A + B) and FUNCTION LENGTH(index-name) all compile clean and throw at run time. LENGTH is absent from BOTH IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and DeliberatelyUnscreened (both dictionaries read directly), so CheckArgumentClasses returns immediately for it (IntrinsicBinder.cs:980) and the catalog's ArgKinds 's' hint is unread. Per the review's own rule, that absence is a genuine finding.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: Two of the four shapes work; the cited test is genuinely spec-derived and pins VALUES (it asserts stdout 'NL=0002\nBL=0004' for FUNCTION LENGTH(N"AB") / FUNCTION LENGTH(B"1011"), citing ISO 15.50). A BOOLEAN LITERAL folds to Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length) - B"1011" returns 4. An ELEMENTARY BOOLEAN DATA ITEM folds to DataItem.ImageWidth; ElementaryImageWidth returns pic.Length for a non-numeric category, i.e. the boolean-position count (3.24 'boolean position <storage required> amount of physical storage required to store ... a single boolean character'), for both USAGE DISPLAY and USAGE BIT since ElementaryByteWidth's '_' arm pins 1 byte per boolean position (D-B1). ⚠ THAT LEG IS ASSERTED FROM CODE READING ONLY - no golden and no xUnit test takes FUNCTION LENGTH of a PIC 1(n) data item; the cited test covers the LITERAL only. MISSING: (a) a BIT GROUP ITEM cannot be written at all - there is no GROUP-USAGE clause in the grammar (no groupUsage rule, no GROUP-USAGE token; DataBinder.cs:1491 states 'GROUP-USAGE is not modeled'), so this leg is unreachable; (b) a TYPE DECLARATION for a boolean item is unreachable for the same reason as AR-15.50.3-1 (TypeDecls is not consulted by the reference resolver). ⛔ REFUTER CORRECTION - TWO DEFECTS IN THE FIRST PASS'S EVIDENCE. (1) Its claim that 'Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length) makes a zero-length boolean literal B"" return 1 rather than 0' is FALSE: B"" never reaches the fold. CobolLexer.g4:690 defines `fragment BOOL_BODY : 'B' '"' [01]+ '"' | ...` - the `+` requires at least one boolean character, so the 8.3.3.4.4 GR4 zero-length boolean literal ('If boolean-character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal', --check OK at 8.3.3.4.4, and note --check FAILS at 8.3.3.4) is rejected at LEX time. That is legal source rejected, but it is an 8.3.3.4 grammar defect, not a 15.50.4 r1 value defect, and it must not be counted here. (2) Its citation '13.18.40.4 rule 4' for the boolean-position count does not exist: --check shows 13.18.40.4 GR1 is the national-vs-alphanumeric position rule and GR3 is the category list; there is no GR4 about boolean positions. The correct anchors are 3.24/3.25 (boolean position) plus the 13.18.40.3 PICTURE symbol rules.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: REFUTER DOWNGRADE (was PARTIAL). Two shapes work and are now pinned by a stronger golden than the first pass cited - tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_byte_length.cob asserts 'LEN-N=' FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-N) for 01 WS-N PIC N(3) and its .out pins 3, i.e. NATIONAL POSITIONS, closing the elementary-usage-national leg (ElementaryImageWidth returns pic.Length for a non-numeric category; the 2-bytes-per-position doubling lives only in ElementaryByteWidth, correct here because r2 counts national positions, not bytes - 3.123 'national character position <storage required>'). A NATIONAL LITERAL folds to s.Value.Length (N"AB" -> 2). ⛔ NEW DEFECT, MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS, AND IT IS A SILENT WRONG VALUE, NOT A MISSING SHAPE: FUNCTION LENGTH(N"") RETURNS 1, NOT 0. Unlike BOOLLIT, NATLIT DOES lex a zero-length literal - CobolLexer.g4:689 `fragment NAT_BODY : 'N' STR_BODY` and :688 `fragment STR_BODY : '"' (~["\r\n] | '""')* '"' | ...` where the `*` admits zero characters. 3.178 defines a zero-length literal as an 'alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal that contains zero characters' (--check OK) and 8.5.4 item 8 lists 'A zero-length literal' among the zero-length items (--check OK); 15.50.3 admits it (unlike, say, the rule at :5470 which explicitly excludes a zero-length literal, 15.50.3 carries no such exclusion). r2 therefore requires 0 national positions, and BindLengthFold's `Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length)` publishes 1 with no diagnostic. STILL MISSING: (a) a NATIONAL GROUP ITEM cannot be written - no GROUP-USAGE clause exists in the grammar (see RV-15.50.4-1); (b) a TYPE DECLARATION for a national item is unreachable (TypeDecls off the resolver). NOTE: a nested national-result function (FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF(A))) takes the runtime .Length arm and returns national positions - not one of r2's four shapes, but consistent with it.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: The fixed-point DISPLAY/BINARY/PACKED/alphanumeric/numeric-edited surface is correct and the cited golden does pin ABSOLUTE values, not merely LENGTH==BYTE-LENGTH agreement (v59_length_agrees.out: OK 001/018/005/002/004/008/016/016/001/003/010/010/007/006/012/016) - verified, because a self-differential alone would have been structurally blind to a shared error. FOUR classes of argument return the wrong number of alphanumeric character positions, all silently or as a runtime bomb. (a) CARRIER-USAGE ITEMS FOLD TO 1. PicInfo.IndexItem, PointerItem, ProgramPointerItem, ObjectReferenceItem and FloatItem all carry Length: 0, Digits: 0 (verified in PicInfo.cs:231-245/445/452) and ByteForm None (PicInfo.ByteForm's '_' arm), so ElementaryImageWidth returns 0 - via `return pic.Length` for the pointer/object categories and via `pic.Digits + 0` for the numeric-category Index/Float - and BindLengthFold's `Math.Max(1, f.Place.Item.ImageWidth)` publishes 1. DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth pins the SAME items at 8 (INDEX/POINTER/PROGRAM-POINTER/FUNCTION-POINTER/OBJECT REFERENCE), 4 (COMP-1/FLOAT-SHORT) and 8 (COMP-2/FLOAT-LONG). So FUNCTION LENGTH(P) = 1 while FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(P) = 8 - exactly the disagreement v59_length_agrees.cob's header declares impossible in a single-byte-character model, and that golden has no index/pointer/object/float row. Inside a GROUP the same child contributes 0 (Math.Max is applied only to the final total), so every group holding a pointer, index, object reference or COMP-1/COMP-2 leaf undercounts by 8/4 per leaf. (b) A NATIONAL CHILD OF AN ALPHANUMERIC GROUP is counted at ONE alphanumeric position per character. r3 governs such a group (3.11 - an alphanumeric group item is any group except a bit/national/strongly-typed/variable-length group), and 3.8 / 3.123 define both position kinds as the 'amount of physical storage required', with D-N1 pinning national = 2 bytes and DISPLAY = 1 byte - so '01 G. 05 A PIC X(3). 05 N PIC N(2).' must return 7 and returns 5. That exact record exists in the corpus as WS-GRP in tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_byte_length.cob, where BYTE-LENGTH(WS-GRP) is pinned at 7 and FUNCTION LENGTH is never called on it - which is why nothing has contradicted this. ImageWidth's own doc-comment states the choice, right for the elementary national item of r2 and wrong for the enclosing alphanumeric group of r3; DataItem.ByteWidth already computes 7. (c) NEW - A REFERENCE-MODIFIED ARGUMENT IS NOT COMPUTED AT ALL. BindLengthFold's `BoundFieldOperand { Place: RefModPlace }` arm returns BoundExprError, which NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundExprError) renders as NotImplemented.Value<long>(...): FUNCTION LENGTH(A(1:3)) compiles clean and throws at run time, although 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 makes the unique data item an ordinary elementary item of r3's kind and RefModPlace already carries the rendered length expression. See AR-15.50.3-1(b). (d) Math.Max(1, ...) FLOORS EVERY ZERO-LENGTH ITEM AT 1. FUNCTION LENGTH("") returns 1, not 0 (STR_BODY admits zero characters, 3.178 + 8.5.4 item 8), and the same clamp makes it impossible for LENGTH ever to return the 0 that 8.5.4 items 1 and 7 require of a group containing only a zero-occurrence ODO table or only zero-capacity dynamic tables.

notes: Neither sub-rule is implemented, and the staging is a RUNTIME throw, not a diagnostic - re-verified end to end. BindLengthFold's third arm matches 'f.Place.Item.IsGroup && OdoModel.TableUnder(...) is { OccursSpec.Depending: not null }' and returns BoundExprError; nothing calls ctx.Edition.Error on that path, and NumericRenderer.cs:132 renders BoundExprError as EmitCore.LoudValue -> `NotImplemented.Value<long>(...)`, so FUNCTION LENGTH over an occurs-depending group COMPILES CLEAN and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. subject: LENGTH function
notes: REFUTER NOTE: the first pass opened with 'EXPLICIT FILLER is included', which is NOT evidence for this rule - r5 is about IMPLICIT filler positions only, and an explicitly-written FILLER entry is an ordinary child that ImageWidth sums like any other. Struck. What is actually verified: COBOL.NET generates NO implicit filler at all, so r5 is satisfied VACUOUSLY, and one branch of that vacuity is a real behavioural difference. SYNCHRONIZED is a documented no-op (DataItem.Synchronized, DataBinder.cs:1910 'no-op here'), and 8.5.1.6.4 is permissive about that - 'Each implementor who provides for special types of alignment shall specify the precise interpretations that are to be made' (--check OK at 8.5.1.6.4) - so an implementation that provides none generates no SYNC filler and is conforming. But 8.5.1.6.3 is NOT implementor-defined for the non-SYNCHRONIZED case: 'Implicit filler bit positions are generated: ... Following a bit data item within an alphanumeric group item, within a strongly-typed group item, or within a bit group item, as needed to advance alignment to a required natural boundary for the next item within that group' (--check OK at 8.5.1.6.3), and the same clause requires consecutive elementary bit items to align 'at the next bit position in storage'. COBOL.NET does not bit-pack - ElementaryByteWidth's '_' arm gives USAGE BIT one byte per boolean position - so no such filler exists to include and the LENGTH answer differs from a bit-packing implementation: '01 G. 05 B PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT. 05 A PIC X.' returns 4 here where 8.5.1.6.3 + r5 + r9 give 2. Whether the 1-byte-per-boolean-position pinning is itself conforming is an 8.5.1.6.3 / D-B1 question rather than a 15.50 one, but r5's bit branch stays UNVERIFIED until it is settled - hence PARTIAL, not CONFORMS-vacuous.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: The PIC X leg is correct and covered by two spec-derived goldens, both re-read: dynamic_length_item.cob cites '15.50.4 r6' in its header and its .out pins 02/14/10/00 including the zero-length state; dynamic_length_figurative.cob pins the figurative-send and zero-length-literal states. A DYNAMIC LENGTH item is excluded from the compile-time fold (ElementaryImageWidth returns 0 when IsDynamicLength, DataItem.cs:368) and routed to a runtime BoundIntrinsicCall, which IntrinsicRenderer's 'Length' case renders as CobolIntrinsics.Length(s); that body is verified to be `public static long Length(string s) => s.Length` (CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs:155) - no trimming, no prefix. For a PIC X item one character position is one byte under the pinned DISPLAY width, so the current length in BYTES is what is returned, and the NOTE about prefixed fields / delimiter characters is satisfied by construction (a bare .NET string, no length prefix, no terminator). MISSING: the NATIONAL leg. A PIC N DYNAMIC LENGTH item matches the arm at IntrinsicBinder.cs:1039-1040 and returns BoundExprError - staged loud, so it compiles clean and throws at run time - because the byte count is 2x the UTF-16 length and no doubling is wired; the arm's own comment says so. Unverified edge (not asserted as a divergence): the byte-equals-character-position identity for the alphanumeric leg rests on the pinned 1-byte-per-DISPLAY-position model while the alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16, so a dynamic-length PIC X item holding characters above U+00FF is self-consistent by definition of the model but has no golden. Edition window 2014,2023 derived from the standard, not the catalog: dynamic-length elementary items predate 2023 - VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 60 records only the 2014->2023 SET enhancement ('The SET statement was enhanced to' set their length), which presupposes their existence at 2014, and Annex E's 2014->2023 change list introduces no dynamic-length or variable-length-group feature.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: ⛔ REFUTER CITATION FIX: the first pass cited '8.5.1.12' for the variable-length-group definition. `cite.py --check 8.5.1.12` FAILS; the rule lives in 8.5.1.12.1 ('A variable-length group is a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item', --check OK at 8.5.1.12.1). That is the one-level-short shape this review is required to catch. The finding itself is CONFIRMED and is the sharpest defect in this subject. A variable-length group is not recognized anywhere in the LENGTH fold - no IsVariableLengthGroup predicate exists in the compiler; only InitializeBinder has an ad-hoc dynamic-table check. Traced arm by arm, such a group falls through all six guards (it is not a RefModPlace; OdoModel.TableUnder returns null because it matches DependingName and a dynamic table has none; the GROUP is neither IsAnyLength nor IsDynamicLength) to the last field arm and folds to a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT with NO diagnostic and NO loud guard. ElementaryImageWidth returns 0 for a dynamic-length child (DataItem.cs:368), so term (b) - the current lengths - is dropped entirely; ImageWidth multiplies each child by '(c.Occurs ?? 1)' while DataItem.Occurs is null for a dynamic-capacity table (verified: IsDynamicTable => OccursSpec is { IsDynamic: true }, and Occurs is documented as null for it, DataItem.cs:164-167), so term (c) is counted as exactly ONE occurrence instead of the current capacity. Concretely, '01 G. 05 A PIC X(4). 05 T PIC X(2) OCCURS DYNAMIC.' at capacity 5 must return 14 and returns the constant 6; '01 G. 05 A PIC X(4). 05 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.' holding "HELLO" must return 9 and returns the constant 4. Both surfaces are live and in the corpus (2014/dyn_capacity_*.cob, 2014/dynamic_length_item.cob) and a grep of every .cob under tests/conformance for 'FUNCTION LENGTH' confirms none calls it on the containing group - which is why nothing has contradicted it. The 8.5.1.12.3 Matching basis for term (c) is likewise absent, and Math.Max(1, ...) additionally makes the 8.5.4 item 7 answer (a variable-length group of all-zero-capacity dynamic tables is a zero-length item) unreachable.

notes: The rule itself is unimplemented: there is no locale-name concept anywhere, so 'associated with a locale in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph' can never be declared, let alone checked; the function reference is rejected first, by name, with COBOLNET1518. *** THE FIRST PASS'S SUPPORTING EVIDENCE IS OVERTURNED, AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. *** It recorded that writing a SPECIAL-NAMES LOCALE clause 'yields a bare ANTLR syntax error'. It does not, for the primary branch of the 12.3.7 format 'LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 }': (a) LOCALE is not a lexer token -- zero hits for LOCALE across all of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/, and the LOCALE phrase of LOWER-CASE etc. is matched on TEXT by IntrinsicBinder#HasLocalePhrase -- so it lexes as IDENTIFIER; (b) specialNameEntry ends in two catch-all alternatives, implementorSwitchEntry ( cobolWord (IS cobolWord)? ... ) and genericClause ( IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER|literal)* ), and cobolWord admits IDENTIFIER; so 'LOCALE FR-LOC IS EXT-NAME' decomposes into entries that both catch-alls accept; (c) the ONLY two consumers of specialNameEntry in the whole compiler are DataBinder.Switches#SwitchBindSpecialNames and MnemonicRegistry#Of, and BOTH silently 'continue' past everything they do not recognise -- there is no unknown-entry diagnostic. Net effect: the clause is SILENTLY ACCEPTED and MnemonicRegistry registers EXT-NAME as a device mnemonic bound to FR-LOC, usable afterwards in e.g. DISPLAY ... UPON EXT-NAME. Only the literal-4 branch ('IS "fr_FR"') is a parse error, because IS followed by a literal starts no entry. This (i) violates A.4.1 ('An implementation shall accept the syntax ... for an optional element only when support ... is claimed'), (ii) contradicts the owner's own decision-3 requirement of UNIFORM not-supported diagnostics, and (iii) contradicts docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 item 5, which tells the user this entry point is a parse error. The in-code claim at DataBinder.Switches.cs (the AlphabetBindNational doc comment, 'the LOCALE phrase ... fails loud at parse') is therefore wrong on both counts.

subject: LOCALE-TIME function
notes: SUSTAINED. Nothing. The two widened ranges this rule grants over CURRENT-DATE -- hours 00 through 24 (a) and seconds 00 through 99 (b, the leap-second allowance) -- have no representation anywhere in src/Cobol.Net.*: no validator, no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION arm, no constant. The reference never reaches argument evaluation; COBOLNET1518 rejects the function by name. Two additions the prior note lacked. (i) The rule's own NOTE is informative and its LEAP-SECOND premise is NOT a 2023 delta -- LEAP-SECOND has 16 spec occurrences and ZERO inside Annex E, so the widened ranges are stable across the 2002/2014/2023 window rather than a late addition, which is why the edition string is the full post-2002 window. (ii) The widening is genuinely BIDIRECTIONAL and both directions are unrepresented: r3(b)'s 00-99 is WIDER than the CURRENT-DATE table row it overrides (§15.21 positions 13-14 admit 00-59 with LEAP-SECOND OFF, 00-nn with ON), and r3(a)'s 00-24 admits the 24:00:00 end-of-day value that the CURRENT-DATE hours field does not. A future implementation cannot reuse a CURRENT-DATE validator here; it needs this clause's own range pair. notes: SUSTAINED, with the design constraint tightened and evidenced. Nothing: there is no returned value and hence no length. The only trace of a result is the catalog row's IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric, and it is never reached -- the emitter's own guard, IntrinsicRenderer.cs `if (sig.Bind == IntrinsicBind.Deferred || sig.RuntimeMethod.Length == 0)`, is the loud backstop behind the bind-time COBOLNET1518, so the empty RuntimeMethod cannot silently render. notes: REFUTER: SUSTAINED, re-derived from the code rather than from the adjudicator's note. CITATION RE-VALIDATED: `--check 15.55.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric."` -> OK §15.55.3 1). subject: LOG function
notes: REFUTER: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. CITATION RE-VALIDATED (`--check 15.55.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be greater than zero."` -> OK §15.55.3 2)), and so was the whole consequence chain the adjudicator built on: `--check 15.3 "the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist"` -> OK §15.3 14) (the tool DOES label that unnumbered paragraph '14)', so the adjudicator's clause label was right, not one level short), and §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 -- 'An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled' -- confirms ExceptionState#ArgumentError's `Set(...)+throw` when on / bare `return 0` when off is the correct fork, NOT a missing Set. THE VERIFIED HALF IS REAL: `Log(double x) => x <= 0 ? ArgumentError(...) : Math.Log(x)` guards at the BODY, so every render channel reaches it -- IntrinsicRenderer#RenderNum routes LOG through `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(...)` (catalog row: Fixed 1..1, kind 'n', Float true, IntroducedIn 85), `grep -rn "Math.Log" src/Cobol.Net.*` returns exactly the two guarded lines and CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs has no Log, so no second unguarded body exists. EcEmitter#FatalAmbientGates wraps the whole STATEMENT whenever EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking is enabled, independent of what the statement contains, so there is no PB7-shaped unreachable-guard hole. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED, AND WHY THIS IS NOT CONFORMS -- the missing part is the PB13 arm, read in RenderFloat rather than sampled: `return num.Receiver.Real || num.Receiver.Receiverless ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true) : new NumX(FromDouble(call, ws), ws);`. The FIXED-receiver arm has TWO §15.55.3 r2 raise sites (the body guard AND FromDouble's `if (double.IsNaN(d)) return ArgumentError(...)`); the Real/receiverless arm has only the body guard, and `x <= 0` is FALSE for NaN in IEEE. So a NaN-valued argument -- which is not 'greater than zero' and therefore violates r2 -- yields Math.Log(NaN) = NaN, and on that arm NOTHING converts it to EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION even with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`. Reachable without exotic input, because the same arm MANUFACTURES the NaN: `COMPUTE C2 = FUNCTION SQRT(0 - 4)` with C2 USAGE COMP-2 takes Receiver.Real, skips FromDouble, and CobolFloat#StoreSingleChecked/the double receiver's bare cast store NaN silently; then `IF FUNCTION LOG(C2) > 0`, `DISPLAY FUNCTION LOG(C2)` and `COMPUTE C2 = FUNCTION LOG(C2)` all propagate NaN with no exception condition, while the byte-identical expression with a PIC S9(6)V99 receiver raises. CobolFloat#Sending's EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE guard does not close this: it fires only on reading a float DATA ITEM and only when EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE checking is separately enabled, so with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION on and EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE off the value rule is silently unenforced. r2 enforcement must not depend on the receiver's shape. TEST EVIDENCE, RE-CHECKED AND TRIMMED: ECT024/ECT025 do exercise FUNCTION LOG(0) and AssertSpec/AssertFatal compile-and-run COBOL.NET alone against a rule-derived expected stdout -- genuinely spec-derived, kept. IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec was REMOVED from test-ref: its AssertSpec helper is sound and it does include a LOG(0) case, but it adds nothing ECT024 does not already pin and it sits in a class whose stated purpose is the legacy differential -- not a reference this row should lean on. ALL THREE surviving fixtures use a FIXED-POINT receiver in a COMPUTE, i.e. every one of them lands on the arm that is NOT the defective one; the Real/receiverless arm is entirely unexercised for LOG's domain error. MISSING TO CLOSE: hoist the NaN->EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION raise out of FromDouble so it applies on both arms (the sweep PB13 did not do -- CLAUDE.md rule 4), and a fixture pinning LOG's domain error in an IF condition and into a COMP-2 receiver. EDITIONS from the standard: the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment to COBOL-85, no Annex E added/changed entry.

subject: LOG function
notes: REFUTER: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. CITATION RE-VALIDATED: `--check 15.55.4 "The returned value is the approximation of the logarithm to the base *e* of argument-1."` -> OK §15.55.4 1). THE NATIVE-ARITHMETIC HALF IS CORRECT and I confirm the adjudicator's reasoning there: §15.55 was read whole (spec lines 32016-32041) and specifies NO equivalent arithmetic expression and NO bound on the result, so `--check 15.4.1 "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined unless otherwise specified in the function definition"` -> OK §15.4.1 2) applies with nothing carved out; Math.Log IS base e; the FromDouble headroom clamp cannot bite because |ln x| <= ~745 for any positive finite double. THE HALF THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT VERIFY -- and it accepted it on SAMPLED OUTPUT, which is exactly what cannot distinguish the two forms. §15.4.1 carries a SECOND, SEPARATE paragraph that is NOT conditioned on having an equivalent arithmetic expression (mechanically validated: `--check 15.4.1 "When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the returned value for numeric and integer functions is contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect."` -> OK §15.4.1). The last-paragraph implementor-defined escape governs the VALUE; this paragraph governs the FORM the returned value is CONTAINED IN, and it is unconditional for every numeric function -- LOG included. READ RATHER THAN RUN: IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFloat has NO arithmetic-mode arm at all. It consults `num.Receiver` only and never `num.StandardDecimal` (which the same file DOES consult for MEAN at RenderNum's "MeanScaled" case and for the §15.93/94 digit cap), so under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL the returned value is still a binary64 quantized through the native FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9) capped by ReceiverContext#FloatWorkingScale -- at most ~17 significant digits of a double, never the §8.8.1.5 standard-decimal intermediate; and on the Real/receiverless arm (`num.Receiver.Real || num.Receiver.Receiverless`) it is a RAW double with no conversion into any temporary standard data item whatsoever, in every arithmetic mode. IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore's standard-arithmetic loud stage (DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic) deliberately lists only ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION, on the in-code reasoning that 'the prose-approximation functions (SQRT, the trig/log family) have NO equivalent arithmetic expression -- implementor-defined in every mode (§15.4.1 last paragraph)'. That reasoning answers the VALUE paragraph and is silent on the FORM paragraph, so LOG under the standard modes is neither implemented to the paragraph nor staged loud against it: it is simply un-adjudicated, which is what makes this PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS. STANDARD-BINARY compounds it -- the mode is acknowledged as not yet implemented in-tree ('standard-binary's 35 rides the P12/P13 STANDARD-BINARY wave', IntrinsicRenderer), yet the §15.4.1 paragraph names it explicitly. NO TEST, deliberately: no spec-derived test pins LOG's returned value in ANY mode. The nearest candidates were re-checked and rejected -- Log10_1000_RoundsTheDoubleArtifact_PinnedToSpec is §15.56 not §15.55; FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy is a legacy differential and cannot close a row; NIST IF116A/IF117A are goldens. tests/conformance/2023/general_format_intrinsics_batch1.cob has no LOG case. test-ref left EMPTY rather than reaching for a net. TO CLOSE: decide the standard-mode disposition for the whole prose-approximation family (implement the §15.4.1 temporary-standard-data-item form, or stage it loud as the four EAE functions already are -- one decision, not per function), then a golden pinning ln(1) = 0 and an inclusive range around ln(10) under native AND standard-decimal. EDITIONS from the standard: 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment to COBOL-85; whole-text grep finds no Annex E added/changed entry for LOG.
