subject: LOG10 function
notes: OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. Citation re-validated: `--check 15.56.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be greater than zero."` -> OK §15.56.3 2). WHAT THE FIRST PASS GOT RIGHT, and it is real: the domain test sits AT THE FUNCTION BODY — `public static double Log10(double x) => x <= 0 ? Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError("LOG10 argument must be > 0 (ISO §15.56.3 r2)") : Math.Log10(x);` — so it is receiver-independent, and the FLOAT-LONG/receiver-less bypass charged against ACOS/ASIN/SQRT at AR-15.8.3-2 genuinely has no analogue here (RenderFloat's `num.Receiver.Real || num.Receiver.Receiverless` arm still calls the guarded body). ⛔ WHAT IT DID NOT CHECK IS THE HALF THAT DECIDES THE ROW: it verified the RAISE SITE is REACHED and never asked whether the CHECKING GATE that site consults is ever turned ON. ArgumentError raises only `if (ArgumentFunctionChecking)`; that ambient flag is emitted in exactly ONE place in the whole compiler — EcEmitter's FatalAmbientGates wrapper (`ExceptionState.ArgumentFunctionChecking = true;` inside the per-statement try) — and only when EcBinder#EcWrap put EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION into the statement's Enabled list, which requires `ContainsIntrinsic(node)`. ContainsIntrinsic = `DirectIntrinsic(s) || s.StatementChildren().Any(ContainsIntrinsic)`, and DirectIntrinsic is a HAND-MAINTAINED switch: BoundDisplay, BoundMove, BoundCompute, BoundComputeBoolean, the six arithmetic nodes, BoundIf's condition, BoundSetTo, BoundEvaluate's WHEN matches — then `_ => false`. StatementChildren makes the walk total over CONTAINERS; it does nothing for a statement's OWN operands. SO: with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` explicitly in force, a LOG10 domain violation written in any OTHER statement shape sets no gate, ArgumentError returns the §15.3 default 0, and the run unit terminates NORMALLY — where §14.6.13.1.1 (--check OK: "During the execution of any statement, if checking for an exception condition is not enabled, the exception condition will not be raised" — the converse obligation when it IS enabled) plus Table 13 at §14.6.13.1.6 (--check OK: `| EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION | Fatal |`) require the condition raised, the last exception status set, and abnormal termination absent a handler. REACHABLE SHAPES for a NUMERIC function-identifier, all outside the list: `PERFORM UNTIL FUNCTION LOG10(WS-Z) > 5`, `SEARCH … WHEN key = FUNCTION LOG10(WS-Z)`, `CALL "SUB" USING BY VALUE FUNCTION LOG10(WS-Z)` (the position PB6/§14.9.4.3 SR22 landed), STRING/UNSTRING senders, INSPECT Format-1's target (the position PB10 landed), WRITE/REWRITE FROM, GO TO … DEPENDING ON. ⚠ NOT MEASURED HERE (read-only pass — no build, no run), AND IT DOES NOT NEED TO BE: the identical predicate was MEASURED failing for the nonfatal twin at open inventory row RV-15.26.4-3 (DIVERGES), whose self-controlling repro under `>>TURN EC-DATA-CONVERSION CHECKING ON` shows a STRING and a `PERFORM UNTIL FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W) = "A?B"` performing the substitution with NO condition set while the very next MOVE in the same program sets it. Same ContainsIntrinsic/DirectIntrinsic gate, same root cause, different exception-name. ⛔ ONE DEFECT, DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT: this row must be attached to the RV-15.26.4-3 fix, not opened as a LOG10 item. The fix is structural per CLAUDE.md rule 5 — a total operand walk driven by the generated bound-tree visitor (a new BoundStatement leaf becomes a compile error) replacing the hand-list; a per-verb patch reproduces the defect at the next verb. DIVERGENT LEG 2002,2014,2023 (the TURN directive and the EC model are 2002+; at --std 85 there is no way to enable checking, so the §15.3 implementor-defined default 0 is all that is available and is conforming). The editions field is the RULE's own window. test-ref EMPTY. ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.ArgumentFunction_CheckingOff_DefaultResultZero / _Enabled_NoHandler_FatalTerminates / _Enabled_DeclarativeResumes_ReceiverUnchanged are all COMPUTE statements (the ONE covered arm) over FUNCTION LOG and FUNCTION NUMVAL — a different clause (§15.55 / §15.67) — so they neither close this row nor could ever have caught the gate hole. test-needed: FUNCTION LOG10(0) and FUNCTION LOG10(-1) with checking ON, one arm inside a COMPUTE and one inside a PERFORM UNTIL condition (the pair is the whole point), plus a checking-OFF arm.

subject: LOG10 function
notes: OVERTURNED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the claimed test-ref is STRUCK. The first pass named the standard-arithmetic half a 'SUSPECTED DIVERGENCE, NOT MEASURED' and rounded to PARTIAL. It does not need measuring — it is decidable by READING the emitter, which is what this pass did. Rule validated: `--check 15.56.4 "The returned value is the approximation of the logarithm to the base 10 of argument-1."` -> OK §15.56.4 1). §15.56 specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so §15.4.1's last paragraph makes the VALUE implementor-defined (--check OK). ⛔ THAT ANSWERS THE VALUE AND NOTHING ELSE. §15.4.1 paragraph 3 (--check OK, both halves) imposes two further requirements that are NOT conditioned on having an equivalent arithmetic expression: (a) "When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the returned value for numeric and integer functions is contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect", and (b) "the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element so long as the value and order of the arguments, the collating sequence, and the locale are unchanged" (LOG10 is not among the four exceptions that sentence names). STANDARD-DECIMAL IS REACHABLE FOR LOG10 — verified, not assumed: DataBinder records NATIVE/STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL as implemented (NumericRenderer#StandardDecimal covers Standard and StandardDecimal), and IntrinsicBinder stages COBOLNET0899 loud for exactly ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION — LOG10 is not staged, so such a program compiles and runs. (a) UNMET BY CONSTRUCTION: IntrinsicRenderer#RenderNum executes `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(ic, sig.RuntimeMethod);` BEFORE any mode test, and RenderFloat never consults num.StandardDecimal — the only Dec-producing intrinsic arm in the file is MeanScaled, unreachable for a Float row. The emitted returned value is therefore a binary64 (float or receiver-less receiver) or an Int128 scaled at ws, never a §8.8.1.5 standard intermediate; it is lifted through CobolDec.From/FromDouble only if it later participates in a binary operation, and `COMPUTE A = FUNCTION LOG10(1000)` has none. (b) UNMET AND DEMONSTRABLE FROM THE CODE ALONE: ws = ReceiverContext#FloatWorkingScale = clamp(max(Receiver.Scale, 9), 0, 38 - IntegerDigits), which is RECEIVER-DEPENDENT, and FromDouble closes `(Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`. Math.Log10(1000) = 2.9999999999999996; into `01 A PIC 9V9(6)` ws = 9, the round carries to 3000000000 and A stores 3.000000; into `01 B PIC 9V9(17)` ws = 17 and B stores 2.99999999999999960. No single returned value truncates to BOTH 3.000000 at six places and 2.999… at seventeen, so the two instances returned DIFFERENT values for identical arguments in one execution — (b) violated, with no run required to see it. THE DESIGN'S OWN JUSTIFICATION IS THE REASONING GAP, quoted from CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs's family header: the trig/log rows "stay conforming under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD / STANDARD-DECIMAL" because "the value is implementor-defined in EVERY mode (§15.4.1 last paragraph)" — a sentence about the VALUE offered as an answer to requirements about the FORM and the SAMENESS. NATIVE HALF: confirmed sound as the first pass reported — Math.Log10 is a genuine approximation, FromDouble rounds rather than truncates, §15.56.4 imposes no numeric bound so the closed-interval overshoot charged at RV-15.8.4-1 has no analogue, and |log10(x)| <= ~308.25 for any finite double keeps the PB13 headroom cap slack. Under native arithmetic the receiver-dependent ws is licensed ("the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor"); it is standard-decimal/standard-binary where that licence runs out. ⛔ TEST-REF STRUCK — conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.Log10_1000_RoundsTheDoubleArtifact_PinnedToSpec was read in full: it does use AssertSpec (COBOL.NET only, no oracle, despite the class name), but it asserts "3000000" EXACTLY, and an implementation that truncates the same double artifact returns 2.999999 and is equally conforming — the test's own comment concedes the legacy's 2.999999 is "conforming but strictly worse" and the file header calls it "the FromDouble ROUNDING choice". It pins an implementor-defined choice inside §15.4.1's latitude, so it certifies this implementation rather than the rule. That is the identical ground on which AR-15.8.3-2 struck OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec, and the precedent is applied consistently here. test-needed: an ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program computing FUNCTION LOG10(1000) into a scale-6 and a scale-17 receiver in one run and asserting the two agree (§15.4.1 (b)), plus a receiver-less `IF FUNCTION LOG10(1000) = 3` arm. STANDARD-DECIMAL leg is 2002,2014,2023 (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL is 2014, plain STANDARD 2002–2014); the editions field is the rule's own window, derived as for AR-15.56.3-1 from §8.11 + the absence of any Annex E item, NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row.

MOVE FUNCTION LOWER-CASE(WS-N) TO WS-R` binds clean (arity 1..1 satisfied, no class screen), then IntrinsicRenderer.RenderStringValue line 397 takes the "UpperCase" or "LowerCase" or "Reverse" arm and renders `Str(ic.Args[0])`; StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundFieldOperand) (line 521) is `OperandText.AsString(n, owner.Num)`, whose FieldAsString final switch returns `CobolNum.FormatDisplay(...)` for a PIC 9 leaf - the numeric item's DISPLAY IMAGE. Only a bare numeric LITERAL is loud (StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundNumericLiteral) => Loud, line 526), and that is a run-time throw, not a cited 15.57.3 diagnostic. notes: SUSTAINED, and STRENGTHENED by a second failure mode the adjudicator missed. Rule --check verified at 15.57.4 3); its antecedent 12.3.6.4 7) a) - 'the uppercase and lowercase mappings of characters for the UPPER-CASE and LOWER-CASE intrinsic functions' - is --check verified at 12.3.6.4. MECHANISM, RE-READ IN THE GRAMMAR: `objectComputerParagraph : OBJECT_COMPUTER DOT (computerName computerAttributes? programCollatingSequenceClause? DOT)?` (CobolParserCore.g4 line 379) with `computerAttributes : ~(DOT | PROGRAM)+` (line 397) - a raw-token SINK. Nothing in CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION IS <locale-phrase> is a DOT or a PROGRAM, and grep finds ZERO occurrences of CLASSIFICATION in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend or src/Cobol.Net.Compiler, so the whole clause is swallowed and discarded. The one pass that reads that sink, VersionConformancePass.VisitComputerAttributes (line 504), switches on child token TEXT for exactly three words - MEMORY, SEGMENT-LIMIT, DEBUGGING (lines 510/513/516) - and CLASSIFICATION is not among them. COBOLNET1518 has exactly ONE raise site (IntrinsicBinder.LocaleUnsupported), reachable only by function name or by the LOCALE argument phrase, so it cannot fire here. NET EFFECT: `OBJECT-COMPUTER. X CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION IS USER-DEFAULT.` compiles with no diagnostic at all - and note that the SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT / LOCALE alternatives of locale-phrase-1 (12.3.6.2) need no SPECIAL-NAMES locale-name, so this is a complete, self-contained request that a locale BE in effect for character classification - after which every FUNCTION LOWER-CASE quietly returns the rule-4 implementor-defined invariant fold instead of the LC_CTYPE mapping the source asked for. ⚠ NEW, FROM RENDERING THE FORMAT: the 12.3.6.2 figure note states the outer bracket encloses CHOICE INDICATORS, so per 5.2.6.4 the CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION and PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses may appear 'in either order'. The grammar fixes the order (computerAttributes then programCollatingSequenceClause), so a program writing CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION *after* PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE has no slot at all and is a PARSE ERROR. The clause is therefore silently ignored in one order and rejects legal source in the other - two defects, one missing production. subject: LOWER-CASE function
notes: OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Rule --check verified at 15.57.4 4). THE RULE HAS A CONDITION AND A CONSEQUENCE, AND ONLY THE CONSEQUENCE IS IMPLEMENTED. CONSEQUENCE (verified): the implementor's choice is made and documented - docs/CONFORMANCE.md lines 118-122 state 'absent a locale, the case correspondence is implementor-defined (15.97.4 r4). COBOL.NET uses the .NET invariant Unicode case tables', which is exactly what `LowerCase(string s) => s.ToLowerInvariant()` does. CONDITION ('when a locale is not in effect') - NOT IMPLEMENTED: the compiler has no notion of a locale being in effect at all, so this branch is taken UNCONDITIONALLY rather than as the else-arm of rules 2 and 3. That is not merely theoretical: per RV-15.57.4-3 (which this same report records as DIVERGES) the OBJECT-COMPUTER CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION clause is SILENTLY ACCEPTED, so a program can put a locale in effect for character classification, get no diagnostic, and still receive the rule-4 correspondence. The adjudicator's own justification - 'No locale is EVER in effect in this compiler (rules 2 and 3 are unreachable)' - contradicts its rule-3 row, where the clause is accepted rather than refused; a silently-swallowed clause is not an unreachable one. Per the two-halves discipline this is PARTIAL, never CONFORMS. ⚠ NOTES CORRECTION, factual: the adjudicator argued 'a choice alone would not have been enough' because the standard's implementor-defined item list demands documentation. It says the opposite - Annex A item 35 reads 'Computer's coded character set (correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when a locale is not in effect). This item is required. THIS ITEM NEED NOT BE DOCUMENTED IN THE IMPLEMENTOR'S USER DOCUMENTATION. (15.57, LOWER-CASE function; 15.97, UPPER-CASE function)'. The documentation is welcome but is not what the standard requires. CHECKED AND NOT A DIVERGENCE (independently re-derived): normative Annex C, 'Mapping of uppercase letters to lowercase letters in the COBOL character repertoire', does exist - but grep for every reference to it in the standard yields exactly two normative consumers, both in the 8.3.1 word-folding rules ('Equivalence of uppercase and lowercase basic letters is achieved by folding ... in accordance with the case mapping described in Annex C'), and NONE in 15.57. So rule 4's implementor latitude is genuine and the invariant tables are a conforming determination; docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 20 (E.2 item 14, DOTLESS I / GREEK FINAL SIGMA deletions) and row 49 (E.3.3 item 6 additions) flag those as 2014->2023 case-mapping changes affecting UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE with an open `<!-- todo -->` gate marker, but under rule 4 they bind the annex, not this function. subject: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: REFUTED: verdict UNCHANGED (DIVERGES is already the floor), but every leg was RE-DERIVED from the implementation and RE-RUN rather than inherited, and two supporting claims were sharpened. THREE independent legs, all in the ONE hand-written arm BindAlgebraicFold. (a) OVER-REJECTS every FLOATING-POINT argument. cite.py --check 15.58.3 'native arithmetic is in effect' FAILS - the clause has exactly rules 1/2/3; that latitude is 15.83.3 r4 (SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC only; --check OK, 'If native arithmetic is in effect, the usage restrictions for argument-1 shall be implementor-defined') and the shipped COBOLNET1516 text cites it as authority for LOWEST. 8.5.2.12 puts the float usages in category NUMERIC, so under NATIVE (the default) a COMP-2 item satisfies r1 outright. The 1516 text's further claim that 'under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is barred by rule 2' is FALSE for COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/-LONG/-EXTENDED: 3.166 (--check OK) restricts the standard binary floating-point usages to float-binary-32/64/128. (b) OVER-REJECTS the counters: 8.5.2.12 rule 4 is literally 'A LINAGE-COUNTER.' under the heading (Numeric category) (--check OK), and the message returned for them - 'shall be a ... DATA ITEM - not a literal, an arithmetic expression, ...' - is backwards; they ARE data items. They arrive as BoundComputedOperand and the `args[0] is not BoundFieldOperand` guard turns them away. (c) UNDER-REJECTS a USER-DEFINED function, which r1's second half bars in words; UdfBindCall returns BoundNumRef over the RETURNING clone and OperandOf maps it to BoundFieldOperand, so the fold reads the TEMP's PicInfo and manufactures a constant. ARCHITECTURAL RESIDUE (sharpened): I read IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs directly - DeliberatelyUnscreened contains exactly four entries (BYTE-LENGTH, BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT) and Verified contains neither algebraic function. subject: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: REFUTED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. PARTIAL says 'correct as far as it goes'. It does not go that far: on a shape the compiler ITSELF accepts, the value returned is provably NOT representable in argument-1, which is the exact thing the rule requires it to be. I confirmed the mechanism by READING the runtime rather than sampling: CobolNum#WrapBinary computes `Int128 modulus = (Int128)1 << bits;` and for a 16-byte BinaryCapacity receiver bits = 128, which C# masks to a shift of 0, giving modulus = 1 - so `m = ((value % 1) + 1) % 1 = 0`, `half = 1 >> 1 = 0`, `m >= half` is true, and EVERY signed 16-byte store returns `0 - 1 = -1`. Its sibling CobolNum#InBinaryRange carries the identical `(Int128)1 << bits`, so with bits = 128 the range test is `value >= -0 && value < 0`, i.e. ALWAYS FALSE - every such store under ON SIZE ERROR is reported as a size error. BindAlgebraicFold hands that receiver `-(BigInteger.One << 127)` = -170141183460469231731687303715884105728, a 39-digit synthesized literal that also bypasses the 31-digit fixed-point limit COBOLNET0801 enforces on SOURCE literals (8.3.1.2). So for `01 C2 PIC S9(19) COMP-5.` the fold asserts a lowest representable value the compiler's own storage layer cannot hold, and `MOVE FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(C2) TO C2` round-trips to -1. Which container range an implementor picks for COMP-5 is implementor-defined; that the returned value be REPRESENTABLE IN ARGUMENT-1 is not. Whoever fixes the fold must fix WrapBinary and InBinaryRange in the same change set. The narrower contradiction stands too: `01 C1 PIC S9(4) COMP-5.` folds to -32768 but renders through its own picture as -2768. THE THREE HOLES also stand, and each is a case where the rule demands a value and none is produced: HOLE 1, no value for ANY floating-point argument although 13.18.60.4 GR15 NOTE 2 gives FLOAT-BINARY-64 a spec-stated -(2**1024 - 2**971) and GR14 NOTE 1 gives FLOAT-BINARY-32 -(2**128 - 2**104), and GR13 makes float-short/-long/-extended implementor-defined, which is still a definite value the rule obliges the compiler to return (the 'BoundNumLiteral cannot carry 1.797E308' objection is false - it is `record BoundNumLiteral(string Text)` and EmitCore routes an E-form literal to a Real NumX; only Decimalize is fixed-point). HOLE 2, no value for LINAGE-COUNTER / LINE-COUNTER / PAGE-COUNTER. HOLE 3, national-form numeric is COBOLNET0899, so 15.58.1's National->Numeric row is unreachable. Conversely an ILLEGAL user-defined-function argument gets a FABRICATED value (AR-15.58.3-1 leg c, re-run this pass: -9999). NEWLY FOUND, adjacent reachability residue: a SECOND `CURRENCY SIGN ... PICTURE SYMBOL ...` clause is a PARSE ERROR (COBOL0001 'unexpected PICTURE'), although 12.3.7 SR21 plainly contemplates two clauses with different symbols, and DataBinder.Switches.cs stores a SINGLE `CurrencyPicSymbol` that the last clause would overwrite and that MaskCapacity is then handed - so multi-currency numeric-edited arguments cannot be declared at all and this rule is unreachable for them. That is a SPECIAL-NAMES/grammar defect, not a fold defect; recorded so it is not lost. WHAT IS CORRECT, and it is a lot: I accept the prior record's run of all SEVEN rows of the clause's own NOTE table, plus the P-scaling, subscripted/qualified, lowercase-mask, BDB, floating-minus, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA and BINARY-SHORT/BINARY-DOUBLE round-trip results. I ADD one boundary the prior pass did not test: bare `USAGE BINARY-CHAR` and bare `USAGE BINARY-SHORT` (no SIGNED/UNSIGNED) fold to -128 and -32768, i.e. signed - consistent with the 13.18.60.2 figure's non-underlined SIGNED alternative, though the figure NOTE in specs/ISO_COBOL.md asserts SIGNED is underlined, which would make the bare form illegal; that transcription contradiction is unresolved and belongs to the USAGE clause row, not here. I ALSO DISPROVED an attack on MaskCapacity: I hand-checked `----9.99`, `$**,**9.99BCR`, `+$$$9.99`, `++++.++` and `ZZZ,ZZ9.99-` against 13.18.40 and the floating-string minus-one rule is right in each. TEST COVERAGE verified this pass to be spec-derived and thin: AssertSpec in IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs is `CompileAndRun` + `Assert.Equal(expected)` with NO legacy or GnuCOBOL leg despite the file name, and the corpus case tests/conformance/2002/highest_lowest_algebraic.cob is headed with 15.43/15.58 and Annex D.32. Between them they pin only 3 of the 7 NOTE rows for LOWEST (S99, 99V9(3), $**,**9.99); S9(4) BINARY, $**,**9.99BCR, BINARY-CHAR SIGNED and BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED remain untested. EVIDENCE: cite.py --check 15.58.4 on the rule text: OK, rule 2. cite.py --check 13.18.60.4 on GR12 and GR15: both OK. READ src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolNum.cs#WrapBinary verbatim: `int bits = 8 * receiver.StorageLength; Int128 modulus = (Int128)1 << bits; if (!receiver.Signed) return Int128.Abs(value) % modulus; Int128 m = ((value % modulus) + modulus) % modulus; return m >= (modulus >> 1) ? m - modulus : m;` and #InBinaryRange: `int bits = 8 * receiver.StorageLength; Int128 modulus = (Int128)1 << bits; ... Int128 half = modulus >> 1; return value >= -half && value < half;`. READ BindAlgebraicFold's container branch: `int bits = 8 * pic.StorageWidth; unscaled = sig.Name == "HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC" ? ... : (pic.Signed ? -(System.Numerics.BigInteger.One << (bits - 1)) : System.Numerics.BigInteger.Zero);`. Prior CONTRADICTION PROBE reproduced the consequences: `S9(4) COMP-5 = -...032768...`, `ROUNDTRIP C1 = -2768`, `S9(19) COMP-5 = -3460469231731687303715884105728` (39-digit fold truncated into a PIC S9(31) receiver), `ROUNDTRIP C2 = -0000000000000000001`, and `01 R2 PIC S9(39)` in the same file rejected `COBOLNET0801 ... 39 digit positions; ISO/IEC 1989 limits fixed-point items and literals to 31 digits (ISO 8.3.1.2)` - the check the synthesized literal bypasses. MY OWN PROBES this pass, --std 2023, E:/Temp/refb5/: r7_bare.cob (LOWALGREF07, `01 BC USAGE BINARY-CHAR.` / `01 BS USAGE BINARY-SHORT.`) -> `BC=-000000000128000`, `BS=-000000032768000`. r13_udf.cob (LOWALGREF13) -> `UDFARG=-000000009999000` for an argument 15.58.3 r1 bars. r6_float.cob (LOWALGREF06) -> COBOLNET1516, no value for a COMP-2 argument. r5_cur.cob (LOWALGREF05, two `CURRENCY SIGN IS ... PICTURE SYMBOL ...` clauses) -> `r5_cur.cob(7,33): error COBOL0001: unexpected 'PICTURE'`. TESTS READ IN FULL: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs#AssertSpec is `var (cok, cout, cdetail) = new CobolNetCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun(source); Assert.True(cok, ...); Assert.Equal(CutRunner.Normalize(expected), cout);` - no oracle leg; #Algebraic_Fold's LOWEST InlineData rows are `01 X PIC S99` -> '-099' and `01 X PIC 99V9(3)` -> '+00.000'. tests/conformance/2002/highest_lowest_algebraic.cob declares N-S99, N-S9K, N-U99V999 and N-EDIT `PIC $**,**9.99` and folds LOWEST over three of them.

notes: VERDICT UPHELD, and the defect is DEEPER than the original record found. The cross-argument class-agreement rule is enforced nowhere: CheckArgumentClasses is per-POSITION by construction (one Kind per function, looped over args) so it cannot express 'all arguments shall be of the same class' even for the functions it does screen, and what stands in its place in BindIntrinsicCore is a two-way PARTITION - `if (sig.ArgKinds == "p" && args.Count > 0 && args.All(IsStringOperand))` routes to MaxString, and any mix that is not all-string falls silently to the numeric MaxScaled path with the non-numeric operands coerced. The compiler already owns this exact check for the sibling rule - CheckRepertoireArgs raises COBOLNET1546 for §15.66.3 (NATIONAL-OF argument-1 shall not be a zero-length literal), OoBinder raises the §14.9.23.3 SR2 twin for INVOKE and CallBinder the §14.9.4.3 SR2 twin - so the diagnostic vocabulary exists and §15.59.3 r3 simply has no arm. Confirmed structurally on re-read: IntrinsicArgumentRules screens CLASS only (ClassOf -> CobolClass -> Admissible/PolymorphicExcluded); there is no literal-LENGTH channel in that table at all, so this cannot be fixed by a Verified row and needs its own per-function literal-shape screen. THE PATTERN IS WIDER THAN MAX: every §15 function carrying 'shall not be a zero-length literal' needs the same sweep (§15.63.3 MIN, §15.71.3/§15.72.3 ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN and the rest of the family). NEW FIX-QUEUE ITEM. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. E:/Temp/pbmax/maxzl.cob `MOVE FUNCTION MAX("" A1) TO RA.` compiles exit=0, no diagnostic, prints ZL=[ABC]; reproduced at --std 85, 2002, 2014. The literal is really zero-length and really selectable: E:/Temp/pbmax/maxzl2.cob `01 SP PIC X(2) VALUE SPACES. 01 R12 PIC X(12) VALUE ALL "*". STRING FUNCTION MAX("" SP) DELIMITED BY SIZE "|" DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO R12.` prints Z=[|***********] - "" and "  " compare equal under §8.8.4.2.7 r2, the leftmost ("") is selected per §15.59.4 r2, and the "|" lands in position 1, proving the returned value has size 0. Contrast: FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF("") is rejected by COBOLNET1546 for the same-worded §15.66.3 rule (IntrinsicBinder.cs#CheckRepertoireArgs).

subject: MAX function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The original adjudication sampled MIDDLE-OF-RANGE outputs (12.34 / -5.00 / 99.99; FLOAT-LONG 2.5 vs 7.25; INDEX 4 vs 9) and read the mechanism as correct. Reading the implementation instead finds THREE independent, probe-confirmed defects, each producing a silently wrong returned value on CONFORMING source, and none of them reachable from the values sampled. ALSO: TWO CITATIONS IN THE ORIGINAL RECORD ARE WRONG, one level off in the way this review has been burned by before - the record cited 'NUMERIC (§8.8.4.2.2, algebraic value)' and 'INDEX (§8.8.4.2.3)'; `cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.2 "For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands"` FAILS, because §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and §8.8.4.2.3 is 'Syntax rules'. The real clauses are §8.8.4.2.4 (Comparison of numeric operands, --check OK) and §8.8.4.2.13 (Comparisons involving index-names or index data items, --check OK). §8.8.4.2.7 / §8.8.4.2.9 in the record are correct. THE THREE DEFECTS: (D1) THE SCALE-ALIGNMENT WIDENING WRAPS Int128 SILENTLY. AlignedArgsEx picks s = max(argument scales) and emits NumericRenderer.Align -> `CobolNum.Rescale(x, from, s, Truncation)`, whose widening arm is a bare `value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`; RoslynBackend sets no checkOverflow, so any argument needing more than 38 digits at the common scale wraps modulo 2^128 BEFORE MaxScaled ever compares it. PIC 9(21) against PIC 9V9(18) - both far inside the 31-digit standard range and both accepted by the compiler's own data description - needs 39 digits and wraps NEGATIVE, so MAX returns the SMALLER argument. This is the PB5/PB13/PB22 unchecked-narrowing family in its widening direction, and AlignedArgs feeds MIN, SUM, RANGE, MEDIAN, MIDRANGE, ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN identically - sweep it. NO ARITHMETIC-MODE LATITUDE IS AVAILABLE: it reproduces verbatim under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.`, where §8.8.4.2.4's native sentence does not apply and the standard instead requires the comparison to be performed as if each operand were converted to a standard-decimal intermediate data item - which both operands fit. (D2) A SINGLE FLOAT ARGUMENT DESTROYS EVERY OTHER ARGUMENT'S CONTENT. AnyRealArgument routes the whole call to RenderFloat, which renders every argument as a C# double and calls `MaxReal(params double[] xs) => xs.Max()`, then quantizes with FromDouble. §15.59.4 r1 says the returned value IS THE CONTENT of the selected argument - not an approximation of it, and §15.59.4 carries no equivalent arithmetic expression, so §15.4.1's native-arithmetic latitude ('the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor', --check OK) does not reach the VALUE. Mixing a FLOAT-LONG item with a fixed-point item is conforming source: §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts both under class Numeric, so §15.59.3 r2 is satisfied. The selection is CORRECT (ORD-MAX and the relation condition both name the fixed argument) and the delivery is wrong by eighteen orders of magnitude. (D3) A NATIONAL GROUP ARGUMENT IS COMPARED WITH THE ALPHANUMERIC COLLATING SEQUENCE. §8.5.2.1 says 'a national group item has class and category national' (--check OK) and §8.8.4.2.9 requires national operands to compare by the current NATIONAL program collating sequence (--check OK). But OperandCategory returns `f.Place.Item.IsGroup ? null : ...`, so nationalArg is FALSE for a national group; BindIntrinsicCore then sets `collate = maxMinStr && ctx.Data.Collating is not null && !nationalArg` = TRUE and the backend passes the 256-entry ALPHANUMERIC __COLLATE weights table over national characters - precisely the aliasing the code's own CHAR/ORD comment says must never happen. Two MAX calls over identical national data return OPPOSITE answers depending only on whether the data is described as an elementary item or as a national group. WHAT IS CONFIRMED CORRECT (and is why this is DIVERGES on boundaries, not NOT-IMPLEMENTED): fixed-point comparison inside 38 aligned digits; the alphanumeric native and PCS paths through CobolString.Compare with §8.8.4.2.7 r2 space padding, never string.CompareOrdinal; and the elementary-national path. Test-ref cleared: conformance:2002/intrinsic_max_collating is spec-derived and remains valid corroboration for the alphanumeric-PCS leg, but a green test cannot close a DIVERGES row. NEW FIX-QUEUE ITEM covering D1 (with the AlignedArgs family sweep), D2 and D3. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only; D1/D2/D3 all reproduce at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023, cobol.exe from src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0; every probe in E:/Temp/rfmax with a unique PROGRAM-ID. CONTROL (ctl.cob, RFMAXCTL): `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MAX(N1 N2)` over PIC 9(4) 12/99 -> CTLNUM=0099; `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(A1 A2) TO RA` -> CTLSTR=XYZ; exit=0. D1: wide2.cob (RFMAXWID2) `01 B1 PIC 9(21) VALUE 999999999999999999999. 01 B2 PIC 9V9(18) VALUE 0.000000000000000001. 01 RB PIC 9(21).` -> `COMPUTE RB = FUNCTION MAX(B1 B2)` prints B21x18=000000000000000000000 (must be 999999999999999999999) and `FUNCTION MIN(B1 B2)` prints MINB=020847100762815390391 - a value equal to NEITHER argument's content, which is the wrap made visible. The same file's in-range control `01 C1 PIC 9(29)` against `01 C2 PIC 9V9(9)` (38 aligned digits) prints C29x9=99999999999999999999999999999, correct - so the boundary is exactly Int128's 38 digits. wide.cob (RFMAXWIDE) PIC 9(30) vs PIC 9V9(9) -> WIDE=000000000000000000000000000000. widerel.cob (RFMAXWREL) shows the shared root cause: `IF B1 > B2` prints REL=B1-NOT-GT-B2, so the relation condition wraps too. widestd.cob (RFMAXWSTD), identical but with `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` -> STDMAX=000000000000000000000, exit=0 - the native-arithmetic escape hatch is closed. D2: fltc.cob (RFMAXFLTC) `01 F1 USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 1.0. 01 N1 PIC 9(18) VALUE 999999999999999999. 01 N0 PIC 9(18) VALUE 1.` -> NOFLOAT= `FUNCTION MAX(N0 N1)` = 999999999999999999 (correct, no float present); WITHFLT= `FUNCTION MAX(F1 N1)` = 000000000000000013; ORD= `FUNCTION ORD-MAX(F1 N1)` = 02 and `IF N1 > F1` = REL=N1-GT-F1 - so the comparison picks N1 and the returned CONTENT is 13. The arithmetic of the corruption is exact: 999999999999999999 -> double 1e18 -> FromDouble at ws=9 -> 1000000000000000013287555072 -> rescale to scale 0 -> 1000000000000000013 -> mod 10^18 -> 13. D3: ngpcs.cob (RFMAXNGPC) under `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `ALPHABET AL IS "ZYXWVUTSRQPONMLKJIHGFEDCBA"` with N1 PIC N(3) VALUE N"AAA", N2 PIC N(3) VALUE N"ZZZ" and NG1/NG2 the same values as one-item NATIONAL GROUPS -> ELEM=ZZZ (elementary, correct - the alphanumeric alphabet must not touch national operands) but GRP=AAA (group - the alphanumeric weights were applied, inverting the order). Identical data, opposite results. Related shape in ngrp.cob (RFMAXNGRP): `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(NG1 NG2) TO RAN` with RAN PIC X(6) compiles exit=0 and prints NGTOAN=[ZZZYYY] - the same MOVE that tests/conformance/negative/max_national_result_to_an.cob rejects for the elementary twin.

subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "A" ALSO "B", "C", "D".` with P1 PIC X VALUE "A", P2 PIC X VALUE "B" prints REL=A-EQ-B (the program's own relation condition confirms the tie is real), then `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P1 P2) TO R1` -> T1=A and `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P2 P1) TO R1` -> T2=B. The selection follows ARGUMENT POSITION over two operands that are equal but not identical, which is leftmost-wins in the form the rule states it. Corroborating, from the original adjudication (size-tie form): E:/Temp/pbmax/maxsize.cob `01 S3 PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 S6 PIC X(6) VALUE "AB".` -> `STRING FUNCTION MAX(S3 S6) ... INTO R12` = C1=[AB |********] (size 3) and the reversed order C2=[AB    |*****] (size 6); national, E:/Temp/pbmax/maxnat3.cob `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N3 N6))` -> L1=000C (3) and `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N6 N3))` -> L2=000F (6); zero-length leftmost, maxzl2.cob `FUNCTION MAX("" SP)` -> Z=[|***********]. Refuter's alphabetic-item repeat, E:/Temp/rfmax/cats.cob: `FUNCTION MAX(AL1 AL2)` over PIC A(3)/PIC A(6) both VALUE "ABC" -> ALPHA1=[ABC|********], reversed -> ALPHA2=[ABC   |*****]. CONTROL: E:/Temp/rfmax/ctl.cob compiles and runs (CTLNUM=0099, CTLSTR=XYZ).

subject: MAX function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The rule is a CONDITIONAL - 'IF THE TYPE OF THE FUNCTION IS alphanumeric or national, the size of the returned value is the same as the size of the selected argument-1' - and it therefore has two halves: the antecedent (deciding the function type, per the §15.59.1 result-type table) and the consequent (the size). The original adjudication verified the CONSEQUENT thoroughly and treated the ANTECEDENT as settled by the V54 fix. THE ANTECEDENT IS MISDECIDED FOR A WHOLE ARGUMENT SHAPE. §8.5.2.1 states 'a national group item has class and category national' (--check OK), so §15.59.1's table gives a NATIONAL function type for national-group arguments. BindIntrinsicCore decides the type with `category = args.All(a => OperandCategory(a) is PicCategory.National) ? National : Alphanumeric`, and OperandCategory is `BoundFieldOperand f => f.Place.Item.IsGroup ? null : f.Place.Item.Pic?.Category` - NULL for every group. So MAX over national group items is typed ALPHANUMERIC, and the rule's own antecedent selects the wrong branch: the returned size is then expressed in alphanumeric rather than national character positions, and the §14.9.25 Table-16 National->AN MOVE guard that the V54 fix installed is bypassed for exactly the shape it was written to catch. The CONSEQUENT itself is confirmed correct in every shape reachable: MaxString returns `xs[ExtremeIndex(...)]`, i.e. the SELECTED element of the params array, so the returned string is the selected argument's own rendered image and carries its own width - nothing re-pads it and no compile-time size is imposed. What is NOT closed is the antecedent for group arguments, and that is why this is PARTIAL and not CONFORMS. The fix belongs with the RV-15.59.4-1 D3 item (same OperandCategory null-for-group root cause, same one-line consequence for both the collating sequence and the result category), not as a separate queue entry. ⚠ The Alphanumeric fallback on a MIXED national/alphanumeric argument list is a different defect and belongs to AR-15.59.3-2 (such a list is not conforming source). EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. THE ANTECEDENT DEFECT: E:/Temp/rfmax/ngrp.cob (RFMAXNGRP) `01 NG1. 05 NA1 PIC N(3) VALUE N"AAA". 05 NA2 PIC N(3) VALUE N"BBB". 01 NG2. 05 NB1 PIC N(3) VALUE N"ZZZ". 05 NB2 PIC N(3) VALUE N"YYY". 01 RAN PIC X(6).` -> `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(NG1 NG2) TO RAN` compiles exit=0 and prints NGTOAN=[ZZZYYY], i.e. a national value delivered into an alphanumeric receiver with no diagnostic. tests/conformance/negative/max_national_result_to_an.cob is the negative golden that rejects the IDENTICAL move for the elementary twin (`01 W-N1 PIC N(3) ... MOVE FUNCTION MAX(W-N1 W-N2) TO W-X.`, reject-at 2002 2014 2023) - so the guard exists, is spec-derived, and does not fire for groups. The same file's `COMPUTE L = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(NG1 NG2))` -> NGLEN=0006, which is the selected group's own size, confirming the consequent still holds numerically even where the type is mislabelled. THE CONSEQUENT, verified across every shape: ALPHANUMERIC via STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE against an ALL "*" background - E:/Temp/pbmax/maxsize.cob C1=[AB |********] (tie, shorter leftmost, size 3), C2=[AB    |*****] (tie, longer leftmost, size 6), C3=[ZZZ|********] (strict winner is the SHORTER argument, PIC X(3) beating PIC X(8), so the size follows the SELECTION and not the widest argument). NATIONAL - E:/Temp/pbmax/maxnat3.cob via FUNCTION LENGTH: L1=000C, L2=000F, L3=000C. REFUTER ADDITIONS: reference-modified argument, E:/Temp/rfmax/refm.cob (RFMAXREFM) `STRING FUNCTION MAX(S9(1:3) T3) ...` -> RM1=[ZZZ|********] against the control `STRING S9(1:3) ...` -> CTLRM=[ZZZ|********], and `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(S9(1:3) T3))` -> RMLEN=0003, so a ref-mod view contributes its VIEW's size, not the base item's 9. ALPHABETIC and NUMERIC-EDITED, E:/Temp/rfmax/cats.cob (RFMAXCATS): PIC A(3)/PIC A(6) -> ALPHA1=[ABC|********] / ALPHA2=[ABC   |*****]; PIC ZZZ9 VALUE 5 against PIC X(2) VALUE SPACES -> NEDIT=[   5|*******] (size 4, the edited image's own width). Zero-length literal selected: maxzl2.cob -> Z=[|***********] (size 0). CONTROL: E:/Temp/rfmax/ctl.cob compiles and runs (CTLNUM=0099, CTLSTR=XYZ), so the clean compile of ngrp.cob is not blanket permissiveness.

subject: MEAN function
notes:
REFUTED (editions, narrowed from "85, 2002, 2014, 2023"): the old window was taken from the CODE UNDER REVIEW — IntrinsicCatalog's own row (`Add(new("MEAN", ..., 85))`) plus `--std 85/2002/2014/2023` probes of this compiler. The 2023 standard cannot establish it. What the spec DOES support: §15.60 appears nowhere in Annex E (neither E.2 nor E.3.3 lists MEAN among the 2014→2023 additions or changes) and nowhere in Annex F, so the clause is unchanged across 2014 and 2023; and bibliography entry [6] records that intrinsic functions reached ISO 1989:1985 only through *Amd 1:1992 intrinsic function module*, i.e. NOT the base 1985 text. Whether COBOL.NET's `--std 85` means 1985 or 1985+Amd 1 is a PROJECT convention, not a spec fact, so 85 and 2002 are dropped rather than asserted.

REFUTED (severity — the verdict stands, the consequence was understated): the previous record showed one PIC X argument returning 0, which reads as "unscreened but harmless". It is not harmless. With the screen absent the binder falls through to the ordinary numeric coercion, so a non-numeric argument is silently REINTERPRETED as a digit image and MEAN manufactures a value: `FUNCTION MEAN(WS-X)` over `PIC X(6) VALUE "123456"` returns 123456.00, and `FUNCTION MEAN(WS-ED)` over `PIC ZZZ,ZZ9.99 VALUE 1234.56` (class ALPHANUMERIC, §8.5.2.1) returns 1234.55 — a WRONG value from an argument whose digits are visibly right, which is the worst shape this defect can take. Zero diagnostics, exit 0, strict mode.

UNCHANGED FINDING: MEAN is enforced NOWHERE. The screen exists (PB1/PB12/PB19 built it) but is driven from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, and MEAN is absent from that dictionary AND from DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its `if (!Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` guard before any class is looked at. The catalog row does declare ArgKinds "n", but that column is deliberately not read (it is the unaudited hint column PB1 refused to screen from). Per the task brief, absence from Verified is a genuine finding, not a reading gap.

FIX SHAPE: one row, `["MEAN"] = ('n', "§15.60.3 r1")`. The 'n' arm of Admissible already means exactly what the rule says (§8.5.2.1 class NUMERIC, numeric-edited excluded), so no new vocabulary is needed — unlike §15.45.3's boolean, which needed PB20 first. §15.60.3 r1 is a single-clause CLASS rule with no value half and no cross-argument half, so a Verified row closes it completely.

SIBLING SWEEP (⌘ rule 4 — every bug is a pattern): the review's earlier batches covered §15.7, §15.8–15.19, §15.32–15.44, §15.45–15.57 and §15.70–15.79. The §15.58–15.69 band that contains MEAN was never reached, and its neighbours carry the SAME one-sentence rule and are equally unscreened: MEDIAN (§15.61.3), MIDRANGE (§15.62.3), plus SUM (§15.88.3), STANDARD-DEVIATION (§15.86.3) and VARIANCE (§15.98.3) further out. MAX/MIN (§15.59/§15.63) are the negative-list 'p' shape already modelled by ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN and need the same treatment.

subject: MEAN function
notes:
REFUTED — THE "WHAT CONFORMS" HALF IS FALSE. The previous record certified the fixed-point half as conforming on the strength of "the exact Int128 sum (identical to the SDIDI addition chain — ≤32-digit sums are exact in both engines)" and "probed TRUE for n=1, 2 and 3". Both are sampling artefacts of small operands, exactly the PB5 mistake the brief names. The premise is wrong: what enters SumScaled is not the arguments, it is the arguments RESCALED to their common scale by AlignedArgsEx → NumericRenderer.Align → `CobolNum.Rescale`, whose widening arm is a bare unchecked `value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)` over Int128. A 31-digit integer argument beside a scale-18 argument aligns to 10^49, and Int128 tops out at 1.70e38, so the operand WRAPS MODULO 2^128 before SumScaled or CobolDec.From ever sees it.

THE HARD DIVERGENCE (no implementor latitude anywhere in it). Under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` at --std 2023, with FIXED-POINT arguments ONLY and no float in the program:
    01 WS-A PIC 9(31) VALUE 1000000000000000000000000000000.
    01 WS-B PIC 9V9(18)  VALUE 2.0.
    IF FUNCTION MEAN(WS-A WS-B) = (WS-A + WS-B) / 2  →  FALSE
    COMPUTE WS-R = FUNCTION MEAN(WS-A WS-B)  →  0000000000009480057455463682825
    COMPUTE WS-R = (WS-A + WS-B) / 2         →  0500000000000000000000000000001   ← correct, same compiler, same mode
§15.4.1 r1 is unconditional under the standard modes ("the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression") and NOTE 2 states the relation "will evaluate to true". It evaluates FALSE, and the compiler's OWN evaluation of §15.60.4's expression proves the correct value is reachable: the SDIDI sum is 1000000000000000000000000000002 (31 significant digits, well inside §8.8.1.5.2 NOTE 2's 34-digit precision) and the quotient 500000000000000000000000000001 is exact. §15.4.1's implementor-defined escapes do not reach this — it is not native arithmetic, no argument is implementor-defined, and no sub-expression produces implementor-defined results.

LEGALITY OF THE WITNESS (checked before relying on it): the 31-digit composite limit is §14.7.7 r2, which binds only "ADD, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statements when native arithmetic is in effect" — not COMPUTE, and not a relation condition, and not any standard mode (§14.7.7 r3 defines statements under the standard modes in terms of arithmetic expressions instead). So the witness is legal source in every statement it uses.

SAME DEFECT UNDER NATIVE, and no size error to warn anyone: the identical program with no OPTIONS paragraph returns 0000000000007534060890583240347 for a true mean of 500000000000000000000000000001 that FITS the PIC 9(31) receiver exactly, with the ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. §8.8.1.3 makes native arithmetic implementor-defined and §15.4.1 asks only for "an implementor-defined approximation", but a value 11 orders of magnitude away, produced by a silent modulo-2^128 wrap, is not an approximation of anything and is not a technique the implementor has specified. Note also that native and standard-decimal wrap to DIFFERENT garbage (7534060890583240347 vs 9480057455463682825), so the "same value for a given function" property of §15.4.1 fails as well.

subject: MEDIAN function
notes:
VERDICT UPHELD, and the §8.8.4.2.4 citation re-validated mechanically (cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.4 "The comparison is performed as if each operand not already in the format of a standard-decimal intermediate data item had been converted to that form" => OK §8.8.4.2.4 Comparison of numeric operands).
The FIXED-POINT arrangement is exactly §8.8.4.2.4: `AlignedArgsEx` computes `int s = xs.Max(x => x.Scale)` and lifts every argument through `NumericRenderer.Align`, whose non-Real arm is `CobolNum.Rescale(expr, x.Scale, toScale, Truncation)` — and because the target is the MAXIMUM scale the rescale only ever multiplies, so it is never lossy and `Array.Sort` over the unscaled Int128 IS comparison with respect to algebraic value regardless of usage.
⛔ THE FLOAT ROUTE BREAKS THE CLAUSE'S OWN STANDARD-ARITHMETIC PARAGRAPH. `RenderNum`'s `if (AnyRealArgument(ic) && …) return RenderFloat(…)` has no arithmetic-mode guard, so ONE COMP-1/COMP-2 argument makes `MedianReal` sort ALL operands as binary64 — including 18-digit fixed-point operands that §8.8.1.5.2 r1 converts into an SDIDI exactly. Distinct algebraic values then compare EQUAL. Order is never INVERTED (round-to-nearest is monotone), so the failure mode is COLLAPSE, not inversion — which is why the sorted position still tracks but the selected value does not. Same one-line root cause as RV-15.61.4-1/-2; fixing the route fixes all three.
Not applicable / not reachable: §15.61.3 r1 confines arguments to class numeric, so §8.8.4.2.5's numeric-vs-alphanumeric arm and the index-item arm cannot arise for a conforming program; the §8.8.4.2.4 signed-zero sentence is vacuous over Int128 (no -0). ⚠ Note the dependency the other way round: that "not reachable" holds only for a CONFORMING program, and AR-15.61.3-1 shows the compiler currently ACCEPTS a non-conforming alphanumeric argument, in which case those arms are reached by whatever coercion the operand renderer applies. Landing the AR-15.61.3-1 row is what makes this paragraph's exclusion real rather than assumed.

subject: MIDRANGE function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES, on THREE legs, all measured. The adjudicator read the body, called the ×5-at-scale-s+1 trick exact — which it is, in the middle — and sampled small operands. THE ×5 IS ALSO WHERE THE DEFECT IS. LEG 1, MIDRANGE-SPECIFIC Int128 HEADROOM LOSS (native arithmetic, the default, the primary path). `MidrangeScaled(params Int128[] xs) => (MaxScaled(xs) + MinScaled(xs)) * 5;` returns at scale s+1, so it needs a factor of ten MORE Int128 range than MAX/MIN/SUM/RANGE, which return at scale s. It therefore wraps at ONE FIFTH the magnitude those do, silently, with no size error — and I isolated a case where MAX and MIN are both CORRECT and MIDRANGE alone is wrong, which is what makes this MIDRANGE's own defect and not the shared alignment residue the adjudicator waved at: P PIC S9(29)V99 = 99999999999999999999999999999.98 and Q PIC SV9(9) = 0.000000002 (both inside the compiler's own 31-digit cap, and the true midrange 49999999999999999999999999999.990000001 FITS the receiver exactly, so no size condition is due). MAX returned 99999999999999999999999999999.98, MIN returned 0.000000002, and MIDRANGE returned 15971763307906153653662539256.81 while the HAND-WRITTEN §15.62.4 EAE `(FUNCTION MAX(P Q) + FUNCTION MIN(P Q)) / 2` returned the correct 49999999999999999999999999999.99. §15.62.4 r1's own stated equality is contradicted by the compiler, on legal source, in the mode §15.4.1 still requires "an implementor-defined APPROXIMATION of the value of that expression" — a value 3.2× off with the top thirty digits wrong is not an approximation, and ON SIZE ERROR did not fire. THE ADJUDICATOR'S DISMISSAL IS FACTUALLY WRONG: it wrote that at the wide boundary "MIDRANGE and the hand-written EAE produce the IDENTICAL garbage, so §15.62.4 r1's equality still holds". I measured both and they are NOT identical — on P1 PIC S9(31)=9999999999999999999999999999999 against Q1 PIC S9(22)V9(9), MIDRANGE gave -2150793182239857356051173691.94 and the written EAE gave +6590568020194783533662374779.4: different magnitude AND different sign. notes: VERDICT SUSTAINED on independent re-derivation. NO CROSS-ARGUMENT CLASS CHECK EXISTS ANYWHERE, and — unlike AR-15.63.3-1 — adding a Verified row cannot fix it. The screen's shape is one `(char Kind, string Clause)` PER FUNCTION, applied per POSITION by `Violation(rule.Kind, args[i])`; it can say "argument-i shall be of class X" and nothing else. "All arguments shall be of the SAME class" is a relation BETWEEN positions, which the table cannot express — the identical structural residue already named in IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs's own comments for SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME (§15.79.3 r3) and INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE ("r3 is a CROSS-ARGUMENT rule ... which a per-position screen cannot express"). This is now the THIRD instance, so it is a design gap in the screen, not three separate misses: the structure wanted is an optional per-function cross-argument predicate evaluated after the per-position pass (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — the shape that makes the next case automatic). The exception half of the rule (alphabetic mixed with alphanumeric) is satisfied trivially and permanently, because PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric and CobolClass has no Alphabetic member by design — so no future tightening can accidentally reject that legal mixture. The MAX/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN siblings carry the same rule text and the same gap. Note the compiler does not merely fail to diagnose: the numeric channel is chosen by `args.All(IsStringOperand)`, so a mixed list silently coerces the alphanumeric operand through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric and returns a wrong value rather than failing loudly. Violation(rule.Kind, args[i])`. The only cross-argument logic in IntrinsicBinder is `if (sig.ArgKinds == "p" && args.Count > 0 && args.All(IsStringOperand))`, which selects the RUNTIME CHANNEL and emits no diagnostic. subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTED: PARTIAL → DIVERGES. The adjudication found ONE broken shape (a figurative argument), called the rest "right on every channel I could reach", and rated it PARTIAL. Reading the IMPLEMENTATION instead of sampling outputs finds TWO MORE, both of which produce a returned value that is the content of NO argument-1 — a flat contradiction of the rule, not an unverified edge. (1) ⛔ THE Int128 ALIGNMENT OVERFLOW (the PB5 shape, one level down). IntrinsicRenderer.AlignedArgsEx aligns every MIN argument to `s = max(argument scales)` via NumericRenderer.Align → CobolNum.Rescale, whose widening arm is `value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)` — an UNCHECKED Int128 multiply. When (max integer digits) + (max fraction digits) across the argument list exceeds 38, the widened operand exceeds Int128 and WRAPS SILENTLY. `FUNCTION MIN(BIGV SMLV)` with `01 BIGV PIC 9(24) VALUE 200000000000000000000000.` and `01 SMLV PIC 9V9(15) VALUE 0.000000000000001.` — two positive, legal, in-range items — returns a NEGATIVE value, and `IF FUNCTION MIN(BIGV SMLV) = SMLV` is FALSE. No EC-SIZE, no diagnostic. §15.63.4 r1 delegates the comparison to §8.8.4.2 simple relation conditions; the compiler's §8.8.4.2 comparison is itself broken at that magnitude (`IF BIGV > SMLV` evaluates FALSE), so the delegation cannot save it. The threshold was pinned: 19+18 = 37 digits OK, 20+18 = 38 digits OK, 24+15 = 39 digits wraps. §15.4.1's native-arithmetic latitude does NOT cover this — that latitude is for functions whose returned value rules "contain one or more equivalent arithmetic expressions" and for the "characteristics and representation of the returned value"; §15.63.4 specifies NO equivalent arithmetic expression, it defines the returned value as the CONTENT of an argument, and no representation choice makes a positive minimum come out negative. ROOT CAUSE AND SIBLING SWEEP: the defect is at the ONE alignment choke point, so it is NOT MIN-specific — the same 39-digit list gives MAX = 0, RANGE = a negative value, plain `BIGV + SMLV` = a negative value, and a bare relation condition the wrong answer. Fix the choke point (a checked/wide alignment, or comparison without a common-scale widening), not the MIN row. (2) ⛔ FLOAT CONTAMINATION OF A FIXED-POINT ARGUMENT'S CONTENT. IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum routes on `AnyRealArgument(ic)`, so ONE float argument sends the whole list through `MinReal(params double[] xs) => xs.Min()` — every fixed-point argument converted to binary64 first. `01 D1 PIC 9(18)V9 VALUE 123456789012345678.9.` with a FLOAT-LONG sibling holding 1.0E30 returns 123456789012345678.1 into a `PIC 9(18)V9` receiver: the selected argument is D1 and the returned value is not D1's content. Worse, TWO distinct arguments collapse to one double and the answer is the content of NEITHER: `FUNCTION MIN(D1 D2 FL)` with D2 = 123456789012345678.8 returns ...678.1 in BOTH argument orders, while `FUNCTION MIN(D1 D2)` correctly returns ...678.8. And the SAME function reference yields two different values depending on the RECEIVER's shape — `IF FUNCTION MIN(D1 FL) = D1` is TRUE (the receiver-less arm keeps binary64 via RealResult) while `COMPUTE R3 = FUNCTION MIN(D1 FL)` gives ...678.1 — which is exactly the shape-dependence PB13 closed, reopened for MIN. The code's own justification at IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum is "each of these functions is an equivalent arithmetic expression over its own operands"; ⛔ THAT PREMISE IS FALSE FOR MIN — §15.63.4 contains no equivalent arithmetic expression (verified on the rendered printed page, folio 888), so §15.4.1's approximation latitude does not reach it. (3) The adjudication's own finding, sustained: `FUNCTION MIN(SPACE identifier)` compiles and then aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException, because IntrinsicBinder.IsStringOperand has arms for BoundStringLiteral, BoundFieldOperand and BoundComputedOperand but NONE for BoundFigurative, so `args.All(IsStringOperand)` is false, the call keeps the numeric RuntimeMethod, and NumericRenderer.Visit(BoundFigurative) emits EmitText.LoudValue("long", "figurative 'S' in a numeric context"). Legal source: §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 (--check OK) plus §15.3 item 2. WHAT IS STILL CORRECT and should not be re-litigated: the exact fixed-point channel below 39 digits, §8.8.4.2.7 r2 space-padding (CobolString.Compare, not string.CompareOrdinal), the alphanumeric PCS, the national PCS, index arguments, and the string selection itself. subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The STRING half is genuinely verified and I strengthened it — leftmost-on-tie is realized by the strict comparison in ExtremeIndex (`if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i;`), MinString returns `xs[k]` (the leftmost ARGUMENT, not a rebuilt value), and I confirmed it through a SECOND, independent tie mechanism the adjudication never touched: a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE that gives two DIFFERENT characters the same weight, where the tie exists only in the weights table. That half stands. WHAT DOES NOT STAND IS THE OTHER HALF AND THE ARGUMENT THAT DISMISSED IT. The record justified skipping the numeric/float channels with "tied numeric arguments have identical content by definition, so returning the value is equivalent and NO DEFECT IS HIDDEN". A defect IS hidden there, and it is hidden precisely BECAUSE MinScaled/MinReal return a computed value rather than a selected argument: (a) on the float channel `MinReal(params double[] xs) => xs.Min()` ties two arguments whose contents are NOT identical — `FUNCTION MIN(D1 D2 FL)` with D1 = 123456789012345678.9, D2 = 123456789012345678.8 and a FLOAT-LONG sibling returns 123456789012345678.1 in BOTH argument orders, the content of neither argument, so there is no "content of the leftmost argument-1" being returned at all; (b) on the exact channel the Int128 alignment overflow documented under RV-15.63.4-1 makes MinScaled return a wrapped value equal to no argument's content. In both cases the value-returning shape is what makes the corruption invisible, which is exactly the risk the record ruled out. Additionally the rule is not delivered AT ALL for a figurative argument (the run-time abort under RV-15.63.4-1), so the tie rule is untestable on a legal argument shape. VERDICT: the tie SELECTION is correct wherever a selection actually happens (the alphanumeric/national channel, native and both PCS variants); it is NOT established on the numeric or float channels, where no selection happens. ⚠ No spec-derived test pins the tie rule; the two LENGTH probes below plus the PCS equal-weight probe are the natural golden — a later refactor of ExtremeIndex to `<=` would silently invert leftmost-on-tie and nothing in the suite would fail. EVIDENCE: Read ExtremeIndex: `int k = 0; for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; } return k;` — strict, first-wins; MinString/OrdMinString/MaxString/OrdMaxString and all three collation overloads funnel through it. Read MinScaled (`Int128 m = xs[0]; foreach (var x in xs) if (x < m) m = x; return m;` — a VALUE, no index) and MinReal (`xs.Min()` — likewise). Probes at --std 2023. Adjudication's, re-checked: two arguments that compare EQUAL but differ in size (`01 Q2 PIC X(2) VALUE "AB". 01 Q4 PIC X(4) VALUE "AB".`) → `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MIN(Q2 Q4))` = 2 and, swapped, = 4; the result tracks argument ORDER, and this also proves FUNCTION LENGTH of a nested string intrinsic is a RUNTIME .Length (confirmed in IntrinsicBinder.BindLengthFold: the `BoundComputedOperand { Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall { ResultCategory: Alphanumeric or National } }` arm returns a BoundIntrinsicCall, not a fold), so the LENGTH-based probes in this subject are sound rather than compile-time constants. XPC PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS EQW.` with `ALPHABET EQW IS "A" ALSO "B", "C", "D".` gives 'A' and 'B' the same weight; `FUNCTION MIN(QB QA)` → PCSTIE-BA=[B] and `FUNCTION MIN(QA QB)` → PCSTIE-AB=[A] — the leftmost of a weights-table tie, correct in both orders. subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The rule has TWO halves and only one is satisfied. THE CONSEQUENT HOLDS, and I verified it harder than the adjudication did: its probes all had the SELECTED argument also be the SHORTEST (P3/P5 → 3 both ways; N2/N5 → 2 both ways), which cannot distinguish "the selected argument's size" from "the minimum of the declared sizes" — an ambiguity the record did not notice. I broke that tie by making the selected argument the LONGER one (`01 A5 PIC X(5) VALUE "AAAAA". 01 B3 PIC X(3) VALUE "ZZZ".` — A5 is the minimum and the longer): LENGTH = 5 in both argument orders, and the MOVE image is "AAAAA" not a 3-character truncation. Also confirmed on a NATIONAL pair and on a DYNAMIC LENGTH item (a runtime size the compiler cannot fold). The mechanism is by construction — MinString returns `xs[ExtremeIndex(...)]` verbatim and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderStringValue passes each argument's own rendered image with no width coercion — so there is no re-padding or normalisation that could lose it. THE ANTECEDENT DOES NOT HOLD. The rule is conditioned on "if the TYPE OF THE FUNCTION is alphanumeric or national", and the compiler decides that with `sig.ArgKinds == "p" && args.Count > 0 && args.All(IsStringOperand)`. IsStringOperand's final arm is `_ => false`, with NO case for BoundFigurative — so `FUNCTION MIN(SPACE identifier)`, whose arguments are ALL of §15.3 type 2 Alphanumeric (§8.3.3.6.3 SR1, --check OK), is typed NUMERIC, never reaches MinString, and aborts at run time with no value and therefore no size. IsStringOperand is also over-wide in the other direction — it admits `PicCategory.Boolean`, a class §15.63.3 r1 excludes outright — so the same predicate that decides this rule's antecedent is wrong at BOTH edges. A rule whose consequent is right and whose antecedent mis-classifies a legal argument shape is PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. ⚠ The companion V54 category resolution IS correct where it is reached: `category = args.All(a => OperandCategory(a) is PicCategory.National) ? PicCategory.National : PicCategory.Alphanumeric`, so a national selection is not mislabelled alphanumeric on the way out. ⚠ Untested by any spec-derived golden; the LENGTH-of-MIN probes below (specifically the selected-is-longer pair) are the corpus row to add. EVIDENCE: Read MinString — `xs[ExtremeIndex(xs, false, ...)]`, the selected argument returned verbatim — and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderStringValue's `"MaxString" or "MinString" => RuntimeApi.Intrinsic(sig.RuntimeMethod, CollatePrefix(ic) + StrArgList(ic))`, which passes each argument's own image with no width coercion. Read IsStringOperand in full: `BoundStringLiteral => true; BoundFieldOperand f => f.Place.Item.IsGroup || f.Place.Item.Pic?.Category is Alphanumeric or NumericEdited or National or Boolean; BoundComputedOperand { Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall { ResultCategory: Alphanumeric or National } } => true; _ => false;` — no BoundFigurative arm, and Boolean admitted. Adjudication's probes retained as corroboration (P3/P5 → 3/3, N2/N5 → 2/2, numeric-edited `PIC ZZ9.99` → EDTMIN=[  5.10] EDTLEN=6, reference-modified `FUNCTION MIN(S8(1:2) S5)` → RMVAL=[AB] RMLEN=2) — noting that none of them can distinguish the two competing hypotheses, which is why the selected-is-longer pair was needed. THE ANTECEDENT FAILURE, E:/Temp/minrefute/fig.cob (MINRFFIG): `MOVE FUNCTION MIN(SPACE S3) TO RS` compiles with NO diagnostic and dies with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... figurative 'S' in a numeric context` — no returned value, hence no size. subject: MOD function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The adjudication read ONE of the TWO bodies that implement MOD and concluded the zero-divisor rule was handled; the other body drops it silently.
THE MECHANISM. `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` routes a MOD call to `CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#ModReal` whenever `AnyRealArgument(ic)` is true, and `ModReal` is `b == 0 ? 0 : a - (b * Math.Floor(a / b))`. That ternary is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT zero-divisor guard and it NEVER calls `ExceptionState.ArgumentError`. It returns a finite 0.0, so neither `CobolIntrinsics.RealResult` (NaN-only) nor `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble` (NaN-only) — the two screens the renderer relies on to keep the EC raise site alive — can see it either. The exception condition is not merely mis-defaulted; it is never SET.
WHY THIS IS NOT COVERED BY THE 'implementor-defined result' LATITUDE THE PRIOR RECORD LEANED ON. §15.3 (--check verified) makes only the RESULT implementor-defined, and only 'if ... checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled'. With checking ENABLED the condition shall be set, and Table 13 (§14.6.13.1.1) gives EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION category FATAL, so the run unit shall terminate. Under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` the float-routed call returned 0 and EXECUTION CONTINUED past it. The prior record's §14.6.13.1.3 latitude ('implementor-defined which fatal exception conditions are detected at COMPILE time') is real and correctly cited, but it is about compile-time detection and cannot excuse a run-time condition that is never set.
REACHABLE WITH FULLY LEGAL ARGUMENTS — this is not a consequence of the AR-15.64.3-1 screen being missing. `A ** 2` with an integer `A` is 'an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value' (§15.3 type 6), hence a legal MOD argument; in a receiver-less context (`DISPLAY`, an `IF` subject) `NumericRenderer#Power` returns it `Real: true`, so `AnyRealArgument` fires and both arguments go to `ModReal`. argument-2 is then an ordinary `PIC S9(18)` integer item whose VALUE is zero — precisely and only the §15.64.3 rule 2 violation.
THE PATTERN (rule 4 — every bug is a pattern). `ModReal` and `RemReal` are the ONLY two bodies in CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs with a domain guard that returns a value without raising; every other guarded real body funnels through `TryIntegerArg`, which does call `ArgumentError`. So the sweep is exactly two functions: MOD (§15.64.3 r2) and REM (§15.77.3 r2), and the fix is to make both guards raise through the same `ExceptionState.ArgumentError` their exact twins already use.
EDITIONS cleared: measured at `--std 2023` only (the `>>TURN` directive is itself post-85), and the availability window is not spec-derivable (Annex E silent on MOD, no VCR row).
RESIDUE, unchanged and still open: the `ArgumentError` -> USE AFTER EXCEPTION declarative dispatch path was not probed here. EVIDENCE: Probe MODRF05, cobol.exe --std 2023, `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, `01 A PIC S9(18) VALUE 11.` `01 Z PIC S9(18) VALUE 0.`:
    BEFORE
    FLOAT ZERO  = 0            <- `DISPLAY ... FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, Z)`: no raise, no termination
    AFTER-FLOAT                <- execution CONTINUED past a FATAL exception condition
    abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): MOD with a zero divisor (15.64.3 rule 2)
The last line is the very next statement, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(A, Z)`, taking the EXACT body — so the two paths are side by side in one run, with the exact one behaving correctly. That is the attribution: the harness, the directive and the receiver are identical; only the routing differs.
Source read, not sampled: `CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs` line body `public static double ModReal(double a, double b) => b == 0 ? 0 : a - (b * Math.Floor(a / b));` and its twin `RemReal`; `CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult` = `double.IsNaN(d) ? ArgumentError(...) : d`; `CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble` screens `IsNaN` only; `ExceptionState.ArgumentError` = `if (ArgumentFunctionChecking) { Set("EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION", fatal: true); throw ...; } return 0;`; `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` line `if (AnyRealArgument(ic) && sig.RuntimeMethod != "Factorial") return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` with `RealMethod("ModScaled") == "ModReal"`. Grep of RealArgs.cs for `ArgumentError`: one occurrence, inside `TryIntegerArg`; `ModReal`/`RemReal` reach it never.
Citations validated: `cite.py --check 15.64.3 "The value of argument-2 shall not be zero."` -> OK §15.64.3 2); `--check 15.3 "If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."` -> OK §15.3 14); `--check 14.6.13.1.3 "It is implementor-defined which fatal exception conditions, if any, are detected at compile time, and the circumstances under which they are detected."` -> OK §14.6.13.1.3 8). Table 13 row `| EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION | Fatal | Function argument error |` read directly in specs/ISO_COBOL.md.

subject: MOD function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The adjudication read `ModScaled`, verified it against an independent floored-modulo oracle, and stopped. THERE ARE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF §15.64.4 IN THIS COMPILER, and the second one returns a different — wrong — value for the SAME legal integer arguments.
(1) THE SECOND BODY. `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` dispatches to `CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#ModReal` whenever any argument renders as binary64: `a - (b * Math.Floor(a / b))` in double. That IS the §15.64.4 equivalent expression, but evaluated in a carrier that cannot hold it: the product `b * floor(a/b)` is the same magnitude as `a`, so past 2^53 the subtraction is catastrophic cancellation and the returned value is off. MEASURED: with `A PIC S9(18) VALUE 100000000` and `B PIC S9(18) VALUE 1000000007`, `FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B)` returns 930000007 (CORRECT — 10^16 mod 1000000007) through the exact path and 930000008 through the float path. `IF FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B) = 930000007` evaluates FALSE, so this is a CONTROL-FLOW defect, not a display artefact.
(2) THE ARGUMENT IS LEGAL, so this is not chargeable to AR-15.64.3-1. §15.3 type 6 admits 'an arithmetic expression that will ALWAYS result in an integer value'; `A ** 2` over an integer item is exactly that. The routing is not caused by a non-integer value — it is caused by the receiver's SHAPE: `NumericRenderer#Power` returns `Real: true` when `_rcv.Receiverless`, so the same expression is exact under `COMPUTE` and binary64 under `DISPLAY` / an `IF` subject. A function's returned value must not depend on the shape of its receiver — the very invariant the PB13 comment block in `RenderFloat` claims to have restored; it was restored for the FLOAT FAMILY and not for the exact family's real-argument twins.
(3) THE PRIOR RECORD'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. It said 'For LEGAL (integer) arguments the renderer's `s = Math.Max(a.Scale, b.Scale)` is 0, so the result is scale 0 as §15.2 item 5 requires.' `A ** 2` is a legal integer argument, and `Power`'s FIXED-receiver arm returns `new NumX(..., ws)` with `ws = ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale` = `max(Scale, 9)` capped by Int128 headroom — 9 for any ordinary picture. So `Math.Max(a.Scale, b.Scale) = 9` and MOD's intermediate carries nine digits to the right of the decimal point, contra §15.2 item 5, for an argument that violates no argument rule. (Read from source; no output can display an intermediate's scale, which is why sampling could not have found it.)
(4) WHAT SURVIVES. `ModScaled` itself is correct and is the right reading of the rule: `FUNCTION INTEGER` floors (§15.44), and `if (a % b != 0 && (a < 0) != (b < 0)) q -= 1;` is the truncating quotient corrected to the floor. The four §15.64.4 NOTE rows, the exact-division and |a|<|b| rows, the large-magnitude row and the P-scaled/COMP-3/COMP shapes the prior pass probed all hold ON THAT PATH.
(5) test-ref CLEARED. `Mod_SignTable_PinnedToSpec` is a legitimate spec-derived fixture (verified by reading `AssertSpec`: COBOL.NET only, literal expected, no legacy/GnuCOBOL leg — `AssertSameAsLegacy` is the separate helper), but it exercises `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(...)` with literal arguments only, i.e. exactly the path that works. It cannot close a row whose defect lives on the path it never enters. Recorded as corroboration; not closure.
EDITIONS: measured — the divergence reproduces byte-identically at `--std 85`, `2002`, `2014` and `2023` (there is no edition arm in the routing). The availability WINDOW is still not spec-derived (Annex E silent on MOD).
UNVERIFIED EDGE, recorded rather than claimed: `NumericRenderer.Align` widens the coarser operand by 10^(s-scale), and `FloatWorkingScale`'s headroom cap is computed from the RECEIVER's digits, not the OPERANDS' — a 30+-digit argument-2 aligned to a scale set by a small receiver would exceed Int128. I could not construct a case that both stays inside §13.18.40.3 SR14's 31-digit cap and produces an observably wrong value (probe MODRF10, `PIC S9(31)` divisor with a `PIC S9(4)` receiver, returned the correct +0009), so I make no claim — but the prior record's flat 'No overflow risk' is stronger than the evidence supports. EVIDENCE: Probe MODRF04, cobol.exe, `01 A PIC S9(18) VALUE 100000000.` `01 B PIC S9(18) VALUE 1000000007.` `01 R PIC S9(18) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE.` — output IDENTICAL at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023:
    POW ONLY    = +010000000000000000     <- `COMPUTE R = A ** 2` is EXACT (10^16), so the power is not the culprit
    MOD COMPUTE = +000000000930000007     <- exact path, CORRECT
    MOD DISPLAY = 930000008               <- `DISPLAY FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B)`, ModReal, WRONG
    IF COND     = WRONG                   <- `IF FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B) = 930000007` is FALSE
10^16 is exactly representable in binary64 (2^16 * 5^16), which is why A was chosen: every input to `ModReal` is exact and the entire error is inside `a - b*Math.Floor(a/b)`. Independent oracle: `python -c "print(10**16 % 1000000007)"` -> 930000007, and the same expression in floats -> 930000008.0, reproducing the compiler's float answer exactly. Probe MODRF02 (A = 123456789) shows the same shape: COMPUTE +000000000643499475 vs DISPLAY 643499476. CONTROL MODRF01 compiles and runs correctly in both contexts, so the divergence is attributable to the routing, not the harness.
Source read, not sampled: `CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#ModReal` = `b == 0 ? 0 : a - (b * Math.Floor(a / b))`; `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` = `if (AnyRealArgument(ic) && sig.RuntimeMethod != "Factorial") return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` with `AnyRealArgument(ic) => ic.Args.Any(a => num.AsNum(a, num.Receiver).Real)`; `NumericRenderer#Power` = `if (b.Real || e.Real || _rcv.Real || _rcv.Receiverless) return new NumX($"System.Math.Pow(...)", 0, Real: true);` else `new NumX($"CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(System.Math.Pow(...), {ws})", ws)`; `ReceiverContext.WorkingScale` = `Math.Max(0, Math.Min(Math.Max(Scale, floor), headroom))` with `FloatScaleFloor` = 9; `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` MOD arm = `case "ModScaled": case "RemScaled": { ... int s = Math.Max(a.Scale, b.Scale); ... }`.
Citations validated: `cite.py --check 15.64.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is"` -> OK §15.64.4 1); `--check 15.2 "An integer function has an operational sign and no digits to the right of the decimal point."` -> OK §15.2 5); `--check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified."` -> OK §15.3 6).

notes: Verdict SUSTAINED after an independent attempt to make the gate reject LEGAL source, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 4 forbids and which a containment predicate is most likely to produce. `InNestedProgram = unit.Parent is not null` is read off the BOUND unit at binder construction (BinderDriver.BindUnitProcedure), so I probed the containment shape most likely to leave Parent unset: a program NESTED INSIDE A FUNCTION DEFINITION. subject: MODULE-NAME function
notes: Verdict SUSTAINED and WIDENED. subject: NUMVAL function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The adjudication verified WHICH POSITIONS a space may occupy and never asked WHICH CHARACTERS COUNT AS A SPACE. §15.67.3 r2 licenses ignoring 'spaces', and r1 defines space-string as 'a string of one or more SPACE characters' -- one character, U+0020 in the alphanumeric and national repertoires. Numval realizes 'space' as .NET `string.Trim()` / `TrimStart()` / `TrimEnd()` (four call sites: the opening `text.Trim()`, the `TrimEnd()` after the CR/DB strip, the `TrimStart()` after the leading-sign strip, the `TrimEnd()` after the trailing-sign strip), every one of which trims the entire `char.IsWhiteSpace` set. TAB, LF, CR, VT, FF, NBSP (U+00A0) and the Unicode space separators are therefore silently ignored as leading, trailing and before-first-digit 'spaces'. None of them is admitted by either general format, so each must raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and yield the §15.3 default 0; instead the value is returned as though the character were not there, with checking explicitly ON. Reachable from ordinary source: a hexadecimal alphanumeric literal, a record read from a file, or any national item carrying U+3000. The defect is a SWEEP, not a one-off: NumvalC delegates to Numval and inherits it; NumvalF uses `Replace(" ", "")` and does NOT; TestNumval/TestNumvalC compare `text[i] == ' '` and do NOT -- so the same §15.67.3 rule is written down in three mechanisms with two different answers, and TEST-NUMVAL contradicts NUMVAL on the same string. Root cause is the trim PREDICATE, not the trim positions; the fix is a space-only trim shared by the whole NUMVAL family (and a drift test asserting NUMVAL and TEST-NUMVAL agree on acceptance for a corpus of strings).
