subject: NUMVAL function
notes: REFUTED in its CONSEQUENCE, not its verdict: NOT-IMPLEMENTED stands (Numval counts digits into a local `digits` whose only test is `if (digits == 0)`; there is no upper bound anywhere in the value path, and native arithmetic is the default mode, so this is the rule governing almost every NUMVAL call). But the adjudication described the consequence as 'the over-long value is carried into the store and high-order-truncated there, so the program gets a plausible wrong number' -- that is too mild by a sign. The accumulation is `unscaled = unscaled * 10 + (c - '0')` on `Int128` with no `checked` context and no `<CheckForOverflowUnderflow>` in Directory.Build.props, so past 38 digits it WRAPS MODULO 2^128 -- silently, and BEFORE Rescaled's saturation guard can see it. Rescaled's own doc comment asserts it is 'SATURATING at the Int128 carrier instead of wrapping' and that 'the saturation is safe'; that invariant is FALSE for NUMVAL because the guard is on the SHIFT and nothing guards the ACCUMULATE. Measured result: a 39-digit argument with NO sign character at all returns a NEGATIVE value. That is the PB5/PB13 quantizer-clamp family's third sibling, in the one place PB13's sweep did not look, and it is exactly the failure mode the brief names -- invisible to output sampling on small receivers, visible only by reading the implementation. Two fixes are needed, not one: (i) the §15.67.3 r3 digit cap itself -- the mechanism already exists one screen over, TestNumval takes a `digitCap` defaulting to 31 and returns the position of the cap+1-th digit, and Numval neither receives nor applies it, so TEST-NUMVAL calls a 32-digit string non-conforming while NUMVAL consumes it; and (ii) a bound on the accumulate, so that even with the cap in place a malformed-but-unchecked path cannot wrap. EDITIONS EMPTY (applies to every row of this subject): the adjudication's '2014, 2023' was inferred from the ABSENCE of a §15.67 item in Annex E.2/E.3. That absence establishes only that the clause is unchanged 2014->2023; it is not a window, and as written it implies NUMVAL is unavailable in 2002/1985, which is false. The 1985 and 2002 windows are not derivable from this document, and IntrinsicCatalog's own row (min edition 85) is the code under review and may not supply them. EVIDENCE: Probe E:/Temp/rfnv/rfnv03.cob (RFNVW03, --std 2023, default native arithmetic) with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, receiverless DISPLAY: D39 `NUMVAL("9" x39)` prints `--170141183460469231731687303715884.105728` (Int128.MinValue at scale 6 -- note the malformed DOUBLE minus sign in the rendered text); D40 `NUMVAL("9" x40)` prints `170141183460469231731687303715884.105727`; N40 prints `-170141183460469231731687303715884.105727`; N41 prints `--170141183460469231731687303715884.105728`; then REACHED-END, no exception. Probe rfnv05.cob (RFNVW05, checking ON) isolates the SIGN: `IF FUNCTION NUMVAL("999999999999999999999999999999999999999") < 0` -> prints P39-SIGN=NEGATIVE, and the same argument stored into PIC S9(9)V9(6) gives P39-STORE=30371588410572Q ('Q' = the -8 overpunch, i.e. -303715884.105728) -- a positive 39-digit argument yielding a negative value, with no size error and no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. RETAINED: pbnv03.cob 31 digits exact, 32 digits -> the leading '1' silently lost; pbnv04.cob repeats the 32-digit case with checking ON and still raises nothing. Read: `digits++` with no cap comparison, versus #TestNumval `if (++digits > digitCap) return i + 1;`. notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The adjudication probed exactly one shape -- a single outermost program carrying its own SPECIAL-NAMES -- and declared the rule closed. It fails in every CONTAINED program. §12.3.4 GR1: 'The entries explicitly or implicitly specified in the configuration section of a source unit that contains other source units apply to each directly or indirectly contained source unit', and §12.3.3 SR1 forbids a contained program from having a configuration section of its own, so a contained program CANNOT restate DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA and is entitled to inherit it. The mechanism is not NUMVAL-specific (the same run shows a contained program rejecting the numeric literal `123,45` with COBOLNET0895), so the ROOT CAUSE is a §12.3.4 GR1 configuration-section scoping defect outside §15.67; but the observable §15.67.3 r5 behaviour is non-conforming and this row cannot read CONFORMS while it is. notes: REFUTED in scope: verdict DIVERGES stands, but the adjudication found ONE divergence where there are TWO, and named the wrong one as the root cause of the worst behaviour. (a) THE ONE THE ADJUDICATION FOUND, re-verified and correct: the value is materialized at `ws = Receiver.WorkingScale(NumvalScaleFloor)` = clamp(max(receiver scale, 6)) and TRUNCATED there. Under NATIVE arithmetic §15.4.1 licenses it ('the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor'); under STANDARD-DECIMAL it does not -- §15.4.1 requires the returned value be 'contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect' and §8.8.1.5.2 gives the SDIDI 'a maximum precision of 34 decimal digits', so NUMVAL("1.2345678") must return exactly 1.2345678. The `case "Numval":` arm never consults the arithmetic mode. (b) THE ONE IT MISSED, and it is worse: `unscaled = unscaled * 10 + (c - '0')` is UNCHECKED Int128 arithmetic (no `checked`, no `<CheckForOverflowUnderflow>` in Directory.Build.props), so past 38 digits the accumulator WRAPS MODULO 2^128 before Rescaled's saturation guard is ever reached. Rescaled's doc comment claims it is 'SATURATING at the Int128 carrier instead of wrapping' and that the saturation is therefore safe -- the invariant is false here, because the guard is on the SHIFT and nothing guards the ACCUMULATE. Measured: a 39-digit argument bearing NO sign character returns a NEGATIVE value, and a receiverless DISPLAY of it renders `--170141183460469231731687303715884.105728` -- a numeric text with TWO minus signs, which is not a valid rendering of any value. So 'the returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1' fails not by a fraction digit but by sign and by magnitude, and the text channel emits malformed output. This is the PB5/PB13 clamp family's third sibling, in the member PB13's sweep did not reach. Two independent fixes: bound the accumulate (and enforce §15.67.3 r3, which would make the wrap unreachable from conforming source), and thread the arithmetic mode into the Numval arm so STANDARD-DECIMAL gets an SDIDI-precision temporary instead of the native 6-fraction-digit one. The receiver-driven working scale remains the shape defect -- the same call yields different precision depending on what it is assigned to, and the LEAST precision exactly where no receiver can absorb it. notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudication's claim was 'All three sign carriers the rule names produce a negative result ... Verified across the four channels the rule can be observed in -- leading minus, trailing minus, CR, DB.' That claim is false as stated. §15.67.4 r2 is a CONTAINMENT predicate -- 'If argument-1 CONTAINS CR, DB, or the minus sign, the returned value is negative' -- and the implementation realizes it as an ALGEBRAIC TOGGLE: the leading-sign arm assigns `neg = true` but the trailing-sign arm assigns `neg = !neg`. On `"-12-"` the two minus signs cancel and NUMVAL returns +12.000000, positive, for an argument that plainly contains a minus sign -- with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking explicitly ON and no exception raised. Under either reading the result is wrong: read as a conforming argument, r2 demands a negative value; read as non-conforming (it matches neither general format, and the sibling TEST-NUMVAL agrees, reporting position 4 in error), §15.3 demands EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and the default 0. It returns +12 instead. PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because the input is reachable only through the AR-15.67.3-1 acceptance leniency: for every argument that actually conforms to r1, each of the four carriers does yield a negative value, and that half is genuinely verified. But the row cannot read CONFORMS while a reachable argument containing a minus sign returns a positive value, and the toggle is the wrong SHAPE for a containment rule -- fixing r1's format screen would hide this defect rather than correct it, so both need doing. Second, independent reason for PARTIAL: the cited spec-derived test covers only TWO of the four sign carriers -- InlineData `"  -123.45 "` (leading minus) and `"12cr"` (CR). There is no DB case and no trailing-minus case, and the trailing minus is precisely the carrier the toggle breaks. TEST-REF STRIPPED to empty for that reason; the test is corroboration only. Also noted, not leaned on: `NUMVAL("-0")` returns +0 -- Int128 has no negative zero, and zero is not negative, so this is not treated as a violation. EDITIONS EMPTY: see AR-15.67.3-3's note. notes: The rule has six halves; two are implemented and four are enforced nowhere. IMPLEMENTED: 'Any leading or trailing spaces in argument-2 are ignored' (NumvalC does `currency.Trim()`), and the NOTE's interior-space currency string survives that trim. NOT ENFORCED, all four silently: (a) 'shall be of the same class as argument-1'; (b) 'shall contain at least one non-space character'; (c) 'shall not contain any of the digits 0 through 9'; (d) 'shall not contain ... \'*\', \'+\', \'-\', \',\', or \'.\'; or the two consecutive letters \'CR\' or \'DB\''. BindNumvalCFamily binds argument-2 through the ordinary operand path and never inspects it; NumvalC trims it and hands it to string.Replace. The all-space case is the worst-behaved: it silently degrades to 'no currency at all' and returns a value, so a program with a typo in its currency literal gets a plausible wrong answer. Note a second-order effect of (b) being unenforced — an all-space argument-2 makes NUMVAL-C behave as NUMVAL, which is a DIFFERENT function's semantics reached without a diagnostic. A class-NUMERIC argument-2 is not diagnosed at compile time either; it survives to run time and aborts there with a NotImplemented feature exception, so the failure is loud but is not the §15.68.3 r2 rejection and is not attributable to the rule. notes: Sub-rules b, c, d, e and f CONFORM; sub-rule a — the two general formats, which is the substance of the rule — is not enforced at all. NumvalC is a STRIP-AND-DELEGATE parser: `text.Replace(cur, "")` removes the currency wherever it occurs (any position, any number of times), `Replace(group, "")` removes grouping separators everywhere INCLUDING after the decimal separator, and the residue goes to Numval, which itself admits a leading AND a trailing sign together (its own comment concedes 'Both present is malformed; the lenient double-strip'). No positional scan of either format survives anywhere on the value path, so non-conforming argument-1 yields a plausible value and EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is never set. The fix is not more strip-and-delegate leniency; it is NumvalC driving the shared scanner (scan-then-value) so one format definition serves both functions. Minor traceability leak of the same delegation: a NUMVAL-C argument failure reports '§15.67.3' (NUMVAL's clause) in its runtime message. ALPHABET REV IS "Z" "Y" "X" "A" "B" "C"`, ORD-MAX("A" "Z") returned 1 and the program's own `IF S1 > S2` printed A-GT-Z, i.e. the function agrees with the relation condition; the national leg goes through the NationalCollation overload per §8.8.4.2.9; and the fixed-point numeric leg aligns every argument to the common scale (widening only, exact) so the unscaled Int128 compare IS the §8.8.4.2.4 algebraic comparison. What does NOT hold: (a) §8.8.4.2.4 makes a floating-point operand class numeric and requires the algebraic comparison, but for a COMP-1/COMP-2 argument NO comparison is generated at all — the call fails to compile (CS1503, the AlignedArgs/AnyReal defect recorded under RV-15.71.4-1); recording it here too because a CONFORMS row is never revisited and this rule is not satisfied for that operand shape. (b) §8.8.4.2.4 paragraph 3 requires, under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY, that the comparison be performed as if each operand were converted to a standard-binary intermediate data item under the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode; the renderer's `OrdMax or OrdMin` case has no arithmetic-mode branch and BindIntrinsicCore's §15.4.1 loud-staging list is only ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION and does not even test ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, so the exact Int128 comparison is used silently in that mode. Test coverage: nist:IF128A tests 07/08 are genuine unequal-length alphanumeric comparisons (ORD-MAX("A", I, "P") with I PIC X(4) VALUE "R"), but the collating-sequence leg is UNCOVERED for ORD-MAX — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MAX only in its comment and calls FUNCTION MAX alone. test-needed: a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE case calling ORD-MAX, and a floating-point-argument case.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: Both selection bodies were read: OrdMax does `if (xs[i] > m)` and ExtremeIndex does `if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)` — a STRICTLY-greater update, so an argument equal to the running maximum never displaces it and the leftmost position is returned. ExtremeIndex is the ONE selection helper shared by MaxString/MinString/OrdMaxString/OrdMinString and all three collation variants, so there is no second mechanism to drift. Re-verified by running: ORD-MAX(1.50 1.5) -> 1 (a cross-scale tie), ORD-MAX("A" "A ") -> 1 (a tie created by the space-padding rule), ORD-MAX(-1.05 -1.5 -1.05) -> 1, and IND(ALL) over 3,9,1,9 -> 2. Both test-refs genuinely exercise the tie: OrdMax_TieTakesFirst_PinnedToSpec asserts FUNCTION ORD-MAX(3, 7, 7, 2) = 002, and nist:IF128A test F-ORD-MAX-09 is FUNCTION ORD-MAX(A, 5, 5, A) with A PIC S9(10) VALUE 5 — a four-way tie.

notes: PB1 landed the NEGATIVE class list; the strongly-typed-group half is unscreened. Identical to AR-15.71.3-1 - ORD-MIN's rule is ORD-MAX's rule (feedback_scan_all_similar: fix both or neither). test-needed.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: §15.72.3 rule 2 bars a zero-length-literal argument. A zero-length-literal guard exists ONLY for NATIONAL-OF (§15.66.3 r3, COBOLNET1546 in CheckRepertoireArgs) and CONVERT (§15.19.3, COBOLNET1514 in BindConvert); there is no shared screen and none for ORD-MIN. subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: The binder's only class logic for an ArgKinds "p" row is 'args.All(IsStringOperand)', which SELECTS the string-vs-numeric runtime body rather than VALIDATING that the arguments share a class (§15.72.3 rule 3), so a mixed-class list is silently accepted. Re-verified at --std 2023: with '01 N1 PIC 9(4) VALUE 7.' and '01 A1 PIC X(4) VALUE "0003".', 'MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(N1 A1) TO R' compiles clean and prints 0002 — the alphanumeric operand is coerced onto the numeric path and 7 is compared against 3. National mixed with alphanumeric is accepted likewise. The PERMITTED alphabetic/alphanumeric mixture is correctly accepted and gives the right answer (PIC A(3) "BBB" + PIC X(3) "AAA" prints 0002) — PicInfo.PicCategory.Alphanumeric covers both PIC A and PIC X, so there is no false rejection to fix. notes: PB2 LANDED. Same rule and same fix as AR/RV-15.71 - ORD-MIN's body is ORD-MAX's body with the comparison reversed, so fixing one without the other would have been the split the DA wave warned about (feedback_scan_all_similar).

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: §8.8.4.2 is honoured on every path that actually emits a comparison: fixed-point numeric arguments are scale-ALIGNED before the unscaled Int128 compare (alignment makes unscaled comparison equal algebraic comparison, §8.8.1) — CLI-verified ORD-MIN(1.0 1.00 1)=1; string arguments go through CobolString.Compare, which space-extends the shorter operand (§8.8.4.2.7 r2 — verified ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1) and honours the alphanumeric PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE — independently re-verified: under 'ALPHABET REVSEQ IS "Z" "Y" "X" "A" "B"' with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REVSEQ, ORD-MIN("A" "Z") returns 2 and the program's own 'IF "Z" < "A"' is TRUE, so the function and the relation condition agree — or the national PCS. PARTIAL for the SAME carrier holes as RV-15.72.4-1: a FLOAT-LONG/COMP-1/COMP-2 list, and (adversarial-pass addition) a division subexpression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, never reach a comparison at all because the emitted C# does not compile (CS1503 double/CobolDec -> Int128). Coverage gap: no test exercises the ORD-MIN PCS leg — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MIN in its CA23 header comment but its body exercises only FUNCTION MAX, so it is deliberately NOT cited; only nist:IF129A is cited (numeric legs 01-07, unequal-length alphanumeric legs 08/09 which exercise the space padding). test-needed: an ORD-MIN PCS fixture and a float/decimal fixture.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS by the adversarial pass. The leftmost-wins selection itself is right on every path that emits one: both bodies update only on a STRICTLY-less compare (OrdMin: 'if (xs[i] < m)'; ExtremeIndex: 'if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)'), CLI-verified ORD-MIN(3 3 3)=1, ORD-MIN(-1 0 -1)=1, ORD-MIN(1.0 1.00 1)=1, ORD-MIN("BB" "AA" "AA")=2, ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1 (equal after §8.8.4.2.7 space padding), and NIST IF129A test (j) 'FUNCTION ORD-MIN(A, 5, 5, A)' with A PIC S9(10) VALUE 5 — four equal values, expected 1 — genuinely covers the tie. But the verdict cannot be CONFORMS: for the SAME operand shapes that make RV-15.72.4-1/-2 PARTIAL there is NO returned value at all, so rule 3 is unrealized there. Verified: '01 F1 USAGE COMP-2. 01 F2 USAGE COMP-2. MOVE 1.5 TO F1 MOVE 1.5 TO F2 MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(F1 F2) TO R' — an exact tie that should return 1 — instead fails with raw Roslyn 'error CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128'; the same happens for a division subexpression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (CobolDec -> Int128). Root cause and proposed owner are identical to RV-15.72.4-1 (DA9: float AND decimal legs for the Int128 variadic statistical family); this record must be re-adjudicated together with it. test-needed: a float/decimal tie fixture.

subject: PI function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Pi() = Math.PI is a legitimate implementor-defined approximation of (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795), and the documentation obligation is discharged: Annex A.1 item 92 (validated - 'Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) ... The value returned does not have to be documented') exempts the VALUE while still requiring the characteristics/representation, and those ARE documented in CONFORMANCE.md SS7 (the row keyed '- (SS15.4.1 / SS14.9.11.4 GR1)', read and confirmed to state that a FLOAT-valued function renders through the same shortest-round-trip CobolFloat.Display a COMP-2 item does). PARTIAL for a receiver-shape leg, re-verified independently on the built CLI at --std 2023: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes through the ONE FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble's scaled double exceeds Int64 at scale >= 19 and SATURATES to long.MaxValue with no size error and no diagnostic - '01 R19 PIC 9V9(19). COMPUTE R19 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R19.' prints 0.9223372036854775807 and PIC 9V9(30) prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807. Neither is an approximation of pi, so rule 1 is violated for every legal 2002+ receiver of 20..31 digits (scale <= 18 is fine: PIC 9V9(18) prints 3.141592653589793280, within approximation license). Not PI-specific - the whole SS15.4.1 float family funnels through the same FromDouble. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test does compile-and-run and asserts the value 3.14159, so it genuinely covers rule 1's happy path, but only at PIC 9.9(5) and only at edition 2014 (AssertSpec dialect argument); the scale >= 19 saturation leg and editions 2002/2023 are test-needed.

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover).

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-decimal arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-decimal-2014', IntroducedIn 2014) - re-verified, 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.' at --std 2002 is rejected with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)'. SS15.73.3 rule 3 requires the returned value to be EXACTLY 3.141592653589793238462643383279503; PI is absent from the IntrinsicBinder staged-loud list (which holds only ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION) and rides the ordinary RenderFloat/Math.PI/binary64 path in EVERY arithmetic mode, so a STANDARD-DECIMAL program silently gets native binary64 digits. FAILING INPUT (re-run independently on the built CLI): 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PISDREV2. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9V9(17). PROCEDURE DIVISION. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R17.' at --std 2014 and --std 2023 prints 3.14159265358979328; rule 3 truncated to the receiver (COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates, SS14.7) requires 3.14159265358979323 - note the earlier draft's expected '...324' was the ROUNDED value and is wrong. At PIC 9V9(30) it prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 (the FromDouble Int64 saturation) against a required 3.141592653589793238462643383279. THE FALSE PREMISE, written in two places - the CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs class header and the IntrinsicBinder staging comment - is 'their returned-value rules are prose approximations, NOT equivalent arithmetic expressions, so the value is implementor-defined in EVERY mode (SS15.4.1 last paragraph)'. It fails on TWO independent grounds, both validated: (a) SS15.73.3 rule 1 is phrased exactly as SS15.4.1's equivalent-arithmetic-expression sentence ('an implementor-defined approximation of the arithmetic expression (3 + 0.14159...)'), so PI DOES have an EAE, and SS15.4.1 then states 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified: 1) the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'; and (b) even on the no-EAE reading, SS15.4.1's last paragraph reads 'its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION' - and rules 2 and 3 are precisely that specification. Test-needed (no test references PI under any standard arithmetic mode). SIBLING CONFIRMED, not merely suspected: 'COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION E.' under STANDARD-DECIMAL prints 2.71828182845904512 where SS15.27.3 rule 3 (validated) requires the exact value truncating to 2.71828182845904523. ALSO: ArithmeticMode.Standard (the 2002-2014 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD' clause, which DataBinder routes to the same CobolDec engine) diverges identically - verified, --std 2002 with ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD prints the same 3.14159265358979328 - so the fix must cover ArithmeticMode.Standard as well as StandardDecimal.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: PB1; the family fixture now covers PRESENT-VALUE's own 15.74.3 r1 rejection rather than relying on a sibling function's.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: test-needed. §15.74.3 r2 (cite.py --check: OK) — the value of argument-1 shall be greater than −1. This is a permissible-VALUE constraint, so §15.3 applies: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'; Annex A.1 item 90 makes only the RETURNED VALUE implementor-defined when checking is off — the condition must still be SET, and must be raised when checking is on. CobolIntrinsics.PresentValue(double rate, params double[] amounts) performs no domain check on rate, unlike its file-mates Log/Log10 which call Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError, and the binder adds none. Reproduced with the built CLI: (a) COMPILE-TIME-detectable literal violation, edition-independent — `COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(-1.5, 100, 200)` is accepted silently at --std 85 AND --std 2023 and prints 600.000000, so the divergence does not depend on the (2002+) EC machinery and holds at every edition; (b) runtime rate with checking explicitly enabled — `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` then `FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(R2 AMT AMT)` with R2 = −2.00 prints 0 and CONTINUES, while the very next `FUNCTION LOG(0)` in the SAME program aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)' — same directive, same run unit, so the mechanism exists and PRESENT-VALUE alone does not use it; (c) rate = −1.00 exactly makes 1+rate = 0, and the binary64 division through FromDouble SATURATES, printing 223372036.8547 with no exception and no diagnostic.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: Holds under NATIVE arithmetic; the standard-arithmetic leg does not. The body `for (int i = 0; i < amounts.Length; i++) pv += amounts[i] / Math.Pow(1 + rate, i + 1)` is exactly Σ argument-2ᵢ / (1 + argument-1)^i for i = 1..n — §15.74.4 r1c, with r1a and r1b as its n = 1 and n = 2 cases — and §15.4.1 licenses 'an implementor-defined approximation' under native arithmetic. Verified with the built CLI: PRESENT-VALUE(0.100 1000 2000 3000) and the hand-written FUNCTION SUM EAE both give 4815.927873, which is also the exact hand-computed value. Annex A.1 item 92 ('Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) … The value returned does not have to be documented') means the documentation test does NOT downgrade the native leg, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md already carries a §15.4.1 / §14.9.11.4 GR1 row. THE PARTIAL: §15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect, and instead of doing so IntrinsicBinder rejects the program with DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic (COBOLNET0899, EditionSeverity.Error) — legal COBOL refused; confirmed by running an OPTIONS/ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE FIX SESSION: that staging condition is `ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.Standard or ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal` and OMITS ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, which §15.4.1 covers equally. I checked whether that opens a SILENT-wrong-answer hole and it does not — today ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is itself loud-rejected earlier by COBOLNET0806 ('obsolete feature … not supported') at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, so standard-binary can never be in effect — but if 0806 is ever lifted (obsolete is not removed; §11.9.5 still defines the phrase in 2023), the 0899 list must gain StandardBinary or PRESENT-VALUE will silently return the native double. The rule itself applies at all four editions; the failing leg needs the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause and so is reachable only from 2002. ⚠ TEST-REF CORRECTED: nist:IF403M was STRUCK on two independent grounds — it is registered 'pending / none / cataloged (not asserted)' in tests/nist/corpus.tsv line 406 so nothing runs it, and its sole PRESENT-VALUE statement compares the function to ITSELF (`IF FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9) = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9)`), which tests determinism, never the equivalent arithmetic expression. nist:IF130A genuinely covers the native leg — F-PRES-VAL-01 range-checks PRESENT-VALUE(0, 23, 12, 9) against 43.9991..44.0009 and twenty-one further paragraphs range-check real values. No test covers the standard-decimal leg (tests/conformance/negative/arith-standard-intrinsic-staged.cob exercises VARIANCE, not PRESENT-VALUE, so it is deliberately not cited).

subject: RANDOM function
notes: PB1; 15.75.3 r1 (class numeric) covered. The VALUE half of RANDOM's rules (r2, zero-or-positive-integer) is a separate, still-open EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION question.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Neither half of 'it shall be zero or a positive integer' is enforced at bind or at run time, and the §15.3 raise ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') never fires for a RANDOM seed. (a) NEGATIVE: CobolIntrinsics.Float.Random(long seed) does `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))`, so a negative seed is silently ALIASED onto a large positive one — REPRODUCED: FUNCTION RANDOM(-5) and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483643) both return 636542013 (the alias is the two's-complement mask 0x7FFFFFFB, NOT abs(), so it does not even agree with .NET's own Random(int) sign handling). (b) NON-INTEGER: IntrinsicRenderer.IntArg truncates to scale 0, so FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75) silently becomes seed 1 — REPRODUCED: RANDOM(1.75) and RANDOM(1) both return 248668584. Concrete failing input: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(-5).` then `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75).` — compiles exit 0, zero diagnostics. The EC machinery EXISTS and is already used by sibling intrinsics (Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError — CobolDate's DATE-OF-INTEGER/DAY-OF-INTEGER range checks, CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble on NaN); RANDOM simply never reaches it, so `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` cannot catch it either. Fix shape: the seed range/integrality check belongs in the runtime body through ExceptionState.ArgumentError (a runtime-valued seed cannot be screened at bind), plus a bind-time diagnostic for the statically-known literal case. test-needed.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) REPLACES the one static _random with a freshly seeded generator and returns its first value, so a subsequent seeded reference restarts the sequence. Re-verified independently at HEAD: RANDOM(42) -> 668106466, argument-less -> 140907298, argument-less -> 125518289, RANDOM(42) again -> 668106466, argument-less -> 140907298 — the restart reproduces the whole PREFIX, not merely the first value. Editions from the catalog window IntroducedIn 85 (the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment, which this compiler treats as part of --std 85); FUNCTION RANDOM was confirmed to compile and run at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. Test-ref nist:IF131A was STRUCK by review: its five RANDOM paragraphs only range-check 0 <= r < 1 and never compare two same-seed references, so it does not exercise this rule. The surviving conformance-test asserts R1 = R3 across an intervening argument-less draw, which is exactly rule 3's observable.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: BARE QUESTION: shall the §15.75.3 rule-4 implementor-defined seed be a FIXED value, so an un-seeded FUNCTION RANDOM sequence is reproducible across runs, or stay the current per-process entropy seed? Why this is not CONFORMS: the field initializer is `private static Random _random = new()`, and on .NET 6+ the PARAMETERLESS Random constructor seeds xoshiro256** directly from OS entropy — there is no seed VALUE at all, which is precisely what Annex A.1 item 144 ('RANDOM function (seed value when no argument on first reference). This item is required.') names as the required determination. Documentation is genuinely waived by item 144 ('The seed value used by the implementor does not have to be documented'), so this is NOT a CONFORMANCE.md gap — it is an unmade choice with an observed user-visible consequence: four consecutive runs of the same program gave first values 925010183 / 038930312 / 356550812 / 117861222. The in-code rationale also misdescribes the mechanism as 'the .NET time-derived default', evidence the behaviour was inherited from the framework rather than chosen, and no compiler survey is recorded (feedback_survey_compilers_on_latitude requires one before settling implementor latitude). Test-ref nist:IF131A was STRUCK: it makes the first reference argument-less but can only range-check the result, so nothing about the seed determination is testable there.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: 15.75.3 r5 - a reference WITHOUT argument-1 returns the next number in the current sequence. Asserted STRUCTURALLY (the two unseeded references differ; a re-seed reproduces the first), never as this implementation's own numbers, because the numbers themselves are implementor-defined and pinning them would be pinning the implementation rather than the rule.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The runtime body conforms (Random.NextDouble() is in [0,1)) and the FLOAT-receiver path (num.Receiver.Real) hands the double through unquantized. The FIXED-POINT receiver path does NOT: RenderFloat wraps the call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in `(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`, so any returned value >= 0.9999999995 quantizes to exactly 1.000000000 — not 'less than one'. THE QUANTIZATION DEFECT IS DEMONSTRATED, not conjectured: on the same shared code path `01 R PIC 9V9(9). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999).` prints 1.000000000 while SQRT(0.999999998) prints 0.999999999. For RANDOM the top bucket is one draw in ~2.1e9 (the seeded back-compat generator's NextDouble is InternalSample() * (1.0/int.MaxValue) and only InternalSample() == 2147483646 clears the threshold; the argument-less xoshiro path has the same ~5e-10 probability), so no short deterministic COBOL input exhibits it — the bound is broken by the emitter's generic rounding, not by the generator. Fix shape: clamp (or round toward zero) at the quantization point for range-bounded functions instead of leaving the < 1 bound to FromDouble's AwayFromZero. test-ref conformance-test:...Random_SeededSequence_PinnedToSpec was STRUCK by review — its receivers are PIC V9(9), which has NO integer position, so a 1.000000000 result would silently store as .000000000, and the test asserts nothing about the range. nist:IF131A is kept as corroboration only (a NIST golden is a regression net, never spec-derived, so it cannot close the row); its WS-NUM is PIC S9(5)V9(6), which can represent 1.0, so its `WS-NUM < MAX-RANGE` legs would in principle catch the violation. test-needed: a spec-derived case pinning the < 1 bound on a receiver able to hold 1.0.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) constructs `new Random(int)`, which on .NET 6+ is pinned to the back-compatible (Knuth subtractive) seeded implementation — deterministic for a given seed. Re-verified across FOUR separate processes at four editions: FUNCTION RANDOM(5) returned 338369841 every time while the argument-less draws in the same programs varied, so the determinism belongs to the seeded path and is not process reuse. Independently corroborated WITHOUT using the compiler as its own oracle: a from-scratch reimplementation of the .NET seeded subtractive generator reproduces the compiler's output exactly for seeds 0 (726243270), 1 (248668584), 5 (338369841), 42 (668106466, 140907298, 125518289) and 2147483643 (636542013) — the sequence is algorithmically determined by the seed, not incidentally stable. Residual TEST gap (not a conformance gap): the test asserts only same-seed equality within one process; no golden pins an actual RANDOM value, so a change of the underlying seeded generator would land silently.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The BEHAVIOUR meets the numeric floor and this was MEASURED, not assumed: `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))` is the identity on 0..2147483647, and an independent reimplementation of the seeded generator (validated against the compiler's own output for five seeds) yields 32768 DISTINCT six-value sequences for the 32768 seeds 0..32767 — zero collisions. Seeds at or above 2^31 alias downward — verified at HEAD that FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483648) == FUNCTION RANDOM(0) == 726243270 and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483649) == FUNCTION RANDOM(1) == 248668584 — which is legitimate latitude precisely BECAUSE rule 3 lets the implementor specify the subset. But rule 3's obligation is to SPECIFY that subset, and Annex A.1 item 145 makes it a required item that 'shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation'. Documented in CONFORMANCE.md section 7: NO — section 7 carries only items 2, 59, 158, 205, 206, 207, 208, 211, 215 plus one unnumbered §15.4.1 row, and the word RANDOM appears nowhere in that file. Conforming needs the entry as well as the behaviour, so PARTIAL until section 7 states the subset. NOTE for whoever writes it: only 0..32767 was actually measured for distinctness — do NOT write '0..2147483647' into CONFORMANCE.md without measuring it, because asserting an unverified subset is the wrongly-documented determination that section 7's own header calls worse than an absent one. test-needed (nothing asserts that two distinct seeds in 0..32767 yield distinct sequences, and nothing checks the CONFORMANCE.md entry).

subject: RANGE function

subject: REM function
notes: DOWNGRADED from CONFORMS on adversarial review. HOLDS on the fixed-point path, verified by execution on both ISO 15.3 legs: RemScaled tests b == 0 on the SCALE-ALIGNED divisor (NumericRenderer.Align only ever widens to max(a.Scale,b.Scale), so no truncation can manufacture or hide a zero) and calls ExceptionState.ArgumentError -- with >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON the run unit dies with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): REM with a zero divisor (15.77.3 rule 2)'; with checking off the implementor-defined default 0 is returned, for a literal 0, a zero-valued item and a zero-valued expression (Z - Z) alike. DOES NOT HOLD for two operand shapes ISO 15.3 item 10 permits, because REM does not COMPILE there at all, so a zero divisor can never reach the check: (a) a FLOAT argument-2 (USAGE COMP-2/COMP-1, category numeric per ISO 8.5.2.12 item 2) -- backend 'CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128' at --std 85/2002/2014/2023; (b) under OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL an arithmetic-expression argument -- 'CS1503: cannot convert from CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDec to System.Int128' (2014+ only, where this compiler admits the clause). Both are the RV-15.77.4-1 emitter defect; rule 2 is listed as PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS so this row is revisited when that lands. CORRECTION to the first pass: it flagged the missing docs/CONFORMANCE.md entry for the implementor-defined default result. NO SUCH REQUIREMENT EXISTS -- ISO A.1 item 90 ('Function-identifier (result when argument rules are violated and checking for the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is not enabled)') says in terms 'The value returned does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' Do not chase it. test-needed: nothing anywhere exercises a zero REM divisor -- the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION tests (ExceptionConditionConformanceTests; IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec) use LOG/NUMVAL/SQRT/FACTORIAL, and the NIST REM cases pass a zero ARGUMENT-1 (IF133A F-REM-TEST-01: FUNCTION REM(0, 20)), never a zero argument-2. A fixture is needed on both legs (checking ON = fatal, checking OFF = 0).

subject: REVERSE function
notes: DOWNGRADED FROM CONFORMS. The reversal ITSELF is exactly right - CobolIntrinsics.Reverse is a position-j <- position-(n-j+1) code-unit reversal with no length change, fed the operand's FULL fixed-width image, and re-verified live at every shape tried: X(6) VALUE "AB" -> [    BA  ] into X(8) (n = the declared width, not the trimmed value); ref-mod W-S(2:3) -> [  B     ]; A(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; N(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; numeric-edited ZZ9 VALUE 42 -> [24      ] (the EDITED image is reversed, correct); alphanumeric-edited XXBXX "AB CD" -> [DC BA   ]; an image-capable group -> [EDCBA   ]. Surrogates need no special handling - 8.5.1.4 item 2 and its closing paragraph ('Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character', cite-checked) make code-unit reversal the spec-mandated behaviour. BUT THREE LEGAL argument-1 SHAPES PRODUCE NO RETURNED VALUE AT ALL - each compiles clean at 85 and 2023 and then throws CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN time, where 15.78.4 r1 requires a character string of length n: (1) an alphanumeric GROUP item containing a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - `01 G2. 05 G2-A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC". 05 G2-N PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE 5.` then `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(G2) TO W-X.` -> 'whole-group image of G2 with a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - the Tier-C byte island'; the argument is legal because 8.5.2.1 makes an alphanumeric group item class AND category alphanumeric, which 15.78.3 r1 admits. (2) a FIGURATIVE CONSTANT - `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(SPACE) TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundFigurative' (IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundFigurative) is a Loud arm); legal because 8.4.3.2.3 SR8 admits a literal, 8.3.3.6.4 GR1 makes SPACE an alphanumeric character value and GR3b fixes its length at one character position - exactly satisfying 15.78.3 r1. (3) `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(ALL "AB") TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundAllLiteral' (the sibling Loud arm); 8.3.3.6.4 GR3c gives it the length of literal-1. The failures are LOUD, not wrong values, and the Tier-C group island is a general deferral (COBOLNET_DESIGN 4.2) rather than a REVERSE-specific bug - but it is NOT recorded in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (grep found no Tier-C / whole-group-image entry), so it is an open GAP, not documented non-support. Fixing StrArgVisitor's two Loud arms is the cheap half and closes the same hole for UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE/TRIM/CONCAT. TEST-REF STRUCK: `conformance:negative/reverse_national_result_to_an` was cited for this rule but does not cover it - it is a `*> reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` COMPILE-REJECT case for the 15.78.1 result-type table and the 14.9.25.3 Table 16 National->AN MOVE guard (CA25); the program never executes, so it cannot exercise a position-reversal rule. The surviving refs do exercise it (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec pins REVERSE("abc 12") -> [21 cba  ] against the SPEC; IF134A checks `IF FUNCTION REVERSE("CAPS") = "SPAC"`; ChannelMatrix reverses "ABCDE", though only differentially against the frozen legacy oracle). Test-needed: goldens for the group, figurative and ALL-literal shapes. Editions: the three failing shapes reproduce identically at every --std, and only the 2023 rule text was available, so the per-edition wording was not re-derived.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: §15.79.3 r1 has TWO halves and only one is implemented. LITERAL-ness is enforced — BindIntrinsicCore raises COBOLNET1517 when argument-1 is not a BoundStringLiteral (verified: `FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME(WS-FMT, "12:34:56")` with `01 WS-FMT PIC X(8)` → COBOLNET1517). The CLASS restriction ('national or alphanumeric') is NOT: ExpressionBinder.BooleanLiteralOperand yields a BoundStringLiteral carrying Category=Boolean, which passes the 1517 test, so `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME(B"0011", "12:34:56") TO WS-F.` compiles clean at --std 2014 and prints +00000.00 with no diagnostic — a boolean literal is neither of the two classes Table 21 ('Anum1 or Nat1') and r1 admit. The prior adjudication argued this away as 'always resolves to EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION', but §15.3's EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION disposition is for an argument whose evaluation produces an INCORRECT VALUE; r1 is a static class rule, and this compiler's own precedent for a §15 argument class rule is a BIND-time diagnostic (CheckRepertoireArgs → COBOLNET1546 for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF §15.26.3/§15.66.3). Correctly ACCEPTED and verified: alphanumeric ("hh:mm:ss"), the §8.3.3.2 Format-2 hexadecimal form (X"68686D6D7373" → +45296.00), national (N"hh:mm:ss"), and an §8.8.3 concatenation expression ("hh:" & "mm:ss" → +45296.00). Secondary over-restriction on the same check: `ALL "hh:mm:ss"` (an §8.3.3.6.4 Format-6 figurative constant representing an alphanumeric literal) binds to BoundAllLiteral, not BoundStringLiteral, and is REJECTED with COBOLNET1517 — verified. Fix shape: give the FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE/SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME/TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME arm a category test (Alphanumeric or National) beside the literal test, in the same place the missing argument-2 class check for r3 must go. test-needed: the shared COBOLNET1517 arm is covered only for FORMATTED-DATE (conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedDate_NonLiteralFormat_1517); there is no SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME leg and no negative test for a wrong-class literal. Editions from IntrinsicCatalog IntroducedIn=2014 (gate verified: --std 2002 → COBOLNET1502).

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: Holds under the IMPLIED >>LEAP-SECOND OFF default, fails on the ON path. Analyze walks argument-2 segment by segment against the tokenized format, checking every data-bearing separator (colon, decimal separator, T, W, Z, offset sign), digit-only content, per-subfield ranges (hh 00-23, mm 00-59, offset-hours 00-23 / offset-minutes 00-59 per §15.3.3.6.2, zero-sign forcing zero magnitude per §15.3.3.6.1), short data and trailing data; a nonzero result routes to ExceptionState.ArgumentError, which sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 — the §15.3 implementor-defined result, which A.1 item 90 expressly says need NOT be documented, so no CONFORMANCE.md entry is owed. Verified: "256100"/'hhmmss' → +00000.00 and, under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)'; "12-34-56"/'hh:mm:ss' → 0; "1234"/'hhmmss' → 0; "123456Z"/'hhmmssZ' → +45296.00; "12:34:56+05:00"/'hh:mm:ss+hh:mm' → +45296.00; "12345650"/'hhmmss.ss' (phantom basic separator) → +45296.50. THE GAP: the seconds range is hardcoded `Fld.Second => (0, 59)` in Analyze — §15.3.3.3 requires 00..<61 when a LEAP-SECOND directive with the ON phrase is in effect, and >>LEAP-SECOND sits in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.KnownIgnoredDirectives, so it is consumed and silently ignored. Verified: a source beginning `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` with `FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss", "235960")` compiles without a word of complaint and returns +00000.00, rejecting a value §15.3.3.3 makes legal. CONFORMANCE.md §3 records >>LEAP-SECOND as documented non-support, but §7.3.17 is core language, not an Annex A.4 optional module, so §4.2.7 does not cover it and A.1 items 111/112 (both required + shall-be-documented) presuppose the directive works — resolving that is an owner call. test-needed: no test exercises an invalid argument-2 for this function, and none exercises >>LEAP-SECOND at all.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) is computed exactly for fraction widths up to NINE digits — Analyze forms `((long)hh*3600 + mi*60 + ss) * 10^f + frac` at scale f, S correctly carrying the fractional-second digits of the seconds subfield (§15.3.3.2), and the offset/UTC subfields correctly NOT entering the sum; both D.31.5.9 worked examples reproduce exactly ("hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" → +18867.81). It breaks at TEN or more fractional-second digits: Analyze accumulates every subfield through a local `int val = 0;` and then does `case Fld.Fraction: frac = val;` even though `frac` is already a long, so the fraction wraps at 2^31 in unchecked arithmetic. Verified at --std 2014: `("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000")` into `01 WS-A PIC +9(5).9(10).` returns +45295.8705032704 instead of +45296.3000000000 (3000000000 − 2^32 = −1294967296); twelve digits `("hhmmss.ssssssssssss", "123456812479168304")` into PIC +9(5).9(12) returns +45296.000730349360 instead of +45296.812479168304; nineteen digits returns +00000.01. §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction width implementor-defined with a floor of nine; COBOL.NET neither enforces nor documents a maximum, and A.1 item 202 ('Time formats and corresponding function values (maximum precision not less than nine fractional digits)', required, 'This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7: NO — §7 currently lists only items 2, 59, 158 and 205–215. So the conforming fix is BOTH halves: widen the accumulator (or reject past the defined maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION) AND add the item-202 row to CONFORMANCE.md §7. The two existing tests exercise the expression only at 0 and 2 fraction digits, so nothing covers the overflow.

ABS function
notes: PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED INDEPENDENTLY (scripts/render-spec-page.py 846; printed folio 816): the format is FUNCTION ABS ( argument-1 ) with FUNCTION and ABS underlined and NO bracketed or optional element, so the transcription is faithful and the lossy-diagram failure mode does not apply. Accepted in ordinary expression positions, re-probed at the CLI: a 1-argument reference binds and evaluates; FUNCTION ABS(1 2) draws COBOLNET1504; the 8.4.3.2 SR2 keyword-omitted form ABS(N) under REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC binds and prints 12.34. NOT ALL LEGAL POSITIONS: 8.4.2.3.2 makes a subscript an arithmetic-expression-1, 8.8.1.1 admits an identifier referencing a numeric data item, 8.5.2.12 items 6/7 make a numeric/integer function exactly that, and 8.4.3.2.3 SR12 expressly names the integer form of ABS as the ONE integer function allowed where an unsigned integer is required -- yet DISPLAY E(FUNCTION ABS(I)) compiles and then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "reference 'E(FUNCTION ABS(I))'" at run time, failing 4.2.2 paragraph 1. Root cause is the D10 subscript-capture residue, not ABS (E(I + 1) works, E(FUNCTION MAX(...)) fails identically). ADJACENT RESIDUE ON THE SAME PATH: 15.7.1's type table (Integer argument -> Integer function) is not modelled -- IntrinsicCatalog hardcodes ABS to IntrinsicType.Numeric -- so the integer form SR12 turns on does not exist as a distinct thing; latent only because SR11/SR12 are not enforced today. EDITIONS, READ BEFORE CLOSING THIS ROW: 85 is excluded on evidence (the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module is the 42 functions of NIST IF101A..IF142A, matching the catalog's 42 IntroducedIn-85 rows; ABS appears in neither, and in no tests/nist program). 2002 vs 2014 is UNRESOLVED -- the 2023 standard cannot adjudicate it (Annex E covers only the 2014->2023 delta) and the sole basis for the compiler's 2014 lower bound is IntrinsicCatalog's own ABS row, sitting under the block comment 'COBOL-2014 additions (windows provisional pending the matrix wave)', which makes deriving the edition set from it circular; 2002 is therefore recorded as APPLYING rather than silently excluded. CONCRETE RISK: cobol --std 2002 today rejects FUNCTION ABS with COBOLNET1502 'was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2014', so if ABS is in fact a 2002 function the compiler rejects legal COBOL-2002. BARE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: was FUNCTION ABS introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 or by ISO/IEC 1989:2014? (Answering it needs a standard plan ratified decision 1 declined to acquire.) test-needed.
