subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED at PARTIAL, but the accept-half verification was incomplete and is completed here. Citation re-validated independently: the §15.40.2 general format is `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 [ argument-4 ] )` with BOTH words underlined (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.40.2). GRAMMAR RE-READ, not inherited: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart* | reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart* | RANDOM subscriptPart? refModPart*`; FORMATTED-DATETIME is not in §8.9, so it takes the plain `functionName` slot. `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` and `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` admit every §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 shape in every position, space-juxtaposed or comma/semicolon-separated (§8.3.5). Arity 3..4 is the catalog row (`IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, 3, 4`); 0/2/5 arguments, `()` and a bare name all draw COBOLNET1504. WHAT THE PRIOR PASS DID NOT CHECK AND I DID: the LEGAL keyword-omitted form. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 permits omitting FUNCTION when the REPOSITORY paragraph declares the function, and `IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction` DOES support it for a non-reserved name — reached from `ExpressionBinder.FieldOperand` before name resolution, gated on `ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic || RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name)` plus `IntrinsicCatalog.TryGet`, with the 3-argument list arriving as the single `subscriptPart` and re-parsed through the SAME `functionArgListFragment`. So the accept half covers both reference forms. `OMITTED` in an argument slot draws COBOLNET1544 (§8.4.3.2 SR7). WHY NOT CONFORMS — unchanged and confirmed: with NO repository declaration, `FORMATTED-DATETIME(A, B, C)` is not a function reference and is not a defined data-name either; `ReferenceResolver.Resolve` returns null WITHOUT a diagnostic and `ExpressionBinder.RefFailure` stages a `BoundOperandError` that fails only at run time, so the format's second required word is unenforced. That is generic unresolved-name staging (`ZZ-NOT-DEFINED(A,B,C)` behaves identically) and is already recorded against §15.17.2, so it is not re-listed as a new fix-queue item. EDITIONS re-derived from the SPEC, not the catalog row: Annex E.2 item 13 enumerates exactly seven intrinsic names new in 2023 (BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE) and FORMATTED-DATETIME is absent, establishing >= 2014 from this document; the 85/2002 exclusion is asserted from the historical standards and is NOT derivable from the 2023 text. TEST: none. tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob is a byte-compare .out snapshot exercising only the 3-argument extended form — corroboration, non-qualifying.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL). The adjudicator's claim "I could construct no legal shape of this general format the grammar rejects" is FALSE; two legal shapes of argument-1 are rejected, and both were found by READING the lexer/binder rather than sampling. (1) HEXADECIMAL-NATIONAL LITERAL. Spec (cite-verified §15.41.3 r1 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal"; §8.3.3.5.2 Format 2 gives the national literal's second form NX"…" / NX'…', and §8.3.3.5.3 SR1/SR2 apply to ALL FORMATS). CobolLexer.g4 has NO NX rule and says so in its own comment on the NATLIT line: "NX\"…\" (hex national) is deferred" (the same line defers BX"…"). `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(NX"00680068006D006D00730073", 45296)` therefore does not lex as one national literal: `NX` takes the IDENTIFIER rule and `"0068…"` the STRINGLIT rule, and because argument separation inside a function-argument region is plain juxtaposition (functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*) the single literal SILENTLY becomes TWO arguments — a 3-argument call whose argument-1 is an unresolvable data reference. Legal COBOL, misparsed and then rejected. (2) CONSTANT-NAME ARGUMENT. §13.10.1 "A constant may be used in place of a literal", §13.10.4 GR1 "the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1 … were written where constant-name-1 is written", §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression" (all cite-verified). `01 TFMT CONSTANT AS "hh:mm:ss".` + `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(TFMT, 45296)` PARSES (dataReference inside arithmeticExpression) but dies at bind — see AR-15.41.3-1. Everything the adjudicator verified positively still holds (FUNCTION + IDENTIFIER name slot, space/comma/semicolon separation, STRINGLIT/NATLIT/HEXLIT/concatenation argument-1, SIGNED_INTEGERLIT argument-3, refModPart* for PB8, arity 2..3 at bind). One correction to its reasoning: the figurative ZERO reaches argument-2 by TWO different routes depending on position — ZeroTokenRewriter rewrites ZERO to ZERO_ARITH only when the adjacent token is an arithmetic operator or a paren, so `FORMATTED-TIME("hh:mm:ss", ZERO)` binds as a numeric 0 while `FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm", ZERO, 120)` (ZERO between two FNARG_SEPARATORs) binds as BoundFigurative('Z'); both happen to render 0, so this is noted, not charged.

subject: FRACTION-PART function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The prior pass's structural readings all RE-VERIFIED and are correct as far as they go: cite.py --check 15.42.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (General format, both words underlined, one parenthesised argument, no optional element); `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate superset; IntrinsicCatalog gives MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 so bare `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART`, `()` and `(A B)` all take COBOLNET1504 in BindIntrinsicCore; the D8 window gate fires COBOLNET1502 below --std 2002; and I confirmed the keyword-omitted route is NOT an over-accept -- KeywordOmittedFunction gates on `(ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic || ctx.Data.RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name)) && IntrinsicCatalog.TryGet(name, out _)`, so `FRACTION-PART(A)` with no REPOSITORY stays a data reference (8.4.3.2.3 SR2 honoured). WHY IT IS STILL NOT CONFORMS -- THE PRIOR PASS'S OWN STATED BASIS IS FALSE. It closed the row on "Net user-visible surface = exactly the general format". It is not. The format writes `( argument-1 )`, 15.6 Table 21 types that position `Num1`, and 15.3 type 10 (cite.py --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified." -> OK, rule 10) makes an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION a licensed occupant of that position. Under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` / `STANDARD-DECIMAL` that shape does not compile: NumericRenderer.CombineCore returns `NumX(CobolDec.*(...), 0, Dec: true)` for every +,-,*,/ under a standard mode, IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's `case "FractionPart"` has no Dec arm, and `CobolIntrinsics.FractionPart` is `(Int128, int)` while CobolDec (a readonly record struct(Int128 Sig, int Exp)) declares NO conversion operators -- verified by reading both files -- so Roslyn emits CS1503 and the user sees "backend compilation failed" on source the general format admits. A format whose argument position rejects a legal argument shape has a broken acceptance half; per the costing rule (one half verified => PARTIAL) this is PARTIAL. It bites at EVERY edition in the window: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is 2002+ (DataBinder rejects it only at 2023) and STANDARD-DECIMAL is 2014+, and NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal covers both. TEST-REF SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: pb2_float_argument_exact_family is a genuine spec-derived conformance fixture (header derives its expectations from 15.64.4/15.77.4/15.44/15.49 rule text, not from observation), but its ONE FRACTION-PART line is `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(D)` with D and R BOTH COMP-2, golden line 7 = `0.5`. It proves the format parses in exactly one shape -- float argument, float receiver, positive value. It exercises no fixed-point argument, no arithmetic-expression argument, and no rejection at all; there is no negative fixture for the arity half and none for the COBOLNET1502 edition half. Diagnostic nit re-confirmed, not a conformance defect: `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART (1:2)` reports COBOLNET1504 rather than the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 argument-list error because ResultRefMod short-circuits on BoundExprError -- illegal either way.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS → PARTIAL. What holds, re-verified independently: the transcribed format is a single unbracketed `FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC ( argument-1 )` with both words underlined; HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC is genuinely NOT a §8.9 reserved word (the printed list runs HEADING · HIGH-VALUE · HIGH-VALUES · I-O — no HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC), so it lexes as IDENTIFIER; the grammar superset is closed by COBOLNET1504 (arity, IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore) and the PB8 ref-mod arm; the D8 introduction gate DOES fire (IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore raises COBOLNET1502 when sig.IntroducedIn > DialectLevel), so --std 85 rejects the reference. THREE THINGS THE ADJUDICATOR ASSERTED WITHOUT VERIFYING, and one of them is false. (1) ⛔ "Nothing LEGAL is turned away" IS FALSE. §8.5.2.12 enumerates the data items of category numeric and items 3/4/5 are A LINE-COUNTER · A LINAGE-COUNTER · A PAGE-COUNTER (mechanically checked). Those are legal argument-1 shapes under §15.43.3 r1, and ExpressionBinder binds all three to BoundLinageCounterRef / the RWCS-counter refs wrapped in a BoundComputedOperand (the FieldOperand arm returns `new BoundComputedOperand(new BoundLinageCounterRef(lcf))`), so BindAlgebraicFold's `args[0] is not BoundFieldOperand` guard rejects them with COBOLNET1516. `FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(LINAGE-COUNTER)` is conforming source and does not compile. (2) The §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 KEYWORD-OMITTED form is verified BY READING ONLY — IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction is gated `DialectLevel < 2002` and now admits zero-or-one suffix after PB7, so `HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(X)` under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC` should route — but NO test exercises it for this function, and PB7/PB9 are the standing proof that this exact path can compile clean and fail at run time. (3) The cited golden is spec-derived (its header cites §15.43/§15.58 + Annex D.32 and derives every value from the PICTURE), but it only compiles the FUNCTION-keyword form in two spacings at one edition; it pins no rejection and no keyword-omitted form. PARTIAL is the honest verdict: the format is right, the argument REGION admits less than §15.3 permits.

subject: INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED: PARTIAL → DIVERGES. Two things the prior pass got wrong. FIRST, the rejection is not one position but TWO. The reference is legal in a SUBSCRIPT — §8.4.2.3.2's subscript diagram admits arithmetic-expression-1; §8.8.1.1 admits 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item'; §8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 makes a function-identifier an identifier; and §8.4.3.2.4 1) closes the loop the prior pass left open, 'A function-identifier references a temporary data item whose value is determined when the function is referenced at runtime' (all --check OK), so the premise is spec-backed rather than assumed. It is EQUALLY legal in a REFERENCE-MODIFIER, unchecked before: §8.4.3.3.3 4) 'Leftmost-position and length shall be arithmetic expressions.' (--check OK). Both funnel through the ONE ReferenceResolver#RenderSegment — InterpretSubscripts calls it per subscript segment AND, on the depth-0-colon branch, for the ref-mod start and length — and RenderSegment handles only SUB_INTEGERLIT, SUB_IDENTIFIER (+ OF/IN), + - * / and parens, its `default: return null` naming FUNCTION explicitly. In SUBSCRIPT mode the word FUNCTION is a plain SUB_IDENTIFIER, so it reaches ResolveSubscriptName, resolves to nothing, and the whole reference fails loud. A VERIFIED rejection of legal source is an active contradiction, not an unverified half — PARTIAL was the wrong shape. SECOND, the acceptance mechanism was described wrongly: PreviousIsFunctionName() reads `_prevNonWsTokenType`, which NextToken() maintains as the token BEFORE last, so at the '(' of `FUNCTION INTEGER (` the last token is IDENTIFIER(INTEGER) and the prev is FUNCTION; OnDefaultLParen keeps DEFAULT mode only because BOTH PreviousIsFunctionName() and PreviousTokenCouldBeDataName() hold. I re-verified independently that INTEGER is not a lexer keyword: it does not appear in §8.9's reserved-word list (searched the clause span mechanically) and tests/version-matrix/cobol-words.json has ZERO occurrences, so functionName's IDENTIFIER alternative carries it and argument-1 parses as a real arithmeticExpression. Arity is enforced at bind (MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 → COBOLNET1504), and the §8.4.3.2.3 2) keyword-omitted form (--check OK) reaches the SAME functionArgList via KeywordOmittedFunction → ReparseArgs. NOT INTEGER-SPECIFIC: RenderSegment rejects every function reference and every non-trivial arithmetic expression in a subscript or ref-mod. Owned architecturally by plan §CUT 2.5 / D10 Step D10.3, but the rejects-legal-COBOL consequence is not recorded there. Corroboration only (NON-QUALIFYING): IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests line 70 is a *MatchesLegacy differential; IntrinsicSpecTests#IntegerFunctionAsSubscript shows the LEGACY engine printing BBB for `DISPLAY WS-ELT(FUNCTION INTEGER(2.9))`, so the greenfield is a regression — a legacy test is a net, never authority. EDITIONS: format text unchanged across the window (no Annex E row); the keyword-omitted leg needs a REPOSITORY paragraph (2002+).

subject: INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN function
notes:
⛔ REFUTER OVERTURN — PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. Every fact in the prior adjudication was re-verified by reading the grammar, the lexer and the binder; none was wrong. What was wrong was the VERDICT GRADE. PARTIAL is for a rule half-verified or an edge unchecked. Here the implementation was located and read, and its measured behaviour is CONTRARY to the rule: the compiler REJECTS conforming source written in this very general format, in four distinct instantiations of argument-1, three of them with no COBOLNET diagnostic at all. Turning legal COBOL away is the outcome CLAUDE.md rule 4 forbids outright and it is not an 'unverified edge'.
CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED MECHANICALLY, not inherited: `cite.py --check 15.45.2 "FUNCTION"` => OK §15.45.2 (General format) rendering `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, nothing bracketed, no repetition: keyword, parentheses and exactly one argument all REQUIRED. `--check 8.4.3.2.3 "boolean expression"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 8) 'Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression.' `--check 15.3 "Boolean. A bit group item, a boolean expression or literal, or an elementary boolean data item shall be specified."` => OK §15.3 3). `--check 8.3.3.4.2 "boolean"` => OK (Format 1 (boolean) — two formats). `--check 8.3.3.4.4 "zero-length literal"` => OK GR4. `--check 8.3.3.4.3 "8 191"` => OK SR1. `--check 13.18.29 "GROUP-USAGE"` => OK.
WHAT IS ACCEPTED (read, not sampled). INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN is absent from src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs (grep returns nothing), so it lexes IDENTIFIER and matches `functionName`; alternative 1 of `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` accepts the written shape. The optional-paren superset is closed at bind — catalog row `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1` and `BindIntrinsicCore` line 454 `if (args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOLNET1504, so the bare name and the two-argument form are rejected. The keyword-omitted §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 route is live at >=2002 (`KeywordOmittedFunction` returns null below 2002; the one-suffix `(args)` shape is admitted) and is gated on a REPOSITORY declaration. The D8 introduction window fires below 2002 (COBOLNET1502), pinned by conformance:negative/boolean_conv_below_2002 (reject-at: 85, expects COBOLNET1502).
DEFECT A — A BOOLEAN-EXPRESSION ARGUMENT IS A RAW SYNTAX ERROR. `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` has NO `booleanExpression` alternative, and I traced the arithmetic chain to ground: arithmeticExpression -> ... -> powerExpression -> unaryExpression -> primaryExpression -> {numericLiteral | ZERO_ARITH | functionCall | dataReference | LPAREN arithmeticExpression RPAREN}. Boolean is unreachable from it. `B-AND` is token B_AND (CobolLexer.g4 line 174, DEFAULT mode, declared long before IDENTIFIER so maximal-munch/rule-order gives B_AND), which starts no `functionArgument`, so `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(BIT-A B-AND BIT-B)` closes functionArgList after BIT-A and then fails expecting RPAREN — an ANTLR syntax error, no COBOLNET code. The `booleanExpression` rule EXISTS (CobolExpressions.g4 line 132, with its full B-OR/B-XOR/B-AND/B-SHIFT/B-NOT tiers) and is already re-used by `compileTimeOperand`, so the alternative was available and simply not wired. The grammar's own header comment above `functionCall` quotes SR8 verbatim — 'an argument is an identifier, literal, boolean expression, or arithmetic expression' — and then implements three of the four. Confirming there is no back door: `IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor` does carry a `Visit(BoundBoolOperand)` arm, but `BoundBoolOperand` is constructed ONLY in ConditionBinder (`ConditionBinder.cs:223`), never on the intrinsic-argument path, so the leaf is dead here.
DEFECT B — A BIT GROUP ITEM CANNOT BE DECLARED. §13.18.29 makes a GROUP-USAGE BIT group 'an elementary item of usage bit and category boolean', which is §15.3 item 3's first admissible shape. GROUP-USAGE exists in COBOL.NET only as a reserved-word row; grep across src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/ finds NO production, and DataBinder.cs:1491 states '(GROUP-USAGE is not modeled — its national/bit group forms are the staged national legs.)'. The DATA DIVISION entry is a raw parse error with no staged COBOLNET0899.
DEFECT C — THE FORMAT-2 HEX BOOLEAN LITERAL HAS NO TOKEN, AND FAILS MISLEADINGLY. §8.3.3.4.2 gives boolean literals TWO formats; CobolLexer.g4 line 740 records 'BX"…" (hex boolean) is deferred'. `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(BX"0F")` therefore lexes as IDENTIFIER `BX` + STRINGLIT — two juxtaposed functionArguments — and surfaces as a COBOLNET1504 ARITY error ('takes 1 argument(s); 2 given') plus an unresolved-name report. A wrong diagnostic on legal source is worse than none: it points the user at the argument count.
DEFECT D — THE ZERO-LENGTH FORMAT-1 LITERAL DOES NOT LEX. `fragment BOOL_BODY : 'B' '\"' [01]+ '\"' | 'B' '\'' [01]+ '\'' ;` requires ONE OR MORE digits, while §8.3.3.4.2 Format 1 brackets boolean-character-1 and §8.3.3.4.4 GR4 says 'If boolean-character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal'. `B""` is legal and does not tokenize. (This also makes the runtime's documented zero-length branch unreachable — see RV-15.45.4-1.)
NET REACHABLE SURFACE: of §15.3 item 3's four admissible argument shapes, exactly TWO are usable — an elementary boolean data item (including the reference-modified form) and a NON-EMPTY Format-1 boolean literal.
TEST EVIDENCE, WEIGHED. conformance:2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv is genuinely spec-derived — its header derives every value from §15.13.4 r1 / §15.45.4 r1 / Annex D.10 and its committed golden `.out` (git-tracked; the sibling .dll/.g.cs/.runtimeconfig.json are build residue) is hand-derived, not a captured snapshot — but it pins only ACCEPTANCE of the FUNCTION-keyword form in two spacings. NOTHING pins the bare name, the two-argument form, the keyword-omitted form for this function, or the §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 ref-mod-of-result rejection. No test can close a DIVERGES row anyway.
EDITIONS, DERIVED FROM THE STANDARD, NOT FROM THE CATALOG ROW (which says 2002 and was deliberately not consulted as authority). INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN is absent from the 2023 introduction's added/enhanced-function list (BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, EXCEPTION-FILE/-N, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE, TRIM) and absent from the Annex E removal/obsolescence material — which establishes 2014 and 2023 mechanically. Its entire domain (usage BIT, PIC 1, class/category boolean, boolean literals) is the COBOL-2002 boolean-data amendment; COBOL-85 plus the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment had no boolean data, so 85 is EXCLUDED. docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md carries no pre-2023 row for these functions and names only the B-SHIFT-* operators as the 2023 boolean addition — consistent.

subject: INTEGER-OF-DATE function
notes: REFUTED DOWN FROM CONFORMS. WHAT IS VERIFIED: the format is 'FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE ( argument-1 )', both words underlined, exactly one argument, no optional phrase and no bracketed alternative. INTEGER-OF-DATE lexes as IDENTIFIER (longest match beats any INTEGER token) and reaches the generic alternative 'FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*'; the catalog row is IntrinsicArity.Fixed with MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 and BindIntrinsicCore rejects any other count with COBOLNET1504 ahead of every per-function arm, so the parenthesis-less form, the empty-parenthesis form and a two-argument list all fail; ResultRefMod rejects a ref-mod on the integer result (Sec 8.4.3.3.3 SR2). WHAT IS MISSING - THE HALF THE PRIOR PASS DID NOT LOOK AT, and it is invisible to output-sampling because the program COMPILES and fails only at RUN TIME (the PB7 shape): the grammar's functionArgument admits fnArgPhraseWord - LEADING, TRAILING, LAST, FIRST, ANY, START, AFTER, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL - for EVERY function, deliberately, as a superset rule the binder is supposed to narrow. It does not narrow it here. IntrinsicBinder.BindArgOperand handles an unconsumed phrase word with 'return new BoundOperandError($"intrinsic argument '{kw.GetText()}'")' and calls NO ctx.Edition.Error, so 'FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(LEADING)' passes arity (1 argument), passes CheckArgumentClasses (ClassOf(BoundOperandError) is null; and INTEGER-OF-DATE has no rule row at all), renders as EmitText.LoudValue -> NotImplemented.Value<long>(...), compiles clean and throws at RUN TIME. Sec 15.46.2's general format admits no keyword in argument-1's position, and Sec 4.2.2 - 'This warning mechanism shall indicate violations of such rules' (--check verified) - requires the violation to be indicated; a runtime throw is not an indication. Contrast the sibling shape one line above, which IS diagnosed: OMITTED gets COBOLNET1544. TWO EVIDENCE CORRECTIONS to the prior pass, neither of which changes the verdict on its own but both of which show the format was reasoned about rather than traced: (a) it asserted 'the FUNCTION keyword is required by the only alternative that can match it, matching the underlining' - that is false about both the standard and this compiler. Sec 8.4.3.2.3 SR2, 'If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required' (--check verified), permits the omission, and IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction implements it - correctly gated at DialectLevel >= 2002 (REPOSITORY is a COBOL-2002 introduction), REPOSITORY-gated, and yielding to a declared data item. That path was absent from the prior code-location and is the second reference form this format wears. (b) COBOLNET1544's message and the BindArgOperand doc comment both cite 'Sec 8.4.3.2 SR7'; the rule is at Sec 8.4.3.2.3 SR7 ('The word OMITTED shall not be specified if intrinsic-function-name-1 is specified' - located by --find; --check confirms Sec 8.4.3.2 does NOT contain the word OMITTED). That is the one-level-short citation shape, in shipped diagnostic text.

subject: INTEGER-OF-DAY function
notes: DOWNGRADED FROM CONFORMS — the ACCEPT half is verified and correct, the REJECT half is INCOMPLETE, so this cannot be rounded up. `cite.py --check 15.47.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>INTEGER-OF-DAY</u> ( argument-1 )"` OK. WHAT IS RIGHT (re-verified, not inherited): the grammar rule is literally `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*`, INTEGER-OF-DAY is a §8.11 intrinsic-function name and NOT a §8.9 reserved word (checked positionally against the spec's own two lists — §8.9 starts at the '### 8.9 Reserved words' header and §8.11 at '### 8.11 Intrinsic function names'; the token sits under §8.11), so it arrives through the ordinary IDENTIFIER `functionName` slot with its hyphens intact; the catalog row is `Add(new("INTEGER-OF-DAY", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "IntegerOfDay", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85))` — Fixed 1..1, matching the single parenthesised argument-1, with no RemovedIn so the D8 gate (COBOLNET1502) never falsely rejects the form at any --std. Arity IS enforced: `args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs` -> COBOLNET1504 + BoundExprError in BindIntrinsicCore, so the paren-less `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY`, the empty `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY ()` and any two-argument form all fail ('0 given' / '2 given') — the grammar's optional parenthesis group does not let the format through. OMITTED in the argument slot is refused (COBOLNET1544, §8.4.3.2 SR7, read at BindArgOperand), and the PB8 arm rejects a ref-mod on this integer result (COBOLNET1543 for the SR6 argument-list confusion, COBOLNET1629 for §8.4.3.3.3 SR2). ⛔ WHAT IS MISSING — the §15.3 rule-14 restriction on the ALL subscript is UNENFORCED IN THIS FORMAT'S ARGUMENT SLOT. `cite.py --check 15.3 "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL."` OK (§15.3 item 14). §15.47.2's general format permits argument-1 exactly ONCE — the definition does not permit a repeated argument — so `T(ALL)` is not an admissible argument-1 here. But IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicArgs calls `TryExpandAll(a, args)` for EVERY catalogued function and TryExpandAll never consults sig.Arity/MinArgs/MaxArgs (whole method read: it keys only on the argument's SHAPE — a sole data reference whose one subscript capture holds a depth-0 ALL); its own doc comment says "when a VARIADIC function references a table", which is precisely the gate the code does not have. Consequence: `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY(T(ALL))` over a table declared `OCCURS 1 TIMES` expands to one operand, passes the 1..1 arity arm and COMPILES, accepting a form the standard does not admit. The exposure is narrow — for OCCURS n>1 the expansion produces n operands and the arity arm rejects it (with a message that misattributes the cause), and an OCCURS DEPENDING table is staged loud — but narrow is not absent, and it is the half of this format's reject direction that nothing checks. ⚠ ALSO RECORDED, charged elsewhere so this row is not double-counted: a call written in exactly this general format fails to produce ANY result when argument-1 renders as floating-point (`CobolIntrinsics.IntegerOfDayReal` does not exist) — the parse and the bind accept the format correctly and the failure is in the emitter, so it belongs to AR-15.47.3-1 and RV-15.47.4-1, but it means a green FMT row here must not be read as 'this form works'. TEST-REF: re-verified ON DISK at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 276; its helper AssertSpec compiles and compares to a HAND-WRITTEN expectation with no oracle involved (AssertSameAsLegacy is a different helper this method does not call), and the case compiles the literal `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY(...)` shape, so the accept direction is EXECUTED. It pins only the positive form, at dialect 85 only; the arity rejection and the ALL over-acceptance are unpinned by any checked-in spec-derived test. EDITIONS from the standard: no Annex E entry, no docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row — present unchanged in all four.

subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
REFUTER PASS. VERDICT RETAINED AT PARTIAL; THE EVIDENCE IS CORRECTED IN TWO PLACES - one test-ref claim is FALSE, and one of the two grounds offered is double-counted from another row.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME, not inherited: cite.py --check 15.48.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 )" -> OK (§15.48.2 General format; both words underlined = required). cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required" -> OK, and I read SR2 in full: "If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required." Table 21 (:29941) independently fixes the arity at two - "Anum1 or Nat1, Anum2 or Nat2" - so the transcription's unbracketed two-argument shape is corroborated without a page re-render.

⛔ CORRECTION 1 - THE TEST-REF WAS OVER-CLAIMED. The adjudicator wrote "The two test-refs write the format's exact shape". They do NOT. I read both on disk: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:756 writes FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYDDD", "2021167") and tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob:34 writes FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYY-MM-DD", "2021-06-16") - BOTH use the §8.3.5 COMMA separator. The general format as printed separates argument-1 and argument-2 by a SPACE, and that shape has NO test for this function anywhere (I grepped tests/ for every occurrence of the name: only those two, plus the GnuCOBOL corpus, which is a differential and never qualifies). The landed FORMATTED-DATE row already records exactly this limit ("comma form only"), so the standard of care existed and this row missed it. The refs are kept because they are spec-derived and do exercise the accept half; the claim about WHICH shape they cover is withdrawn.

⛔ CORRECTION 2 - THE CONSTANT-NAME GROUND IS DOUBLE-COUNTED HERE. The adjudicator's "SECOND BAR TO CONFORMS" (argument-1 written as a constant-name draws COBOLNET0844 + COBOLNET1517) is REAL - I re-derived it end to end in the code - but it is a rule about what argument-1 may BE, which is §15.48.3 r1's territory, where it correctly reads DIVERGES with the full evidence. Counting it a second time on the general-format row inflates the finding. Removed from the grounds for this verdict.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS IS PARTIAL - ONE OF THE FORMAT'S TWO REQUIRED WORDS IS UNENFORCED. Read in the code, not sampled: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE is not an §8.9 reserved word and is absent from the grammar's reservedIntrinsicArgFn (SIGN | SUM only - I read the production), so it arrives through `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` as functionName; `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` supplies both §8.3.5 separations; the catalog row is IntrinsicArity.Fixed 2,2 so BindIntrinsicCore raises COBOLNET1504 at any other count - including the NO-PARENTHESIS form, which the grammar's `(LPAREN ... RPAREN)?` admits and only the arity screen rejects, untested - and COBOLNET1501 for a name that is not an intrinsic. But only SR2's PERMISSION is implemented: KeywordOmittedFunction computes isFn from ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic / RepositoryIntrinsics and returns null when neither names the function, so RefExpr's final arm builds `new BoundExprError(RefFailure(dref))` - and I read ReferenceResolver#Resolve to its end and confirmed it returns null with NO diagnostic (`if (item is null) return null;`), so nothing calls ctx.Edition.Error anywhere on that path. Non-conforming source (the omitted FUNCTION word with no REPOSITORY paragraph) COMPILES CLEAN and fails only at RUN time as an internal NotImplemented. §4.2.2's warning mechanism indicates nothing. The mechanism is GENERIC unresolved-name staging and is name-independent; the identical finding is already landed against COMBINED-DATETIME and FORMATTED-DATE. ADDITIONAL WITNESS, not a new queue item.

PARTIAL RATHER THAN DIVERGES, AND I CONSIDERED THE DOWNGRADE EXPLICITLY: the FUNCTION-keyword shape the general format actually prints IS implemented, binds, and produces the right value, and the arity superset is closed by COBOLNET1504. One required word enforced, one not, is one half implemented - which is also the disposition the five landed sibling FMT rows of this family carry (FMT-15.17.2 / 15.38.2 / 15.39.2 / 15.40.2 / 15.41.2), all on this same single ground.

EDITIONS derived from the STANDARD, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row: I grepped every occurrence of the name in specs/ISO_COBOL.md - the TOC, the §8.11 intrinsic-function-name list, Table 21, §15.48, Annex D.31.5.8 and the index - and ANNEX E CARRIES NONE, so the function is not a 2023 addition and stands unchanged at 2014 and 2023. The 2002 boundary is not derivable from the 2023 text and is not asserted.

subject: INTEGER-PART function
notes: REFUTER: verdict held at PARTIAL, but the RATIONALE IS REPLACED - the adjudicator's PARTIAL rested on the standard-arithmetic CS1503, and that defect is MIS-ATTRIBUTED here. Format re-validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.49.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>INTEGER-PART</u> ( argument-1 )"` -> OK (General format). Nothing is bracketed, so FUNCTION, the parentheses and the single argument are all REQUIRED. WHAT CONFORMS, each claim re-read at source rather than taken over: the grammar rule really is `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:325-329) and `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` (:421), so INTEGER-PART arrives as IDENTIFIER by ANTLR longest-match; IntrinsicCatalog.cs:106 is `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1`; `ArgsOf(Core.FunctionArgListContext? list) => list?.functionArgument() ?? []` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:155) turns BOTH the no-parenthesis form and `FUNCTION INTEGER-PART()` into zero arguments, and BindIntrinsicCore's gate `if (args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs)` (:454) then raises COBOLNET1504 - so the grammar's optional parenthesis group is genuinely closed at bind time, and a two-argument call is rejected by the same gate. RE-ATTRIBUTION: the compiler ACCEPTS the format for a compound argument-1; what fails is the emitted VALUE path, so the standard-arithmetic CobolDec/CS1503 defect is booked against RV-15.49.4-1 (now DIVERGES) and is only cross-referenced here. WHY THIS IS STILL PARTIAL AND NOT CONFORMS - the unverified legs, stated plainly: (a) EVERY conforming claim above rests on READING; there is no spec-derived fixture pinning the zero-argument reject, the two-argument reject, or the parenthesis-less form - the whole §15.49.2 negative surface is untested, and per the brief a net does not substitute; (b) the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 KEYWORD-OMITTED reference form was verified only STRUCTURALLY for this name. INTEGER-PART is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it does not take the `reservedIntrinsicArgFn` alternative; it must route through IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction, which requires `RepositoryAllIntrinsic || RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name)` AND returns null when `ctx.Symbols.TryResolve(name, ...)` finds a same-named data item, then re-parses the captured subscript text through ReparseArgs/FunctionArgFragment. Every keyword-omitted fixture in the corpus is about some OTHER shape (2023/pb7_keyword_omitted_zero_arg, 2023/pb9_reserved_intrinsic_names, 2002/udf_keyword_omitted, 2002/repository_paragraph) - none exercises a one-argument, non-reserved intrinsic name, which is exactly the PB7 hazard class: a route that is silently unreachable while the program still COMPILES, so output-sampling cannot see it. NOT edition-scoped as a format question - the same reference is legal in all four editions.

subject: LENGTH function
notes: The one-argument form parses, binds and folds. The optional PHYSICAL keyword is entirely absent; the PHYSICAL leg is 2014+ (it exists only for variable-length groups, and ReservedWords.Table.cs dates the word to 2014). Verified mechanically: grep finds NO occurrence of PHYSICAL anywhere under src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/, so it is not a lexer token, and fnArgPhraseWord lists only LEADING/TRAILING/LAST/FIRST/ANY/START/AFTER/ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL. `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` makes the separator OPTIONAL, so 'FUNCTION LENGTH ( G PHYSICAL )' splits into TWO space-separated arguments; the catalog row is Fixed 1..1 and there is no PHYSICAL arm, so a legal 2014/2023 general format is rejected. REFUTER CORRECTION to the first pass's evidence: it asserted the single diagnostic COBOLNET1504. BindIntrinsicCore binds the arguments FIRST (`var args = BindIntrinsicArgs(argCtxs)`, IntrinsicBinder.cs:453) and only THEN checks arity (:454), so the word PHYSICAL is bound as a data reference and fails name resolution before the arity error is raised; the exact diagnostic sequence was never run and should not be stated as fact - what is verified is that the construct cannot parse-and-bind. Separately: PHYSICAL does not appear in the transcribed 8.9 reserved-word list at all (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md finds it only in the 15.50.2 / 15.14.2 formats, the 15.50.4/15.14.4 rule text and the index entry 'PHYSICAL 14.9.51.4, 15.28'), while ReservedWords.Table.cs:323 records it as 'added 2014 (GnuCOBOL 2014 list; dropped by 2023 8.9)'. If that table row is right, PHYSICAL is not reserved under --std 2023 even though the 2023 general format underlines it - an inventory/transcription conflict to settle, though it is not what blocks the parse today. Same defect in FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH's format (15.14.2), which carries the identical [PHYSICAL] phrase.

subject: LOCALE-COMPARE function
notes: The format is CATALOGUED but never ACCEPTED. The row models it (IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing 2..3 = two required arguments plus the bracketed locale-name-1; IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric matches §15.51.1 'The function type is alphanumeric.' --check OK), which is why a reference draws the named COBOLNET1518 rather than COBOLNET1501; the Unsupported arm returns before the arity check, so the 2..3 bounds are dead and a mis-arity call also reports 1518. TEST-REF SUSTAINED BUT ITS DESCRIPTION CORRECTED: both artefacts exist and are read — LocaleDispositionTests.cs:41 compiles MOVE FUNCTION LOCALE-COMPARE("A" "B") TO WS-R at edition 2023 and asserts !ok plus the diagnostic substrings 'COBOLNET1518' and 'A.4.9'; it does NOT assert the §4.2.7/§A.4.1 text the adjudicator credited it with, and the negative-corpus .err carries the bare string 'COBOLNET1518'. Neither is nist:, characterization: or a legacy differential. They pin the DISPOSITION, not format acceptance. REACHABILITY RE-VERIFIED on all three reference forms (the PB7/PB8 failure shapes): FUNCTION-keyword (BindIntrinsic:79), keyword-omitted via KeywordOmittedFunction -> ReparseArgs -> BindIntrinsicCore (:256, gated on REPOSITORY ALL/named INTRINSIC and on the name not resolving to a data item), and ref-mod of the result (FinishIntrinsic -> ResultRefMod returns the existing BoundExprError at :121, so no second diagnostic stacks). ALSO FOUND, outside this clause set (§12.3.8): 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOCALE-COMPARE INTRINSIC.' is ACCEPTED SILENTLY — DataBinder.cs:336 adds any functionName to RepositoryIntrinsics with no IntrinsicBind.Unsupported test — so the A.4.1 'accept the syntax only when support is claimed' posture is enforced at the reference site ONLY. Editions narrowed per AR-15.51.3-1.

subject: LOCALE-DATE function
notes: The general format FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE ( argument-1 [ locale-name-1 ] ) is NEVER ACCEPTED. The catalog row (Alphanumeric, OptionalTrailing, MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 2) carries Bind == IntrinsicBind.Unsupported, so BindIntrinsicCore returns LocaleUnsupported() -- a LOUD bind-time COBOLNET1518 BY NAME -- before arity or argument screening. REFUTER RE-DERIVED THE DISPOSITION RATHER THAN INHERITING IT: A.4.9 item 3 is literally 'LOCALE-DATE function (15.52)'; A.4.1 reads 'An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for an optional element only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor'; 4.2.7 additionally requires the implementor to identify the non-support in user documentation, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 item 5 plus the A.4.9 row of section 5 do so. The decision is the OWNER'S, not this review's: docs/COMPLETION_ROADMAP_COUNCIL.md line 1 'Status: RATIFIED (2026-07-03, owner)' + decision-table row 3 + plan line 1559. Verdict is NOT-IMPLEMENTED (no code implements the ACCEPT path; only the reject exists), not NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, because the decision already exists. TWO PROPERTIES THE FIRST PASS NEVER CHECKED, both verified here and both holding: (1) the reject is ctx.Edition.Error, NOT ctx.Edition.Removed, so --permissive cannot downgrade it into a warning that would leave a BoundExprError to reach codegen (EditionContext.cs Error vs Removed); (2) there is no PB7-shaped keyword-omitted hole -- the FUNCTION-keyword entry AND the keyword-omitted re-parse both funnel through the same BindIntrinsicCore, so 'LOCALE-DATE(x)' under REPOSITORY ... FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC rejects identically. Ordering note: the Unsupported arm sits AFTER the D8 window check, so at --std 85 a program collects COBOLNET1502 and COBOLNET1518 together. TEST-REF DELETED by this pass (it claimed conformance:LocaleDispositionTests#LocaleDate_A49 and conformance:tests/conformance/negative/locale_functions_a49.cob; both exist, the latter is manifest-registered): they assert the REJECT -- the negation of this format rule -- not the rule, so they cannot close it; neither one ever writes the [ locale-name-1 ] branch, so even the reject is covered only for the one-argument shape; and their sample FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE(20240229) is not a conforming argument-1 under 15.52.3 r1 at all. EDITIONS re-derived from the standard, NOT from the catalog row: LOCALE-DATE is not among the 42 functions of the 1989 intrinsic-function amendment and is absent from Annex E (the 2014->2023 delta), and the locale module is a 2002 addition; docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md carries NO locale row at all, so the 2002 edge is a ratified decision-#1 provisional edge.

subject: LOCALE-TIME function
notes: SUSTAINED. A LOUD REJECT; no form of the general format is accepted. The format PARSES -- functionCall/functionArgList in CobolExpressions.g4 is `functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` with functionArgument reaching arithmeticExpression, so `FUNCTION LOCALE-TIME ( arg [ loc ] )` admits the space-separated optional second operand -- and the catalog shape matches the format's underlined-required argument-1 plus bracketed optional locale-name-1 (IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, MinArgs 1, MaxArgs 2). Bind=Unsupported makes every reference COBOLNET1518, the conforming disposition for an unclaimed optional module under §4.2.7 + A.4.1 given ratified decision 3 -- and the A.4.1 documentation duty is discharged in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (A.4.9 'Not claimed'), which the prior report did not verify. TEST-REF KEPT after audit: LocaleDispositionTests is in tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance, asserts the diagnostic derived from Annex A, and is neither a nist:, a characterization: nor a *MatchesLegacy* differential -- but its reach is NARROWER than the prior note admitted: it pins one form only, `FUNCTION LOCALE-TIME(120000)`, whose argument is an integer literal of a class §15.53.3 r1 forbids, so it exercises no part of the format that is actually interesting. ** COVERAGE GAPS CLOSED BY RUN, NOT BY TEST ** (prebuilt cobol.exe, --std 2023): the TWO-ARGUMENT form `FUNCTION LOCALE-TIME(WS-T LOC1)` -> COBOLNET1518; the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 KEYWORD-OMITTED form (`REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` + `MOVE LOCALE-TIME(WS-T) TO WS-R`) -> COBOLNET1518, so the PB7-shaped hole does not exist here (KeywordOmittedFunction routes through the same BindIntrinsicCore); `--permissive` -> still COBOLNET1518, confirming EditionContext.Error is unconditional and the 1518 site does not route through the Removed() severity seam; `--std 85` -> COBOLNET1502 *and* COBOLNET1518 (a double diagnostic; both statements are true, but the 1518 text hard-codes 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex A A.4.9' even when targeting 2002 -- a small edition-fidelity wart in the message). NONE of these four behaviours is pinned by any test. See AR-15.53.3-1 for the ArgKinds category defect in the same catalog row.

subject: LOCALE-TIME-FROM-SECONDS function
notes:
The general format is deliberately NOT accepted - the A.4.1 posture for an unclaimed optional element ('An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for an optional element only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor' - --check OK at A.4.1; 4.2.7 --check OK). Verified beyond the adjudicator: COBOLNET1518 is raised through EditionContext.Error, which is NOT demotable (only Removed() consults Permissive), so the reject holds under --permissive too; and the keyword-omitted reference form (REPOSITORY ... INTRINSIC / ALL INTRINSIC) re-enters the SAME BindIntrinsicCore, so there is no PB7-shaped run-time hole. The row's shape (OptionalTrailing, 1..2, ArgKinds 'ns', IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric = the 15.54.1 'function type is alphanumeric') matches the format, but none of it is enforced - COBOLNET1504 is below the Unsupported return.
** OVERTURN 1 - the claimed EDITION DEFECT is withdrawn to UNRESOLVED. ** The first pass declared '** DEFECT: the catalog row's edition window is one edition too wide **' (2002 -> should be 2014). That is not derivable from the authority. (a) The 2023 spec attributes NO edition to 15.54: D.31.4 (Locale date and time intrinsic functions - LOCALE-DATE/-DAY/-TIME/-TIME-FROM-SECONDS) carries no edition sentence at all, and the ONLY in-spec function attribution anywhere is D.31.3.1's 'Two additional functions were added by ISO/IEC 1989:2002' (the TEST-DATE/TEST-DAY pair). D.31.5.1 likewise carries no edition sentence. subject: LOG function

ENFORCED HALF: IntrinsicCatalog#Build's LOG row is `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1`, which is what produces the COBOLNET1504 arity rejections, and LOG is correctly not over-reserved (functionName : IDENTIFIER). TWO ADMISSIONS OF SOURCE THE FORMAT FORBIDS, both re-verified BY READING, not by re-running the adjudicator's programs. (1) PHRASE-WORD ARGUMENT: CobolExpressions.g4:355 is `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression`, with fnArgPhraseWord at :362 admitting LEADING/TRAILING/LAST/FIRST/ANY/START/AFTER/ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL; its own comment concedes 'A superset rule: which words a given function admits is the binder's §15 job', and §15.55.2 IS that job for LOG, with no binder arm discharging it. subject: LOG10 function
notes: DIVERGES SUSTAINED — the lexer mechanism was re-read on disk rather than taken on trust, and it holds. Format: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>LOG10</u> ( argument-1 )` (§15.56.2, both words underlined = required, one required argument in required parentheses). THE PARSER SIDE IS CLEAN: LOG10 is not a lexer token and is not §8.9-reserved (§8.11 lists it as an intrinsic-function NAME, `--check 8.11 "LOG10"` -> OK), so it reaches `functionName : IDENTIFIER`; arity is enforced from the catalog row (MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 -> COBOLNET1504). THE LEXER REJECTS A LEGAL WRITTEN FORM — a SIGNED floating-point literal argument. §8.3.3.3.3 r2 re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.3.3.3.3 "The literal to the left of the"` -> OK §8.3.3.3.3 2), "It may be signed and shall include a decimal point" — the sign is PART of the literal; §8.8.1.1 makes a numeric literal an arithmetic expression and §15.56.3 r1 admits class numeric, so `FUNCTION LOG10(+1.5E3)` (value 1500, so r2 is satisfied too) is conforming source. MECHANISM, verified line by line: CobolLexer.g4 `FLOATLIT : ( [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]* | '.' [0-9]+ ) 'E' [-+]? [0-9]+ ;` carries NO leading sign and cannot start at '+' or '-'; inside the argument region `SignedLiteralCanStart()` is true (InFunctionArgs, and unconditionally at `InputStream.Index == 0` for the primed fragment re-parse), so `FN_SIGNED_DECIMALLIT : {SignedLiteralCanStart()}? [+-] DEC_BODY` with `fragment DEC_BODY : [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+` takes "+1.5" — 4 characters, the longest match available, beating PLUS (1) and FN_SIGNED_INTEGERLIT "+1" (2) — and the orphaned "E3" lexes as IDENTIFIER. functionArgList is plain juxtaposition, so the parser sees TWO arguments and the binder reports COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION LOG10 takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO §15.3)" on legal source. The UNSIGNED form `FUNCTION LOG10(1.5E3)` lexes correctly (FLOATLIT wins by longest match), which is exactly why output-sampling misses this. ⛔ NAME-INDEPENDENT, ALREADY OPEN, DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT: this is the same lexer defect recorded at FMT-15.34.2 (EXP, DIVERGES, still GAP) and it hits every §15 function whose argument-1 admits a numeric literal. One fix — a signed FLOATLIT alternative in the FN_* region, ordered before FN_SIGNED_DECIMALLIT — not one per function. DIVERGENT LEG 2002,2014,2023 (floating-point literals are a 2002 introduction); the editions field is the LOG10 general format's own window. test-ref EMPTY — nothing in tests/conformance/** references LOG10, and tests/conformance/2002/float_literal.cob only writes `MOVE -1.5E3 TO WS-A`, where the predicate is false and MINUS+FLOATLIT parses correctly.

subject: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The prior record closed this row on the 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 keyword-omitted form working under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.`. That form is SILENTLY DEFEATABLE, and the defeat produces a WRONG VALUE with no diagnostic. 8.3.2.1 rule 5 (--check OK): 'Intrinsic-function-names may be used as user-defined words and system-names, except for - intrinsic function names LENGTH, RANDOM, SIGN, and SUM; and - intrinsic function names identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph.' So inside a scope whose REPOSITORY names LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC (by name or by ALL), the word may NOT be a user-defined word - that prohibition is exactly what keeps SR2's keyword-omitted form unambiguous. COBOL.NET never enforces it. `01 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999.` compiles clean under BOTH `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC`, and the compiler then resolves the collision with a HAND-WRITTEN PRECEDENCE RULE in place of the standard's prohibition: KeywordOmittedFunction contains `if (ctx.Symbols.TryResolve(name, ctx.ActiveScope, out _)) return null;   // a declared data item wins - never a mis-routed subscript`, and its own doc comment states the policy as 'Data-item-safe: a name that ALSO resolves to a declared data item stays a subscript (a data item wins - zero regression).' That policy is only safe if the illegal declaration is rejected, and it is not. Consequence demonstrated: with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC.` and a table named LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC in scope, `MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1` - literally 15.58.2's format in its SR2 alternative - yields +7 (the table element) instead of -999, with ZERO diagnostics. ROOT CAUSE: DataBinder#Bind fills RepositoryIntrinsics / RepositoryAllIntrinsic and those sets are consumed ONLY at reference sites in IntrinsicBinder; nothing consults them at DECLARATION time, so 8.3.2.1 r5 is written down nowhere. WHY THE PRIOR RECORD'S CONTROL DOES NOT ATTRIBUTE THIS AWAY: its control was `MOVE ZZQQ-NOPE(A) TO R1`, and ZZQQ-NOPE is not an intrinsic-function-name, so 8.3.2.1 r5 has nothing to say about it - there is no control that makes this generic. SECOND LEG, retained from the prior record and re-run: `LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1)` with NO REPOSITORY at all compiles with zero diagnostics and aborts at RUN TIME with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException - the PB7 shape, invisible to output sampling. SCOPE: the defect is compiler-wide across every intrinsic-function-name, so it is one fix serving many inventory rows; file it once and cross-reference. CONFORMING LEGS, verified this pass and unchanged: two required words, exactly one argument, parentheses required, arity 0 and 2 both COBOLNET1504, `()` also 1504, ref-modification of the numeric result correctly rejected COBOLNET1629 (8.4.3.3.3 SR2), the SR2 form works under BOTH `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC` when no data item shadows it, and the name IS correctly available as a user-defined word when NO REPOSITORY function-specifier names it (8.3.2.1 r5's default). editions deliberately EMPTY: the 2023 document does not date 15.58 in Annex E or F, so the window is not spec-derivable from the document under review, and IntrinsicCatalog's own 2002 row is not admissible evidence. EVIDENCE: cite.py --check 8.3.2.1 'Intrinsic-function-names may be used as user-defined words and system-names, except for': OK, rule 5. cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted': OK, SR2. MY OWN PROBES, --std 2023, unique PROGRAM-ID per file, all under E:/Temp/refb5/. CONTROL r4_ctrl.cob (LOWALGREF04, `MOVE FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1`) -> `CTRL R1=-000999000`, so every rejection below is attributable. r1_repo.cob (LOWALGREF01, `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC.` + `MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1`) -> `R1=-000999000`, the SR2 form. r2_refmod.cob (LOWALGREF02, `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1)(1:2)`) -> `error COBOLNET1629: ... is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function, so its result cannot be reference-modified (ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2)`. r11_empty.cob (LOWALGREF11, `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC()`) -> COBOLNET1504 '0 given'. r3_udw.cob (LOWALGREF03, NO REPOSITORY, `01 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999 VALUE -12.`) -> compiles and prints `UDW=01K` (= -012): CORRECT per 8.3.2.1 r5's default. ⛔ r9_allint.cob (LOWALGREF09, `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` + `01 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999 VALUE -12.`) -> COMPILES CLEAN, prints `ALLINT-UDW=01K`; r10_named.cob (LOWALGREF10, `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC.` + same declaration) -> COMPILES CLEAN, prints `NAMED-UDW=01K`. Both are source 8.3.2.1 r5 forbids. ⛔ r12_shadow.cob (LOWALGREF12, `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC.`, `01 TBL. 05 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999 OCCURS 3 TIMES.`, `MOVE 7 TO LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(2)` then `MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1` with A1 = 2) -> compiles with ZERO diagnostics and prints `SHADOW=+000007000`: the SR2 function reference silently became the data item. r8_norepo.cob (LOWALGREF08, no REPOSITORY, `MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1`) -> compiles with zero diagnostics, then at run time `Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1)'`. Code read: IntrinsicBinder.cs#KeywordOmittedFunction lines `bool isFn = ctx.Data.UserFunctionNames.Contains(name) || ... || ((ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic || ctx.Data.RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name)) && IntrinsicCatalog.TryGet(name, out _));` then `if (ctx.Symbols.TryResolve(name, ctx.ActiveScope, out _)) return null;`. DataBinder.cs#Bind REPOSITORY loop: `if (re.ALL() is not null) RepositoryAllIntrinsic = true; else if (re.functionName() is { } inf) RepositoryIntrinsics.Add(inf.GetText());` - and no declaration-time consumer anywhere.   · it REJECTS a form the format requires. `{ argument-1 } …` over a table(ALL) argument whose table has OCCURS DEPENDING ON is legal COBOL — §15.3 r14 gives the range as "determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause" — and TryExpandAll expands ALL at BIND time, which cannot see a runtime count, so it emits a BoundOperandError and the program throws at run time.

subject: MEDIAN function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Two independent grounds.
(1) ⛔ THE VARIABLE-REPETITION HALF OF THE FORMAT IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. `{ argument-1 } …` is precisely what §15.3 means by "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times" — and §15.3 then defines THREE ranges for the ALL subscript it entitles: a plain OCCURS count, "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause" (cite.py --check 15.3 => OK §15.3 14)), and "If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table." Only the FIRST works. `TryExpandAll` emits `new BoundOperandError($"table(ALL) over OCCURS DEPENDING table '{name}' …")` at its `if (levels[i].OccursSpec?.Depending is not null)` arm — the program COMPILES CLEAN and dies at RUN time. That is the PB7 shape exactly: invisible to output sampling because compilation succeeds. And the token DYNAMIC appears in NO .g4 file in src/Cobol.Net.Compiler, so the dynamic-capacity range can never be produced at all. So for the one case the `…` exists to express — an argument count that is genuinely variable — MEDIAN produces no value.

subject: MIDRANGE function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator verified the SYNTAX SHAPE and stopped there. The format's load-bearing element is `{ argument-1 } …` — the VARIABLE-REPETITION argument list — and §15.3 r14 defines, normatively, the form that list may take: "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL", with TWO further sentences the compiler does not implement — "If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table" and "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause." TWO GAPS, BOTH PB7-SHAPED — the program COMPILES CLEAN with no diagnostic and dies at RUN TIME, which is precisely why probing a fixed-OCCURS table(ALL) and reading its correct answer could not see them. (1) table(ALL) over an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table: IntrinsicBinder.TryExpandAll tests `levels[i].OccursSpec?.Depending is not null` and emits a BoundOperandError BY DESIGN (its own doc-comment says "a runtime quantity this bind-time expansion cannot produce; staged loud by name"), which lands as NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. (2) table(ALL) over an OCCURS DYNAMIC (dynamic-capacity) table: TryExpandAll builds its OCCURS-level chain from `n.Occurs is not null`, which is null for a dynamic-capacity item, so levels.Count (0) != innerSegs.Count (1) and it falls into the WRONG arm — the diagnostic reads "table(ALL) subscript count for 'T'", which misdescribes the defect and would send the next reader after a subscript-arity bug that is not there. THE VERDICT IS PARTIAL, NOT CONFORMS-WITH-A-NOTE: a run-time NotImplemented on legal source is unimplemented feature, i.e. debt under CLAUDE.md rule 3, and it is unimplemented for MIDRANGE specifically because MIDRANGE is one of the variadic functions §15.3 r14 exists to serve. WHAT IS GENUINELY RIGHT (re-verified, so the fix is not over-scoped): the arity screen rejects the zero-argument and empty-parenthesis forms the format forbids; a single argument, n arguments, negatives, fractions, identifiers, a nested MIDRANGE call, a fixed-OCCURS table(ALL), and the §8.4.3.2 SR2 keyword-omitted comma-separated form under REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC all bind correctly — including the keyword-omitted form COMBINED with table(ALL), which I probed specifically because that is where PB7 lived. The transcribed diagram is corroborated by the §15.6 summary row `| MIDRANGE | Num1 … | Num |` (one-or-more numeric in, numeric out); I did not re-render the PDF and record the adjudicator's render as corroboration, not as my own evidence. EDITIONS: the ODO leg was probed at --std 85 and --std 2023 and fails identically at both; I do not state an edition window for the dynamic-capacity leg because I did not derive OCCURS DYNAMIC's introduction from the spec. EVIDENCE: cite.py --check 15.62.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MIDRANGE</u> ( { argument-1 } … )" -> OK §15.62.2 (General format). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause." -> OK §15.3 14) (Arguments). REFUTER PROBE 1, E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidodo.cob (PROGRAM-ID RFMIDODO): `05 T PIC S9(4)V99 OCCURS 1 TO 5 TIMES DEPENDING ON N` with N=3, T(1..3) = 1.00/5.00/9.00, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MIDRANGE(T(ALL))`. COMPILED CLEAN at --std 2023 (no diagnostic at all) and at --std 85; at RUN TIME both threw `CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... table(ALL) over OCCURS DEPENDING table 'T' (current-count expansion, 15.3)`. Correct answer is (1.00+9.00)/2 = 5.0000. REFUTER PROBE 2, E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmiddy2.cob (PROGRAM-ID RFMIDDY2): `05 T PIC S9(4)V99 OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP`, same three values. COMPILED CLEAN at --std 2023; the run printed CAP=0000000003 (so the capacity register is correct and populated) and then threw `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... table(ALL) subscript count for 'T'`. ATTRIBUTABLE CONTROLS, both compiled and ran: E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidfix.cob (fixed `OCCURS 3 TIMES`, same values) printed FIX=000005000{ = 5.0000 — correct; E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidrep.cob under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` printed REPALL=000005000{ for the keyword-omitted `MIDRANGE(T(ALL))` and REPLIT=000005500{ for `MIDRANGE(1, 2, 10)` — so the keyword-omitted path is NOT the defect and the fixed-OCCURS ALL expansion is correct. E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidctl.cob printed CTL=000005750{ for MIDRANGE(1.5 2.5 10.0) = 5.7500. Source read: IntrinsicBinder.cs#TryExpandAll — the ODO arm and the `levels.Count != innerSegs.Count` arm.

subject: MIN function

Printed folio 888 / PDF page 918 renders as `FUNCTION MIN ( { argument-1 } … )` with FUNCTION and MIN both UNDERLINED and nothing bracketed — exactly what specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.63.2 carries, so the transcription is faithful and no falsely-restrictive OCR residue is in play here. The grammar rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate SUPERSET — the parenthesised group is optional there and the per-function arity is the binder's job. subject: MOD function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL, and the test-ref and editions are both withdrawn. THREE separate refutations.
(1) THE CITED TEST DOES NOT TEST THIS RULE. `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.Mod_SignTable_PinnedToSpec` is a genuine spec-derived fixture (read it: `AssertSpec` runs COBOL.NET ONLY and asserts a literal — it is not the `AssertSameAsLegacy`/`DifferentialGolden` helper in the same file), but what it pins is the four §15.64.4 NOTE rows, i.e. the RETURNED VALUE. It contains no arity arm, no separator arm and no rejection arm, so it cannot close a GENERAL FORMAT row. The adjudication's own note conceded the point — 'the negative arity arms are probe-verified only, not pinned by a fixture' — and then listed the test anyway. test-ref cleared.
(2) THE ALL-SUBSCRIPT FORM IS ACCEPTED, AND MOD'S FORMAT DOES NOT PERMIT IT. §15.3 rule 14 (--check verified) grants the device conditionally: 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a VARIABLE number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name ... followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL.' §15.64.2's format is `FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )` — fixed at two, no ellipsis — so ALL is not available to MOD at all. `IntrinsicBinder.TryExpandAll` runs for EVERY argument of EVERY function and never consults the catalog's arity kind; its own doc comment states the correct rule ('when a VARIADIC function references a table with the ALL subscript') and the code does not implement it. The only thing standing between the expansion and acceptance is the arity screen counting the EXPANSION, so the restriction is enforced ONLY when the element count happens to miss 2 — an accident of the OCCURS count, not a rule. This is the shape memory-flagged as `model_the_rule_shape_not_one_case`: a screen that measures the wrong quantity.
(3) EDITIONS WERE NOT MEASURED AND NOT SPEC-DERIVED. The prior record asserted '85,2002,2014,2023' while every FMT probe in its own evidence ran at `--std 2023` alone. The window is also not derivable from the standard here: §15.64 carries no edition qualifier, Annex E (substantive changes) does not mention MOD, and `docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md` has no MOD row — so the only remaining source is the trailing `85` in IntrinsicCatalog's own MOD row, which is the forbidden derivation (deriving the answer from the code under review). Cleared rather than guessed.
WHAT SURVIVES AND IS RE-VERIFIED: the printed diagram (rendered PDF page 919) is `FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )` with FUNCTION and MOD underlined, no optional element, no ellipsis — the OCR transcription is faithful; the generic keyword-led `functionCall` rule plus the catalog row `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2` rejects 0/1/3 arguments with COBOLNET1504; the §8.4.3.2.3 keyword-omitted (REPOSITORY ... INTRINSIC) form resolves; and reference modification of the result is correctly refused (a boundary the prior pass did not probe). EVIDENCE: Re-probed with the already-built compiler, `--std 2023`, unique PROGRAM-ID per file, all under E:/Temp/modref/.
 · CONTROL MODRF01 — `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(A B)` -> +000000000000000001 and `DISPLAY ... FUNCTION MOD(A B)` -> 1. The harness is sound, so every rejection below is attributable.
 · MODRF08 — `FUNCTION MOD()` -> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION MOD takes 2 argument(s); 0 given (ISO 15.3)`.
 · MODRF06 — `MOVE FUNCTION MOD(11 5)(1:1) TO T` -> `error COBOLNET1629: 'FUNCTION MOD' is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function, so its result cannot be reference-modified (ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2)`. Correct; the format admits no reference modifier.
 · MODRF07 — `05 E PIC S9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.` then `FUNCTION MOD(E(ALL) B)` -> `COBOLNET1504: ... 2 argument(s); 4 GIVEN`. Note the count: the ALL expansion has already happened and the arity screen is counting its OUTPUT. The rejection is incidental.
 · MODRF09 — THE REFUTATION. The identical program with `OCCURS 1 TIMES` COMPILES CLEAN (exit 0) and prints `ALL1 = +0001`. So `FUNCTION MOD(E(ALL) B)` is accepted whenever the expansion lands on 2, and §15.3 rule 14's restriction is nowhere enforced.
Source read, not sampled: `IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore` calls `TryExpandAll(a, args)` inside the per-argument loop with no arity/variadicity guard; `IntrinsicCatalog.Build` row is `Add(new("MOD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ii", "ModScaled", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85))`.
Citations validated: `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.3 "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL."` -> OK §15.3 14); `--check 15.64.1 "The MOD function returns an integer value that is argument-1 modulo argument-2."` -> OK §15.64.1. Annex E scanned for MOD: absent (so 2014->2023 is unchanged; nothing establishes 85/2002 from the spec text).

notes: CONFORMS SUSTAINED -- and, unlike the adjudication, it now survives the boundaries it had merely asserted. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` compiles AND RUNS correctly, so the omission license does not strand NUMVAL. subject: NUMVAL-C function
notes: REFUTED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the `editions` field emptied. (A) ORDER. The prior record found ONE order violation (ANYCASE accepted between argument-1 and argument-2) and held the row at PARTIAL. BindNumvalCFamily's `foreach (var a in argCtxs)` is positionally blind in BOTH directions and has no once-only guard, and two further accepted shapes are non-conforming under ANY reading of the general-format diagram — including a lossy OCR of it — so settling them needs no PDF render: (a) ANYCASE placed BEFORE argument-1, `FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE WS-A "USD")`, where argument-1 sits immediately after the open parenthesis in the format and §15.68.3 r1 names it the first argument, so nothing admits a keyword ahead of it; (b) ANYCASE specified TWICE, `FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(WS-A "USD" ANYCASE ANYCASE)`, where the format carries exactly one [ANYCASE]. Both compile clean and evaluate as though ANYCASE sat in its legal place. A format that silently accepts three distinct shapes it does not describe is a divergence, not a partial implementation. Only the ANYCASE-vs-argument-2 ORDERING is genuinely diagram-dependent, and the verdict no longer rests on it. (B) EDITIONS EMPTIED. The prior record's window was inferred from Annex E.3.3 item 1's 'has been clarified to be consistent with the rest of the standard'. Annex E is INFORMATIVE and E.1 scopes it to 'the substantive changes between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' — 'clarified' fixes no introduction edition and says nothing whatever about 1985 or 2002. Per the edition discipline an unproven window is left EMPTY rather than half-asserted; the observation is retained here. The gate itself remains unverified and unbuilt: neither ANYCASE nor the LOCALE phrase has an edition predicate of its own, so ANYCASE compiles at --std 85 and --std 2002 on the strength of a catalog row (IntroducedIn 85) that is the code under review and cannot be its own evidence. POSITIVE, newly probed: a reference-modified argument-1 binds and values correctly, and arity is genuinely enforced (COBOLNET1504). EVIDENCE: Probe E:/Temp/refnvc/fmtord.cob, --std 2023, compile exit 0, run exit 0: `NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE WS-A "USD")` -> ACPRE=1234.56 (ANYCASE before argument-1, accepted and honoured); `NUMVAL-C(WS-A "USD" ANYCASE ANYCASE)` -> ACDUP=1234.56 (ANYCASE twice); `NUMVAL-C(WS-A(1:11) "usd")` -> REFMD=1234.56 (reference-modified argument-1, correct). Read IntrinsicBinder.BindNumvalCFamily: `foreach (var a in argCtxs) { if (KeywordWordOf(a) == "ANYCASE") { anycase = true; continue; } operands.Add(BindArgOperand(a)); }` — no position test, no once-only test; the only guard is `operands.Count is < 1 or > 2` -> COBOLNET1504. Carried from the prior record: fmt2.cob `NUMVAL-C(WS-A "USD")` and `NUMVAL-C(WS-A, "USD")` both 1234.56; `NUMVAL-C(WS-A ANYCASE "USD")` -> 1234.56; anycase.cob `NUMVAL-C(WS-A, "USD" ANYCASE)` -> 1234.56; locale.cob `NUMVAL-C(WS-A LOCALE)` parses and reaches COBOLNET1518; anycase.cob compiles exit 0 at --std 85 and at --std 2002. cite.py --check 15.68.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>NUMVAL-C</u> ( argument-1" -> OK §15.68.2 (General format), re-run by the refuter. Read Annex E's own heading ('(informative)') and §E.1 verbatim; §E.3.3 1) reads 'The ANYCASE keyword of the NUMVAL-C function has been clarified to be consistent with the rest of the standard.'

subject: NUMVAL-F function
notes: REFUTED: verdict UNCHANGED (PARTIAL) but ONE of the adjudicator's two grounds is now DISPROVED and a NEW, CONCRETE ground replaces it. (a) DISPROVED-AS-A-WORRY: I probed the §15.2 FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form (REPOSITORY. FUNCTION NUMVAL-F INTRINSIC) — the PB7 shape the review brief flags — and it WORKS. That attack fails; the format is reachable in both written forms. (b) STILL OPEN, unchanged: the EDITION window is unproven. The catalog row carries IntroducedIn = 2014 and --std 2002 therefore rejects the format with COBOLNET1502, but per the review's own rule the window may not be taken from the catalog row, and the in-repo spec cannot supply it — Annex E of ISO/IEC 1989:2023 lists only 2014→2023 changes (its sole NUMVAL hit is the unrelated NUMVAL-C ANYCASE item), specs-private holds only the 2023 PDF, and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md has no NUMVAL-F row. THE OPEN QUESTION, needing ISO/IEC 1989:2002 §15: if NUMVAL-F predates 2014, COBOLNET1502 rejects legal 2002 source. editions therefore stays EMPTY. (c) NEW GROUND FOR THE PARTIAL, and it is not speculative: the format's argument-1 position does not accept every legal argument-1. FUNCTION NUMVAL-F(ZERO) and FUNCTION NUMVAL-F(ALL "1") are admitted by §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 (cite.py --check OK) wherever 'literal' appears, and §15.69.3 r1 puts 'literal' there — both compile clean and abort at run time. Detail and probes on AR-15.69.3-1. The SHAPE of the format (one required argument, no optional LOCALE leg) is confirmed conforming; arity is diagnosed at COBOLNET1504. EVIDENCE: Read IntrinsicCatalog.cs: `Add(new("NUMVAL-F", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "NumvalF", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014));`. NEW probe E:/Temp/nvfr/r-e.cob (PROGRAM-ID NVFRE05, --std 2023, `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION NUMVAL-F INTRINSIC FUNCTION ABS INTRINSIC.`): control `COMPUTE R = ABS(-7)` printed A-CONTROL-ABS=000007000 and `COMPUTE R = NUMVAL-F("1.5E+2")` — the FUNCTION keyword omitted — printed B-NOKEYWORD=000150000. The adjudicator's arity and edition-gate probes reproduce: 2 arguments → COBOLNET1504, --std 2002 → COBOLNET1502.

subject: ORD function
notes: Re-verified independently. The canonical PDF was re-extracted at PDF page 930 (printed folio 900): the general format is literally 'FUNCTION ORD ( argument-1 )' — no brackets, no optional element, so there is no room for the falsely-restrictive OCR failure mode; the §15.70.2 transcription is faithful. Grammar (read, not inferred): functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; ORD is not a reserved word and reaches functionName as an ordinary word. Exact arity 1 comes from the catalog row Add(new("ORD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "Ord", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85)) and is enforced by BindIntrinsicCore's MinArgs/MaxArgs gate. RE-PROBED with the built CLI at --std 2023: 'FUNCTION ORD' and 'FUNCTION ORD()' each give COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given', 'FUNCTION ORD(A B)' gives '1 argument(s); 2 given', and the one-argument form binds. Both test-refs exist on disk and both call the one-argument format with value assertions (IF127A has 10 FUNCTION ORD call sites).

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: 15.71.2 FUNCTION ORD-MAX ( {argument-1} ... ) - the variadic format, now covered by a SPEC-DERIVED golden (the previous NIST-only cover is a regression net and cannot close a row). The golden also pins 15.71.4 r3 leftmost-wins on a tie.

notes: 15.72.2 FUNCTION ORD-MIN ( {argument-1} ... ) - variadic format covered by a spec-derived golden, replacing a NIST-only cover.

subject: PI function
notes: Citation re-validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.73.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>PI</u>"` OK - the transcribed format is both words underlined (required) with NO argument list. The FUNCTION-keyword spelling is correct and was re-verified on the built CLI at --std 2023: FUNCTION PI binds and evaluates in DISPLAY / MOVE / COMPUTE / IF, arity 0..0 is enforced ('FUNCTION PI (1)' -> COBOLNET1504), and the 2002 window is gated ('--std 85' -> COBOLNET1502, catalog row IntroducedIn 2002). PARTIAL because the other legal spelling of this same reference is broken: SS8.4.3.2.3 SR2 ('the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier', validated) applies when REPOSITORY declares FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC, and IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction returns null unless the dataReference carries EXACTLY ONE subscriptPart suffix (`if (suffixes.Length != 1 ...) return null;`), so a ZERO-argument keyword-omitted intrinsic can never route - it is the only call path (the two ExpressionBinder chokepoints RefExpr/FieldOperand are the sole call sites). Re-verified: 'COMPUTE R05 = PI.' under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.' compiles with exit 0 and NO diagnostic, then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "reference 'PI'" at run time; 'COMPUTE R05 = PI ().' is a hard parse error (COBOL0001 'no viable alternative'). Same hole for every zero-argument intrinsic (E, RANDOM, CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED) - one pattern, one fix. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test is the ONLY greenfield test that references PI anywhere under tests/ (grep-verified); it exercises the empty-parens spelling 'FUNCTION PI ()' at edition 2014 only, so neither the bare SS15.73.2 two-word format nor the SR2 keyword-omitted zero-argument form is covered - test-needed for both.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function

subject: RANDOM function
notes: PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED BY REVIEW (scripts/render-spec-page.py 935 = printed folio 905): the diagram is exactly `FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( [ argument-1 ] ) ]`, FUNCTION and RANDOM underlined, BOTH bracket levels present — the specs/ISO_COBOL.md transcription is faithful, no OCR over-restriction. Grammar `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` admits all three shapes; the catalog row RANDOM/OptionalTrailing/MinArgs 0/MaxArgs 1 plus the BindIntrinsicCore arity check bound it.
